# R7 — Low-spec hardware profile (LOCKED, UNPROVEN)

> ### SUPERSEDED IN PART 2026-08-11 — THE CAPABLE-GPU PROFILE
>
> **This recipe was solved for an Intel iGPU with 15.4 GB RAM. That
> machine is gone** (migrated to an RTX 5080 Laptop / 31.4 GB on
> 2026-08-10), and Ryan ruled on 2026-08-11: adopt everything that
> improves landscape quality and resolution. Six values changed in
> `DefaultEngine.ini`; the rest of R7 stands, including every trap below,
> which is why this is an amendment and not a replacement.
>
> | cvar | was | now | why |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | `sg.GlobalIlluminationQuality` | 0 | **3** | no GI at all was the largest gap to AAA |
> | `sg.ReflectionQuality` | 0 | **3** | |
> | `r.DynamicGlobalIlluminationMethod` | 0 | **1** | Lumen measured **38.2x** the noise floor |
> | `r.ReflectionMethod` | 0 | **1** | |
> | `r.ScreenPercentage` | 70 | **100** | free here; a MINOR quality lever, do not oversell it |
> | `r.Nanite.MaxPixelsPerEdge` | 4 | **1** | see below — it changed meaning |
>
> Added: `r.Lumen.HardwareRayTracing=1`,
> `r.Lumen.HardwareRayTracing.LightingMode=1` (hit lighting),
> `r.Shadow.Virtual.ResolutionLodBiasDirectional=-0.5`,
> `r.Nanite.Tessellation=1`, and the six downstream GI/reflection values
> the `sg.*` groups expand to at @3.
>
> **`r.Nanite.MaxPixelsPerEdge` IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS, AND NOBODY
> CHANGED IT — ITS MEANING CHANGED.** R7 set it to 4 as a rasterisation
> saving affecting *mesh* silhouette. On 2026-08-11 the LANDSCAPE became
> Nanite, so from that moment it governed *terrain* silhouette — the exact
> thing the displacement work was buying — at a quarter of the available
> resolution. Measured 4 -> 1, single change, 19 stations: **mean +9.25%
> edge energy, 17 of 19 gaining**, and it recovers the same three stations
> that lost most when Nanite came on (`verify_ground` +36.7%,
> `forest_floor` +27.3%, `sweep_0060` +22.7%). Cumulative from
> pre-displacement: **mean +7.49%, 18 of 19 above the noise floor.**
>
> **THE PINS BELOW APPLY TO THE NEW VALUES TOO, AND THIS IS THE WHOLE
> REASON THEY ARE PINNED.** `[SystemSettings]` sets an `sg.*` cvar's VALUE
> WITHOUT RUNNING THE GROUP (measured, see below), so
> `sg.GlobalIlluminationQuality=3` on its own moves nothing. The six
> `@3` expansions are therefore pinned explicitly beside it —
> `r.Lumen.DiffuseIndirect.Allow`, `r.Lumen.FinalGatherMethod`,
> `r.LumenScene.SurfaceCache.AtlasSize`, `r.Lumen.Reflections.Allow`,
> `r.Lumen.Reflections.DownsampleFactor`, `r.SSR.Quality` — exactly as
> `grass.DensityScale` is. Both are set so the two agree and a later group
> expansion is idempotent rather than a silent revert.
>
> **UNVERIFIED, AND SAY SO: the ini is an OVERRIDE, not the state in
> effect** (non-negotiable 17). Every value above was verified in the LIVE
> editor as render state, but the CONFIG FILE has not been proven to
> deliver them — that needs an editor restart, which was deliberately not
> done because the editor holds unsaved landscape-Nanite state.
> **First cold boot must re-read all of them.**
> Artefact: `_verify/20260811_quality_profile.txt`.

Now largely absorbed into **R0**, which owns the literal config values.
R7 retains the reasoning and the traps.

## PRECONDITIONS
- R0's config files in place.

## EXACT VALUES
See R0. Verified 2026-08-02 by headless boot: all ten `sg.*` groups,
screen percentage, Nanite and pipeline-cache cvars confirmed applied via

2. Relaunch the editor (ini changes take effect at startup only).
3. `python scripts/recover_state.py` and diff the cvar table.

  6 s default is unreliable here.

## ORDERED STEPS
**Launching onto a specific level** — avoids a map transition entirely:
```
UnrealEditor.exe <uproject> /Game/Alpine
```
**Repairing an asset too heavy to open** — a FoliageType or StaticMesh
is an ASSET, not level state, so it can be fixed with no level loaded:
```
UnrealEditor.exe <uproject> /Engine/Maps/Templates/OpenWorld
# ... repair the asset ...
# then RESTART directly onto the target level. Do NOT transition.
```

## VERIFICATION
- `python scripts/verify_landscape.py --timeout 25` passes the rule-7
  identity gate and reports the expected actor census.

## CHUNKED WORK ON OVER-MEMORY WORKLOADS (amendment 2026-08-03)

This host has ~1.8 GB free with the editor open. Any operation over a
large asset pack must assume it will saturate, and be built so that
**partial progress survives**:

1. **Enumerate without loading.** Listing is cheap; loading is not.
2. **Work in chunks that APPEND results before the next chunk starts.**
   A saturated editor then costs one chunk, not the whole run.
3. **Resume from what is already recorded**, so a re-run continues
   rather than restarting.
4. **Size the chunk by ESTIMATED COST, not by item count** — see
   REJECTED. Batching does not bound an unbounded unit cost.

**Completion signal:** the script's own final report block plus a
non-zero results file. **Stall test:** editor CPU delta ≈ 0 AND working
set flat AND no log write for 30+ minutes ⇒ hung; kill, log, restart
directly onto the target level.

## REJECTED
- `Loading /Game/Alpine FROM the OpenWorld template` → asserts
  `World Memory Leaks` at `EditorServer.cpp:1951` → restart the process
  directly onto the target level; a workaround that adds a state
  transition adds that transition's failure modes → R8.
- **`Loading a DragonCave asset on this hardware`** → **its textures are
  far beyond the 8K that already hung the editor.** Measured from the
  registry: `12288x4096`, `16384x4096`, `16384x8192`, `20480x8192` and
  **`28672x4096`** (~117 megapixels). KiteDemo's 8192² cooked at an
  estimated 4.6 GB; these are several times larger again → **do not load
  DragonCave assets on this host without a per-asset cost budget.**
  Registry tags answered every enumeration question without loading any
  of them → 2026-08-03.
- **`Assuming the NaniteEnabled registry tag is always present`** → it is
  present on **115/115 DragonCave meshes** (84 ON, 31 OFF) and **absent
  on all 47 KiteDemo meshes**. Absence is "the tag was not written for
  this asset", NOT "Nanite is off" → report it as COULD NOT READ per
  pack, and never infer the state from a missing tag → 2026-08-03.
- **`Treating load_asset as read-only`** → **it can trigger a DDC BUILD.**
  Auditing KiteDemo logged
  `Building texture ... (TFO_AutoDXT, 8192x8192) (Required Memory
  Estimate: 4608.999984 MB)` against 1.8 GB free, and the editor hung for
  20+ minutes with 0 CPU and a 0.13 GB working set, returning nothing.
  Native Fab packs ship without DDC-cooked data for the local cache, so
  the FIRST load cooks them → **read the Asset Registry
  (`find_asset_data` tags) instead, and load only when a question truly
  requires it** → 2026-08-03.
- `Chunking by ITEM COUNT to bound memory` → does not help when a SINGLE
  item exceeds the budget; a chunk of one still hangs → size chunks by
  ESTIMATED COST, or remove the cost by not loading → 2026-08-03.
- `Calling a script read-only because it writes nothing` → writing
  nothing is not costing nothing; ask what it makes the ENGINE do, not
  what it makes the SCRIPT do → 2026-08-03.
- `Retrying a script after "REFUSE (rule 7): no editor nodes answered"
  immediately following heavy work` → that is **saturation, not a
  crash**: the editor stops answering remote execution while still
  answering UDP discovery → wait several minutes; do not retry → R8.
- `Executing against whichever editor holds the port` → PID 18400, an
  unrelated project's editor, was observed holding it → verify the
  connected instance's project path matches `UE_PROJECT_ROOT` before
  every remote execution (CLAUDE.md rule 7) → R8.

# R-STAMP — Terrain feature compositing (PROVISIONAL, UNPROVEN)

Informed by: LESSONS 2026-08-03 (stamp compositing), R1's catalogue spec,
schema v1.12.

**Campaign Pass 1.** R1's catalogue spec defines a STAMP as a terrain
FEATURE — ridge, canyon, crater, outcrop — that is *composited INTO a
base heightmap before import, never imported alone*. There was no such
step; `terrain/stampit_catalogue.json` held 52 STAMP entries the pipeline
could not spend. This is that step.

**PROVISIONAL, not LOCKED:** the compositor is verified offline and its
output exists on disk, but **nothing has been pushed to the editor**. The
landscape still carries the unstamped heightmap. See ADOPTION below —
that is deliberate, and it is the dangerous part of this recipe.

## PRECONDITIONS
- UE 5.8. **No editor contact** — this recipe is entirely offline and
  imports no `unreal`. It may be run with the editor closed.
- Python: `numpy`, `Pillow`. No new dependency **for the compositor
  itself** — corrected 2026-08-08, because as written this read as a
  claim about the whole recipe and the ADOPTION step below it needs
  `scipy`: `derive_aux_maps` imports `terrain_erosion`, which does
  `from scipy import ndimage` at module level (`terrain_erosion.py:29`)
  and cannot load without it. Full package list is in R0's
  PRECONDITIONS.
- `recipes/alpine.json` valid under schema v1.12, carrying a `stamps`
  block. Validate with `import_heightmap._validate_recipe`.
- `terrain/alpine_heightmap.png` present — 16-bit greyscale, no alpha,
  2017×2017 (R1).
- `terrain/stampit_catalogue.json` present, built by
  `scripts/catalogue_heightmaps.py`. 52 entries, all `category: "STAMP"`.
- Stamp sources on disk under `LandscapeLab/Content/StampIt/`. These are
  **Fab vendor content and are gitignored** — the catalogue's `sha256` is
  the durable reference, not the path.

## EXACT VALUES

### Grid, measured from the recipe (not assumed)
```
resolution      2017 x 2017 px
spacing         4.000 m/px          span 8064.0 m
world extent    X -4032.0 .. 4032.0 m    Y -4032.0 .. 4032.0 m
origin_m        [-4032.0, -4032.0]
z_scale         2560.0 m over the full 16-bit range
                = 0.039063 m per heightmap unit
base relief     0 .. 31457 units = 0.00 .. 1228.81 m (48.0% of range)
ADD headroom    1331.19 m before the highest pixel overflows uint16
```
**Array COLUMN is world X and array ROW is world Y.** Read out of
`place_foliage.py:192, 213, 234-236`, not assumed. Transposing it places
every stamp at the mirror of where the recipe says, and every downstream
check agrees with the mistake because they all read the same file.

### The one locked placement
```
id              east_ridge_outcrops
stamp_sha256    ce0cc91ab19c27051f819cf3d54c4c02aba4327c26fe4665dde3ed2408a3d1b4
  -> filename   HM_Rugged_Rocks_14_Ex.png   tag "outcrop"   4096x4096
centre_m        [2668.0, 2568.0]      size_m   1200.0  (= 300 px)
rotation_deg    0.0    flip_x false   flip_y   false
blend           ADD    datum "min"    amplitude_m 180.0
falloff         0.35   falloff_shape  "chebyshev"   opacity 1.0
```
Tunables — locked default, valid range, what it affects:
- `amplitude_m` **180.0**; > 0; metres spanned by the stamp's full 0..1
  range. Raising it past the measured **1331.19 m** headroom is refused,
  never wrapped.
- `falloff` **0.35**; (0, 1]; fraction of the HALF-WIDTH over which the
  mask ramps 1 → 0. Smaller = harder edge. `0` is refused (division by
  zero in the mask).
- `opacity` **1.0**; (0, 1]. `0` is refused — it is a placement that
  reports success and does nothing.
- `datum` **"min"**; `zero|min|mean|median`; where the stamp's own value
  range is pinned. **ADD only**; `anchor_m` is forbidden on ADD and
  required on MAX/MIN/MASKED.

### Normative: a stamp is a FULL FIELD, not a delta
All 52 catalogue entries report `relief_stats.min == 0` and
`max >= 65534`. A stamp value of 0 means "the bottom of the stamp's own
range", **not** "no change". Same class as the heightmap's 32768 datum: a
number arrives and means something other than what was assumed.

### Normative: every blend mode applies through the mask
With `H` the base in metres, `s` the resampled stamp 0..1, `m` the mask:
```
ADD     target = H + (s - D) * amplitude_m        D from `datum`
MAX     target = max(H, anchor_m + s * amplitude_m)
MIN     target = min(H, anchor_m + s * amplitude_m)
MASKED  target =     anchor_m + s * amplitude_m

H' = H + m * (target - H)      for EVERY mode
```
so at `m == 0` every mode is exactly the identity. A raw
`np.maximum(H, stamp)` cannot be feathered and leaves the rectangular
seam. `D` is measured only over pixels where `m > 0`.

### Normative: the falloff is smoothstep, and that is CORRECTNESS
```
r = max(|u|,|v|) (chebyshev)   or   sqrt(u²+v²) (euclidean)
t = clamp((1 - r) / falloff, 0, 1)
m = t·t·(3 - 2t) · opacity
```
A LINEAR ramp is C0 but not C1: its derivative jumps at `r = 1-falloff`
and at `r = 1`. **Terrain shading reads the SLOPE**, so a derivative
discontinuity draws a visible crease even though the height field is
continuous. Measured on the alpine base — max |slope change| in the edge
annulus:

| Mask | max slope change |
|---|---|
| smoothstep | **0.410°** |
| hard cut (control) | **12.751°** |
| 16-bit quantisation floor | 0.559° |

The smoothstep result is **below the quantisation floor** — i.e. not
merely better, but indistinguishable from no seam at this bit depth.

`chebyshev` keeps the whole square and feathers to its edge; `euclidean`
inscribes a circle and discards the corners (21.5% of area).

### Normative: `base` ≠ `output` ≠ `heightmap.source`
Enforced by the **validator**, not the script. Compositing onto the
previous output accumulates stamps every re-run **while reporting
success** — hard pipeline rule 3. Making it unrepresentable beats
rejecting it at runtime (non-negotiable 3).

## ORDERED STEPS
```
1. python scripts/composite_stamps.py --selftest
   # Runs 14 gate tests + determinism + base-immutability. Do this FIRST:
   # it is the only step that proves the tool before it touches data.

2. python scripts/composite_stamps.py --dry-run
   # Reports grid, headroom and per-placement deltas. Writes nothing.

3. python scripts/composite_stamps.py
   # Writes terrain/alpine_stamped.png AND its .stamps.json sidecar.
   # Never writes the base.
```
Step 1 precedes step 2 because a compositor whose gates have not been
exercised has not been shown to refuse anything.

**ADOPTION IS A SEPARATE, DELIBERATE ACT AND IS NOT PART OF THIS RECIPE.**
The output is not `heightmap.source` and the validator refuses to let it
be assigned by accident. Adopting a stamped map means editing the recipe
by hand, and it invalidates — the sidecar lists this explicitly under
`downstream_invalidated`:
```
textures/alpine_weights.png                      (make_layer_weightmap.py)
terrain/alpine_flow.png / alpine_deposition.png  (make_alpine_terrain.py)
foliage/alpine_Conifer.json + 160,448 PLACED INSTANCES (place_foliage.py)
```
**Adoption orphans the Z of all 160,448 conifers.** Do it behind a
RISKY-OP CHECKPOINT — a named tag, e.g. `pre-stamp-adoption` — and
re-bake and re-place in the same session, or do not adopt.

### ADOPTION — MANDATORY ORDERED STEPS (revised 2026-08-06; executed and verified that day)

**Editing `heightmap.source` changes a FILE. Adoption changes the WORLD,
and it is not complete until a live-world instrument reads the adopted
file.** The 2026-08-03 "adoption" followed the file-side steps perfectly,
verified completely, and changed nothing — the push step was NEVER IN THE
PROCEDURE (root cause: WHY THE PUSH DID NOT PERSIST, commit 20f6e5eb).
These steps are mandatory text so the recipe can no longer describe a
world change that never touches the world.

1. RISKY-OP CHECKPOINT: named tag. Edit `heightmap.source` by hand.
   Hash-assert the adopted copy against the producer's sidecar
   (non-negotiable 20).
2. **PUSH: `python scripts/push_heightmap.py --push --expect-change
   --timeout 25`.** `--expect-change` is correct on an adoption — the
   difference is the point. It does NOT widen the 4-unit tolerance; the
   pre-import render-target check still gates the write texel-for-texel
   and the post-push export read-back is load-bearing (exit 5 = do not
   save).
3. **EXIT GATE A — independent read-back**: `--probe-size` +
   `--probe-layout`, compared OFFLINE against BOTH the adopted map and
   its predecessor. The export must match the ADOPTED map under IDENTITY
   at delta 0.0. Verified 2026-08-06: 161/161 texels at 0.0 vs v2 while
   v1 missed by median 1135 — the instrument flipped exactly.
4. **COLLISION FLUSH, SAME SESSION**: `force_layers_full_update()` on the
   `Landscape` actor (stub `unreal.py:597908`, class at :597565). The
   edit-layer import path DEFERS collision
   (`LandscapeEditInterface.cpp:438-440`); the dirty region lives in
   MEMORY and dies with the editor session, so a later-session flush is a
   proven no-op (measured 2026-08-05: identical p50/p90/max before and
   after).
5. **EXIT GATE B**: `python scripts/check_collision_truth.py --n 100`
   must EXIT 0 (p90 <= 0.30 m). Exit 4 "could not measure" is NOT a
   pass. First-ever PASS 2026-08-06: p50 0.026 / p90 0.209 / max 0.716 m
   vs v2, 100/100 hits, reproduced on a second seed (p90 0.159).
6. ONLY IF GATES A AND B PASS: `save_level.py` dry-run, confirm the
   scope, then `--save`. Then re-bake weights, re-place/re-verify
   foliage, and re-run `check_collision_truth` + `verify_grounding.py`
   post-save. Instances planned on the adopted map may simply be correct
   — MEASURE before moving anything (2026-08-06: conifer max 0.001 m,
   boulder max 0.103 m, both unchanged through the push).

**REJECTED (anti-spec), adoption steps:**
- `first push after the staging source changes, trusted first try` ->
  symptom: REFUSE at stage `verify_rt`, "drawn render target is FLAT
  (min 0.500 max 0.500)", exit 6, nothing written -> cause: the staging
  texture `/Game/Debug/T_PushHeight_Source` was re-imported and the
  material sampled its 32x32 placeholder mip before streaming finished
  (`push_heightmap.py:2064-2090`, the documented residency race) ->
  correct: re-run the push once; the texture is resident on the second
  run (2026-08-06: retry pushed and verified clean, worst |dv| 0.00
  units on 1280 samples). Two refusals in a row = stop and diagnose
  (standing rule 6), not a third retry.
- `flush collision in a LATER session` -> symptom: call returns "ok",
  collision unmoved to three decimals -> cause: the deferred dirty
  region died with the pushing session -> correct: flush in the SAME
  session as the push (2026-08-05 measurement, R-COLLISION-REBUILD).
- `adoption = edit heightmap.source + re-derive downstream` -> every
  gate green, world unchanged, instances float by up to ~273 m ->
  correct: adoption ENDS with gates A and B, above (2026-08-03
  post-mortem, WHY THE PUSH DID NOT PERSIST).

## RULING — RE-ERODING AN ADOPTED TERRAIN IS A TERRAIN CHANGE (2026-08-03)

`terrain/alpine_flow.png` and `alpine_deposition.png` are BYPRODUCTS of
the hydraulic erosion inside `make_alpine_terrain.py`. After adoption they
describe a surface that no longer exists, and `place_foliage` reads the
flow map for Conifer `flow_bias: 0.45` — so a foliage re-place against
them is a **silently wrong forest**.

**Refreshing them is NOT re-generating the terrain.** The distinction is
a ruling, not a preference:

| | What it is | Approval path |
|---|---|---|
| **Aux refresh** — `scripts/derive_aux_maps.py` | Runs the SAME `hydraulic_droplets` on a COPY, keeps flow + deposition, **discards the eroded height**. Asserts the source array is unchanged before writing. | None. It cannot alter the terrain. |
| **Re-erosion** — letting the droplets keep their height | Carves drainage THROUGH the newly stamped ridges. Changes the approved landform. | **FULL PATH**: composition → hillshade render → Ryan's confirmation. Never a side effect of an aux refresh. |

Re-erosion is **deferred, not rejected** — it is a genuinely promising
idea (carved drainage through the new massifs may be what elevates the
traversal corridor) and is in `BACKLOG.md` as a candidate v3 terrain
iteration, to be judged AFTER the region is dressed.

## VERIFICATION

**(a) Independent instrument.** The compositor does NOT verify itself.
The evidence is a **hillshade render of base vs output**, produced by a
separate path and inspected as pixels:
`_verify/20260803_rstamp_hillshade_before_after.png`. Non-negotiable 10 —
look at the pixels before running a statistic.

**(b) The gate was tested in BOTH directions.** `--selftest` proves the
following bad inputs are REFUSED, with exit codes:
```
overflow -> uint16 wrap                       exit 4
underflow below 0                             exit 4
non-finite composite                          exit 4
non-finite even with --allow-clamp            exit 4
placement entirely off-map                    exit 6
edge clip with allow_edge_clip = false        exit 6
base == output                                schema
output == heightmap.source                    schema
anchor_m present on an ADD placement          schema
opacity 0   (a silent no-op)                  schema
falloff 0   (division by zero in the mask)    schema
NaN amplitude_m                               schema
empty placements array                        schema
```
and that **one good input is ACCEPTED**: edge clip with
`allow_edge_clip = true`. Thirteen refusals and one acceptance — a gate
that only refuses is as untested as one that only accepts.

**(c) Objective numbers for the locked placement**, from the sidecar:
```
mask_pixels        89,401          moved_pixels    76,594
delta_max_m        179.963         (against amplitude_m 180.0)
delta_mean_abs_m    24.932
pre_clamp_max      34,207 units    clamped: FALSE, 0 pixels either side
base_sha256        402df999...     output_sha256   c8c97650...
```
`delta_max_m` 179.963 against a declared 180.0 is the mask's smoothstep
peak falling just short of 1.0 at the sampled grid — expected, and the
tolerance is **< 0.05 m**. A `delta_max_m` of exactly 180.0 would mean
the mask reached 1.0, and a value **above** 180.0 means the datum is
wrong.

**Determinism:** two in-process composites are bit-identical, and the
base array is unchanged after two runs. Both asserted in `--selftest`.

## REJECTED
- **`MAX blend with an anchor_m above the local ground`** → **it FLOODS.**
  `MAX` compares absolute surfaces, so everywhere the base sits below
  `anchor_m` the stamp wins and the whole footprint is lifted to at least
  the anchor. Signature, all three visible at once in
  `_verify/20260803_compose_v1.png`: an **artificial flat plateau** at
  exactly `anchor_m`, a **straight mask-edge seam** where the falloff
  reaches zero against that plateau, and a **jump in snow fraction**
  (17.5% → 33.8% of the map from one 5 km placement) → **`ADD` with
  `datum: min` is the EMBOSSING DEFAULT**: it adds the stamp's relief on
  top of the existing surface, so the base shape survives and no plateau
  can form → R-STAMP, 2026-08-03.
- **`Composing landform stamps and assuming steep faces got texture`** →
  **stamps add large-scale SLOPE faster than fine RELIEF, so composing
  MORE of them makes this WORSE.** Measured after the Pass 1
  composition: `|laplacian| < 1.0 m` on **45.2%** of faces steeper than
  45°, and the stamped surface was **smoother on steep ground than the
  base it came from** (median 1.133 m vs **1.289 m**). The symptom is
  **glossy featureless walls** at render time, and it cannot be fixed in
  the material because the landscape normal is derived from the height
  field → **`stamps.detail_relief`** (schema v1.16), a slope-masked
  ridged-noise pass applied AFTER every placement, so it also reaches
  steep ground no stamp touched → R-STAMP, 2026-08-03.
- **`Choosing detail_relief wavelength by eye instead of against the cell
  size`** → the first attempt used `wavelength_m: 64, octaves: 5,
  gain: 0.55, amplitude_m: 4.5` and moved the smooth-face fraction by
  **2.5 points** (45.2% → 42.7%), i.e. it did essentially nothing while
  reporting a healthy `±2.27 m ridge on 58.81% of the map`. **64 m is a
  LANDFORM scale, not a cliff-texture scale on 4 m cells**, and the
  amplitude that survives to the fine octaves is `gain^(n-1)` of the
  total — 0.09× at octave 5. Measured median |laplacian| of the detail
  field alone: **0.387 m**, against a base terrain median of 1.289 m.
  → derive it: for a ripple of amplitude `A` and wavelength `L` on cells
  of size `c`, `|lap| ≈ A(2π/L)²c²`. Characterised on a 4 m grid:

  | wavelength | octaves | gain | amp | median &#124;lap&#124; |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | 64 m | 5 | 0.55 | 4.5 | 0.387 |
  | 48 m | 4 | 0.60 | 6.0 | 0.671 |
  | 32 m | 3 | 0.70 | 7.0 | 1.353 |
  | **28 m** | **3** | **0.75** | **9.0** | **1.954** |

  Keep the finest octave comfortably above one cell (28/4 = 7 m here);
  at or below the cell size it is aliasing, not relief → R-STAMP,
  2026-08-03.
- **`Reporting a detail pass by its own amplitude and coverage`** → "±2.27 m
  ridge on 58.81% of the map" is TRUE and tells you nothing about whether
  the defect was fixed. It is the instrument reporting on itself
  (non-negotiable 8) → verify with the SAME statistic that diagnosed the
  problem: the fraction of steep faces below the |laplacian| threshold →
  R-STAMP, 2026-08-03.
- **`Smooth fbm for the detail pass`** → turns a glossy wall into a
  *lumpy* glossy wall; broken rock has CRESTS, not bumps → **ridged**
  noise, `(1 − |noise|)²` per octave → R-STAMP, 2026-08-03.
- **`A one-sided detail field`** → every steep face is lifted, the mean
  surface rises and **the snowline moves** — a scene change disguised as
  a texture change → mean-centre the field before scaling, and record
  `net_mean_m` in the sidecar so the claim is checkable → R-STAMP,
  2026-08-03.
- **`MIN blend used for anything but capping`** → it only ever removes
  height, so using it to "add a valley" deletes terrain wherever the
  stamp is low. **`MIN` is the BASIN TOOL**: `anchor_m` sets the floor
  and `amplitude_m` the cap, which is how the foothill basins that carry
  the region's difficulty gradient are made → R-STAMP, 2026-08-03.
- **`A pure euclidean or chebyshev falloff on a large placement`** → the
  contour where the stamp stops contributing is a **perfect circle**
  (or square), and at airship altitude that shape is legible as a soft
  tonal ring even though the height field is continuous across it —
  nothing in real terrain is a circle → **`falloff_jitter`** (schema
  v1.15) perturbs the contour with deterministic value noise. Measured
  bar: coefficient of variation of the outer contributing radius
  **≥ 0.05**; the eight locked placements measure **0.089 – 0.367** →
  R-STAMP, 2026-08-03.
- **`Two-sided falloff jitter`** → `r_j` can fall BELOW `r`, so the mask
  is still non-zero at the geometric footprint edge and meets a hard cut
  there — **reintroducing the exact seam the smoothstep falloff exists to
  prevent, as a side effect of fixing a cosmetic problem** → the jitter
  is **ONE-SIDED**, `r_j = r · (1 + jitter · n01)` with `n01 ∈ [0,1]`, so
  `r_j ≥ r` always and the mask is provably zero on and outside the
  footprint. Verified by sampling dense rings at r = 1.0, 1.0001, 1.2,
  1.5 across every jitter/scale combination: max mask **1.5e-31** →
  R-STAMP, 2026-08-03.
- **`Linear interpolation in the jitter noise`** → its derivative jumps
  on every lattice line, drawing a faint **rectangular grid** into the
  falloff — one geometric fingerprint traded for a worse one → smoothstep
  fade in `_value_noise`; same argument as the falloff mask itself,
  terrain shading reads the SLOPE → R-STAMP, 2026-08-03.
- **`Assuming a placement fits because centre ± size/2 is inside the
  map`** → **rotation expands the bounding box by `|cos θ| + |sin θ|`**
  (1.41× at 45°), so a placement that fits unrotated clips once turned.
  The edge gate refused three times during the Pass 1 composition —
  `summit_massif_south`, `foothill_basin_east`, `drainage_south` — each
  correctly, at exit 6 → size the footprint from the ROTATED extent, and
  move the placement inward rather than setting `allow_edge_clip` →
  R-STAMP, 2026-08-03.
- `Dropping a stamp in with np.maximum(H, stamp)` → a **rectangular seam**
  you cannot feather, and a slope discontinuity the shading draws as a
  crease → every mode applies through the mask, `H' = H + m*(target-H)`
  → R-STAMP.
- `A LINEAR falloff ramp` → C0 but not C1; the derivative jumps at both
  ends and terrain shading reads the SLOPE, so a visible crease survives
  a continuous height field → **smoothstep** `t·t·(3-2t)`; measured
  0.410° vs 12.751°, below the 0.559° quantisation floor → R-STAMP.
- `Treating a stamp as a DELTA` → a stamp value of 0 subtracts the full
  amplitude instead of doing nothing, because all 52 catalogue entries
  span 0..65535 → a stamp is a FULL FIELD; `amplitude_m` scales it and
  `datum`/`anchor_m` pin it → schema v1.12.
- `stamps.output == stamps.base` → stamps ACCUMULATE on every re-run
  **while reporting success**, breaking idempotence (hard pipeline rule
  3) → refused by the validator, not by the script → schema v1.12.
- `stamps.output == heightmap.source` → adopting a stamped map becomes a
  **side effect of running the compositor**, silently orphaning 160,448
  conifer Z values → refused by the validator; adoption is a deliberate
  recipe edit → schema v1.12.
- `anchor_m on an ADD placement` → an inert field that reads like a
  setting; this project has paid for inert fields repeatedly → `datum`
  and `anchor_m` are MODE-EXCLUSIVE, required in their mode and
  forbidden outside it → schema v1.12.
- `opacity 0 / falloff 0` → `opacity 0` is a placement that reports
  success and changes nothing; `falloff 0` divides by zero in the mask →
  both refused; the valid range is **(0, 1]** → R-STAMP.
- `Letting an ADD overflow uint16` → the value **wraps**, so a peak
  becomes a pit and the map still validates as a 16-bit PNG → refused at
  exit 4 with the measured headroom (1331.19 m) printed → R-STAMP.
- `Assuming array row is world X` → every stamp lands at the mirror of
  its recipe position, and every downstream check agrees with the
  mistake because they all read the same file → **column is X, row is
  Y**, read from `place_foliage.py:192, 213, 234-236` → R-STAMP.
- `Adopting terrain/alpine_stamped.png without re-baking` →
  `textures/alpine_weights.png`, the flow/deposition maps and all
  160,448 placed conifers are computed against the OLD surface and are
  silently orphaned → adopt only behind a named risky-op checkpoint,
  re-baking and re-placing in the same session → R-STAMP, BACKLOG.

# R-ASSET — Asset intake (PROVISIONAL, UNPROVEN)

Governs **every** asset entering the project. PROVISIONAL because the
skeletal/retarget half has never been executed — the Paragon import
chain becomes its first worked example.

## PRECONDITIONS
- R0 satisfied. `ASSETS.md` exists and is writable.
- Source archive staged under `Free/` (or a recorded equivalent).
- `WORLD_VISION.md` read, for the photoreal-coherence check.

## EXACT VALUES

### QUALITY TIER — LOCKED RULING 2026-08-03

**The photoreal lane takes the HIGHEST AVAILABLE TIER, everywhere.**

| Dimension | Locked value |
|---|---|
| Mesh source quality | **Nanite source quality** where the vendor offers it; **High** where it does not |
| Textures | **4K preferred**; take the highest shipped if 4K is absent |
| Consistency | **ONE TIER EVERYWHERE** |

**Mixed tiers across regions is a REJECTED pattern.** Not because a lower
tier looks bad on its own, but because tier inconsistency is miserable to
diagnose later: a region that reads slightly wrong sends you hunting
lighting, materials and LODs before you think to check what tier its
source assets came in at. One tier removes that entire class of
investigation.

**Disk is the tradeoff, and it is accepted.** Do not silently
down-tier to save space. If a download would breach the disk floor,
**stop and report** so the user can prioritise — never substitute a
lower tier to make it fit.

- Tunable: none. This is a ruling, not a parameter. Changing it is a
  decision for Ryan, and changing it for ONE asset is forbidden outright.
- Disk floor: **50 GB free.** Check before and during any bulk intake.
  Baseline at batch 1: 204.7 GB free of 475.5 GB.

**Recorded in `ASSETS.md` for every asset, before import:**
- Source (vendor, URL, version/date) and **licence**.
- Intended role and the recipe that will name it.
- Photoreal-coherence verdict against WORLD_VISION's Paragon /
  Megascans / MetaHuman lane.

**Naming and folders (locked):**
```
/Game/Meshes/<object_name>          static meshes  (FLAT — no subfolders)
/Game/Meshes/Materials/M_<name>     mesh materials
/Game/Surfaces/T_<SurfaceId>_C|_N|_R   surface sets
/Game/Textures/T_<Biome>_<Layer>    landscape layer textures
/Game/Foliage/FT_<Species>          foliage types
/Game/Foliage/GT_<biome>_<Name>     grass types
```
The importer is **flat** — a `/Game/Surfaces/<name>/` prefix matches
nothing (this broke a save allow-list, R6 REJECTED).

**Import settings (locked):**
- Static mesh: normalized through `scripts/blender/normalize_asset.py`
  to a **base-centre pivot**, verified within 1 mm, gated at ≤1.0 m
  horizontal / ≤0.25 m vertical.
- Textures: 16-bit single-channel sources in mask roles
  (`alpha`, `roughness`) are converted to 8-bit at import. sRGB OFF for
  masks/normals/roughness, ON for albedo.
- Collision: `collision_with_world = False` for foliage (measured on
  `FT_Conifer`).
- LODs: built by R5's `percent = screen_size²` rule, **section-complete
  at every level**.

### THE THREE INTAKE BRANCHES (2026-08-03, first full execution)

An asset enters by exactly one of three paths. They differ in what
arrives, who builds the materials, and what verification means.

**BRANCH 1 — WEB-DOWNLOAD** (zip of USD / FBX / textures)
- Source: a vendor zip in `Downloads`, staged to `Free/_intake/<pack>/`.
- Materials: **we build them** with `make_foliage_material`, explicit
  `--slot` per role. The ambiguous-role guard applies.
- Scale: **must be measured**, never assumed — FBX unit traps are real.
- Verification: pivot gate, LOD chain, spawn + render.
- Examples: `rock_collection_04`, `tree_english_oak_forest_01`,
  the fir and grass sets.

**BRANCH 2 — FAB-PLUGIN** (native `.uasset`, in-editor Fab window)
- Source: the Fab window inside the editor. **The plugin is enabled by
  engine default** (`Fab.uplugin` declares `"EnabledByDefault": true`),
  so it does NOT appear in `.uproject` — see REJECTED.
- **DESTINATION: named top-level folders under `Content/`, NOT
  `Content/Fab/`.** Measured 2026-08-03: `Content/KiteDemo`,
  `Content/DragonCave`, `Content/Atlantis_Ruins`, `Content/StampIt`.
  Anyone looking for `Content/Fab/` finds nothing and would wrongly
  conclude the import failed.
- Materials: **ship already wired. VERIFY, do not rebuild.** The sampler
  audit still applies — check sampler type against each texture's
  compression, because a mismatch is silent.
- These assets **bypass our naming convention** (they keep vendor
  folder structure). That is accepted for native packs; do NOT rename
  them, and record the real path in `ASSETS.md`.
- Verification: scale check, Nanite state, sampler audit, spawn+render.

**SOURCE IS IGNORED; DERIVATIVES ARE COMMITTED.** The 15.9 GB of Fab
content is gitignored — it is vendor SOURCE, re-downloadable, and
`ASSETS.md` carries source/licence/path. Anything the pipeline CREATES
on top of it is **pipeline output and MUST be committed**: it is not
re-downloadable.

**Git cannot enforce that line, so a convention plus a check does.**
Git will not re-include a file whose parent directory is excluded, so no
`!negation` can rescue anything placed inside a Fab folder. Two holes
follow, both verified:

1. **NEVER AUTHOR INTO A FAB FOLDER.** A material instance or scatter
   registration written to `Content/KiteDemo/...` is silently ignored and
   vanishes on a fresh clone, with no error. Every derivative goes to a
   project convention path (`/Game/Meshes/Materials/`, `/Game/Foliage/`,
   ...) — all confirmed tracked by `git check-ignore`.
2. **AN IN-PLACE MODIFICATION IS NOT A COMMITTABLE DERIVATIVE.** Enabling
   Nanite on a Fab static mesh, or changing its LOD or collision, edits
   an ignored file: the asset re-downloads in its original state and the
   change is gone. **Express it as a REPLAYABLE STEP in the recipe
   instead.** That is strictly better than committing bytes — it is
   idempotent and survives a vendor update, which a committed blob would
   not.

Enforced by `python scripts/check_fab_boundary.py`, which baselines the
ignored tree and reports anything added or modified inside it. Run it
after any bulk operation on Fab content. Baseline at batch 1: 972 files,
15,891 MB.

**RISKY-OP CHECKPOINT CAVEAT — recovery for ignored content is
RE-DOWNLOAD, NOT GIT.** A git tag cannot roll back files git does not
track. Any checkpoint taken before a bulk operation on Fab folders MUST
say so in its tag message, naming the pack and its Fab source, so the
next session knows the restore path is the Fab library rather than
`git checkout`.

**BRANCH 3 — LAUNCHER-VAULT** (separate projects)
- Arrives as a whole project, not Content-folder assets.
- **NEVER bulk-merged.** Create as a separate project, then cherry-pick
  individual assets through this recipe. See `BACKLOG.md`.

### ORM-PACKED MATERIALS — third material branch

Some vendors ship one packed texture instead of separate maps.
`rock_collection_04` ships `T_<name>_A` (albedo), `_N` (normal), `_ORM`.

**Channel mapping, MEASURED 2026-08-03 across four ORM textures — not
assumed from convention:**

| Channel | Role | Measured evidence |
|---|---|---|
| **R** | Ambient occlusion | mean 0.72–0.80 **and `corr(R, albedo luminance)` POSITIVE on all 7** — cavities darken in both maps together |
| **G** | Roughness | mean 0.64–0.67 **and `corr(G, albedo luminance)` NEGATIVE on all 7** — rougher where the albedo is darker, the opposite sign to R |
| **B** | Metallic | **identically 0.000, sd 0.000** — consistent with a dielectric rock |

**EPISTEMIC STATUS: confirmed by convention + consistency, NOT yet by a
nonzero specimen.** This is deliberately weaker than it first reads, and
the weakness is the point.

A flat-zero channel is *consistent* with `B = Metallic` on a rock — but a
rock's metallic map is legitimately all-zero, so **a flat channel cannot
distinguish "B is Metallic and correctly zero" from "B is unused
padding".** Both predict exactly what was measured.

**R and G ARE now discriminated, B is not.** A second measurement
(2026-08-03) correlated each channel against albedo luminance across all
7 rocks: **R correlates POSITIVELY, G NEGATIVELY, on every one.** Those
opposite signs are a real discriminating observation — occlusion darkens
with the albedo in cavities, while roughness rises where albedo falls.
A swapped R/G would have produced the opposite signs. So the R/G half of
the mapping is measured, not merely conventional.

**B remains undiscriminated**, and no rock can settle it.

The mapping is almost certainly right — ORM is a near-universal
convention. It is recorded here as the working assumption, not as a
measurement.

### MEGASCANS BRANCH — notes measured 2026-08-05 (Wild Grass)

**RAW OMITS DISPLACEMENT.** The `Raw/<id>_tier_0` tier ships `B`, `N`,
`ORM` and **no `H`**. Only `High/<id>_tier_1` carries the height map. So
**High is not merely sufficient for the HeightLerp path, it is
REQUIRED** — a Raw intake cannot feed displacement at all.

**THE HEIGHT DISCRIMINATOR SUPERSEDES THE ALBEDO TEST as the reference
method for ORM channel identification.** Occlusion tracks DEPTH
regardless of pigment — a physically grounded, class-portable premise,
where the albedo test's premise is rock-specific. Measured on Wild Grass:

| chan | corr(height) | corr(albedo) | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| R | **+0.189** | −0.134 | AO — tracks depth 3.7x more than G |
| G | −0.051 | **−0.623** | Roughness — tracks albedo 4.6x more than R |

**Two ORTHOGONAL signals giving opposite assignments is a stronger proof
than the original rock result**, which rested on one. Without a height
map, `unpack_orm.py` falls back to the albedo test **and states in its
report that it used the weaker instrument** — instruments declare their
own grade.

**SOURCE IS 8-BIT; THE EDITOR EXPORT IS LOSSLESS.** `export_assets`
writes 8-bit PNG, which would silently flatten a 16-bit source. It does
not here: `blueprint_get_texture_source_disk_and_memory_size()` returns
**67,108,864 bytes over 4096² = exactly 4 bytes/pixel = BGRA8**. A
16-bit RGBA source would be 8 bytes/px, a 16-bit grayscale 2. So
`texture_16bit.stage_8bit` correctly reports *"not the 16-bit
single-channel defect class"* rather than fabricating precision.

**UPGRADE CONDITION.** Promote this entry to *measured* the first time a
**metallic-bearing asset** shows a **nonzero B that lands where metal is
visibly present**. `Content/Atlantis_Ruins` is the likely first
specimen — ruins commonly carry metal trim, and the pack ships 12
skeletal meshes. Until then, verify per pack rather than trusting the
acronym; the channel ordering is a convention, not a standard.

*(This follows the precision note on the heightmap hashes: 102 distinct
hashes did not prove independent terrains either, and saying so was what
kept that claim honest.)*

- Import: `_ORM` is a MASK texture — `sRGB = OFF`,
  `compression_settings = TC_Masks`.
- Wire `G` to Roughness. Do NOT wire `B` to Metallic for a dielectric;
  leave Metallic at the constant 0 and save the sampler.

### ANIMATION-ONLY FBX — THE SKELETON IS A PREREQUISITE, NOT A STEP

Measured 2026-08-03 on `animations.zip` (1,374 FBX, 2,401,071,840 bytes
uncompressed), and confirmed at the engine source:

**A mesh-free animation FBX will import NOTHING unless a skeleton
already exists and is selected.**
`InterchangeGenericAnimationPipeline.cpp:660` gates skeleton creation on
`IsSkeletonValid()` being **TRUE** — i.e. a skeleton must ALREADY be
set. With no mesh and no skeleton the pipeline falls through to the
early return at `:710-714` and produces no asset at all, silently.

**Consequence: acquiring and importing the UE5 mannequin skeleton is
STEP 0 of any animation intake, not an optional extra.** The project
already has one at `Content/Mannequin` (26 uassets), delivered with the
template content.

Measured facts about this pack, each independently re-derived:
```
FBX version        7300            UnitScaleFactor 1.0 (centimetres)
UpAxis             2 (+1)          FrontAxis 1, CoordAxis 0
TimeMode           6 = 30 fps      1 animation stack per file
structure          89 Models (1 Root + 88 LimbNode), identical in all 1374
                   0 Geometry, 0 Deformer, 0 Material, 0 Texture
                   -> animation-only, one single skeleton across the pack
total              153,748 frames, 5,124.9 s
durations          min 0.1667 s, median 3.6667 s, max 25.0 s
```

**NAMING TRAP: every imported AnimSequence lands as
`<basename>Unreal_Take`, not `<basename>`.** Any later step that looks
up an asset by its source basename finds nothing.

**Retarget procedure (skeletal) — VALUE UNVERIFIED, never executed.**
Intended shape: IK Rig per source skeleton → IK Retargeter chain mapping
→ retarget → verify by playing one locomotion clip and checking foot
contact. Exact chain mappings per source skeleton (Paragon, MetaHuman)
are unknown until we run it. Recovery: `BACKLOG.md`.

## ORDERED STEPS
```
1. Record source + licence + role in ASSETS.md.        (BEFORE importing)
2. Photoreal-coherence check against WORLD_VISION.md.  Reject here if it fails.
3. Run R3 steps 1-5 (manifest, normalize, import, material).
4. Run R5 to build the LOD chain.
5. If skeletal: build IK Rig + IK Retargeter, retarget.  [UNVERIFIED]
6. Spawn one instance and RENDER it.
7. Flip verified-in-engine to YES in ASSETS.md — only now.
```
Step 1 precedes step 3 because an asset whose licence nobody recorded is
an asset we may not ship, and that is cheapest to discover before the
import work.

## VERIFICATION
- `ASSETS.md` row complete: source, licence, role, coherence verdict.
- Pivot read-back inside the gate.
- LOD chain section-complete.
- **A render exists** showing the asset in the scene. The
  verified-in-engine flag flips ONLY after spawn + render proof —
  settings read-backs are not sufficient (R3).

## REJECTED
- `Flipping verified-in-engine on a successful import` → the grass was
  "imported successfully" and invisible for two sessions → flip it only
  after a RENDER → R3.
- `Importing a multi-object vendor file ad hoc` → one asset per OBJECT,
  which can silently overwrite recipe-named meshes → KNOWN HAZARD,
  unfixed → `BACKLOG.md`.
- `Trusting a vendor's published extent` → 22× error on
  `grass_medium_01` → measure `get_bounds()` → R3.
- `Nested asset folders` → the importer is flat; a nested path matches
  nothing and fails silently in allow-lists → use the flat convention
  above → R6. **(Applies to BRANCH 1 only — native Fab packs keep their
  vendor structure and must not be renamed.)**
- **`Reading .uproject to determine whether a plugin is enabled`** →
  **you get a false NEGATIVE.** `Fab.uplugin` declares
  `"EnabledByDefault": true`, and a `.uproject`'s `Plugins` array holds
  **per-project OVERRIDES ONLY** — absence carries no information about
  state. This produced a reported "the Fab plugin is disabled, this is
  the gating click", escalated to the user, while the plugin was working
  and 15.9 GB of Fab content was already on disk → **query the LIVE
  editor**, or check the plugin's delivered content, or read the
  `.uplugin`'s `EnabledByDefault` → CLAUDE.md non-negotiable 17.
- `Looking for Fab content in Content/Fab/` → the folder does not exist;
  you conclude the import failed → Fab delivers to **named top-level
  folders** (`Content/KiteDemo`, `Content/StampIt`, ...) → 2026-08-03.
- `Rebuilding materials that shipped with a native Fab pack` → wasted
  work, and you lose vendor wiring you cannot reproduce → **VERIFY
  native materials, do not rebuild.** The sampler audit still applies →
  2026-08-03.
- `Assuming ORM channel order from the acronym` → a wrong channel drives
  roughness from the AO map and the surface reads uniformly wrong →
  **measure it**; the flat-zero channel is metallic on any dielectric →
  2026-08-03.

# R-GAEA — AlpineLab_v1 terrain package intake (LOCKED, PARTIALLY PROVEN)

Intake path for a Gaea 2 export package into a UE5 landscape. Proven
through resize + verification on build `002`; the editor import half is
written and **NOT YET RUN**.

## 1. THE GAEA GRAPH

    Mountain + Ridge
      -> Combine [Max]
      -> Erosion2 [ Duration 21.65, Downcutting 0.45,
                    ErosionScale 1413.25 ]
      -> Snow     [ Melt 0.45, Snow Line ~0.65,
                    Depth channel via Autolevel ]

## 2. TWO GOTCHAS, both Gaea 2.3 behaviour

- **Snow Line is INVERTED.** A LOWER value produces MORE snow. Setting
  it "higher for more snow" gives the opposite of the intent and reads
  as a broken sim rather than a reversed control.
- **The Snow channel exports as a degenerate near-1-bit PNG when the sim
  output is uniform.** The file is present, correctly named and correctly
  sized, and carries no information. **Presence is not content.**
  `verify_build.py` checks distinct-value count for exactly this, and
  file SIZE is NOT a usable proxy — on build 002 `Snow_Snow.png` is 515
  KB against ~11 MB siblings and is perfectly healthy at 42,677 unique
  values; it is small because it is 12% coverage compressing well.

## 3. PACKAGE CONTRACT — build 002, measured at intake

All 16-bit greyscale PNG, 4096², verified by `scripts/verify_build.py`:

    AlpineLab_v1_Height_normalized.png  0-65535  mean 20477.9  THE heightmap
    Erosion2_Flow.png                   0-65535  20.0% nonzero, sparse
    Erosion2_Wear.png                   0-6019   NEEDS REMAP
    Erosion2_Deposits.png               0-512    NEEDS STRONG REMAP
    Snow_Snow.png                       0-65535  hard coverage
    SnowMask_Out.png                    0-65535  graded depth, autoleveled

**PROVENANCE — the heightmap was normalized before export.** The
pre-normalization Gaea output spanned **496-24763** of 65535 and was
stretched to full range. This matters and is not bookkeeping: the
normalization ALREADY changed the height mapping, so any "Gaea metres"
figure applied naively to the imported landscape is wrong by that ratio.

`Snow_Out.png` is the un-normalized original height and is **EXCLUDED**;
it lives in `_archive/` and must not be imported.

## 4. ORDERED STEPS

```
0. python scripts/rebuild_terrain.py --go          (only when REBUILDING;
                                                    see section 9)
1. python scripts/verify_build.py --build <pkg>/002
2. python scripts/resize_gaea_build.py --build <pkg>/002 --archive-excluded
3. python scripts/verify_build.py --build <pkg>/002/UE5_Ready \
       --expect-size 4033x4033
4. IN THE EDITOR, BY HAND: Landscape Mode > New > Import from File
       heightmap  UE5_Ready/AlpineLabHeight.png    <- the ALIAS, not
                                                      the canonical name
       Z scale    180.81 for build 002 — see section 6
       full click-list: IMPORT_CHECKLIST.md
5. IN THE EDITOR: run scripts/ue5_import_alpinelab.py
```

Step 0 is skipped for an existing package; it is how the NEXT one is
made. Steps 1 and 3 are the same gate at two sizes, which is deliberate:
the resize is the step most likely to go wrong quietly.

Step 4 is manual **because UE 5.8 cannot create a landscape from
Python** — verified against the generated stub for this install: there
is no create/import-landscape function in the reflected surface, and the
only two import entry points are methods on an EXISTING `LandscapeProxy`
taking a `TextureRenderTarget2D`, not a file
(`unreal.py:531939` and `:531954`). The Landscape tool's own Import
dialog does heightmap, section layout and scale in one place; scripting
around it would reimplement a solved problem badly.

## 5. THE MASKS IMPORT AS TEXTURES, NOT WEIGHTMAPS

Decided for this build, with reasons, because the brief left it open:
a weightmap import needs a render target, a `LandscapeLayerInfoObject`
per layer AND a landscape material declaring matching layers — none of
which exist for a new evaluation landscape, so "import as weightmaps"
silently becomes "author a layered landscape material first". Texture
import via `AssetImportTask` is the ordinary path and loses nothing: the
16-bit data is preserved and a texture can be promoted later.

Settings inherited from `import_layer_textures.py`, and READ BACK after
setting: `srgb=False`, `TC_VECTOR_DISPLACEMENTMAP` (uncompressed —
a block compressor destroys thin drainage lines), `TA_CLAMP` both axes
(these map 1:1 onto the terrain and must never tile).

## 6. Z SCALE = 180.81 — RESOLVED 2026-08-09, PROVENANCE **MEASURED**

Set the Landscape actor's **Z scale to 180.81** in the import dialog.
X and Y stay at whatever gives the footprint you want; Z is the one that
carries a physical claim.

**Where the number comes from — and why the obvious answer is wrong by
2.7×.** The Gaea project file carries the elevation range:

    C:\Users\ryanb\AppData\Roaming\QuadSpinner\Gaea\2.0\Autosaves\
      AlpineLabe_v1_2026-08-09_19-12-59.terrain      (JSON, read-only)
        /Assets/$values[0]/Terrain/Height  =  2500.0     metres

That 2500 m is the **project's full range, not this build's span.** §3
records that the sim occupied only **496-24763** of 65535 before the
export was normalized to full range. So:

    occupancy   (24763 - 496) / 65535  =  0.37029
    low  edge   2500 *   496 / 65535   =    18.92 m
    high edge   2500 * 24763 / 65535   =   944.65 m
    SPAN S                             =   925.73 m

    Z = S / 512 * 100                  =   180.81

(512 m is what UE's 16-bit height range spans at Z scale 100.)

Typing the project range straight in gives `2500/512*100 = 488.3` — a
landscape 2.7× too tall, which would look *plausible* and be wrong. The
normalization is the whole trap, and it is why this value is derived in
`scripts/ue5_import_alpinelab.py` beside its arithmetic rather than
typed as a constant.

**What this is NOT.** It is a measurement of the PROJECT's declared
range, not of any real-world mountain. A tune-by-eye adjustment against
reference photography is a legitimate later change — but it should be
recorded as a **stylistic** override of a measured value, not as a
correction to it.

**Caveat carried from §7:** the 4096 → 4033 resample changed
metres-per-pixel by 1.56%. It does **not** touch Z — vertical mapping is
16-bit-value-to-centimetres and is independent of raster size — but it
means horizontal distances off this landscape are 1.56% short of the
Gaea plan unless X/Y scale compensates.

## 7. R1's REJECTED ENTRY IS NARROWED — RULED 2026-08-09

**Ryan's ruling, applied.** The R1 REJECTED entry is amended in place at
`RECIPES.md:552`, with its original wording quoted there verbatim so
nothing is lost. The rule is now:

> **Never resample height and masks independently or with differing
> filters; whole-package resampling in a single verified operation
> (enforced by `verify_build.py`) is permitted.**

**`AlpineLab_v1/002` was the motivating case** — 4096 → 4033, the first
intake to resample at all. It is narrowed rather than grandfathered:
nothing here gets an exemption, the RULE changed to name the actual
defect.

The reasoning, kept because the next reader will want it:

- The recorded failure mode is *height resampled while the weightmap is
  not*, so the two fall out of register. That is a defect of
  **independence**, not of resampling. Here the heightmap and all five
  masks went through one operation at an identical factor to an
  identical target, so they remain in register with each other. Means
  preserved almost exactly (height 20477.9 → 20477.9, wear
  985.8 → 985.9).
- **The permission is now enforced, not intended** (non-negotiable 24 —
  a requirement checked in prose and in code is one requirement, badly
  stored). `verify_build.py` collects the dimensions of the heightmap
  and every mask in a `UE5_Ready` set and **exits 4 if more than one
  distinct size is present.** Proven on `002/UE5_Ready`: *"dimension
  agreement: all 6 files at 4033x4033"*.
- What resampling DOES change is **metres-per-pixel, by 1.56%** — the
  "geometry stretches" half of the old entry. That is a scale question;
  it lands in §6, not in register.
- A measured side effect worth knowing: resampling SPREAD the sparse
  masks. `Erosion2_Flow` went from **20.0% to 43.1% nonzero** while its
  mean moved only +4.6% — Lanczos tails widening thin drainage lines at
  low amplitude. Harmless for a mask that gets remapped; not harmless if
  anyone ever treats flow coverage as a measured quantity.

## 8. REGISTRATION IS CHECKED OFFLINE, BEFORE THE EDITOR EVER SEES IT

The §7 ruling permits whole-package resampling **because register is
preserved**. That claim is now tested rather than argued.
`verify_build.py --build <pkg>/UE5_Ready` runs `check_registration()`:

- Take the brightest **1%** of `Erosion2_Flow` (drainage lines).
- Convert the HEIGHTMAP to percentile ranks, 0-100.
- Report the median height-rank under those flow pixels.

Water runs downhill, so a registered flow mask must sit **below** the
median terrain. A random control of the same pixel count is drawn in the
same run and must land at ~50, which is what makes a low flow median
evidence rather than an artefact of the statistic
(non-negotiable 8 — the control uses a different population, not the
same one measured twice).

Measured on `002/UE5_Ready` after the resize:

    flow median rank   37.7
    random control     50.1      (control valid: |50.1 - 50| < 5)
    separation        -12.4      PASS

**This is a REGISTER test, not a terrain-quality test.** It proves the
masks still point at the same ground the heightmap describes. It says
nothing about whether the erosion looks good.

## 9. THE CANONICAL REBUILD — ONE COMMAND

    python scripts/rebuild_terrain.py --go

That is the whole invocation. It builds the Gaea project headlessly into
the next unused `NNN` folder, normalizes the height the way build 002
was normalized by hand, and runs `verify_build.py` on the result.
**Without `--go` it is a dry run** that completes the entire preflight,
prints the exact Gaea command it would execute, and writes nothing.

Useful flags: `--project <file>` (default
`C:\Dev\LandscapeLab\TerrainData\AlpineLab_v1\AlpineLabe_v1.terrain`),
`--root`, `--resolution` (default 4096), `--seed`, `--ignore-cache`.

**`Gaea.BuildManager.exe` STILL DOES NOT WORK, and licensing did not fix
it.** It fails with *"The application to execute does not exist:
`C:\Program Files\QuadSpinner\Gaea 2\Gaea.BuildManager.dll`"* — an
apphost with no assembly behind it, exactly the absence the old BROKEN
entry recorded. **`Gaea.Swarm.exe` is the headless path** and it works;
flags verified against its own `--help` (Gaea Build Swarm 2.3.0.1).

**THE NORMALIZATION IS WHERE THE Z SCALE LIVES.** Gaea writes the height
as `Snow_Out.png` occupying part of the 16-bit range; the stretch to
full range destroys exactly the information section 6 derives Z from. So
the script records it first, into `height_normalization.json` beside the
output: source min/max, occupancy, span in metres, derived Z scale, and
sha256 of both files. **Normalizing without recording the range is how a
landscape ends up 2.7× too tall and plausible.**

**PROVEN, offline, no Gaea and no editor:**

    python scripts/prove_rebuild_terrain.py        12/12

The load-bearing one: `normalize_height` applied to build 002's archived
`Snow_Out.png` reproduces the adopted heightmap at **16,777,216 of
16,777,216 samples identical, max |diff| 0**. The rest drive each
refusal with input that should trip it — flat height, 8-bit height, a
build that wrote nothing, two candidate output directories, and a
`verify_build` contract that moved.

**REQUIRES A SAVED `.terrain`, and there is not one yet.** Every
`AlpineLabe_v1*.terrain` on this machine is a Gaea AUTOSAVE. The script
REFUSES rather than reaching for the newest one: an autosave is a
derived record Gaea rotates and overwrites, so building the canonical
terrain from one is how a rebuild quietly stops matching the project.
Save it once from Gaea (`File > Save As`) to the default path above.
`--project <autosave>` is accepted if you deliberately want that.

## 10. THE IMPORT ALIAS — `AlpineLabHeight.png`

**Hand the dialog `UE5_Ready/AlpineLabHeight.png`, never
`AlpineLab_v1_Height_normalized.png`.** Same bytes, sha256 asserted
equal by `verify_build.py` on every run; different name, because the
canonical one makes UE 5.8 offer a tiled import that **creates no
landscape**.

`rebuild_terrain.py` writes both on every build. `verify_build.py`
declares the mapping in `ALIASES`, refuses (exit 6) if the alias is not
byte-identical to its canonical, and prints which tiled tokens each file
in the package matches.

Manual steps, success criterion and the failure modes already hit:
**`IMPORT_CHECKLIST.md`** in the repo root.

## R-GAEA REJECTED

- `Importing AlpineLab_v1_Height_normalized.png in the landscape dialog`
  → *"Use 'AlpineLab_v<v>_Height_normalized.png' Tiled Image?"*; answer
  YES and **no Landscape actor is created**, with no modal error →
  **import the alias `AlpineLabHeight.png`** → R-GAEA §10,
  `IMPORT_CHECKLIST.md`.
  Source: `LandscapeTiledImage.cpp:14-24` (tokens `u v x y`, each
  matched as `<token>(-?[0-9]+)` **anywhere in the base filename** — no
  underscore in the pattern, `v1` is enough);
  `LandscapeEditorUtils.cpp:80` (YES swaps in the glob pattern);
  `LandscapeTiledImage.cpp:86-104` (only `u`/`x` set tile X, so a
  `v`-only name leaves X = -1); `:105` (`if (X >= 0 && Y >= 0)` adds no
  tile); `:149-155` (zero tiles → "No files found").
  Answering **NO** is safe — `Filename = Filenames[0]`, the plain file.
- `Detecting the tiled trigger with the regex _\d+_` → reports the
  canonical filename as CLEAN, because `_v1_` is underscore-LETTER-
  digit-underscore → **use `[uvxy]-?[0-9]+` on the base filename**,
  which is `verify_build.tiled_prompt_tokens` → R-GAEA §10. The wrong
  regex was written from the reported symptom instead of the source, and
  it disagreed with a known-bad case — which is what sent me to the
  source.
- `Renaming the canonical heightmap to dodge the prompt` → the
  provenance name that R-GAEA, the sidecar and the recipes all refer to
  disappears → **COPY to an alias and hash it** → R-GAEA §10,
  non-negotiable 20.
- `Importing the masks when the landscape check failed` → a level with
  no terrain reports "masks imported: 5 of 5" and reads as a partial
  success → **the landscape check is a GATE; refuse and import nothing**
  → `ue5_import_alpinelab.py:main`.
- `Verifying the Z scale by reading scale.z back` → proves the dialog
  wrote the number, not that the geometry came out that way →
  **also check the height SPAN against 512 m x Z/100** (925.7 m at
  Z 180.81) → non-negotiable 8, `ue5_import_alpinelab.py`.
- `Gaea.BuildManager.exe for headless builds` → *"The application to
  execute does not exist: Gaea.BuildManager.dll"* → **use
  `Gaea.Swarm.exe`** → R-GAEA §9. The Indie licence does NOT ship the
  BuildManager assembly; this is unchanged from Community.
- `Building from an autosave .terrain` → the rebuild silently stops
  matching the project the moment Gaea rotates the file → **save the
  project to a stable path and build that** → R-GAEA §9. This is
  non-negotiable 20 (adopted artefacts are copies at stable names)
  applied to the generator's input.
- `Normalizing the height without recording the source range` → the
  occupancy ratio is destroyed, and with it the only route to the Z
  scale; the naive answer is then 2.7× too tall and looks fine →
  **write `height_normalization.json` before the stretch** → R-GAEA §6,
  §9.
- `sha256 equality as the acceptance test for a RE-ENCODED image` → two
  byte-different files that are pixel-identical read as a failure (26 MB
  filter-0 vs 14 MB adaptive, 16,777,216/16,777,216 samples equal) →
  **decode and compare pixels; keep the sha inequality as the positive
  control** → `prove_rebuild_terrain.py`. Hashing is right for a file
  COPIED (non-negotiable 20) and wrong for a file RE-ENCODED.
- `Defaulting Z scale to UE's 100 when the project range is unreadable`
  → an unmeasured vertical scale that reads as a decision →
  **report UNKNOWN** → `derive_z_scale` returns `None`, R-GAEA §6.

# R12 — Rock, cliff and talus scatter (LOCKED, UNPROVEN)

Places rock meshes as instanced foliage against the **same deposition
field** the Pass 2 landscape material uses for its scree sub-surface.
Four roles are specified; the alpine recipe currently ships **one**
species, `Boulder` (role `hero`). The rest are specified and unplaced —
see WHAT IS NOT HERE.

Informed by LESSONS: "THE TALUS MODEL IS RIGHT AND THE TERRAIN HAS NO
CLIFFS", "MASS WAS CONSERVED AND THE FIELD WAS STILL WRONG", "EVERY
METRIC PICKED THE MOSS", and "DEPTH MEANT COUNT IN ONE FILE AND INDEX IN
ANOTHER".

## 1. PURPOSE

A rock is not placed by a material layer's weight. Cliff rocks live on a
slope band, talus lives on a **computed deposition field**, and hero
boulders live on meadow. So a rock species declares a `mask`, not a
`layer` + `weight_share`, and it does **not** draw from
`foliage.density_per_hectare` — that number is the tree budget, and
coupling the two would move every rock whenever anyone retunes the
forest.

## 2. EXACT VALUES

### 2a. Shared physical facts — `recipes/alpine.json` -> `foliage.rock_scatter`

**Read by BOTH this scatter and the Pass 2 material's scree mask**
(CLAUDE.md non-negotiable 19). Neither consumer keeps a copy. These are
properties of rock, not style knobs.

    repose_deg               35.0    valid 25-40    angle of repose; raise it and fans run further
    cliff_source_slope_deg   45.0    valid 35-70    what counts as a rockfall SOURCE
    source_smooth_m          16.0    valid 8-32     landform smoothing before the source test
    runout_m                120.0    valid 40-300   how far debris travels from its source
    mfd_exponent              1.3    valid 1.0-2.0  multiple-flow-direction concentration
    max_steps               600      valid >= 400   routing cap; HITTING IT IS A REFUSAL
    saturation                0.03   valid 0.01-0.2 deposit -> probability, p = 1 - exp(-d/s)

`source_smooth_m` is **not** cosmetic. `stamps.detail_relief` adds plus
or minus 4.7 m of ridged noise at 28 m wavelength to every face steeper
than 30 degrees, which tilts individual 4 m cells past any slope
threshold. Measured on the adopted terrain: cell-scale slope >= 50 deg
covers **9.152%** of the map, 16 m landform slope about **5.3%**. So
roughly **40% of the cell-scale cliff area is texture, not landform**,
and a source test run on cell-scale slope manufactures phantom cliffs.

### 2b. Per-species — a `foliage.species[]` entry that declares `role`

`role` is the discriminator. The rock and vegetation key sets are
**disjoint**, enforced by `_validate_rock_species` in
`scripts/import_heightmap.py`. The shipped species:

    {"name":"Boulder","role":"hero",
     "mesh":"/Game/KiteDemo/Environments/Rocks/Medium_Boulder_001/Medium_Boulder_001",
     "mask":{"kind":"layer","layer":"Grass","slope_deg":[0.0,22.0],
             "exclude_talus_above":0.2},
     "height_m":[120.0,700.0], "density_per_hectare_on_mask":0.35,
     "scale_range":[0.75,1.7], "align_to_normal":0.85, "tumble_deg":12.0,
     "embed_frac":0.18, "cull_distance_m":140.0, "lod_depth":4}

Bounds, all enforced and all proven to refuse (section 4c):

    role                          one of cliff | talus | hero
    mask.kind                     one of slope | talus | layer
    mask.layer                    must NAME a material layer in this recipe
    mask.saturation               REQUIRED when kind == talus
    density_per_hectare_on_mask   (0, 500]   ON-MASK, not map-average
    embed_frac                    [0, 0.5]   0 leaves rocks sitting on the surface like decals
    tumble_deg                    [0, 90]
    align_to_normal               [0, 1]     rocks EMBED — this inverts R4's world-up rule for trees
    scale_range                   0 < min <= max
    cull_distance_m               (0, 5000]
    lod_depth                     [1, len(rock_scatter.LOD_PERCENT)] AND == the MEASURED lod_count

### 2c. Measured mesh facts — `Free/_measured/rock_pivots.json`

**Not optional, and not from the Fab registry.** Written by
`scripts/measure_rock_meshes.py`, one asset per remote call.

Pivots are **box-centred, not based**: `base_offset_z_m` is approximately
minus `extent_z` on nearly every rock (`Medium_Boulder_001`: extent
0.65 m, base offset -0.618 m). Placing at terrain Z would sink every rock
to its waist.

**Nanite is FALSE on all 13** — measured from the reflected
`nanite_settings`, definitively, not absent. Pass 3 does not enable it.

Measured LOD chains (LOD0/1/2/3 triangles). **Every one of the thirteen
has exactly 1 material slot:**

    boulder_medium_01      4136 / 1186 /  892 /  596
    boulder_medium_02      2712 /  946 /  756 /  620
    boulder_small          2572 / 1284 /  992 /  504
    mountain_rock          9088 / 2272 /  567 /  454
    mountain_rock_closed  15320 / 3842 /  936 /  560
    hero_boulder_large    13998 / 2814 /  840 /  536
    cliff_face_01         29154 / 7288 / 1821 / 1457
    scree_bend            27354 / 6837 / 1708
    scree_slab_001        33855 / 8405 / 2325 /  829
    scree_slab_001a       15566 / 7756 / 1509 /  372
    scree_slab_001b       20218 / 10078 / 1984 /  585
    scree_slab_002a       15425 / 3855 /  963 /  770
    scree_slab_002b       11947 / 2985 /  745 /  597

Measured LOD screen sizes for `boulder_medium_01`: 1.504 / 0.752 / 0.319
/ 0.238. The cost model's generated-chain assumption is 1.0 / 0.5 / 0.21
/ 0.088 — the vendor switches to the deepest LOD much **nearer** the
camera. See REJECTED.

## 3. ORDERED STEPS

1. `python scripts/measure_rock_meshes.py` — pivots, Nanite, LOD chain,
   screen sizes, material slots. One asset per remote call,
   `resource_guard` before each, STOPS below 1.0 GB free.
   *This is first because every later step refuses without its output.*
2. `python scripts/import_heightmap.py --validate` — recipe gates,
   including `lod_depth` against the measurement.
3. `python scripts/rock_scatter.py` — dry run. Reports mask area,
   instance count, rotation gate and triangle budget. Writes nothing.
4. `python scripts/rock_scatter.py --write` — writes
   `foliage/<biome>_<Name>.json`.
5. `python scripts/place_foliage.py --place` **handed the vegetation
   plans AND the rock plans in ONE run.**
   **THIS ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING AND NOT UNDOABLE IF BROKEN.**
   `place_foliage.py:449-472` runs an orphan sweep over `/Game/Foliage`
   before adding anything: every `FT_*` asset whose name is not in the
   plan list handed to *that* run has `remove_all_instances` called on
   it. A rocks-only run therefore **deletes all 157,554 conifers,
   silently, and reports success.**
6. `python scripts/capture.py` — pipeline rule 4; this is a scene change.
7. Verification, section 4.

## 4. VERIFICATION

### 4a. Objective pass tests — measured on the adopted terrain

    cliff source cells        356,274  (570.0 ha)     tolerance +/- 5%
    routing steps                 360  (cap 600)      MUST be < cap, else REFUSE
    deposit p99                 1.322                 tolerance +/- 10%
    apron area p > 0.2          305.4 ha              tolerance +/- 10%
    apron area p > 0.5          262.6 ha              tolerance +/- 10%
    Boulder candidates          2,209 -> placed 759
    Boulder mask area         2,287.3 ha (probability-weighted)
    embed depth            0.18 .. 0.40 m along the surface normal
    rotation gate    max |pitch| 32.72   max |roll| 27.32
                     yaw 0.18..359.33, mean 180.97     PASS

**DISCRIMINATION IS THE ACCEPTANCE TEST, not apron area.** A talus field
that ignores what is above it reads as noise. The naive "scatter on 25-38
degrees" band covers **1,460 ha** of this map, of which **90.4% has no
cliff feeding it**. That difference is the entire design, and a run whose
discrimination collapses toward 0% has silently become a slope band.

*`mask ha` is the PROBABILITY-WEIGHTED area (sum of p times cell area),
not the count of cells with p > 0. For a soft mask those differ by about
20x, and only the weighted figure divides into a density that means
anything.*

### 4b. Independent instrument (non-negotiable 8)

The planner reports its own numbers, so it does not verify itself.

- **`python scripts/prove_gates.py`** — breaks the CPU models
  deliberately and feeds the validator values that must be rejected. It
  shares no code with the planner. Current: **7/7 mutations refused,
  25/25 probes rejected, dead-gate sweep clean over 38 checkers.**
- **The editor** decides the LOD chain and the material slots, via
  `measure_rock_meshes.py`. The planner may not model them — see
