## R-BAKE — SKELETALMESH -> STATICMESH FOR SCATTERABLE FOLIAGE (2026-08-14)

**Status: PROVEN. 8 of 8 baked and verified**, `pre-skeletal-to-static-bake-20260814`.

Megaplants ships its tree variants as **SkeletalMesh**; the foliage system
instances **StaticMesh only**. This converts them without going near the
reduction path.

### PROCEDURE

    python scripts/bake_skeletal_to_static.py            # dry run
    python scripts/bake_skeletal_to_static.py --go

### LOCKED VALUES

    destination      /Game/Meshes/Trees      (REFUSES vendor roots)
    naming           SM_<source asset name>
    nanite           OFF   (--nanite to enable; unmeasured on dense foliage)
    collision        OFF   (--collision; 150k instances do not want per-tree
                            collision)
    LOD chain        COPIED from the source, never regenerated

**THE LOD CHAIN IS COPIED.** `create_new_static_mesh_asset_from_mesh_lods`
takes an ARRAY of DynamicMeshes, one per source LOD, so the vendor chain
carries across verbatim. This deliberately avoids reduction, where the
project has a documented casualty: `ReductionSettings[0]` IS LOD 0, so the
obvious chain decimates the source mesh.

### THE API, resolved against THIS install before a line was written

    GeometryScript_AssetUtils.copy_mesh_from_skeletal_mesh      PythonStub:415697
    GeometryScript_NewAssetUtils
        .create_new_static_mesh_asset_from_mesh_lods            :416423
    SkeletalMeshEditorSubsystem.get_lod_count / get_num_verts   :633577 / :633508
    DynamicMesh.get_num_triangle_i_ds()   (METHOD, not library) :265344
    unreal.new_object(unreal.DynamicMesh)                       :707201

### VERIFICATION — silhouette, materials and LOD structure, NOT triangle parity

    bounds        every axis within 1 cm of the source
    LOD count     equal
    materials     count equal AND slot names carried
    triangles     delta reported; tolerance +/- 15%
    vertices      reported as a SECOND quantity on the same artefact pair

Measured 2026-08-14, all 8 VERIFIED:

    mesh                       tris src -> dest      delta    verts src -> dest
    Norway_Spruce_01_A         139,851 -> 125,321   -10.4%    72,223 -> 72,223
    Norway_Spruce_01_B         146,409 -> 128,707   -12.1%    74,952 -> 74,952
    Norway_Spruce_01_C          71,915 ->  63,283   -12.0%    37,038 -> 37,038
    Norway_Spruce_01_D          50,928 ->  44,952   -11.7%    26,568 -> 26,568
    Baltic_Pine_01_A           351,106 -> 331,779    -5.5%   179,347 -> 179,154
    Baltic_Pine_01_B           112,464 -> 105,668    -6.0%    58,513 -> 58,376
    Baltic_Pine_01_C           225,899 -> 213,113    -5.7%   115,805 -> 115,671
    Baltic_Pine_01_D           171,353 -> 160,755    -6.2%    87,927 -> 87,803

**The triangle loss is the StaticMesh build welding and dropping degenerate
faces, and the VERTEX column is what says so** — identical on all four
spruces, within 0.1% on the pines, with bounds matching to under a
centimetre everywhere. Triangles alone could not have distinguished that
from geometry loss.

### OPEN — AND IT BLOCKS ANY SCATTER

**Every baked mesh has exactly ONE LOD**, because the skeletal sources do
(PVE handles distance at runtime). The incumbent `fir_tree_01` ships
505,494 / 126,374 / 22,293 / 3,892 and culls at 730 m. Scattering a
single-LOD 125k-332k triangle tree into that cull disc would be
catastrophic — the whole worst-case triangle budget assumes a chain.
**Generate an LOD chain before placing anything**
(`StaticMeshTools.generate_lods` + `set_lod_thresholds`, R5's
`percent = screen_size^2`).

### 5. REJECTED

**`GeometryScript_NewAssets`.** The class is `GeometryScript_NewAssetUtils`.
The wrong name read as knowledge and would have died on the first call.
Resolve the enclosing class from the stub line number, not from memory.

**`GeometryScript_MeshQueries.get_num_triangle_i_ds(mesh)`.** It is a METHOD
on `DynamicMesh` (:265344), not a library function.

**Requiring exact triangle parity as the acceptance test.** The StaticMesh
build welds and removes degenerates, so no correct bake can match exactly.
The first gate demanded equality and rejected all 8 correct bakes. Correct:
bounds + materials + LOD count, with the triangle delta reported and
bounded.

**Wrapping the whole material loop in one `try`.** One failing
`set_editor_property("imported_material_slot_name", ...)` zeroed the entire
carry-over, and all 8 meshes came back with `WorldGridMaterial` in slot 0
and nulls after it. **The gate caught it** — `materials 0` against 3
expected. One optional cosmetic field must not be able to discard the
assignment; make each step independently fault-tolerant.

**Baking into the vendor folder.** Refused by the tool, by name. R-ASSET
forbids authoring into a Fab folder and `Content/Megaplant_Library/` is
gitignored, so the output would be lost work that looks like committed work
the moment the pack is re-downloaded.

**Deleting the failed bakes with `Remove-Item -Force`.** Standing rule 2's
hook refused it, correctly. `.uasset` removal goes through the editor API
(`AssetTools.delete`) under standing rule 4 anyway.

## R-PIE — MEASURING FRAME COST IN PLAY IN EDITOR (2026-08-15)

**Status: PROVEN.** Executed twice on `/Game/Alpine8K`, tags `pie001` and
`pie002`, three stations each. Artefacts `_verify/20260815_pie_unit1_pie001.md`
and `_verify/20260815_pie_unit1_pie002.md`. Informed by LESSONS 2026-08-15
"THE FIRST PIE FRAME THIS PROJECT HAS EVER MEASURED".

Tool: `scripts/measure_pie_cost.py`. Premise-prover: `scripts/probe_pie.py`.

### WHY THIS IS A SEPARATE RECIPE FROM R-FRAMECOST

`RECIPES.md:6373` already calls PIE *"a different calibration class that does
not exist"*. It exists now, and the classes may not be mixed. Measured
difference at the SAME camera, same session:

    editor viewport      256 landscape proxies, FORCE-RESIDENT
    PIE                    4 landscape proxies, 9 foliage actors, STREAMING

### THE PROCEDURE

1. **Verify the node** (standing rule 7) before anything.
2. **Refuse if the editor is already in play.** A session you did not start
   cannot be told from your own at teardown.
3. `LevelEditorSubsystem.editor_request_begin_play()` — PythonStub 606201.
   It is a REQUEST: PIE exists on a LATER TICK. Settle 30 s.
4. **Enable the default-off CSV categories with the literal word `enable`.**
   See REJECTED. `CsvCategory VSM enable`, `CsvCategory GPUScene enable`.
   `SceneCulling` is default-ON (`SceneCulling.cpp:105`) and needs nothing.
5. **Per station, in this order and no other:**
   a. **Teleport the pawn to a perch FIRST** (250,000 cm; the terrain tops out
      at 1552.5 m). World Partition streams around the PAWN.
   b. Settle 25 s for streaming.
   c. **Then** trace for ground — `SystemLibrary.line_trace_single`,
      `TRACE_TYPE_QUERY1`, top-down, against COLLISION. Read the hit with
      `to_dict()`; `FHitResult`'s fields are protected in 5.8.
   d. Teleport to `ground + height_above_ground`.
   e. **Wait 6 s, THEN read `get_player_view_point()`** and refuse the station
      if it disagrees with the target by more than 5 m.
   f. `CsvProfile frames=300`, then reduce the CSV.
6. `editor_request_end_play()`, then **CONFIRM** with `is_in_play_in_editor()`.
   A request that returns is not a session that stopped.

### VALUES THAT WORK

    settle after begin play        30 s
    settle after a teleport        25 s
    settle before reading camera    6 s
    frames per station            300
    perch Z                   250,000 cm
    max view-vs-target drift      500 cm
    min editor CPU ratio          0.30 CPU-s per wall-s

### MEASURED, TAG `pie001` (categories OFF — the clean cost run)

    station              GPUTime   GameThread   RenderThread   RHI
    forest_floor           7.816       7.198          5.309    2.779
    canopy_250m            5.082       7.084          5.198    2.765
    airship_1500m          3.404       7.022          5.055    2.523

`forest_floor` reproduces the editor series' 7.92 ms to within 0.10 ms.

**`FrameTime` is pinned at 16.667 ms in every run — a 60 fps cap, not a cost.
Nothing here is frame-rate evidence.** Same standing as R-FRAMECOST.

### MEASURED, TAG `pie002` (categories ON — the diagnostic run)

`VSM/FreePages` 1820 / 1978 / 2024 against `r.Shadow.Virtual.MaxPhysicalPages`
= 2048. **Peak usage 228 pages of 2048, 11%. Virtual shadow map pages are NOT
the constraint** at any station, and no work should be aimed at them.

### CALIBRATION CLASS — quote it or the numbers are not reusable

PIE inside the editor process; `/Game/Alpine8K`; viewport 1614x943;
streaming LIVE; FOV **90** (the PlayerController's, NOT the recipe camera's
75 and NOT the editor viewport's); `DefaultPawn`, no `PlayerStart`, engine
default GameMode; Lumen on; `r.ScreenPercentage` 100;
`r.Nanite.MaxPixelsPerEdge` 1.0; `r.Nanite.Foliage` 1.

**The game thread figure carries EDITOR overhead and is an UPPER BOUND on a
cooked build, not the shipping number.** No cook has ever been produced here.

## R-PIE REJECTED

**`CsvCategory VSM 1` — and `PHASE2_PLAN.md` unit 1 prescribes exactly this.**
SYMPTOM: the command returns normally, the capture succeeds, and **every VSM
column is silently ABSENT from the CSV**. Observed across all three stations
of tag `pie001`. CORRECT: `CsvCategory VSM enable`. REFERENCE:
`CsvProfiler.cpp:1138-1148` — `HandleCSVCategoryCommand` compares the second
argument against the literal strings `enable` and `disable`; `"1"` matches
neither, so `bIsOperationValid` goes false and the command falls through to a
usage error **without enabling anything**.

**`CsvCategory VSM` with the argument omitted.** SYMPTOM: works the first
time and turns the category back OFF on the second run. CORRECT: always pass
`enable`. REFERENCE: `CsvProfiler.cpp:1152-1153` — the argument-less form
TOGGLES. Pipeline rule 3 (idempotent) forbids it.

**Tracing for ground before teleporting the pawn.** SYMPTOM: `no collision
hit between +5000 m and -1000 m` at a location where terrain demonstrably
exists. CORRECT: teleport to the perch, settle, then trace. REFERENCE: World
Partition streams around the pawn; the pawn spawns at the world origin
because the level has no `PlayerStart`, and a station 4.8 km away is outside
the loading range. **"Not streamed" and "no terrain here" are the same
answer** — non-negotiable 6.

**Reading `get_player_view_point()` in the same payload as the teleport.**
SYMPTOM: view point reads `[0,0,0]` while the pawn's own location reads back
exactly on target. CORRECT: read it at least one tick later. REFERENCE:
`APlayerController::GetPlayerViewPoint` returns the camera manager's CACHED
point, gated on `GetCameraCacheTime() > 0` with the engine's own comment
*"Whether camera was updated at least once"*.

**Comparing a `pie001` number against a `pie002` number.** SYMPTOM: an
apparent +0.52 ms regression at `forest_floor` (7.816 -> 8.338) with nothing
changed but the diagnostic categories. CORRECT: **the instrument's own
settings are part of the calibration class.** Categories-off runs and
categories-on runs are two series, not one.

**Quoting `SceneCulling/NumStaticInstances`.** SYMPTOM: 284,424 at all three
stations in `pie001`; 284,424 / 4,264 / 4,264 in `pie002`. Same stations,
same order, same session. CORRECT: **do not use this column until it has had
its own single-variable run.** It is declared `ECsvCustomStatOp::Accumulate`
(`SceneCulling.cpp:2676`), so what it means depends on how many times the
update ran in a frame — but that is an inference, and a statistic that
disagrees with itself is not evidence either way.

**Concluding "5.8 Python cannot start real PIE".** SYMPTOM: a stub grep for
`editor_play` / `request_play` / `end_play` returns only
`editor_play_simulate`, and Simulate has no PlayerController and no player
camera. CORRECT: `editor_request_begin_play()` exists at PythonStub 606201
and matches none of those three patterns. REFERENCE: non-negotiable 6 — **a
negative from a search is only evidence if the search could have found the
thing.**

### THE SCALE CONTROL IS PART OF THE PROCEDURE, NOT AN EXTRA

Always run it. Connectivity on a per-cell slope mask is sampling-dependent,

    cell    crossable   largest   regions   reachable
    1 m        60.67%    17.75%    219828     29.26%
    2 m        64.17%    21.36%     64546     33.28%

## R-WALK REJECTED

**Reading "19.87% of the mount mask exceeds MaxStepHeight" as a walkability
defect** — and `PHASE2_PLAN.md` unit 2 specifies exactly this metric.
SYMPTOM: a large, alarming fraction that no terrain change improves.
CORRECT: read it as a restatement of the slope distribution. REFERENCE: 45 cm
over a 100 cm cell is **24.23 degrees**, and the mount profile admits 35
degrees = **70 cm of rise per cell**, so every slope in between trips the
metric while being entirely walkable. A character walks UP a walkable slope;
it does not step onto it.

**Auditing step height on a 1 m-per-vertex heightmap at all.** SYMPTOM: a
number that looks like a step-height census. CORRECT: **a step is a rise over
a SUB-METRE horizontal distance and is below this map's Nyquist limit by
construction.** `MaxStepHeight` is not a terrain constraint here; it applies
to PLACED geometry — rocks, roots, stairs, thresholds. Note Nanite
displacement (+/-0.4 m) does NOT create collidable steps: landscape collision
is the heightfield, not the displaced surface.

**Grading `world.min_connected_frac` on a map whose resolution differs from
the one the bar was written for.** SYMPTOM: mount reachability reads 29.26%
against a 0.8 bar — a FAIL by nearly 3x on the PRIMARY movement mode — and

at **4 m per vertex**. Do not act on the 1 m verdict. REFERENCE:
non-negotiable 22 — a threshold is only meaningful conditioned on the scale
it is evaluated at. This is the fifth resolution-dependent parameter the 8K
re-terrain exposed, and the first that lives in a BAR rather than a generator.

**RECOMMENDED AND NOT YET RULED:** make the evaluation scale a PHYSICAL
property of the agent — a mount occupies ~2-4 m of ground, so slope sampled
at 1 m asks whether a horse can stand on a dinner plate — and declare it
beside `MOVEMENT_PROFILES`, never beside the bar. Not applied unilaterally:
**a gate whose bar moves to make a failing number pass needs its reasoning
ratified before the number.**

border.** SYMPTOM: a one-cell ring of enormous false rises where the map's
opposite edges are compared. CORRECT: exclude the border; the tool does.

Ask **how many elements are in the mesh's `agg_geom`**. Do NOT ask whether it
has a `BodySetup`: `InstancedStaticMesh.cpp:2877-2882` early-returns only on
a NULL BodySetup, so a mesh with a BodySetup and an EMPTY agg_geom creates
per-instance bodies, logs nothing, and collides with nothing.

All via `get_editor_property` — these are struct fields, not accessors.
An element array that RAISES is recorded as unreadable and the total is set
to None, never to a low number.

## R-CHARACTER — THE CHARACTER MOVEMENT DECLARATION (2026-08-15)

**Status: PROVEN for the declaration; the CHARACTER ITSELF IS NOT BUILT.**
`recipes/character.json` + `scripts/verify_walkable_profile.py`.
`PHASE2_PLAN.md` unit 5's second acceptance clause. Narrative: LESSONS
2026-08-15. Schema: `recipes/schema.md` → CHARACTER RECIPE.

### THE SHAPE: THE RECIPE NAMES A PROFILE, IT NEVER TYPES AN ANGLE

    "movement": { "profile": "walk", ... }

`walk` is a KEY into `terrain_erosion.MOVEMENT_PROFILES`, which holds the
engine's own 44.765083° (`acos(0.71)` from `SetWalkableFloorZ(0.71f)`,
`CharacterMovementComponent.cpp:682`). The angle is DERIVED at read time and
is deliberately absent from the recipe. Ruling 19: declared once, derived
twice. **The verifier REFUSES any `movement.*` key whose name contains
"angle" or "slope"** — a typed angle is a second copy, and a second copy is a
second thing to drift.

### VALUES, EACH READ FROM THE 5.8 CONSTRUCTOR ON 2026-08-15

    max_walk_speed_cm_s      600.0    CharacterMovementComponent.cpp:694
    max_step_height_cm        45.0    :689
    jump_z_velocity_cm_s     420.0    :679
    max_acceleration_cm_s2  2048.0    :733
    gravity_scale              1.0    :677
    capsule radius / half     34 / 88 Character.cpp:78 InitCapsuleSize

Written out in FULL rather than left implicit. Non-negotiable 17 says a
config file records overrides and never the state in effect — so a recipe
that lists only overrides describes nothing. The recipe says what the
character IS; the verifier catches the day the engine stops agreeing.

**`max_step_height_cm` stays at the engine default deliberately.** R-WALK
established that at 1 m per vertex a step is below the heightmap's Nyquist
limit, so `MaxStepHeight` is not a terrain constraint on this world at all —
it governs PLACED geometry only.

### THE RULING-19 GATE, CHECKED HERE AND NOT AT NAVMESH BUILD TIME

`navigation.agent_profile` must not exceed `world.primary_movement_mode` in
`recipes/alpine_8k.json`. Both are `mount` (35°) today. **Drift upward is
SILENT** — the navmesh grants paths onto ground the character slides off and
nothing errors — so it is gated before the packages are written.

**The asymmetry is INTENDED and is not drift:** the player on foot walks
44.765° while the navmesh is built for the mount at 35°. The gate is
one-directional, `agent <= world primary`, never equality. The player may go
where the AI will not path.

### VERIFIED

    offline (no editor)  profile is a key, not an angle; ruling 19 gate
    --live               walkable_floor_angle 44.765083 == profile
                         all five movement values == CDO
                         capsule 34 / 88 == Character CDO
                         exit 0

## R-CHARACTER REJECTED

**Prose keys inside `recipes/character.json`.** SYMPTOM: the first version
carried `_what_this_is`, `_profile_is_a_key_not_an_angle`, `_sources` and
five more explanatory arrays — and the verifier's own "no typed angle" scan
**refused the recipe**, because a documentation key was named
`_profile_is_a_key_not_an_angle` and contains the word "angle". CORRECT: the
recipe is DATA; the reasoning lives here and the contract lives in
`schema.md`. REFERENCE: R-ALPINE8K REJECTED already ruled this — *"adding a
schema key to hold prose is the 'invent a key to get past the validator'
antipattern"*. **The tempting fix was to exempt underscore-prefixed keys from
the scan; that would have opened a hole in the gate to accommodate a pattern
the project had already rejected.**

**Reading the capsule off `CapsuleComponent`'s CDO.** SYMPTOM: `capsule
radius 22 / half height 44` against a recipe saying 34 / 88, reported as

`capsule_component`. REFERENCE: `CapsuleComponent`'s CDO is the GENERIC
component default; `ACharacter` initialises its OWN capsule subobject at
`Character.cpp:78`. **The generic CDO answered plausibly and was about a
different object** — the same class as `get_component_by_class` reading 0 on

**Pointing this tool at the engine CDO once a project character class

## R-GAMEPLAY — ADDING A RUNTIME MODULE TO THIS PROJECT (2026-08-15)

**Status: PROVEN.** `LandscapeLab/Plugins/LandscapeLabGameplay`, built clean
in 35 s first try, verified on a cold boot with a new node id. Tool
`scripts/verify_gameplay_plugin.py`. Narrative: LESSONS 2026-08-15 "UNIT 7".

### THE PROCEDURE

1. **A new PLUGIN, never a game module and never a `.uproject` edit.**
   Standing rule 4 forbids the edit; `PluginManager.cpp:420-433` honours
   `EnabledByDefault` on a project plugin with no `.uproject` entry at all.
   The project file stays byte-identical.
2. **Module `Type` must match when the code runs.** `LandscapeLabEditor` is
   `"Editor"`. Gameplay classes are `"Runtime"` or they do not exist in a
   cooked build — the one place they must.
3. **Engine plugin dependencies go in THIS plugin's `Plugins` array**, not in
   the project file (ruling 2). They then live beside the code that needs
   them, so "why is X on?" is answerable by attribution.
4. **CLOSE THE EDITOR.** A new module cannot be added by Live Coding.
5. Build:

       "C:\Program Files\Epic Games\UE_5.8\Engine\Build\BatchFiles\Build.bat"
         LandscapeLabEditor Win64 Development
         -Project="<UE_PROJECT_ROOT>\LandscapeLab.uproject" -WaitMutex

6. **Relaunch and verify on a COLD BOOT**, never from the `.uplugin`.

### THE UFUNCTION CONVENTION, CARRIED FORWARD

`void` + an explicit `bOutSuccess`, **never** `bool` with out-params: a
`UFUNCTION` returning `bool` alongside out-params LOSES the bool in the
Python binding — Python gets `(...outs) or None`, so the failure flag
disappears exactly when it is needed. Established 2026-08-12; applied to
`ApplyMovementSpec`.

### WHAT THE COLD-BOOT CHECK MUST ASK, AND IN WHAT ORDER

    1. is the plugin in get_enabled_plugin_names()
    2. is GameplayStateTree in it        <- THE DISCRIMINATING ONE
    3. is unreal.<Class> reflected, with a reachable CDO
    4. is the UFUNCTION present on it

## R-GAMEPLAY REJECTED

**Verifying a plugin from its `.uplugin`.** SYMPTOM: a green check over a
plugin that is not loaded. CORRECT: read `get_enabled_plugin_names()` on the
running editor. REFERENCE: non-negotiable 17 — a config records what was
overridden, never what is in effect. Three recorded instances in this project
already (`sg.*` in `[SystemSettings]`, `t.MaxFPS`, `Fab` read as disabled
from `.uproject`).

**Checking only that YOUR plugin is enabled.** SYMPTOM: passes identically
whether or not the declared dependencies were honoured. CORRECT: assert
`GameplayStateTree` specifically. It ships `EnabledByDefault: false` (ruling
1) and nothing else in this project enables it, so **it is the only result
that could not be true by accident.**

**Treating `get_enabled_plugin_names()` as proof the module loaded.**
SYMPTOM: a plugin reads enabled while its DLL failed to load, and the editor
carries on. CORRECT: also ask for the reflected class and its CDO — a
different representation of the same fact.

**Treating a reflected class as proof the binary is current.** SYMPTOM: a
stale DLL from a previous build reflects the class perfectly and is missing
the new function; it reads exactly like a working module until something
calls it. CORRECT: assert the UFUNCTION by name.

**`Ctrl+Alt+F11` / Live Coding to add a new module.** SYMPTOM:
`Unable to build while Live Coding is active`, read as "just unlock the
DLL". CORRECT: Live Coding recompiles EXISTING modules only. A new module
means a full build means a closed editor.

**Quitting the editor without reading the dirty count first.** SYMPTOM: a
**Save Content** modal that blocks the game thread and therefore blocks
remote execution — the only channel that could see or answer it. CORRECT:
read `get_dirty_content_packages()` + `get_dirty_map_packages()` and refuse
to quit on a non-zero count. **Refuse equally on an UNREADABLE count: an
unreadable count is not a zero.** Route the decision to the asset's owner
rather than discarding on their behalf.

## R-WALKTEST — DRIVING THE PLAYER AND JUDGING THE RESULT (2026-08-15)

**Status: PROVEN.** `scripts/walk_character.py`. Artefact
`_verify/20260815_unit5_walk_walk003.md`: **1000.1 m, no stall, no fall.**
Narrative: LESSONS 2026-08-15.

### THE PROCEDURE

1. PIE, settle 30 s.
2. `unreal.register_slate_post_tick_callback` drives the pawn with
   `add_movement_input(dir, 1.0, force=True)` every tick and samples 4x/s.
   **A Python loop cannot do this** — a payload blocks the game thread, so the
   character receives input and never ticks.
3. Poll a SUMMARY only. Never the trace.
4. Stop: unregister, write the trace to
   `Saved/ll_walk_log.json`, delete the global.
5. End PIE and CONFIRM.

### VALUES THAT WORK

    sample rate        4 /s          settle            30 s
    stall bar          3.0 s under 20 cm/s
    fall bar           1.0 s of descent beyond tan(walkable) x distance
                       + 60 cm per-sample margin
    walkable           70 deg (profile "climb")

### CHOOSING A HEADING — SWEEP AT THE MAP'S OWN RESOLUTION

A straight kilometre is NOT available from the `forest_floor` spawn at the
44.765 deg walking limit; the best clear run is **934 m**. At 70 deg many
headings clear 1200 m. **Sweep at 1 m, not 2 m** — the map is 1 m/vertex and
a 2 m sweep steps over the 1 m ledges that stop the character.

## R-WALKTEST REJECTED

**Walking a straight line from the PlayerStart, now that it stands in the
town.** SYMPTOM: **STALLED**, twice, at 29.2 m and 58.4 m, with `is_falling`
0.1–0.3% and worst excess descent 0.0 cm — i.e. the pawn is firmly on the
ground and cannot proceed. Reads exactly like a terrain or step-height defect
and is neither: the walker has NO STEERING, and the spawn was moved on
2026-08-26 into a settlement of 1,142 solid volumes, aimed at an 11 × 11 × 34 m
landmark 29 m away. CORRECT: choose the heading by measurement, not by eye —
`scripts/find_clear_heading.py` marches each bearing against the planned
footprints inflated by the 34 cm capsule — and note what it returns from this
spawn: **0 of 360 bearings clear to 1200 m with street slabs counted**, 9 of
360 (2.5%) without them, widest clear arc **3.0°**. A 3° arc is 2.6 m wide at
50 m and an unsteered walker drifts more than that, so bearing 259 failed too.
**A straight-line walk cannot leave this town.** The fix is a start point on
reachable ground OUTSIDE the settlement, or a walker with steering — not a
larger budget and not a different bar. REFERENCE: R-WALKTEST was proven on
2026-08-15 against a spawn in a forest clearing, where the only obstacles were
foliage the walker brushes past; a procedure stamped PROVEN carries the world it
was proven on.

**Two literals for the trace dump, one per teardown path.** SYMPTOM: none on

`PAYLOAD_FORCE_STOP`, so the file written when the ordinary reply is LOST — the
only occasion it is the sole surviving copy — silently carried a subset. Every

into both payloads by `_trace_dump(indent)` and substituted at import, with two
import-time assertions: no payload may still carry an unsubstituted placeholder,
and every payload must still contain the dump. A shared constant that nothing
checks is still two copies the moment someone re-inlines one. REFERENCE:
non-negotiable 24; found by the audit gate before first execution, not by any

cannot find the defect.

**Sampling residency on the movement cadence.** SYMPTOM: not measured; rejected
by construction. `get_all_actors_of_class` iterates the world, and at 4/s it
would make the instrument a material part of the streaming load it exists to
measure. CORRECT: its own coarser cadence, default 2.0 s, declared and
overridable; `--residency-every 0` disables it. REFERENCE: non-negotiable 5 — a
check that consumes the value it is verifying verifies nothing.

**Returning the trace in the reply.** SYMPTOM: a COMPLETED 1621-sample walk
reports `NO MARKER` and the trace is nearly lost. CORRECT: write it to a file
BEFORE replying and read it off disk; degrade to a forced teardown when a
reply is lost rather than discarding the run. REFERENCE: same class as
`save_level`'s 418 KB reply exceeding the remote-exec deserialization limit.

**Calling a fall "Z dropped N below the spawn".** SYMPTOM: **FELL THROUGH:
YES** on a clean walk that descended a mountainside 100 m over 1 km with
`is_falling` never true. CORRECT: over one sample the ground can drop at most
`tan(walkable) x horizontal distance moved`; a fall is sustained excess
beyond that. **On real terrain, descending is the job.** Measured on the same
trace, the worst excess is 0.0 cm.

**`ACharacter.get_character_movement()` in Python.** SYMPTOM: raises; the
exception is swallowed; `is_falling` logs `None` on every sample and the
analysis prints **"falling samples 0.0%"**. CORRECT:
`Pawn.get_movement_component().is_falling()` — `is_falling` is on
`NavMovementComponent`, PythonStub 506206. **An all-`None` column must print
COULD NOT READ, never a percentage** (non-negotiable 6).

**`WalkableFloorAngle = x`.** SYMPTOM: the property reads back correct and the
character still refuses the slope. CORRECT: `SetWalkableFloorAngle(x)`, which
also recomputes `WalkableFloorZ` — the value the floor test actually reads.
The engine sets the pair through `SetWalkableFloorZ` at
`CharacterMovementComponent.cpp:682` for the same reason.

**Sweeping headings at coarser than 1 m.** SYMPTOM: a heading reported clear
to 934 m blocks the character at 240 m. CORRECT: sample at the map's own
resolution; a 2 m sweep steps over a 1 m ledge.

**Reading a straight-line stall as a terrain defect.** SYMPTOM: the walker
stops at 97 m and stays there. CORRECT: measure the terrain at the stop
point. Both early stops were slopes of **52.66** and **64.39 deg** with
1 m rises of **74** and **320 cm** — past the walkable floor AND past the step
height at once. A straight-line walker with no steering stops at the first
such feature; that is the test's property, not the world's.

**Editing a source file with a PowerShell `-replace` round trip.** SYMPTOM:
`SyntaxError: invalid non-printable character U+FEFF`, and every em-dash
turned to mojibake. CORRECT: use `Edit`. `Get-Content` with no `-Encoding`
reads UTF-8 as Windows-1252 and `Set-Content -Encoding utf8` writes the
damage back with a BOM. **Standing rule 3's mechanism in a different
container** — a shell round trip over text whose encoding was never declared
has no failure mode that announces itself.

## R-GAMEPLAY AMENDED 2026-08-15 — DECIDING WHETHER AN EDITOR IS SLOW OR HUNG

Added after enabling `MetaHumanCharacter` stalled the editor on startup for
11 minutes. Narrative: LESSONS 2026-08-15.

### THE FOUR-INSTRUMENT READING

No single instrument decides this. Take all of them:

    working set        flat over 2 min          -> suggestive only
    editor CPU         < 0.1 CPU-s per wall-s   -> suggestive only
    DDC growth         0 MB over 2 min          -> DECISIVE
    ShaderCompileWorker count                   -> context
    log mtime          minutes since last line  -> DECISIVE
    window CLASS       SplashScreenClass        -> still starting

**DDC growth is the one that closes it.** Shader compilation shows a flat
parent CPU by construction — the work is in child processes — but it still
writes to disk. No CPU AND no DDC growth AND no new log line is hung.

**`MainWindowTitle` is not a tell.** It reads *"Unreal Editor - <project>"*
on the SPLASH SCREEN, identical to a loaded editor. Use `GetClassName`:
`SplashScreenClass` vs `UnrealWindow`.

## R-GAMEPLAY REJECTED — additions

**Enabling a BETA plugin for the FIRST time through a `.uplugin` dependency.**
SYMPTOM: the editor never finishes starting; 2.41 GB working set, 0.02 CPU-s
per wall-s, no DDC growth, and **zero lines from the plugin in a 105 KB log**.
CORRECT: enable a first activation through the editor's **Plugins UI**, where
a prompt has someone to answer it; use the descriptor route for every
activation after that, once it is known not to ask anything. **A dialog
blocking the game thread also blocks the only channel that could report it** —
the same shape as the Save Content modal. REFERENCE: root cause NOT
established; log preserved at
`_verify/20260815_metahuman_enable_stall.log`.

**Raising the page file because an editor hung.** SYMPTOM: a plausible fix
that costs a reboot and changes nothing. CORRECT: memory starvation shows
heavy paging and PEGGED CPU and disk. A hang at **2.41 GB against a 223 GB
commit limit with the CPU idle** is a process waiting on something, and no
amount of page file addresses a blocking wait.

**Assuming a plugin that fails to load must need compiling.** SYMPTOM: time
spent on a build that was never required. CORRECT: check for the DLLs first —
`MetaHumanCharacter` ships **7 prebuilt binaries** in an installed 5.8 engine.

## R-HERO — MAKING A METAHUMAN THE PLAYABLE CHARACTER (2026-08-16)

Status: **PROVEN** for everything below the line marked NOT OWNED BY THIS
RECIPE. Verified in PIE on a fresh editor and photographed:
`_verify/20260816_hero_press_play_FIXED.png`.

### WHAT THIS BUILDS

    /Game/Hero/MHC_AlpineHero          AUTHORED, tracked, Ryan's sculpt
    /Game/Hero/Generated/SKM_HeroBody  derived, gitignored
    /Game/Hero/Generated/SKM_HeroFace  derived, gitignored
    /Game/Hero/Generated/SM_HeroHead_TRELLIS  derived, gitignored

### THE STEPS

1. **`python scripts/build_hero_assets.py --go`** — duplicates the MetaHuman
   preview meshes into real packages and resolves their materials. Idempotent;
   a second run reports "already present, refreshed materials only".
2. **Point `recipes/character.json` at them.** `assets.skeletal_mesh` takes the
   BODY, and the new `assets.face_mesh` takes the FACE. `face_mesh` is optional
   and its absence leaves the character exactly as it was.
3. **`python scripts/apply_character_recipe.py --ini-only`**, then RESTART the
   editor. Config UPROPERTYs are read at class load; the tool says so itself.
4. **`python scripts/find_hero_spawn.py --near-cm "X,Y"`** to choose ground
   that is clear of trunks, then add it as a NAMED CAMERA in the world recipe
   and set `spawn.from_camera` to it.
5. **`python scripts/place_player_start.py --go`**, then CHECK THE ARTEFACT —
   the package it names must show as modified in `git status`.
6. **Verify in PIE**, never in the editor world (see REJECTED).

### VALUES THAT WORK

    movement.profile            climb          (70 deg walkable floor)
    capsule                     34 / 88 cm
    camera.arm_length_cm        400.0
    camera.probe_size_cm        4.0            probe stays ENABLED
    camera.socket_offset_z_cm   70.0
    PlayerStart pitch           -10.0          NOT positive; see REJECTED
    spawn clearance             15.3 m to nearest trunk, 3.4 deg slope

### A CHARACTER WITH TWO MESHES

`ACharacter` owns one Mesh (`Character.h:352`). A MetaHuman is a body
(`metahuman_base_skel`, 342 bones) plus a face (`Face_Archetype_Skeleton`, 875).
`ALandscapeLabCharacter` therefore carries a `FaceMesh` component created
UNCONDITIONALLY in the constructor — `CreateDefaultSubobject` runs at CDO
construction, long before config is read — and given the body as its LEADER POSE
component in `ApplyConfiguredAssets`. One pose, one authority.

**`ABP_Unarmed` DRIVES THE METAHUMAN BODY.** The AnimBP targets `SK_Mannequin`
at 161 bones, `metahuman_base_skel` has 342, and BOTH skeletons'
`compatible_skeletons` arrays are EMPTY. It works anyway — the frames show a
natural standing pose, not a T-pose. **Recorded as MEASURED, NOT UNDERSTOOD.** Do
not read this as a licence to treat the two skeletons as interchangeable
generally.

### NOT OWNED BY THIS RECIPE — and it is visible in every frame

**THE HERO IS UNTEXTURED WHITE, BY CONSTRUCTION.** MetaHuman's Assemble is not
reflected in Python — there is no unpack and no build anywhere in the 5.8 stub —
and the skin lives in parameter OVERRIDES on a dynamic material instance whose
getter hard-refuses that type (see REJECTED). **The fix is one click and it is
Ryan's: Assemble, in the MetaHuman panel.** Then repoint the recipe at the
assembled meshes and re-run step 3.

The BODY is also still the female medium template, and the FACE is MetaHuman's
default rather than the man in `hero/reference/hero_face_bald_frontal.jpg`.

## R-HERO REJECTED

**Verifying the character by spawning it in the EDITOR world.** SYMPTOM: both
meshes read `null` and `GetResolvedSpec` returns empty strings, which looks
exactly like a broken config. CORRECT: verify in PIE. The config is applied in
`PostInitializeComponents` and input is bound in `BeginPlay`, and an
editor-world spawn is not a fair test of either. REFERENCE: measured
2026-08-16 — identical config read `null` in the editor and resolved fully in
PIE minutes later.

**`unreal.Rotator(0.0, YAW, 0.0)` to set a spawn's yaw.** SYMPTOM: the actor's
rotation reads `(roll 180, pitch 45, yaw 180)` and the third-person camera sits
BELOW the player looking up. CORRECT: `Rotator(ROLL, PITCH, YAW)` — pitch is
the second argument, so this sets PITCH, and the engine normalises pitch 135 to
that triple. The PlayerController inherits the PlayerStart's rotation and the
boom follows it. REFERENCE: `PythonStub:66750`; the same casualty is recorded
in CLAUDE.md from 2026-08-12 and recurred here in a committed tool.

**Reading back only LOCATION after placing an actor.** SYMPTOM: "drift 0.000 cm"
and exit 0 over a scrambled rotation, indefinitely. CORRECT: read back every
field that was written. A value that is never read back is a value nothing
defends.

**`EditorLoadingAndSavingUtils.save_dirty_packages(True, True)` after a Python
actor edit.** SYMPTOM: returns **True** and writes NOTHING; every subsequent
read-back agrees with the change because every read-back is reading editor
memory. CORRECT: reach the actor's own package with `get_package()` and
`save_packages([pkg], False)`, and PRINT THE PACKAGE NAME so the caller can
check its mtime and `git status`. A Python actor edit does not reliably flag
the external actor package dirty. REFERENCE: measured 2026-08-16 — no file
under `__ExternalActors__` changed in ninety minutes while the editor reported
the actor at its new location throughout.

the camera ends up INSIDE the canopy, which is worse than the close-up it was

**Placing a spawn by tracing ground alone.** SYMPTOM: the player begins inside a

that is both clear and walkable. Rank by nearness to a chosen point, NOT by
clearance alone: maximum clearance returns ground 1349 m from any tree, which is
above the treeline.

**Reading a MetaHuman's skin off its material to rebuild it.** SYMPTOM:
`TypeError: Cannot nativize 'MaterialInstanceDynamic' as 'Object' (allowed
Class type: 'MaterialInstanceConstant')`. CORRECT: there is no Python route;
parameter NAMES enumerate (80 of them on the face material) and the VALUES do

**Concluding "the face mesh is not rendering" from a frame.** SYMPTOM: three

**Reporting a body-constraint experiment as a finding.** SYMPTOM: setting
`Masculine/Feminine` to -2.0 and +2.0 yields BYTE-IDENTICAL body bounds

does nothing. Report it as unusable. REFERENCE: zero dirty packages afterwards

## R-TRELLIS — IMAGE TO 3D HEAD ON A BLACKWELL GPU (2026-08-16)

Status: **PROVEN** — 472,734 vertices, 945,456 faces, watertight, 64 s, from
`hero/reference/hero_face_bald_headcrop.png`. Views:
`hero/generated/hero_head_views.png`.

### THE ENVIRONMENT, AND WHY IT DEVIATES

TRELLIS installs PyTorch 2.4.0+cu118, which has **no sm_120 support at all**, so
the documented path cannot work on an RTX 5080. Required deviation:

    WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04     NOT 26.04 -- see REJECTED
    CUDA toolkit          12.8.93   (wsl-ubuntu repo, no display driver)
    conda env python      3.11      NOT 3.12 -- distutils
    torch                 2.11.0+cu128, capability (12, 0), sm_120 in arch list
    xformers              0.0.35, installed --no-deps
    spconv                spconv-cu126
    kaolin                NOT INSTALLED -- shim, see R-HERO's sibling note

### THE GATE, WHICH IS NOT A VERSION STRING

`torch.cuda.get_device_capability()` must read `(12, 0)` AND `sm_120` must
appear in `torch.cuda.get_arch_list()` AND a real matmul and a real reduction
must agree with a CPU reference. A build lacking sm_120 kernels can still report
`(12, 0)` and fail at launch. `scripts/wsl_exec.sh` + the gate script.

### RUNNING IT

    ATTN_BACKEND=xformers      NOT sdpa -- see REJECTED
    SPCONV_ALGO=native
    XFORMERS_DISABLED=1        routes DINOv2 away from xformers only

Formats `["mesh"]` only. Geometry is the deliverable; the gaussian rasterizers
(`diffoctreerast`, `mip-splatting`) serve radiance-field rendering and texture
baking and were never installed.

## R-TRELLIS REJECTED

**`wsl --install -d Ubuntu` and taking what you get.** SYMPTOM: Ubuntu 26.04,
whose only Python is 3.14.3 with NO `python3.11` or `python3.12` package
available at all. CORRECT: `-d Ubuntu-24.04` explicitly. REFERENCE: measured by
`apt-cache policy`, which returns nothing for both. NOTE the assumption that was
FALSE and must not be re-derived: NVIDIA **does** publish an `ubuntu2604` CUDA
repo. The repo was never the problem; the Python floor was.

**`ATTN_BACKEND=sdpa`.** SYMPTOM: the run prints `[SPARSE] Backend: spconv,
Attention: flash_attn` while the environment says `sdpa`, and flash-attn is not
installed. CORRECT: `xformers`. `trellis/modules/sparse/__init__.py` accepts
ONLY `xformers` or `flash_attn` and silently keeps its default otherwise, while
the DENSE attention module does accept `sdpa` — the same variable honoured by
one reader and dropped by another.

**Leaving xformers enabled for DINOv2 on Blackwell.** SYMPTOM:
`NotImplementedError: No operator found for memory_efficient_attention_forward`,
with `fa3F` and `cutlassF-pt` both requiring capability <= (9, 0) and `fa2F`
supporting only fp16/bf16. CORRECT: `XFORMERS_DISABLED=1`, read at
`dinov2/layers/attention.py:21`. It does not affect TRELLIS's own sparse
attention, which imports xformers directly.

**`pip install xformers` without `--no-deps`.** SYMPTOM: the resolver is free to
replace the torch that passed the sm_120 gate, and nothing announces it.
CORRECT: `--no-deps`, then RE-VERIFY torch's version, capability and a live
kernel afterwards.

**Installing kaolin to satisfy FlexiCubes.** SYMPTOM: a long source build with
no wheel for torch 2.11+cu128. CORRECT: the library path imports exactly one
symbol, `check_tensor`, used in six `throw=False` assertions; everything else is
under `examples/`. Implement it — `scripts/trellis/kaolin_check_tensor_shim.py`
— and NEVER as `return True`, which would satisfy the import while disabling
every assertion it stands for.

**Running `setup.sh` whole.** SYMPTOM: one failure and no information about
which of seven extensions caused it. CORRECT: piecewise, with a marker per
stage. Four separate blockers were each attributable this way.

## R-HERO REJECTED — additions 2026-08-16 (the face conform)

**`conform_to_target_meshes` with `auto_solve=True` and no tracking inputs.**
SYMPTOM: **the editor CRASHES** — `Assertion failed: IsValid()`
(`Templates/SharedPointer.h:1133`) with four frames of
`UnrealEditor_MetaHumanCharacterEditor` above the Python plugin; the client sees
`ConnectionResetError [WinError 10054]`, which is what a dead editor looks like
and is not itself diagnostic. CORRECT: populate `curve_tracking_points`,
`camera_view_info` and `image_size` — render the target mesh from a known
camera, read the pixels as BGRA, and run
`track_face_landmarks_from_image`, whose own docstring says *"Use with a
front-facing portrait of the target mesh — typically a SceneCapture2D render."*
**`auto_solve` is not evidence that the tracking inputs are optional**, and
assuming it was is what crashed the editor. REFERENCE: crash context preserved
at `_verify/20260816_conform_crash/CrashContext.runtime-xml`; nothing was
damaged — `git status` clean, `MHC_AlpineHero.uasset` unchanged, restore point
`pre-hero-face-conform-20260816` not needed.

**Passing an undecimated reconstruction to the solver.** SYMPTOM: the call ran
over ten minutes before dying; building a 472,734-element `unreal.Array` crosses
the Python binding once per element. CORRECT:
`scripts/trellis/decimate_head.py` to ~40k triangles, which is ample for a shape
solve and records the bbox change so the silhouette is checked rather than
assumed.

**Scaling the target mesh by its bounding box width or depth.** SYMPTOM: three
scale estimates that disagree by 2x — 50.3 on width, 26.4 on depth, 37.4 on
height. CORRECT: scale from HEIGHT, and better, crop the armour collar out of
the MESH. The collar is what inflates width and depth, it is geometry the solver
has no use for, and cropping the input IMAGE did not remove it from the
reconstruction.

### A CORRECTION TO THIS RECIPE'S OWN EARLIER CLAIM

An earlier note in this session read `ConformTargetMesh.head_vertex_indices` and
`FitToVerticesParams`'s index-free vertex array as implying MetaHuman ARCHETYPE
topology, and concluded a raw TRELLIS mesh was **not** a drop-in. **That is
wrong and is withdrawn.**

`MetaHumanCharacterEditorSubsystem.get_mesh_data_for_conforming(mesh)` takes a
StaticMesh or SkeletalMesh and returns `(vertices, triangle_indices)` — "the
same data that the interactive conform tool uses internally" — and those map
one-to-one onto `head_vertices` and `head_vertex_indices`. **The indices are
TRIANGLES.** Arbitrary topology IS supported, and that is the whole point of the
conform path as against `fit_state_to_target_vertices`, which does take the
archetype's own 33,845 vertices with no indices.

Measured, and useful to the next attempt:

    SM_HeroHead_TRELLIS   472,734 verts   extent (0.696, 0.921, 0.998)
    SKM_HeroFace          33,845 verts    extent (34.99, 24.28, 37.32) cm
                          bbox Z 134.7 .. 172.0 -- CHARACTER space, Z up

Same axis convention on both, so the alignment needs scale and translation only,
no rotation.

## R-HEROFACE — sculpting the hero's face from reference photographs

**Status: PROVEN for sculpt + rig. The UNPACK step is UI-ONLY and is NOT
scriptable in 5.8.** Narrative: `LESSONS.md` 2026-08-16 (evening).
Instruments: `scripts/hero_face/`.

### WHAT IT DOES
Moves a MetaHuman Character's face onto proportions measured from reference
photographs, entirely from Python, and verifies the result against those
photographs by a route that never uses the engine's renderer.

### THE FRAME — derive it, never assume it
`get_face_landmarks` returns 79 unlabelled points; the reflected surface says
nothing about axes, units or anatomy.

    lateral axis  X, by bilateral-symmetry test: median nearest-mirror
                  residual 0.7% of span about the cloud mean, against
                  13.7% (Y) and 4.0% (Z). Sagittal plane x = -0.01011.
    up axis       Z            depth axis  Y, +Y anterior
    anatomy       read off an orthographic X-Z plot, which IS a front view
                  once X is lateral and Z is up:
                    7 forehead  59 glabella  6 nose bridge  64 nose tip
                    65 subnasale  5/50/4 lips  62 chin crease  8 chin
                    12 under-chin   60 crown
                    13/14/15 POSTERIOR midline (back of skull, nape)

### THE UNIT IS 745 — the whole recipe in one number
`get_face_landmarks` REPORTS in one space; `translate_face_landmarks`
ACCEPTS another.

    requested   landmark moved   ratio
      0.001       1.343e-06      744.85
      0.01        1.342e-05      745.32
      0.1         1.342e-04      744.99
      1.0         1.342e-03      745.11
     10.0         5.876e-03     1701.97   <- SATURATED

**To move a landmark by X landmark-units, request X * 745.** Above ~1.0 per
call the face model constrains the move, so ITERATE rather than ask once.

### PROCEDURE
1. `probe_face_state.txt` -> landmarks + coefficients to disk.
2. `plan_face_sculpt.py` -> region predicates over normalised head
   coordinates, symmetrised by mirror-pairing, emitting ABSOLUTE TARGETS.
3. `apply_face_sculpt.txt --set COMMIT=True --set PASSES=12 --set SPAWN=False`
   -> iterates `(target - current) * 745` clamped to 1.0, prints residual per
   pass, `commit_face_state`, `save_asset`.
4. `dump_face_mesh.txt` + `render_face_mesh_offline.py` -> a picture, and the
   width-at-height comparison against the reference silhouette.
5. `plan_lateral_correction.py` + step 3 again -> close the measured
   lateral shortfall. Damped 0.6, clamped 1.18.
6. `autorig_hero.txt --set BLOCKING=False` (~25 s), then
   `save_character.txt`. **`can_build_meta_human` must read true before the
   character can be assembled.**
7. **RYAN, IN THE UI:** open `MHC_AlpineHero` and press Assemble. Nothing in
   Python unpacks.

### MEASURED RESULT, 2026-08-16
    pass 1  residual 0.00844 -> 0.00153 units (82% closed, 20 passes)
    pass 2  residual 0.00256 -> 0.00093 units (64% closed, 10 passes)
    asset   104,960,609 -> 104,977,162 -> 143,762,092 -> 145,442,446 B
    mesh    33,845 verts / 64,094 tris, extent 0.11497 x 0.08275 x 0.12433

**Pass 2 widened the cranium and cheeks by +7.1% to +8.1% and moved the jaw
by +1.0% / +0.2%.** The mandible is where the face model resists: the hero
remains 13-22% wider at the jaw than the sculpt will go. Recorded as a
property of the model, not as a failure of the pass.

### VERIFICATION — and the two instruments that must NOT be used
- **USE** the character asset's BYTES on disk. Every "did it take?" question
  in this work was settled by a size and hash change.
- **USE** mesh geometry via `get_mesh_data_for_conforming` on the preview
  `FaceMesh_N`, rasterised offline.
- **DO NOT** use `get_face_landmarks` alone. It reads the field the setter
  wrote and reported success on a sculpt that moved nothing
  (non-negotiable 8) -- that is how the 745x unit error survived its first run.
- **DO NOT** use facial rig joints via `get_socket_location`. They return
  reference-pose positions and read 0.0 movement on a WORKING sculpt, even
  after `assemble_for_preview`. A gate built on them is a FALSE REFUSAL.

### REJECTED

| Wrong thing | Symptom you will see | Correct thing |
|---|---|---|
| deltas in landmark units | asked 3.48e-03, moved 6.08e-06 (0.17%); every tool reports success | multiply by **745** |
| one-shot delta | lands short of target and silently stays there | iterate; the model saturates above ~1.0 per call |
| offset-based spec | a second run sculpts the face twice, undetectably | absolute TARGETS; re-running is a no-op |
| region predicates without symmetrisation | nose wing 45 without mirror 67, jaw 3/30 without 43/63 -> a CROOKED face | mirror-pair the delta field; all 79 pair, residual 0.000e+00 |
| `request_auto_rigging(blocking=True)` | **EDITOR DIES.** `Assertion failed: IsValid() [SharedPointer.h:1133]` -- the same assertion as the recorded `conform_to_target_meshes` crash | `blocking=False`; watch the log for "Auto-Rigging finished in N seconds" |
| spawning the MetaHuman actor before `save_asset` | editor WEDGES, twice: log stops at `InternalPromptForCheckoutAndSave started...` -> `FlushAsyncLoading`, game thread 0.04 CPU/wall, untitled modal, committed sculpt LOST | `--set SPAWN=False`. The spawn brings up `/Temp/MetaHumanCharacter/LightingEnvironments/...` streamed levels and the save deadlocks on them |
| `save_asset` again before `build_meta_human` | same wedge | the autorig step already saved it |
| `build_meta_human(absolute_build_path=...)` | logs **"MetaHuman Character assembly succeeded"** and writes NOTHING; everything lands in `/Engine/Transient.MHC_..._Collection:` | there is **no reflected unpack in 5.8**, with any path. Assemble in the UI |
| landmark-derived width profile vs photo silhouette | ratios up to 87 on bands of n=1-4 | 79 points are not a silhouette; use the MESH's 33,845 vertices |
| rendering the MetaHuman preview actor | pure white, mean RGB 255/255/255, nonwhite fraction 0.0000, four times | the preview mesh is ~0.12 units tall and its components sit at world origin and do NOT follow `set_actor_location`; it is inside the near clip plane. Rasterise the mesh offline |
| comparing two sculpt passes by their ratio tables | jaw "got worse" 1.159 -> 1.308 | each table is normalised by its OWN cranium width; when the cranium widens the denominator moves. Compare ABSOLUTE widths at matched heights (`compare_sculpt_passes.py`) |
| `get_local_bounds` on the face component | `AttributeError` -- it is a `DebugSkelMeshComponent` | `get_actor_bounds`, or enumerate: `get_num_bones` / `get_bone_name` / `get_socket_location` exist |
| `ue_exec.py --timeout 240` | ~240 s of nothing, then 3 s of work | it is a DISCOVERY WINDOW, not a deadline. Use 12-15 |

### THE ORDERING CONSTRAINT, read out of the editor log
    sculpt  ->  textures  ->  rig  ->  build
Rigging LOCKS texture editing (*"Face and body texture selection are locked
while the character is rigged. Unrig to modify them."*) and building REQUIRES
a rig. Unrigging to do texture work is what left the character unrigged.
**A sculpt does NOT invalidate the rig** -- measured: `can_build_meta_human`
read true immediately after pass 2, before any re-rig.

### R-HEROFACE, ADDENDUM — GROOMS (hair, beard, moustache, eyebrows)

**Status: PROVEN to the saved asset. Not yet seen in a rendered frame.**
Added 2026-08-16 under THE NEW-ELEMENT RULE: grooms are a new element type
for this project.

#### THE DISTINCTION THAT DECIDES WHETHER THE HERO IS BALD
`try_add_item_from_wardrobe_item` makes an item **AVAILABLE** in the palette.
It does **NOT** put it on the character. The instance must SELECT it.
Stopping after the add yields four successful-looking tool reports over a
hero who still has no hair.

    col = subsystem.get_preview_collection(character)
    key = col.try_add_item_from_wardrobe_item(slot, wardrobe_item)  # available
    col.get_editor_property("default_instance") \
       .set_single_slot_selection(slot, key)                        # WORN
    subsystem.on_edit_preview_collection(character)                 # REQUIRED
    EditorAssetLibrary.save_asset("/Game/Hero/MHC_AlpineHero", False)

`on_edit_preview_collection` is not optional — the engine docstring states
that any code modifying the preview collection must call it to propagate the
edits back to the Character asset.

#### SLOTS (from `get_slot_names()`, measured not assumed)
    Beard  Body  Bottom Garment  Character  Eyebrows  Eyelashes  Hair
    Mustache  Outfits  Peachfuzz  SkeletalMesh  Top Garment

#### THE VALUES, for this hero
    Hair       WI_Hair_M_Layered        (WI_Hair_L_MessyClumps = longer)
    Beard      WI_Beard_M_Stubble
    Mustache   WI_Mustache_M_Stubble
    Eyebrows   WI_Eyebrows_M_Dense
All under `/MetaHumanCharacter/Optional/Grooms/Bindings/<Slot>/`, class
`MetaHumanWardrobeItem`, engine content under the UE EULA.

#### PROCEDURE
1. `apply_hero_grooms.txt --set GO=False` — probe. Reports the slot names and
   whether each item resolves; mutates nothing. **Run this first**: it turns
   a missing asset into a refusal instead of a half-applied groom set.
2. `apply_hero_grooms.txt --set GO=True` — add + propagate + save.
3. `select_hero_grooms.txt --set GO=True` — recover the key per slot with
   `get_item_keys_for_slot`, select, propagate, save.
4. `verify_grooms_on_disk.py` — verify from the SAVED BYTES.

#### VERIFICATION
Positive-controlled byte search of `MHC_AlpineHero.uasset`: the four selected
groom names present (3 hits each) and five deliberately unselected names
(`Hair_L_Straight`, `Beard_L_Full`, `Mustache_L_Handlebar`,
`Eyebrows_S_FlatThin`, `Hair_M_Mohawk`) at **0 hits**. The script WITHHOLDS
its verdict entirely if any control appears — a substring search that matches
everything proves nothing.

#### REJECTED

| Wrong thing | Symptom | Correct thing |
|---|---|---|
| add without selecting | every call returns a valid `MetaHumanPaletteItemKey`, the asset grows, and the hero is still bald | `set_single_slot_selection` on `default_instance` |
| skipping `on_edit_preview_collection` | edits sit on the preview collection and never reach the Character asset | call it after every modification |
| carrying item keys between payloads | keys are not stable across runs | recover them with `get_item_keys_for_slot(slot)` |
| verifying with the tool that wrote it | reports success by construction | positive-controlled byte search of the saved asset |
| spawning the MetaHuman actor anywhere in this flow | save deadlocks in `FlushAsyncLoading`, work lost | never spawn before a save |

#### R-HEROFACE, ADDENDUM — ALWAYS HAND THE CHARACTER BACK

**Every payload that calls `try_add_object_to_edit` MUST call
`remove_object_to_edit` when it is done.** The engine's own docstring says so
and this project ignored it in nine payloads.

The failure mode is not a leak. It is a **LOCKOUT WITH A LYING MESSAGE**:

    Error: TryAddObjectToEdit called for 'MHC_AlpineHero' which is already
           added for editing
    Error: Failed to open MHC_AlpineHero failed to create editing state.
           The asset may be corrupted

Ryan double-clicked the asset and was told his hero **may be corrupted**. It
was not: it had saved cleanly minutes earlier and passed
`AssetCheck: Validating asset` on the way in, 145,447,390 B,
`can_build_meta_human` true. The editor cannot distinguish "another client
holds the editing state" from "the bytes are bad", and it reports the
alarming one.

**Fix:** `scripts/hero_face/release_character.txt` — reports
`is_object_added_for_editing` before and after, so the release is measured.
Restarting the editor also clears it, expensively.

**This is the misleading-diagnostic class, from the other side.** This project
has repeatedly caught tools that report success while doing nothing; here an
engine reported CATASTROPHE over an asset that was fine. Both are the same
defect: a message asserting a cause the code never established.

| Wrong thing | Symptom | Correct thing |
|---|---|---|
| leaving the character registered for edit | the Content Browser refuses to open it and says **"The asset may be corrupted"** | `remove_object_to_edit` at the end of every session; `release_character.txt` |

## R-TREECOLLIDE — MAKING SCATTERED INSTANCES COLLIDE (2026-08-16)

**Status: PROVEN.** `PHASE2_PLAN.md` unit 6. Declaration: `collision` on every
instanced species, schema **v1.23**. Tools
`scripts/apply_foliage_collision.py` (write),
`scripts/measure_foliage_collision.py` (read),
`scripts/verify_tree_collision.py` (prove),
`scripts/save_foliage_actors.py` (persist). Artefacts
`Free/_measured/foliage_collision.json`,
`_verify/20260816_pie_unit1_unit6_collision_on.md`. Narrative: LESSONS
2026-08-16 (night).

**SUPERSEDES R-COLLIDE's framing.** R-COLLIDE is correct about the MESH and
its measurement stands. Its REJECTED entry names
`SM_PVE_Norway_Spruce_01_A`'s zero primitives as the blocker on unit 6; it is
**one of two defects and not the decisive one.** All fourteen `FT_*` foliage
types read `NoCollision`, so the three species with vendor-authored capsules
did not collide either.

### THE FOUR STEPS, IN THIS ORDER. THE LAST ONE IS THE ONE THAT GETS SKIPPED.

    1. author a capsule ONLY where the mesh is repo-TRACKED
    2. set the FOLIAGE TYPE's body_instance + custom_navigable_geometry
    3. RESTART the editor  (the collision profile is read at engine init,
       and FixupData -> LoadProfileData runs only on load)
    4. SAVE THE FOLIAGE ACTORS WITH only_dirty=False

**Step 4 is not bookkeeping.** `FFoliageStaticMesh::UpdateComponentSettings`
copies the foliage type onto the component (`InstancedFoliage.cpp:1822`) and
runs at LOAD, so after step 3 the editor's components are correct — and a
load-time fixup does **not** dirty the package it corrected. Measured:
`get_dirty_content_packages()` returns **0** with 1,093
`InstancedFoliageActor`s holding corrected components. The external actor
packages on disk still carry the OLD serialized `BodyInstance`, World
Partition streams PIE from those packages, and **the game gets
`NoCollision` while the editor is provably correct.**

### THE VALUES THAT WORK

    collision.enabled              "query_only"
    collision.profile              "FoliageBlockQueryOnly"
    collision.navigable_geometry   "yes"
    capsule (Conifer only)         radius_cm 38.0, z 0.0 .. 2731.0

`FoliageBlockQueryOnly` is declared in `LandscapeLab/Config/DefaultEngine.ini`
under `[/Script/Engine.CollisionProfile]` with `CollisionEnabled=QueryOnly`,
`ObjectTypeName="WorldStatic"`, `CustomResponses=` (empty = Block every
channel), `bCanModify=False`.

### THE ACCEPTANCE TEST, AND WHY IT IS SHAPED THIS WAY

    python scripts/verify_tree_collision.py --recipe recipes/alpine_8k.json \
        --per-species 6 --settle 60 --timeout 25

**Every `FHitResult` field is protected or absent in the 5.8 Python surface**
— `component`, `distance`, `location`, `time`, `normal`, `item` all report
"protected and cannot be read". A trace yields hit-or-miss and nothing else.
So the test is a DIFFERENTIAL: each trunk trace runs twice, the second time
with every `InstancedFoliageActor` in `actors_to_ignore`, and counts only when
the first HITS and the second MISSES. Terrain is hit by both and counts as
nothing — which matters, because a horizontal trace on alpine ground hits the
landscape readily (a 16 degree slope rises 86 cm over the 3 m approach).

Traces run on **VISIBILITY**, deliberately: the `NoCollision` profile sets
`Visibility=Ignore` (`BaseEngine.ini:3103`), so a Visibility hit proves the
profile's RESPONSES were loaded and not merely that a flag was set.

Result: Conifer 5/6, ConiferPine 6/6, SpruceSub 5/6, SpruceSapling 5/6, with
6/6 negative controls missing on every species.

### COST, MEASURED AGAINST THE RIGHT CALIBRATION CLASS

    station forest_floor_control, PIE, 300 frames, CSV categories ON

                        pie002 (off)   unit6 (on)    delta
    GameThreadTime mean     8.055        8.261       +0.206
    GameThreadTime p50      7.986        8.128       +0.142
    GameThreadTime p90      8.611        8.790       +0.179
    GPUTime mean            8.338        8.335       -0.003

**+0.21 ms GameThread against unit 6's +0.5 ms abort bar. PASSES.** GPU is
unchanged to three decimals, which is what collision should do.

**The comparator is `pie002`, NOT `pie001`.** This run had the diagnostic CSV
categories enabled and `pie001` did not; the recorded cost of those categories
is +0.52 ms GPU, and this run's GPUTime sits +0.519 above `pie001` — the
instrument's own settings, reproduced. Comparing against `pie001` would have
read as +1.06 ms and tripped a bar that was never crossed.

**Stated as a limit:** this is a CROSS-SESSION A/B, not a single-variable run
in one process. `SceneCulling/NumStaticInstances` reads 346,285 here against
284,424 in `pie002` at identical residency (4 landscape proxies, 9 foliage
actors) — that field is already recorded as NOT REPRODUCING and is not quoted
as a confound or as a finding.

## R-TREECOLLIDE REJECTED

**`collision_enabled = QUERY_ONLY` together with `collision_profile_name =
BlockAll`, which `PHASE2_PLAN.md` unit 6 prescribes.** SYMPTOM: reads back
exactly right in the session that wrote it, and silently becomes
`QUERY_AND_PHYSICS` on the next editor start. CAUSE: `BlockAll` declares
`CollisionEnabled=QueryAndPhysics` (`BaseEngine.ini:3104`), and
`UFoliageType::PostLoad` -> `FBodyInstance::FixupData`
(`InstancedFoliage.cpp:806-812`) -> `LoadProfileData` (`BodyInstance.cpp:4567`)
-> `UCollisionProfile::ReadConfig` (`:4509`) writes the PROFILE's own
`CollisionEnabled` over whatever was serialized, on EVERY load. CORRECT: a
profile whose own `CollisionEnabled` IS `QueryOnly`, so the two fields cannot
contradict.

**Dodging that by leaving the profile as `Custom`.** SYMPTOM: collision works,
the player is blocked, and a walk test passes — while trees are INVISIBLE to
visibility traces. CAUSE: `Custom` stops `ReadConfig` running, so the response
container stays the one `UFoliageType`'s constructor left, which is
`NoCollision`'s — and that sets `Visibility=Ignore` and `Camera=Ignore`
(`BaseEngine.ini:3103`). Breaks line of sight, AI perception and weapon traces
later, far from the change that caused it. CORRECT: a real profile with
`CustomResponses=` empty.

**`custom_navigable_geometry = "no"` to keep trees out of the navmesh**, as
`PHASE2_PLAN.md` unit 6 prescribes. SYMPTOM: reads like a safety measure and
does the opposite of what the name suggests. CAUSE: per
`NavRelevantInterface.h`, `No` means the custom export callback is not called
**but the default collision export still runs**; for an ISM that callback is
`DoCustomNavigableGeometryExport` (`InstancedStaticMesh.cpp:5435-5438`), which
exports PER-INSTANCE transforms and is the path that makes 63,981 instances
navmesh obstacles at all. CORRECT: `"yes"` — the engine default
(`InstancedFoliage.cpp:868`) — declared explicitly. `"dont_export"` is the
value that actually excludes.

**Quoting the MESH's `collision_profile` as the runtime answer.** SYMPTOM:
`Free/_measured/mesh_collision.json` reports `BlockAll` on all six meshes while
nothing in the world collides. CAUSE: that field is the MESH's
`BodySetup.default_instance`; the component's `BodyInstance` is overwritten
from the FOLIAGE TYPE at `InstancedFoliage.cpp:1822`. Two different objects,
one path. CORRECT: read the foliage type — `measure_foliage_collision` prints
both in one table.

**Sizing an authored capsule from `RENDER_DATA` or
`get_section_from_static_mesh` on a NANITE mesh.** SYMPTOM: a confident radius
derived from a mesh nobody renders. CAUSE: both return the Nanite FALLBACK
proxy. Measured on `SM_PVE_Norway_Spruce_01_A`: the fallback overstates the
mesh by **6.6% in Z and ~36% in X**, and its low-Z bands hold 1–8 vertices,
giving radii scattered 7–63 cm with no cylinder in them. CORRECT:
`GeometryScript_AssetUtils.copy_mesh_from_static_mesh` with
`GeometryScriptLODType.SOURCE_MODEL` — 76,343 vertices and a clean trunk. Check
`build_scale` before assuming a conversion factor: it is `[1,1,1]` here, so the
two are different MESHES, not one mesh in two unit systems.

**Extrapolating the trunk radius from the sibling vendor capsules.** SYMPTOM: a
tight fit across three assets (`r/h ~ 0.030`, `r ∝ h^0.85`, 4.5 m / 16.7 m /
22.1 m) giving **78 cm** at 29.12 m — more than double the real trunk. CAUSE:
vendor capsules are GAMEPLAY-FATTENED VOLUMES, not trunks; this mesh measures
`r/h = 0.0120`. CORRECT: measure the mesh. A tight fit across three samples
says the samples agree with each other, not that they measure the thing you
want.

**Declaring the capsule as the engine's `length`.** SYMPTOM: a capsule one
diameter shorter than intended, silently. CAUSE: `KSphylElem.length` is the
LINE SEGMENT — "add Radius to both ends to find total length"
(`SphylElem.h`) — but it reads as a total height. CORRECT: the recipe declares
`radius_cm` + `z_min_cm` + `z_max_cm`; the tool derives `length` once and
refuses a span that does not exceed its own diameter. `length_cm` is a REFUSED
key with a `prove_gates` probe holding the refusal.

**Authoring collision onto a gitignored vendor mesh.** SYMPTOM: works, then
vanishes on re-download. CAUSE: `RECIPES.md`'s Fab-boundary rule names
"changing its LOD or collision" on a Fab static mesh as its worked example.
CORRECT: `apply_foliage_collision` refuses by `git check-ignore` against the
real file, and treats "could not decide" as a refusal rather than as tracked.
Of the four tree meshes only `SM_PVE_Norway_Spruce_01_A` is tracked — it is the
one this project exported itself, and the only one with no simple collision,
which is not a coincidence.

**`save_dirty_packages` after setting the foliage types.** SYMPTOM: reports
success, writes nothing, and PIE keeps the old collision. CAUSE: the load-time
`UpdateComponentSettings` that corrected the components does not dirty their
packages — 0 dirty against 1,093 corrected actors. CORRECT:
`save_foliage_actors.py`, which saves with `only_dirty=False`, and VERIFY FROM
`git status` — 1,073 of 1,093 packages modified on disk — never from the tool's
return value.

**Making `collision` an optional field with a sensible default.** SYMPTOM: the
exact failure being fixed, reproduced — silent, invisible, green on every
asset-level check. CAUSE: the original defect was not a wrong value but an
absent one; `place_foliage` contains no occurrence of the string "collision" in
any form, so `UFoliageType`'s constructor default (`InstancedFoliage.cpp:640`)
stood for the life of the project. CORRECT: REQUIRED on every instanced
species, REFUSED on grass (`LandscapeGrass.cpp:3170-3172` hard-codes
`NoCollision` there, so the field could not mean anything), 16 `prove_gates`
probes holding it. **A default you never named is a decision you never made.**

## R-NAVBUILD — BUILDING THE NAVMESH IN A WORLD PARTITION WORLD (2026-08-17)

**Status: PROVEN** for one 1024 m chunk. `PHASE2_PLAN.md` unit 8.
Declaration: `navigation` in the world recipe, schema **v1.24**; the AGENT
lives in `recipes/character.json` and is not restated. Tools
`scripts/apply_navigation_config.py`, `scripts/build_navmesh_chunk.py`.
Artefact `_verify/navmesh_build_WorldPartitionNavigationDataBuilder.log`.
Narrative: LESSONS 2026-08-17.

### THE ORDER, AND EVERY STEP IS LOAD-BEARING

    1. --ini      write the config block          (ARecastNavMesh +
                                                   UNavigationSystemV1)
    2. RESTART    config reaches the CDO at engine init
    3. --world    WorldSettings + NavMeshBoundsVolume actors
    4. SAVE       force, only_dirty=False        <- SEE BELOW
    5. RESTART    so SetConfig runs against the saved agent
    6. SAVE       force again, the navmesh actor  <- SEE BELOW
    7. build      commandlet, editor CLOSED

**Steps 4 and 6 are the ones that get skipped, and skipping them produces a
build that logs 166 warnings and silently makes nothing.**

### THE VALUES THAT WORK

    tile_size_uu                           1600.0
    average_layers_per_tile                1.5
    max_simultaneous_tile_generation_jobs  16
    min_region_dimension_uu                400.0
    data_gathering_mode                    "lazy"
    chunk_grid_size_cm                     102400
    builder_loading_cell_size_cm           102400

`AgentMaxSlope` is DERIVED from `character.json` `navigation.agent_profile`
via `MOVEMENT_PROFILES` and never typed (ruling 19, re-checked in the
applier). `AgentRadius` / `AgentHeight` / `AgentStepHeight` go into
`+SupportedAgents`, NOT into the RecastNavMesh section — see REJECTED.

### THE COMMAND

    UnrealEditor-Cmd.exe <uproject> /Game/Alpine8K
        -run=WorldPartitionBuilderCommandlet
        -Builder=WorldPartitionNavigationDataBuilder
        -SCCProvider=None -Unattended -NoSplash

`-CleanPackages` removes existing chunk actors; run it before a measured
build so the byte figure means something.

### MEASURED, ONE 1024 m CHUNK

    wall clock      30.0 s   (commandlet execution 20.18 s)     bar 30 min
    peak commit     19.6 GB  of a 223.4 GB limit                bar 200 GB
    min free RAM    16.5 GB
    commandlet      PeakPhysMemoryMB 4584, PeakVirtMemoryMB 4374

    RecastNavMesh actor        9563.4 KB
    NavDataChunkActor 3_-4     9526.6 KB   <- the cell with the volume
    NavDataChunkActor 3_-3       76.7 KB
    NavDataChunkActor 2_-4       74.0 KB
    NavDataChunkActor 2_-3        4.2 KB

Four chunk actors for one chunk is arithmetic, not a defect: the volume's
bounds ARE the cell boundaries, so it touches the neighbours along its edges.

### THE ACCEPTANCE TEST IS A PROJECTION, WITH A NEGATIVE CONTROL

    PlayerStart          (354600, -321400, 31139.5)
    projects to navmesh  (354600.0, -321400.0, 31020.1)   difference 119 cm
    character.json       spawn.height_above_ground_cm = 120

    inside  the declared cell   25/25 project, z 25604..36465
    outside the declared cell    0/4 project        <- NEGATIVE CONTROL

The negative control is what makes the inside hits mean anything: it shows
the navmesh is bounded by the volume rather than global.

**Query extent must span the cell's own relief.** A fixed query height with
a ±20 m tolerance read 7/25 on this navmesh; ±120 m reads 25/25 on the same
data. A coverage number is a property of the query as much as of the navmesh.

## R-NAVBUILD REJECTED

**Building without saving the world after the nav actors change.** SYMPTOM:
the commandlet logs `NavData RegistrationFailed_AgentNotValid ... will be
removed. This warning will disapear once the map is saved` — 166 times — and
produces packages containing nothing usable, while the EDITOR reads the
correct values the whole time. CAUSE: `SetConfig` corrects the navmesh actor
in MEMORY at load and does NOT dirty its package, so `save_dirty_packages`
writes nothing; the headless commandlet loads from disk. CORRECT: force-save
the nav actors with `only_dirty=False`. Same defect as unit 6's foliage
collision, six hours later, in a different subsystem. **An engine message
saying "this will disappear once the map is saved" means the disk and the
session disagree RIGHT NOW.**

**Reading the commandlet's EXIT CODE as the success test.** SYMPTOM: exit 1
on both the broken run and the healthy one. CAUSE: the single "error" is
`LogHttpListener: Error: HttpListener unable to bind to 127.0.0.1:8000` —
the IncrediBuild port conflict, unrelated to navigation — and `Failure -
1 error(s)` is computed from it. Warnings fell 166 → 2 between the runs while
the exit code did not move. CORRECT: judge on the log's warning summary and
on a projection query. `build_navmesh_chunk.py` prints the exit code and
refuses to conclude cost from it.

**Setting `AgentRadius` / `AgentHeight` on ARecastNavMesh.** SYMPTOM: the CDO
reads the declared values and the ACTOR reads 35/144, with every other
property on the actor correct. CAUSE: `NavigationSystem.cpp:2874-2875` and
`:4729` call `NavData->SetConfig(SupportedAgents[...])`, which overwrites the
navmesh's agent dimensions. With `SupportedAgents` empty — verified, no entry
anywhere in engine or project config — `FNavDataConfig`'s fallbacks stand.
CORRECT: `+SupportedAgents=(Name="Default",AgentRadius=...,AgentHeight=...,
AgentStepHeight=...)` under `[/Script/NavigationSystem.NavigationSystemV1]`.
`AgentMaxSlope` is NOT part of `FNavDataConfig` and correctly stays on the
navmesh.

**Setting `TileSizeUU` or `AgentMaxSlope` on the navmesh ACTOR instead of in
config.** SYMPTOM: the value reverts with only a log warning. CAUSE:
`ARecastNavMesh::PostLoad` (`RecastNavMesh.cpp:963-1015`) forces both back to
the class default when the voxel cache is on. CORRECT: config, which moves
the CDO too, so the comparison it makes is your value against your value.

**Declaring a `tile_size_uu` above `CellSize * 1024`.** SYMPTOM: the build
uses a different tile size than the recipe says. CAUSE:
`GetClampedTileSizeUU` (`RecastNavMesh.cpp:75-81`) clamps silently. CORRECT:
the schema refuses anything outside [300, 19456] at the shipped `CellSize=19`.

**Relying on `bWholeWorldNavigable` instead of bounds volumes.** SYMPTOM: no
navmesh anywhere and a build that succeeds. CAUSE: its `UPROPERTY` is
commented out at `NavigationSystem.h:370` with the engine's own "currently
broken". CORRECT: `ANavMeshBoundsVolume` actors, declared in the recipe, which
also makes the tile budget computable without an editor.

**Leaving `TileSizeUU` and `AverageLayersPerTile` at the engine defaults for
a world-sized navigable region.** SYMPTOM: none at build time — the engine
logs an error and CLAMPS, leaving a navmesh quietly smaller than the region.
CAUSE: 8128 m at 1000 uu tiles and 3 layers needs ~1.99M tiles against
`TileNumberHardLimit` 1,048,576 (`RecastNavMesh.cpp:551`). CORRECT: 1600 uu
and 1.5 layers gives 388,622. A `prove_gates` probe holds this.

**Running the builder with an editor open.** SYMPTOM: `unable to unlink old
... Invalid argument`, the class this project already paid for during the
density revert. CORRECT: `build_navmesh_chunk.py` refuses to start while
`UnrealEditor.exe` is running, and treats an unreadable process list as a
refusal rather than as "no editor".

**Extrapolating a whole-world build cost from this one.** SYMPTOM: a
confident 21-minute figure. CAUSE: the builder iterated 81 loading cells to
produce navmesh in ONE, so most of the 20 s was iteration with nothing to do.
CORRECT: a whole-world volume and its own measured run. This is the
misleading-denominator class.



**Extrapolating navmesh build cost from the tiles nearest the town.** SYMPTOM:
none until the campaign runs long. CAUSE: `NavBounds_Town` and `_TownEast` are
the only two tiles in the region that are basin-flat AND had 2,541 trees cleared
out of them; their 17.6 MB/tile is not the region's. CORRECT: build ONE
full-density tile first. Measured 2026-08-27 on a 6,782-tree tile: +12.96 MB,
+6.0 s, +0.4 GB, and **+0.76 km2 of reachable ground from a 1.08 km2 tile** --
the last being the figure that decides whether a tile is worth building at all.

**Assuming the navmesh builder is incremental.** SYMPTOM: a batch plan that
bounds peak memory by building a few tiles at a time. MEASURED: 13 packages
created, 10 DELETED -- it discards every chunk actor and regenerates. Per-tile
cost is NOT additive across runs; a batch bounds RISK (the cost curve is learned
as you go) and not peak. Peak commit turned out nearly flat anyway -- 20.0 to
22.2 GB across a 36x increase in coverage -- because the builder streams cells.

**THE MEASURED COST CURVE, so the next order of magnitude need not be guessed:**

    volumes    nav MB    wall s    peak commit GB    chunk actors
       2        35.18      36.0         20.0              10
       3        48.14      42.0         20.4              12
       9       116.01      46.0         20.6              16
      72       756.58     110.0         22.2              64

Prediction from the 9-volume point: ~830 MB, actual 756.58. Bars 2.5 GB / 30 min
/ 60-90 GB all cleared with room.

**Sizing a navmesh volume grid by hand.** SYMPTOM: 72 chances to mistype a
bound, and no single place saying what the grid IS. CORRECT:
`scripts/plan_navmesh_tiles.py` derives every volume from ONE declaration,
anchored on the already-built town volume so the two existing volumes ARE grid
cells and are carried through with their hand-measured bounds untouched --
renaming or moving them would invalidate every reachability sidecar bound to
them. The anchor being exactly one tile is ASSERTED, not assumed.

**Clipping edge tiles to the landscape without a minimum size.** SYMPTOM: 81
volumes where the region holds ~64, nine of them SLIVERS as thin as 9.6 m,
because the grid is anchored on the town rather than the landscape corner and
the only guard was "wider than one TileSizeUU" (16 m). CORRECT: drop a clipped
tile below 30% of a full tile, and COUNT the drops in the report rather than
skipping silently. Caught by reading the printed bounds and noticing y values
9,600 cm apart where they should be 104,000.

**A proximity radius equal to the resolution of the thing it queries.**
SYMPTOM: 7 of 440 encounters projected but were unreachable. CAUSE: a 60 m
"near reachable ground" radius against a lattice sampled at 60 m admits a
candidate a full cell away from anything measured. CORRECT: well INSIDE the
resolution -- 30 m here. **AND THAT IS NOT SUFFICIENT ON ITS OWN**: at 30 m, 3
of 320 still failed and one sat 8.1 m from a reachable cell. Those are genuine
pockets; no radius separates them. Proximity is a PREFILTER, the path query is
the authority, and tightening further is fitting the prefilter to the answer.

**Pruning a plan in place to satisfy its verifier.** SYMPTOM: none immediately;
later, `check_plan_freshness --reproduce` reports DIFFERS forever, because the
producer no longer emits what is on disk. CORRECT: non-negotiable 20's adopted
artefact -- `<region>_all.json` stays the reproducible PLAN and
`<region>_verified.json` is the plan minus what the BUILT NAVMESH refused,
stamped against BOTH sources. A placer reads the verified file.
`scripts/adopt_verified_encounters.py` refuses a rows file whose count does not
match the plan (index-pruning across two runs deletes the wrong rows), a rows
file with no verdicts, and any drop above 10% -- a verifier suddenly refusing
that many rows is a FINDING, not an input.
