## R-HEROCAP — THE FACE-COMPARISON CAMERA (2026-08-17)

**Status: PROVEN.** Built, framed, and its noise floor measured at n=4.
Informed by LESSONS 2026-08-17.

**What it is for.** Every claim this pipeline makes about the hero's face —
"the joint moved", "the brow widened", "the restore was clean" — is a
comparison between two renders. The renders are therefore the measurement,
and a camera that drifts between them fabricates findings. Ryan ruled out
hand screenshots (framing drift is indistinguishable from joint movement) and
offline rasterisation (it renders exported geometry, not the assembled
post-import character). This is the replacement.

    scripts/hero_face/likeness/build_capture_stage.py   frames it ONCE
    scripts/hero_face/likeness/capture_shot.py          takes every picture

### THE LOCKED VALUES

    level          whatever is OPEN. The stage is built in it and nothing
                   is saved. A payload that switches levels fatals the
                   editor (EditorServer.cpp:1951).
    subject        SkeletalMeshActor of the Face mesh at Z 250,000 cm,
                   above the terrain, against sky
    resolution     2048 x 2048
    fov_angle      24.0 deg horizontal  (~85 mm on a 36 mm sensor)
    exposure       AEM_MANUAL, bias 0.0, min == max brightness 1.0,
                   motion blur 0.0
    warm-up        30 TRIGGERED captures, then the shot. Never
                   bCaptureEveryFrame.
    persist        always_persist_rendering_state TRUE  <- MANDATORY
    cvars          r.Streaming.FullyLoadUsedTextures 1
                   r.VT.MaxUploadsPerFrame 512
                   r.VT.MaxContinuousUpdatesPerFrame 512
    grooms         every Groom/Hair component hidden, re-asserted per shot
    azimuth        90.0 deg  (SEARCHED, then locked)
    camera         loc [0.0, 86.784, 250167.345]  rot [0.0, -90.0, 0.0]
    lights         Key 90,000 / Fill 30,000 / Rim 45,000 lux, aimed
                   RELATIVE to the locked azimuth at -30 / +45 / +180 deg
                   and pitch -22 / -8 / -5

### THE THREE RULES THAT MAKE IT AN INSTRUMENT

1. **The framing is SEARCHED once and set ABSOLUTELY thereafter.** The
   builder derives the camera from `get_actor_bounds`; `capture_shot.py`
   reads no property of the subject at all. A face that changes shape must
   not be able to move the camera.
2. **Every setting is read back and disagreement REFUSES (exit 5).**
   Transform, fov, render-target size, `capture_every_frame`, light
   intensity. The camera-rotation read-back is what caught the
   `Rotator(ROLL, PITCH, YAW)` recurrence.
3. **A delta is not evidence until it beats the noise floor.**
   `capture_shot.py --noise-floor --repeats N` takes N shots of the
   UNCHANGED character, compares EVERY pair, and adopts the WORST.

### THE NOISE FLOOR, MEASURED 2026-08-17 AT n=4

    a-b p90 0.00758   a-c 0.00559   a-d 0.00301
    b-c 0.00305       b-d 0.00514   c-d 0.00450     interpupillary units

    ADOPTED BAR   p90 0.00758 IPD = 0.057 cm
                  max 0.01140 IPD = 0.086 cm
    scale         0.01745 cm/px, IPD 429.79 px = 7.502 cm
                  pinhole off the locked camera, APPROXIMATE

**This bar belongs to this stage, this level, this editor session and this
GPU** — the same calibration class R13 puts on every frame-cost figure.
Re-measure it after an editor restart before quoting a delta across one.

### VERIFICATION

    python scripts/hero_face/likeness/build_capture_stage.py --azimuths "90"
      -> GATE PASS, yaw_frac within ~0.01 of 0.500, manifest updated
    python scripts/hero_face/likeness/capture_shot.py --noise-floor --repeats 4
      -> six pairs printed, worst adopted, written to manifest.json
    python scripts/hero_face/likeness/capture_shot.py --stage baseline
      -> one PNG named baseline_<UTC>.png, gate PASS, floor quoted

## R-HEROCAP REJECTED

**`always_persist_rendering_state` left at its default False.** SYMPTOM: a
pure-white 2048 square frame, mean 254.85, nonwhite 0.027, from a capture
that reports success. CAUSE: every `capture_scene()` starts with no
rendering history, so the face's virtual textures
(`MID_MI_Face_Skin_Baked_LOD*_VT_*`) never leave their white fallback.
CORRECT: set it True and warm up; mean 161.90, nonwhite 1.000, converged by
10 frames. **Do not chase this through exposure** — four exposure sweeps, a
near-clip check and a post-process bypass all failed to explain it, and the
frames got WHITER as the bias dropped, which is the tell that the pixels are
a fallback texture and not an exposure.

**Choosing the azimuth from frames nobody opened.** SYMPTOM: the search
picks 270, which is the BACK of the head. CAUSE: every candidate was white
and therefore rejected, so the "best" was the least-bad noise. CORRECT: open
a downsized preview of the chosen frame before locking it. A statistic that
says "a real image" (mean 161.7, std 92.8, range 0-255) is satisfied by the
back of a head.

**`set_editor_property("intensity_units", unreal.LightUnits.LUX)`.**
SYMPTOM: a note in the build report, the actor created, and the light left at
engine default — a silhouette against the level's own 130,000 lux sun.
CAUSE: `ELightUnits` has no LUX member because a directional light's units
are fixed (`DirectionalLightComponent.cpp:1509` returns
`Unitless /* Lux */`), and the AttributeError fires while evaluating the
ARGUMENT, so the `intensity` line below it never runs. CORRECT: set
`intensity` directly in lux, and READ IT BACK.

**`unreal.Rotator(pitch, yaw, roll)`.** SYMPTOM: the camera pitches -90 and
photographs the ground; the light rig carries its pitch as roll. CAUSE: the
constructor is **(roll, pitch, yaw)**, PythonStub:66750 — third instance in
this project. CORRECT: `Rotator(roll, pitch, yaw)`, and assert the read-back
rather than relying on remembering the order.

**Deriving the camera from the subject's bounds on a comparison shot.**
SYMPTOM: none visible — every frame looks correctly framed. CAUSE: a joint
edit changes the head's bounds, so the camera moves with the face and the
comparison measures the sum of the two. CORRECT: set the manifest transform
absolutely; read no property of the subject.

**A noise floor at n=2.** SYMPTOM: p90 0.00240 IPD, and a later 0.005 delta
read as a real move. CAUSE: the floor itself varies 3.2x between pairs; the
n=2 answer sat near the bottom of its own spread. CORRECT: n>=4, compare
every pair, adopt the WORST. Averaging the pairs hides the bad case a real
delta can then sit under.

## R-HERODNA — APPLYING A METAHUMAN DNA TO A SKELETAL MESH (2026-08-17)

**Status: PARTIAL — the write is PROVEN, the APPLY is NOT.** Read the
REJECTED section before reaching for any of this. Narrative in LESSONS
2026-08-17 (later).

**What works, verified.** Reading and writing joint translations in the
2.5-format DNA, through the LandscapeLabEditor plugin:

    unreal.LandscapeLabTools.read_dna_joints(path)
      -> names, translations, count, format, ok, error
    unreal.LandscapeLabTools.write_dna_joint_translations(
         in_path, out_path, indices, translations)
      -> count, layer_note, ok, error

`write_dna_joint_translations` REFUSES an in-place edit of the canonical
file, refuses duplicate or out-of-range indices, and SELF-VERIFIES by
re-loading the written file and comparing every requested joint to 1e-4 cm.
Measured: joint 804 `FACIAL_C_Jaw` -0.106097 -> 1.893903 on X, confirmed off
disk. **The edit lands in the DEFINITION layer; SaveDNAToFile writes All.**

**What does NOT work, and it is not the write.**

    unreal.LandscapeLabTools.apply_dna_to_skeletal_mesh(
        dna_path, reader_source, mesh,
        update_joints, update_base_mesh, rebuild_render_data, attach_dna,
        probe_bone_names)
      -> probe_before, probe_after, bone_count, stages, reader_info,
         ok, error

with `reader_source="file"` ROTATES THE WHOLE HEAD. See REJECTED.

### THE COORDINATE FACT, MEASURED

    spine_04, the DNA root (parent to itself)
      exported DNA file    (0, 120.0077,   4.3415)     Y-up
      mesh ref skeleton    (0,   4.3415, 120.0077)     Z-up

Exact Y/Z swap. `USkelMeshDNAUtils::UpdateJoints` applies
`GetNeutralJointTranslation` RAW, and `UpdateBaseMesh` likewise assigns
`GetVertexPosition` straight into `Vertex.Position`. **Neither converts.**

**A DNA DECLARES ITS OWN AXES.** `FCoordinateSystem` of `EDirection`
{Left, Right, Up, Down, Front, Back}, `DNACommon.h:47,268`, reachable via
`IDNAReader::GetCoordinateSystem()`. The wrapper's `reader_info` prints it
together with translation unit, rotation unit and whether the reader is
legacy-wrapped. **Read it; do not infer the convention from a magnitude.**

### THE THREE READERS

    "file"    LoadDNAFromFile        raw. MEASURED WRONG for this asset.
    "legacy"  ReadDNAFromFile        FLegacyDNAReader, "applies the legacy
                                     Maya->UE coordinate swizzle on geometry
                                     queries" (DNAReader.h:39-44). Joints
                                     (x,-y,z), rotations (-y,-z,x) --
                                     which is NOT the swap measured, so this
                                     is a candidate, not the answer.
    "mesh"    GetDNAReader(SkelMesh) the DNA the mesh already carries. The
                                     live hypothesis: export_dna plausibly
                                     writes DCC space for a Maya round trip.

**The acceptance test for whichever reader is right is an IDENTITY ROUND
TRIP**: apply the UNEDITED canonical DNA and require every probe bone to come
back to its original component-space translation. Only then does a delta on
top of it mean anything.

### RESTORE, AND IT IS NOT WHAT THE PLAN ASSUMED

Re-applying the canonical DNA is NOT a restore — with the wrong reader it
reproduces the damage. The restore is:

    EditorLoadingAndSavingUtils.reload_packages(
        [asset.get_outermost()],
        ReloadPackagesInteractionMode.ASSUME_POSITIVE)

Nothing is ever saved, so the bytes on disk are still the assembled hero.
**Never INTERACTIVE** — a modal blocks the game thread, which is the only
channel that could report it. Verified: probes returned to
(-0.1066, 3.985, 162.3585) and bounds to [18.724, 10.859, 26.277].

### BACKUP, MANDATORY, BEFORE ANY WRITE

`Content/MetaHumans/MHC_AlpineHero/Face` is gitignored derived content, so a
git tag cannot hold it. Copy it aside ON DISK, timestamped, and hash-prove
the DNA beside it. 48 files / 364.8 MB. This is the rule the 2026-08-16
hero regression bought.

## R-HERODNA REJECTED

**`apply_dna_to_skeletal_mesh(..., reader_source="file", update_joints=True)`
on an exported DNA.** SYMPTOM: the head leaves the frame; every bone's Y takes
its old Z. CAUSE: the exported DNA is Y-up, the mesh Z-up, and `UpdateJoints`
applies the value raw. PROVEN INNOCENT OF THE EDIT by a control — the
UNEDITED canonical DNA does exactly the same thing. CORRECT: unknown as of
this entry; settle it with the identity round trip above before applying
anything.

**Predicting the render from `UpdateJoints`'s source and not measuring it.**
SYMPTOM: a confident, specific, mechanical claim that a joints-only write is
INVISIBLE. CAUSE: the component poses from the USkeleton asset, not from the
mesh's reference skeleton, so the new bind pose and the old animation pose do
not cancel. CORRECT: render it. A source reading is a hypothesis.

**A rigid nudge as the positive control for a landmark metric.** SYMPTOM: a
0.2 cm translation of the subject reads 0.9x the noise floor and the control
"fails". CAUSE: the landmark frame is iris-centred and IPD-scaled, so
translation cancels EXACTLY — as does an X-scale, because the normalising IPD
is measured along X. CORRECT: a SHAPE change. Z-scale 1.02 reads 5.4x the
floor. **Know what your metric is invariant to before choosing its control.**

**Re-applying the canonical DNA as the "restore" arm.** SYMPTOM: a restore
step that would have reproduced the damage and then declared itself clean.
CORRECT: `reload_packages(..., ASSUME_POSITIVE)`, and prove it by probe AND
by render.

**A probe that dirties the package.** SYMPTOM: a read with every stage off
leaves `SKM_MHC_AlpineHero_FaceMesh` dirty, and a Save Content modal waits at
the next editor close. CAUSE: `Modify()` / `MarkPackageDirty()` called
unconditionally. CORRECT: guard both on whether a stage will actually mutate.

## R-HERODNA — ADDENDUM 2026-08-17: THE READER QUESTION IS SETTLED, NEGATIVELY

The previous entry left three candidate readers and said the measurement did
not yet pick one. **It has now been run, and none of them works.** Artefact:
`_verify/hero_likeness/20260817_dna_reader_identity.md`.

**THE DNA DECLARES ITS OWN CONVENTION**, so this is read rather than inferred
(`IDNAReader::GetCoordinateSystem()`, `DNACommon.h:47,268`):

    format 2.5   axes X=Left  Y=Up  Z=Front   translation cm   rotation deg
    870 joints

**IDENTITY ROUND TRIP** — apply the UNEDITED canonical DNA with UpdateJoints
and require every probe bone to return to its original component-space
translation. Mesh reloaded from disk between arms.

    reader   legacy-wrapped   worst probe delta   identity
    file           no            164.42 cm          NO
    legacy         YES           205.44 cm          NO
    mesh           no            164.42 cm          NO

`mesh` gives byte-for-byte the same answer as `file`, so **the DNA the mesh
CARRIES is in the same Y-up space as the exported file** — the hypothesis
that `export_dna` writes DCC space while the mesh keeps UE space is REFUTED.
`legacy` is WORSE, and its own source says why: `(x, -y, z)` on joint
translations is a Y negation, not the Y/Z swap the data needs.

**CONCLUSION: `USkelMeshDNAUtils::UpdateJoints` cannot reproduce this mesh's
reference skeleton from this DNA under any reader in 5.8.** The mesh's
reference skeleton was not produced by `UpdateJoints`; it came through the
MetaHuman assemble/Interchange path, which applies a conversion the RigLogic
utilities do not. This is the same shape as the 2026-08-16 finding that
`duplicate_asset` cannot carry a transient MetaHuman mesh: **a general-looking
utility that is not the pipeline the asset actually came from.**

### THE CONVERSION, DERIVED AND CORROBORATED, NOT APPLIED

    UE.x = -DNA.x      (DNA X=Left, UE Y=Right)
    UE.y =  DNA.z      (DNA Z=Front)
    UE.z =  DNA.y      (DNA Y=Up)

    check  DNA spine_04 (0, 120.0077, 4.3415) -> (0, 4.3415, 120.0077)  EXACT

Corroborated by a DIFFERENT REPRESENTATION: the capture stage measured the
hero's face pointing along **+Y** in world (azimuth 90 frontal, 270 the back
of the head), which `DNA Z=Front -> UE Y` predicts.

**NOT PROVEN, and both gaps are named.** spine_04's X is zero, so the X SIGN
is untested. And `UpdateJoints` reads `GetNeutralJointRotation` too, so a
converted DNA needs its ROTATIONS converted or every child composes through a
wrong parent — which needs `FDNACalibSetNeutralJointRotationsCommand`
(`DNACalibSetNeutralJointRotationsCommand.h`, present in 5.8) wrapped
alongside the translation command. The acceptance test is the identity round
trip, and it fails closed: a converted DNA that does not reproduce the mesh
exactly is not the conversion.

## R-HERODNA REJECTED — additions

**`reader_source="legacy"` as the fix for the coordinate mismatch.** SYMPTOM:
worse, not better — worst probe delta 205.44 cm against `file`'s 164.42.
CAUSE: `FLegacyDNAReader::GetNeutralJointTranslation` returns `(x, -y, z)`, a
Y negation; the data needs a Y/Z swap. The header's promise of a
"legacy Maya->UE coordinate swizzle" is true and is not the swizzle this
asset needs. **Read the adapter's actual arithmetic, not its docstring.**

**`reader_source="mesh"` on the hypothesis that the mesh's attached DNA is in
UE space.** SYMPTOM: byte-for-byte identical to `file`. CAUSE: the mesh
carries the same Y-up DNA. A plausible mechanism, refuted in one run, and
cheap because all three readers were wrapped in a SINGLE plugin rebuild
rather than three round trips.

## R-HEROIMPORT — THE SANCTIONED METAHUMAN DNA ROUND TRIP (2026-08-17)

**Status: PROVEN for the round trip; the EDIT is not yet proven.** The
identity round trip passes at 1.13x the noise floor. What has NOT been shown
is any DNA edit that changes the rendered face — see the OPEN block.
Supersedes the `USkelMeshDNAUtils` route, which is CLOSED (see R-HERODNA).
Narrative in LESSONS 2026-08-17 (later still).

**Ruled by Ryan 2026-08-17.** UpdateJoints failed identity on all three
readers, so patching it with a derived swizzle would be calibrating the
instrument to the answer. This is UE's own tooling, which is what the
original brief's rule 3 required all along.

    scripts/hero_face/likeness/sanctioned_import.py   import + identity arm
    scripts/hero_face/likeness/use_preview_mesh.py    stage -> preview mesh

### THE PARAMETERS, AND THE DOCSTRING THAT IS WRONG

    ImportFromDNAParams
      import_whole_rig        False    <- FACE-ONLY. Nothing is locked.
      isolate_head_from_body  False
      alignment_options       NONE

The reflected doc claims `import_whole_rig=False` means "the head DNA file
will only be used for neck alignment". **FALSE.**
`MetaHumanCharacterEditorSubsystem.cpp:6647-6656` shows the false branch
calling the SAME `FitToFaceDna` as the whole-rig branch and then
`CommitFaceState`; `FitToFaceDna` (`:6504-6520`) calls
`FaceState->FitToFaceDna(...)` then `ApplyFaceState`. `bImportWholeRig` adds
`CommitFaceDNA`, which is what makes the body type fixed and non-editable.

**The params are READ BACK after being set** — a struct that silently kept a
default would import the wrong thing and report success.

### THE SAFETY EQUIPMENT, MANDATORY

    /Game/Hero/MHC_AlpineHero_Master     duplicate, never imported into
    hero/dna/MHC_AlpineHero_Head.dna     canonical, never edited in place
    _trash/hero_likeness_backups/<UTC>/  uasset copies, hash-proven

`compare_face_state(working, master, 0.001)` returned TRUE at creation, so
the duplicate is faithful — verified numerically rather than by opening it.
Content under `Content/Hero` and `Content/MetaHumans` is derived/gitignored
in places, so a git tag cannot hold it; the on-disk copy is the restore.

**RESTORE IS `reload_packages`, NOT A RE-IMPORT.** Re-importing the canonical
DNA is not an undo. Restore destroys the preview actor, calls
`remove_object_to_edit`, then
`reload_packages([pkg], ReloadPackagesInteractionMode.ASSUME_POSITIVE)`.
Never INTERACTIVE: a modal blocks the game thread, the only channel that
could report it.

### THE RENDER LOOP — PREVIEW, NOT ASSEMBLE

    try_add_object_to_edit(character)          register (~3.6 GB)
    assemble_for_preview(character)            editor pipeline, preview
    spawn_meta_human_actor(character, True)    transient, tracks the character
    -> Face component, 875 bones, transient SkeletalMesh
    -> point HeroStage_Subject at it, re-point after EVERY assemble

The preview Face mesh's bounds are IDENTICAL to the assembled mesh's —
origin `[0.0, 2.697, 250151.053]`, extent `[18.724, 10.859, 26.277]` — so the
locked camera, lights and noise floor from R-HEROCAP carry over untouched.
A full Assemble needs a rig, writes 252 packages and has hung this editor on
memory; it has no place inside a compare loop.

**The preview mesh is TRANSIENT and is replaced by every preview assemble.**
Re-point every time, and print the object path, or a stale pointer renders
the previous state and calls it current.

### THE ACCEPTANCE SEQUENCE, IN ORDER

    a  duplicate to master; compare_face_state(working, master, 0.001) TRUE
    b  noise floor in the rebuilt stage, with --cycle-assemble
    c  IDENTITY ROUND TRIP: import the UNEDITED canonical DNA, render,
       require <= 2x floor
    d  only then any edited arm

**Measured 2026-08-17, the passing run:**

    baseline  settle 1  7.66x floor   REJECTED, unresolved preview
              settle 2  0.86x floor   accepted
    import    ImportErrorCode.SUCCESS
    after     settle 1  0.43x floor   accepted
    DELTA     0.00947 IPD = 0.0709 cm = 1.13x floor        PASS

### A CAPTURE IS NOT A MEASUREMENT UNTIL IT REPRODUCES

A freshly reloaded character renders a **faceted, unresolved preview** —
pointed crown, polygonal facets, asymmetric open mouth — that resolves after
further assembles. Baselines and post-import renders therefore shoot
repeatedly, re-assembling between, until two CONSECUTIVE renders agree inside
the floor. Exit **9** rather than return an unsettled frame.

## R-HEROIMPORT REJECTED

**Taking a baseline immediately after a restore.** SYMPTOM: the identity arm
reads 7.50x the floor and "importing the unedited canonical DNA changed the
face" is one sentence from the record. CAUSE: the freshly reloaded preview is
faceted and unresolved; the number was the preview converging. CORRECT:
require two consecutive agreeing renders. **The frames settled this in one
look and no statistic could have.**

**Reading a single passing number as the answer.** SYMPTOM: 0.68x on the
first identity run. CAUSE: that baseline happened to come from an
already-settled state — right answer, lucky conditions, and it would have
masked the procedure defect entirely. A pass whose conditions you cannot
state is not yet evidence.

**Re-importing the canonical DNA as the restore step.** SYMPTOM: a "restore"
that leaves the character in the imported state and then reports it clean.
CORRECT: `reload_packages(..., ASSUME_POSITIVE)`.

**Labelling `compare_face_state`'s tolerance in centimetres.** SYMPTOM: a
report saying the state differs by more than 1 cm while the render moved
0.043 cm. CAUSE: the API documents "vector norm" over vertices AND vertex
normals; it is not a distance, and 1 cm of surface would be over 57 px in
this render. CORRECT: print it as a norm and say it is not a distance.

**Trusting the reflected docstring for `import_whole_rig`.** SYMPTOM: an
avoidable, PERMANENT body-type lock accepted on the belief that the
alternative does nothing. CORRECT: the code, `:6647-6656`.

## OPEN, STATED PLAINLY

- **NO DNA EDIT HAS YET CHANGED THE RENDERED FACE, AND THAT IS NOW MEASURED
  RATHER THAN INFERRED.** With the settling instrument:

      identity, UNEDITED canonical DNA            1.13x floor
      +2.0 cm on FACIAL_C_Jaw X, joints only      1.26x floor

  Both settled arms printed their own working, and both rejected an
  unresolved first baseline on the way (7.66x and 7.73x).

  Both at or below the floor: the import round-trips cleanly and the joint
  edit does nothing. (A confounded earlier pair read 7.48x against 7.50x;
  both of those were the unsettled-preview artefact and neither was about
  the DNA.) `FitToFaceDna` fits the state to the DNA's GEOMETRY, and a
  neutral-joint-translation edit leaves geometry untouched.
- **So Pass 1 must edit VERTEX POSITIONS.**
  `DNACalibSetVertexPositionsCommand` ships in 5.8 and needs a wrapper beside
  the existing joint one. That changes the ruled joints-first strategy and is
  Ryan's call.
- The parametric fit is limited by what the MetaHuman face model can express
  — the same effect already measured as the model resisting the mandible.
  `import_whole_rig=True` would reproduce a DNA exactly and lock the body;
  this path fits and does not.

## R-HEROGEOM — MOVING THE HERO'S FACE BY EDITING DNA GEOMETRY (2026-08-17)

**Status: PROVEN.** The first DNA edit in this project to change the rendered
face. Ruled by Ryan 2026-08-17: Pass 1 is GEOMETRY-FIRST, superseding
joints-first, which is dead by measurement on both routes. Narrative in
LESSONS 2026-08-17 (night). Runs on top of **R-HEROIMPORT** (the sanctioned
round trip) and **R-HEROCAP** (the camera).

    scripts/hero_face/likeness/edit_dna_geometry.py    write the edited DNA
    scripts/hero_face/likeness/sanctioned_import.py    import + render + delta

**Why geometry and not joints, in one line:** `FitToFaceDna` fits the
parametric state to the DNA's GEOMETRY and never reads the neutral joints, so
a joint write is dead weight and a false audit trail.

**What the fit path buys:** it REGENERATES model state from geometry, so rig
self-consistency — teeth following, pivots staying honest — is enforced by
the engine rather than by our edit discipline. That is why a raw vertex edit
is safe through this path and was never safe through raw application.
**Not yet measured for teeth/eyes — BACKLOG B-FITCOHERENCE.**

### THE SPACE, AND IT IS NOT UE's

`MHC_AlpineHero_Head.dna` declares, via `IDNAReader::GetCoordinateSystem`
(`DNACommon.h:47,268`) and printed on every run:

    format 2.5;  axes X=Left  Y=Up  Z=Front;  cm;  degrees;  870 joints

    head_lod0_mesh   index 0   24,049 verts
      X -19.034 .. 19.034    Y 140.878 .. 178.439    Z -11.616 .. 14.988
    teeth_lod0_mesh  Y 156.547 .. 162.072
    eyeLeft_lod0     Y 165.627 .. 168.458
                                          (50 meshes, 8 LODs)

So the jaw is LOW Y and FRONT Z, and "down" is -Y. **Nothing converts to UE
space.** Only LOD0 is edited; the fit reads LOD0 and the other seven head
LODs are deliberately untouched.

### THE PROVEN EDIT

    python scripts/hero_face/likeness/edit_dna_geometry.py \
      --out-dna LandscapeLab/Saved/HeroDNA/jaw_down2cm.dna --mesh 0 \
      "--box-min=-12,148,4" "--box-max=12,158,15" "--delta=0,-2,0"

    -> selected 1,661 of 24,049; self-verified 1661 selected + 512 untouched

**Use `--flag=value` for any negative coordinate.** argparse reads a bare
`-12,...` as an option and exits 2 with no message.

### THE RESULT, MEASURED

    render delta   0.07899 IPD = 0.5908 cm = 7.09x floor
    settles        baseline 0.30x, after 0.33x  (both clean)

    region        |d|_cm            region       |d|_cm
    chin           1.299            mouth         0.128
    jaw_L          0.894            forehead      0.085
    jaw_R          0.794            nose_tip      0.050
    cheek_L        0.509            eye_inner_L   0.039
    nasion         0.344            FLOOR         0.083

    CHIN vertical -1.299 cm against a commanded -2.00 cm
    ATTENUATION    0.650      <- FIRST ENTRY IN THE GAIN TABLE

**The negative control is inside the same measurement:** forehead, nose and
eye all sit at or below the floor, and the falloff is monotone from the chin
outward. A fit that had merely rescaled the head would have moved the
forehead too.

**To land a target: command target / 0.65.** Re-derive per region; 0.65 is
the chin's number under this box, not a constant.

### VERIFICATION

    python scripts/hero_face/likeness/edit_dna_geometry.py ... (self-verifies)
    python scripts/hero_face/likeness/sanctioned_import.py --dna <edited>
    python scripts/hero_face/likeness/sanctioned_import.py --restore

Always restore afterwards; the character is left IMPORTED by design so the
render can be inspected first.

## R-HEROGEOM REJECTED

**Editing neutral joint translations to move the face.** SYMPTOM: 1.26x the
floor against an unedited DNA's 1.13x — indistinguishable, i.e. nothing.
CAUSE: `FitToFaceDna` fits to GEOMETRY. CORRECT: vertex positions. Dead on
both routes, for two different reasons; see R-HERODNA for the other.

**A hard-edged box as the edit shape.** SYMPTOM: visible vertical seams on
the chin in the render — vertices just inside moved 2 cm, their neighbours
just outside moved none, and the fit smooths but does not remove it. CORRECT:
`FDNACalibSetVertexPositionsCommand::SetMasks(TArrayView<const float>)` takes
a per-vertex mask; a box is a SELECTION, not a brush. **Found in the frame,
not in the statistic** — the numbers were clean.

**Verifying only the vertices you moved.** SYMPTOM: none, until a DNACalib
command defaults the rest. CAUSE: the command replaces EVERY position of the
mesh, so read-all/modify-some/write-all is the only correct shape and the
carry-through is the part that can silently fail. CORRECT: re-read and check
a sample of UNSELECTED vertices too.

**A box that selects nothing, written anyway.** SYMPTOM: a DNA byte-identical
to its input, reported as a successful edit. CORRECT: refuse, and name the
DNA's declared axes in the message, because a caller who has hit this is
almost certainly working in UE space by mistake.

**Judging an arm against another session's floor.** SYMPTOM: a wrong
multiple. This session measured 0.01114 IPD where the previous two measured
0.00835 and 0.00758 — same stage, same script, same subject, different
process. Re-measure per session, R13's calibration class.

## R-HEROFIT — THE LIKENESS LOOP (2026-08-18)

**Status: BUILT AND PROVEN AS AN INSTRUMENT; DEMOTED AS AN AUTHOR.** It
converges, it is self-correcting, and its objective function was wrong.
Narrative in LESSONS 2026-08-18. Runs on R-HEROCAP (camera), R-HEROIMPORT
(round trip) and R-HEROGEOM (the edit).

    scripts/hero_face/likeness/fit_face.py          the loop
    scripts/hero_face/likeness/edit_dna_geometry.py the edit
    scripts/hero_face/likeness/face_coeffs.py       the parametric controls

### THE TWO REFERENCES, AND THEY ARE NOT INTERCHANGEABLE

    SHAPE       hero/reference/hero_face_bald_frontal.jpg
    APPEARANCE  hero/reference/hero_example_pic.jpg   (== haired frontal)

**MEASURED COST OF CONFUSING THEM**, same instrument, bearded minus bald:

    jaw_width +0.570 cm   chin_height -0.514   cheek_width +0.202

About 1.29 cm of a 2.616 cm residual is BEARD. A fit pointed at the bearded
image widens the jaw to match stubble, and the result reads bloated: against
the correct target the fitted hero came out 0.482 cm too wide at the jaw and
0.343 cm too long at the chin.

### THE MEASUREMENT FRAME — ASYMMETRIC ON PURPOSE

    REFERENCE   iris-centred, IPD-NORMALISED   (its scale is unknown)
    RENDER      iris-centred, FIXED SCALE      (fixed_ipd_px 429.027)

The camera is locked and the head sits at a fixed distance, so render pixels
are absolute at 0.01745 cm/px. **Normalising the render by its own IPD makes
the ruler a function of the thing being edited** and is the single cause of
every oscillation this loop showed. Freeze it once from a canonical frame.

### THE PARAMETRIC COEFFICIENT LAYOUT (decoded 2026-08-18, undocumented)

    [0]       region count = 22
    [1..8]    global transform
    per region:  [count][count PCA coefficients][8 transform floats]
                 -- the LAST region has no transform block

    check: 9 + sum(1 + count_i) + 21*8 = 9 + 1220 + 168 = 1397   EXACT

Each transform ends in a centre in the DNA's declared space (X=Left, Y=Up,
Z=Front, cm) and the X values are symmetric L/R pairs.
`set_face_model_coefficients` accepts a vector verbatim (read-back exact,
0 of 1397 altered).

### THE LOOP'S OWN RULES, EACH BOUGHT BY A FAILURE

    gain == the observed response, NOT old_gain/response
    gain updates DAMPED by a geometric mean (a single estimate is noisy)
    gain HELD when the command or the move is below the noise floor
    step cap TAPERS as a region closes
    cumulative command and iteration history PERSIST in the manifest
    captures must REPRODUCE twice before counting
    REFUSE if IPD drifts more than 1.5% between iterations

### RESULT

    2.616 -> 0.311 cm total residual, monotone, -88%
    three of four addressable regions inside a 0.150 cm deadband
    ...against a CONTAMINATED target. Re-run against the bald frontal.

## R-HEROFIT REJECTED

**Pointing the fit at the appearance reference.** SYMPTOM: convergence, and
a face that reads wider and heavier than the target. CAUSE: a beard adds
volume at the mandible, which is where jaw_width and chin_height measure.
CORRECT: shape from the bald frontal, appearance from the haired one. **The
rule was already written in the same manifest, forty lines above the field
that broke it.**

**Normalising the RENDER by its own IPD.** SYMPTOM: regions nobody commanded
move; the residual goes backwards; two regions read as "structurally
unaddressable". CAUSE: the eyes are the ruler and edits reached them --
+2.7% from geometry, +1.37% from a parametric probe. CORRECT: freeze the
render's scale. The reference keeps its normalisation; the asymmetry is the
point.

**gain = old_gain / observed.** SYMPTOM: the loop rings and every step clamps
at max_step. CAUSE: inverted -- it shrinks the gain when the render
over-moves. CORRECT: gain = observed, damped.

**Updating a gain from a move below the noise floor.** SYMPTOM: a gain slams
to its clamp and the next command jumps to max_step in the wrong direction.
CORRECT: hold the gain; small commands happen precisely when a region is
already near target.

**Running the loop as single-iteration processes without persisted state.**
SYMPTOM: oscillation between two states forever. CAUSE: the cumulative reset
to zero each process, so every call corrected a state it had not produced.
CORRECT: the character's state is a property of the project, not of one
process.

**Reading _verify/hero_likeness/fit_history.json as the record.** SYMPTOM:
"only one iteration recorded", and the session's best state looks
unrecoverable. CAUSE: that file holds the IN-PROCESS list; the MANIFEST is
what accumulates across runs. CORRECT: read `fit.iterations_run`.

**Seven scalar ratios as the objective for "looks like this character".**
SYMPTOM: -88% residual, no gain in resemblance. CAUSE: widths at three
heights plus a chin drop cannot express a contour, and most of the
reference's identity is hair, stubble, skin, age, eye colour and lighting --
none of it geometry. CORRECT: contour objective for shape; grooms, skin and
presentation for likeness; and an ATTENDED author with this loop as the
verifier. **An objective function is a claim about what matters, and it is
the least tested claim in any fitting pipeline.**

## R-HEROWHOLERIG — THE WHOLE-RIG IMPORT ARM, MEASURED (2026-08-18)

**Status: MEASURED ON AN EXPENDABLE DUPLICATE, PASSING BOTH CRITERIA.** One
edit, not an accumulation — see OPEN. Narrative in LESSONS 2026-08-18 (night).
Runs on R-HEROCAP (camera), R-HEROIMPORT (the round trip), R-HEROGEOM (the
edit). The tool is unchanged: `sanctioned_import.py --whole-rig`.

### WHY THIS ARM EXISTS

R-HEROFIT's ceiling: `import_whole_rig=False` sends every import through
`FitToFaceDna`, which RE-SOLVES the whole parametric state, so the render's
own reproducibility degrades ~4x once edits accumulate (0.27 cm floor at
cumulative 0.3..0.7 cm against 0.0698 cm canonical) and the loop chases a
target that moves further than its 0.15 cm deadband. Whole-rig replaces the
rig from the DNA instead of fitting to it, so the question is whether the
measurement holds still at an edited state.

### THE PROCEDURE — EXACT

    1  duplicate_asset /Game/Hero/MHC_AlpineHero -> ..._Scratch, SAVE it,
       and prove it: compare_face_state(scratch, source, 0.001) TRUE
    2  use_preview_mesh.py --character <scratch>          stage -> its preview
    3  capture_shot.py --noise-floor --settle 2 --repeats 4
                       --cycle-assemble <scratch>          FLOOR, state 0
    4  sanctioned_import.py --character <scratch> --whole-rig --identity
    5  re-measure the FLOOR                                state A
    6  edit_dna_geometry.py --region chin_jaw --delta=0,-2,0
    7  sanctioned_import.py --character <scratch> --whole-rig --dna <edited>
    8  re-measure the FLOOR                                state B

**Use a SEPARATE MANIFEST COPY for the scratch.** `--noise-floor` WRITES
`capture.noise_floor` into whatever manifest it is given, so measuring a
scratch state against the canonical manifest would overwrite the working
character's calibration with a number belonging to a different asset.

**MEASURE ALL THREE FLOORS BY THE SAME METHOD.** The verdict is the RATIO
between states, and a floor measured with `--cycle-assemble` is not
comparable to one measured without it.

### THE NUMBERS — MEASURED 2026-08-19 04:1x-04:37Z, one editor session

    state                                         floor p90    spread   gate
    0  scratch, parametric canonical (control)     0.0463 cm    1.98    passes
    A  whole-rig, UNEDITED canonical DNA           0.0837 cm    3.82    passes
    B  whole-rig, feathered -2.00 cm chin DNA      0.0559 cm    1.97    passes

    fit path, same rig, prior session
       canonical                                   0.0698 cm    3.10    passes
       edited, cumulative only 0.3..0.7 cm         0.27   cm    5.52    REFUSED

    identity arm    render delta 0.0486 cm = 1.05x floor, PASSED
    state 0 vs A    chin 0.005  jaw 0.001  brow 0.003  bridge 0.004 cm

    chin ratio      commanded -2.0000 cm  ->  rendered -1.9613 cm   0.981
                    frame sd 0.013 cm over 11 frames (6 at A, 5 at B)
                    fit path, SAME DNA BYTES:      -2.1553 cm   1.078

    negative control, same measurement
       jaw +0.068  cheek +0.064  temple +0.029  eye_spacing +0.007 cm
       against a 0.0559 cm floor, while the chin moved 1.96 cm

**THE DNA IS HASH-PROVEN ACROSS BOTH ARMS.** The edited DNA was regenerated
from the canonical through the manifest's own `chin_jaw` region and came out
BYTE-IDENTICAL to the prior session's `jaw_down2cm_feathered.dna`
(sha256 `ff9e44b1…`, 6703 weighted / 1661 core both times). The two arms
therefore consumed the same bytes and the comparison is single-variable.

### OPEN — STATED PLAINLY

- **ONE EDIT, NOT AN ACCUMULATION.** The fit path's ceiling appeared under
  ACCUMULATED edits. This proves a single 2.0 cm edit, which is larger than
  the accumulation that broke the fit path, but it is not the same test.
  Chain a second edit onto the edited DNA and re-measure before the loop
  relies on it.
- **`brow_height` -0.125 cm and `nose_bridge` -0.211 cm moved 2-4x the floor
  from OUTSIDE the edit box** (box tops at Y 160.5; eyes at Y 165.6+, and the
  edit self-verified 512 zero-weight vertices). Pose moved with them: roll
  -0.06 -> +0.60 deg, yaw_frac 0.5029 -> 0.5209, ipd 429 -> 422 px. **NOT a
  rigid pitch** — a pitch foreshortens chin and brow TOGETHER, and here the
  chin lengthened 15% while the brow shortened 6%. Leading explanation is the
  LANDMARK MODEL re-fitting to an out-of-distribution long jaw, i.e.
  instrument bias rather than geometry. **UNRESOLVED, and it bounds the ratio
  at ~0.1-0.2 cm rather than at the 0.013 cm frame spread.**
- **THE BODY-TYPE LOCK WAS NOT OBSERVED.** `fixed_body_type` reads **False**
  on the scratch after TWO whole-rig imports, identical to the master.
  MEASURED, NOT CONCLUDED: the asset was dirty and unsaved, and the lock may
  live where that flag does not report. R-HEROIMPORT's cost claim is neither
  confirmed nor refuted, and nothing may treat the lock as absent on that
  reading alone.

## R-HEROWHOLERIG REJECTED

- **Measuring a scratch state against the canonical manifest.** `--noise-floor`
  overwrites `capture.noise_floor` in the manifest it is handed. Symptom: the
  working character's calibration silently becomes a number measured on a
  different asset, and every later gate runs against it. CORRECT: copy the
  manifest per asset under test.
- **Judging the arm on the identity render delta alone.** 1.05x the floor is
  a p90 over 478 landmarks and hides per-measure agreement. The finding worth
  having is state 0 vs A agreeing to 0.005 cm on every named measure — an
  order of magnitude below the floor.
- **`--timeout` on `ue_exec` / the likeness tools read as an execution
  budget.** It is a DISCOVERY WINDOW and is spent in full. A first attempt at
  `--timeout 180` inside a 120 s shell timeout was killed BEFORE the payload
  was ever sent, and read as "the duplicate failed". CORRECT: 12-25, with the
  shell's own timeout raised instead.

### R-HEROWHOLERIG — DEPTH-2 RESULT AND THE RESTORE THAT FATALS (2026-08-19)

    state                                        floor p90    spread   gate
    0  scratch, parametric canonical              0.0463 cm    1.98    passes
    A  whole-rig, UNEDITED canonical DNA          0.0837 cm    3.82    passes
    B  depth 1, chin -2.00 cm                     0.0559 cm    1.97    passes
    C  depth 2, + jaw +-1.00 cm per side          0.0942 cm    2.85    passes

    edit 1  chin  -2.0000 commanded -> -1.9626 rendered   ratio 0.98
    edit 2  jaw   +2.0000 in the width            -> +1.3959   ratio 0.70

**Depth 2 holds: 1.13x the whole-rig canonical floor, against the fit path's
3.9x and a REFUSAL.** The 0.70 is NOT attributed to depth — `read_dna_meshes`
shows the same jaw mask moving the head's widest vertices only 0.1876 cm for
a 1.0 cm command (558 core vertices inside 3372 weighted), so the mask's
delivered displacement varies by location and the jaw landmark's own weight is
unknown. **The discriminating control is the same jaw edit at DEPTH 1, and it
is UNRUN.**

**DO NOT USE `--restore` ON A WHOLE-RIG-IMPORTED CHARACTER.** Measured
2026-08-19: `reload_packages(..., ASSUME_POSITIVE)` on the scratch seven
seconds after `LogUObjectGlobals: Reloading 1 Package(s)` raised
`EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION reading 0x470` and took the editor with it
(`_verify/20260819_wholerig_restore_crash/`). The same call is proven on the
FIT path. **The undo on this path is a fresh duplicate from the tracked
source**, which is one call and always available.

**A RATIO WITHOUT ITS MASK IS NOT A MEASUREMENT OF THE PATH.** Before reading
any command-vs-rendered number as evidence about the import, read the DNA
bounds: `read_dna_meshes` costs one call and says how much displacement the
mask actually delivered.

### R-HEROWHOLERIG — THE SHAPE LOOP CONVERGED (2026-08-19)

**Five iterations, 1.5382 -> 0.1668 cm, all four fitted regions inside the
0.15 cm deadband.** Chain, boxes, deltas and the final DNA hash:
`_verify/hero_likeness/shape_chain_converged.json`. Run on an expendable
duplicate; the working character was never written.

    iter 1   1.8308 cm   OVERSHOT, worse than canonical
    iter 2   0.7260
    iter 3   0.5245
    iter 4   0.4122
    iter 5   0.1668      chin +0.016  jaw +0.001  cheek +0.098  temple +0.052

#### THE FOUR RULES THE LOOP PAID FOR

1. **REBUILD FROM CANONICAL EVERY ITERATION.** Each iteration re-derives the
   whole command set and re-applies it to the canonical DNA. Whole-rig import
   is EXACT APPLICATION, so the previous edit is replaced rather than added
   to; a mis-estimated ratio then re-aims the move instead of compounding it.
   Iteration 1 overshot to WORSE THAN CANONICAL and cost nothing.

2. **DELIVERY IS DIRECTION- AND AMPLITUDE-DEPENDENT. A SINGLE GAIN PER REGION
   IS NOT ENOUGH.** Measured on `jaw_width`, same mask, four commands:

       +1.000 per side (widening)   1.16 cm of width per side-cm
       -0.729 per side (narrowing)  2.60
       -0.302 per side              3.20
       -0.245 per side              4.53

   A landmark on the SILHOUETTE does not move with the local vertex; the
   visible contour slides across the surface as curvature changes.

3. **THE REGIONS ARE COUPLED — IT IS A JACOBIAN, NOT FOUR GAINS.** Iteration 3
   reduced the jaw NARROWING command and the jaw came out NARROWER, because
   the cheek and temple widening that had been propping that landmark out was
   reduced in the same step. Read a region's response only with its
   neighbours' commands held, or accept iteration.

4. **A MASK MUST REACH THE LANDMARK IT DRIVES, AND ONE HERE DID NOT.** The
   manifest's `temple_width` box (Y 171..177) sits on the CROWN and delivered
   **0.16 cm of width per side-cm** against 446 weighted vertices. Re-aimed to
   Y 163..172 it selects 3194 vertices (2045 core) and delivers **1.03** —
   6.4x — because the temple landmark sits near the eye band, not the crown.
   **Check delivery before believing a gain: a mask that misses reads as a
   region that resists.**

#### WHAT THE CONVERGED METRIC DOES NOT BUY

`brow_height` finishes at **-0.5730 cm**, the largest single residual on the
board, and is UNADDRESSABLE frontally — its landmark sits in the eye band,
which is the ruler. The reference's brow shelf is substantially a SHADOW and
belongs to presentation lighting, not to the mesh.

**The metric converging is not the likeness converging.** Widths at three
heights plus a chin drop cannot express age, brow shelf, skin or iris. The
rendered face at 0.1668 cm is coherent, seam-free and still smooth, young and
round-ish against a weathered 40s reference.

## R-HEROBODY — THE BODY, MEASURED (2026-08-19)

**Status: DIAGNOSED AND CORRECTED.** The hero read androgynous in his first
landscape render; the cause was not a broken parameter but a value that was
never applied. Instrument: `scripts/hero_body/body_silhouette.py`. Narrative
in LESSONS 2026-08-19 (day).

### THE INSTRUMENT

    ortho camera, LOCKED       260 cm across 1024 px = 0.253906 cm/px
    silhouette                 subject frame MINUS subject-hidden plate
    heights                    anchored to BONE world-Z, not to fractions
    widths                     longest contiguous run in the row
    settle gate                shots until two consecutive agree (0.30 cm)

**ORTHOGRAPHIC IS THE WHOLE DESIGN.** A perspective camera makes a width a
function of distance, so "wider" and "nearer" become the same measurement.
With `projection_type` ORTHOGRAPHIC and a locked `ortho_width`, cm-per-pixel
is a constant of the camera and the subject cannot move the ruler.

### THE FINDING, AND IT IS A VALUE NOT A MECHANISM

    character                Masculine/Feminine   Across Shoulder   Chest
    MHC_AlpineHero                  -1.0              39.5212      110.0420
    MHC_AlpineHero_Master           -1.0              39.5212      110.0420
    MHC_AlpineHero_Scratch          -1.0              39.5212      110.0420
    MHC_AlpineHero_Scratch2         -1.0              39.5212      110.0420

**All four sat at -1.0, including the master, which predates every edit of
2026-08-18/19. The -2.0 recorded on 2026-08-16 was never applied** — which
matches that session's own note that a +-2.0 swing produced byte-identical
bounds INCLUDING the baseline. The write never landed; the value never moved;
the record recorded the intent.

    Masc/Fem  +2.0   shoulder 19.55   chest 30.98   hip 34.79   s/h 0.562

and the model's OWN derived measurements move with it (`Across Shoulder`
39.52 -> 44.21 at -2.0; 32.93 at +2.0), which is a second representation
rather than a louder version of the first.

**APPLIED to the working character 2026-08-19:** `Masculine/Feminine` -1.0 ->

#### THE IDENTITY ARM, RE-SPECIFIED — and why the old form could not pass

The arm as written asserts *the render is unchanged across the import*. On a
body-modified character that is **false by mechanism**: the parametric render
carries body-authored face state, and an exact DNA application legitimately
discards it. Measured 2026-08-19 on the working character at body -2.0:

    pre-import (parametric)   jaw 14.5891  cheek 17.2261  ipd 444.75
    post-import (canonical)   jaw 12.4971  cheek 15.5538  ipd 427.41
    -> 11.18x floor, REFUSED

**A gate that can never pass on a class of input is not guarding that class,
it is blind to it.** What whole-rig import actually guarantees is
DNA-DETERMINISM, so the gate is now:

    PRIMARY    import twice, compare: must sit inside the floor
               MEASURED 0.72x floor (0.0319 cm)  PASS
    SECONDARY  post-import measures match the whole-rig-canonical table
               at the SAME body setting
    ADVISORY   pre-vs-post delta, RECORDED not gated — it measures
               body-authored face adaptation, which is a finding

#### THE BODY DRIVES THE PARAMETRIC FACE — AND NOT THE IMPORTED ONE

Single variable, one duplicate, no whole-rig import:

    Masc/Fem  -1.0   jaw 14.1204  cheek 16.7217  temple 16.7403  ipd 435.17
    Masc/Fem  -2.0   jaw 14.5886  cheek 17.1877  temple 17.1840  ipd 443.68
                     +0.468       +0.466         +0.444          +2.0%

+0.47 cm at the jaw is **10.6x the noise floor**. The mechanism is named in the
API: `fit_face_state_from_body_with_eyes_teeth_dna` — the body FITS the face
state.

**But after a whole-rig import the face is BODY-INDEPENDENT**, which is what
makes the locked likeness safe:

    whole-rig canonical   scratch body -1.0   working body -2.0   delta
      jaw_width               12.5150            12.4971         -0.018
      cheek_width             15.5021            15.5538         +0.052
      temple_width            15.6807            15.7025         +0.022
      chin_height            -13.3199           -13.2710         +0.049

**So body work before the lock changes the face; body work after the lock does
not.** Set the body first — which is the order the operator ruled for other
reasons.

  FIT, so exporting routes a fit product into the anchor. Fitters are verifiers,
  not authors. It also destroys the arm permanently — a canonical exported from
  state X identity-passes at state X by construction.
- **`duplicate_asset` COPIES THE LOADED OBJECT, NOT THE FILE.** Scratch2 was
  duplicated from Scratch while Scratch held an IN-MEMORY jaw edit, so its
  "canonical" baseline read jaw 13.6027 against the true 12.5138 — the edit,
  carried invisibly into a new asset. It cost nothing here because every shape
  iteration rebuilds from the canonical DNA and the final state was measured
  against the reference directly, but it made iteration 1 overshoot and it put
  a wrong number into an advisor packet. **Duplicate from a SAVED state, or
  measure the duplicate before trusting it as a baseline.**
- **`fit.fixed_ipd_px` 429.027 was calibrated at body -1.0.** A parametric face
  at body -2.0 renders IPD ~444, a 3.7% disagreement worth ~0.5 cm on a
  jaw-width. `measure_state` and this recipe's tables use the CAMERA constant
  (0.017454 cm/px) for renders and `fixed_ipd_px` only for the reference photo,
  which is correct; `fit_face.py` still uses `fixed_ipd_px` for render measures
  and would be wrong on a parametric body-modified character. Harmless on the
  LOCKED character (which renders 427), and it is a live trap for any future
  parametric work.


### R-HEROWHOLERIG — THE LOCKED HERO IN THE WORLD, AND A GATE THAT WATCHED THE WRONG THING (2026-08-19)

    _verify/20260819_hero_in_world/hero_wide_20260819T141324Z_b.png
    hero_portrait_..._b.png   hero_env_..._b.png

Assembled from the LOCKED working character (OPTIMIZED/HIGH, 83 packages
saved), spawned in Alpine8K at (354600, -321400), ground-clamped by trace to
z 31019.47 with 256 proxies resident, facing camera. The body correction is
visible: broad shoulders and pectoral definition where the same shot at
`Masculine/Feminine` -1.0 read androgynous.

#### THE PRESENCE GATE PASSED AND THE PIXELS DISAGREE

Ruling 4 promoted presence to a HARD GATE on landscape renders. It was
implemented as: every required groom component exists, carries a groom asset
AND a binding asset, and reads `visible`. On this render it returned

    Beard     Beard_M_Stubble      Beard_M_Stubble_Binding      visible
    Mustache  Mustache_M_Stubble   Mustache_M_Stubble_Binding   visible
    Eyebrows  Eyebrows_M_Dense     Eyebrows_M_Dense_Binding     visible
    -> presence_missing []   ships_as DELIVERABLE

**and the close portrait shows no beard, no moustache and no brows on the lit
half of the face.** The bindings are the durable assembled ones, not the
transient `GroomBindingAsset_NN` — so this is not the stale-binding case.

**THE GATE IS THE FAILURE, NOT THE RENDER.** It asserts COMPONENT STATE and
calls the result presence, which is the same shape as the defect the presence
manifest was written to stop: *settling cannot see absence* became *a
checklist cannot see absence either* when the checklist reads properties
instead of pixels. A component can be present, bound, visible and drawing
nothing — B-HAIRGROOM has said exactly that about Hair for two days, and the
gate as written would have shipped Hair as present too.

**CORRECT FORM, and it is the same trick the body ruler already uses:** render
the frame TWICE, once with the required grooms hidden, and require the
difference to be non-empty in the region each groom occupies. A groom that
draws nothing produces an identical frame, and identical frames are the one
thing a difference mask cannot miss. Until that exists, **a landscape render
ships as a DIAGNOSTIC with respect to grooms**, whatever the component state
says.

**~~NOT YET DIAGNOSED:~~ ANSWERED 2026-08-19 (night) — SEE R-HEROGROOM BELOW.**
whether the beard fails to draw for B-HAIRGROOM's
reason, or is simply sub-pixel stubble at 2.1 m with the jaw in shadow. Those
predict different things under the difference test above, which is why the
test comes before the theory.

**The test was built and run, and the answer is BOTH, in a way neither branch
anticipated.** The beard IS sub-resolution at 2.1 m — measured 1.8-3.1x the
repeat floor there against 10.6x at 0.9 m — so that branch is correct. And
B-HAIRGROOM's own cause turned out to be the same class of measurement error
rather than an asset defect: **grooms converge over frames after their assets
first load in an editor session, and every bald render was taken too early.**
`Hair_M_Layered` renders at 83x the floor, untouched.

**The standing ruling above — "a landscape render ships as a DIAGNOSTIC with
respect to grooms" — SURVIVES, and is now measured rather than precautionary.**
At the 6.2 m landscape framing the ENTIRE FACE is 10,120 px and all four grooms
sit at 1.8-2.5x floor. It is DIAGNOSTIC because the pixels cannot carry the
claim, which is a fact about the camera, not about the character. The gate that
enforces it is `groom_presence.py`; the framing table is in R-HEROGROOM.

## R-HEROGROOM — PROVING A GROOM IS IN THE PICTURE (2026-08-19)

**Status: PROVEN** — exercised in four directions in one session (refuses a
converging subject, passes a converged one, reports ABSENT for a genuinely
sub-resolution groom, refuses when its own control cannot clear the floor).
Informed by `LESSONS.md` 2026-08-19 (night). Supersedes the component-state
presence check described in R-HEROWHOLERIG and in `manifest.json`, which
returned DELIVERABLE on a portrait containing no visible grooms.

### THE ONE-LINE RULE

**A groom is present when hiding it CHANGES THE PICTURE. Nothing else counts —
not the asset, not the binding, not `visible`, not a log line.**

### THE PROCEDURE

    1  place_hero_in_world.py  --dist <cm> --fov <deg> --cam-up --look-up
    2  groom_presence.py       (same framing, no arguments about the subject)
    3  if exit 0            -> shoot with world_shot.py, THIS framing
       if exit 7            -> re-run step 2; the grooms are still converging
       if exit 6            -> a required groom is genuinely not in the picture
                               at this framing. Move the camera or fix the groom;
                               do NOT ship it as a deliverable.

**Step 2 is not optional and must be re-run whenever the FRAMING changes.** A
verdict belongs to the framing it was measured at.

### EXACT VALUES THAT WORK

    subject          BP at /Game/Hero/Unpacked/MHC_AlpineHero/BP_MHC_AlpineHero
    spawn            X 354600.0  Y -321400.0, ground by line trace -> z 31019.47
    yaw offset       -90.0   (the Blueprint's forward axis is NOT +X)
    gated portrait   --dist 90 --fov 24 --cam-up 155 --look-up 155, 2048 sq
    delta threshold  8 of 255 per channel
    bar              max(3 x repeat floor, 200 px)
    tolerance        0.30 between the two passes
    r.AntiAliasingMethod  0 for the gate, RESTORED afterwards (was 4)

    converged signal, 0.9 m, against a repeat floor of ~1,100-1,700 px
        Hair       96,147 - 97,338 px     83x floor
        Eyebrows   18,635 - 19,590 px     16x
        Beard      12,357 - 13,409 px     10.6x
        Mustache    3,809 -  4,553 px      3.3x     <- the limiting groom
        control (face mesh hidden)     ~1,471,000 px   1,266x

## R-HEROGROOM REJECTED

- **A PRESENCE GATE THAT READS COMPONENT PROPERTIES.** `groom_asset` set,
  `binding_asset` set, `visible` true — all three read correctly on a portrait
  with no beard, no moustache and no brows in it, and the run was stamped
  `ships_as DELIVERABLE`. **Symptom:** a bald render that every check passes.
  **Correct:** hide the groom and require the picture to change.
- **ONE PASS.** A single measurement on a freshly loaded editor manufactures
  false ABSENCES: measured 3,564 px for Eyebrows on the first pass and 19,205 px
  on the next with nothing changed. **Symptom:** a groom reported missing that
  is merely unfinished, and — because the reading is confident and repeatable
  within that pass — two days spent looking for an asset defect that does not
  exist. **Correct:** two passes, refuse on >30% drift.
- **COUNTING CHANGED PIXELS OVER THE WHOLE FRAME.** Two captures of an
  unchanged subject differ over 11.3% of this frame because the FOREST does not
  re-render identically. **Symptom:** the gate refuses everything, including a
  hidden face mesh, and looks broken. **Correct:** build a stability map from
  three unchanged-state frames and measure only where the frame reproduces —
  floor 472,199 px -> 1,119 px on the same scene.
- **BLAMING TEMPORAL AA FOR THAT FLOOR.** `r.AntiAliasingMethod 4 -> 0` moved it
  11.3% -> 10.5%. It is kept (an instrument should not be a function of the
  frames before it) but it is **not** the cause, and reaching for it first cost
  a cycle. **Correct:** look at the difference MAP before theorising about its
  mean.
- **A DIFFERENTIAL WHOSE ARMS DIFFER IN TIME AS WELL AS IN THE VARIABLE.**
  Pointing the editor viewport at the character produced a fully groomed render
  where pointing it away produced a bald one — and the arms were taken in
  sequence, so elapsed warm-up moved with the variable. **Symptom:** a
  spectacular, reproducible-looking image that confirms the wrong mechanism.
  **Correct:** the reversal control. Put the variable back and see whether the
  effect comes back; here it did not, and a fresh respawn with the main view
  180 deg away matched the main-view-on numbers to 1.3%.
- **EXPECTING A "FULL" GROOM TO READ FURTHER OUT THAN ITS STUBBLE SIBLING.**
  `Mustache_S_Full` measures 3,731 px at 1.1 m against `Mustache_M_Stubble`'s
  3,703 px — same footprint, same mean delta, same ABSENT verdict. **Symptom:**
  a swap made to fix a read-distance that does not move it, and a caveat
  retired on an assumption. **Correct:** re-measure at the same framing before
  and after, and note that the visible fullness above the lip in the new render
  is `Beard_S_Full` extending onto it, not the moustache.
- **READING A LOW GROOM SIGNAL AS OCCLUSION WITHOUT TESTING IT.** The natural
  explanation for the above is that a dense beard masks the moustache's
  MARGINAL contribution. **Measured and refuted:** hiding the beard first and
  then the moustache gives 3,739 px against bare skin versus 3,696 px against
  beard, a ratio of 1.01. **Correct:** the hide-the-neighbour-first control,
  two extra frames, whenever a groom reads low beside a dense neighbour. The
  gate measures MARGINAL contribution and that limitation is real — it is just
  not what was happening here.
- **VERIFYING GROOM COLOUR FROM THE WRITE, OR FROM THE RENDER.** Twelve writes
  returned true with twelve UNREADABLE read-backs; and a colour sampled over a
  sparse groom's difference mask returns the skin between the strands.
  **Symptom:** either a false pass or a false fail, from an instrument that
  never touched the parameter. **Correct:** read `scalar_parameter_values` off
  the assembled `MI_WI_*` instances, and enumerate the variants rather than
  addressing the one whose name you expect.
- **EDITING A VENDOR GROOM ASSET, or duplicating it to clear
  `enable_global_interpolation`.** The flag correlated with failure across five
  assets and pointed nowhere: the two flagged hairs are also the two heaviest
  grooms, and heavier grooms converge later. `Hair_M_Layered` renders at 83x the
  floor untouched. **Correct:** spend frames, then measure.

## R-GROOMBIND — PUTTING ANY GROOM ON ANY CHARACTER (2026-08-19 overnight #2)

**Status: ~~PROVEN~~ RETRACTED THE SAME NIGHT, ONE HOUR LATER. DO NOT FOLLOW
THE PROCEDURE BELOW.**

The bindings it produces render a **BALD CROWN with a clump of strands hanging
at the jaw** — only strands far from the scalp draw, the roots never attach.
It was locked on GATE NUMBERS that were every one of them true, over a picture
nobody had opened: `Hair PRESENT, 155,153 px, 87.2x floor, drift 0.0%` was the
hanging clump, not a hairstyle. Three grooms reproduce it. The correction and
the rule it bought are in `LESSONS.md` 2026-08-19 (overnight #2), CORRECTION.

    Hair_M_BobMessy + the ASSEMBLE's binding    full hair on the scalp
    Hair_M_BobMessy + a binding from the below  bald crown, clump at the jaw

The two bindings are IDENTICAL in every exposed field — same groom, same
target mesh, `source_skeletal_mesh` null on both, same type, same 100
interpolation points, same matching section.

**ROOT CAUSE, from the engine's own log, after two wrong answers:**

    LogHairStrands: Display: Waiting for groom bindings to be ready 0/1
        (BND_...) ...        <- all EIGHT bindings created tonight

**`create_new_groom_binding_asset_with_path` creates the asset and its BUILD
NEVER COMPLETES.** 0 of 1 ready, no later line, no error; held four minutes
and re-rendered identical. The strands that draw are the free-hanging ends,
which need no root attachment — hence a bald crown with a clump at the jaw.
Whether the build can be FORCED is UNKNOWN and is the first question for a
future session.

**GREP `LogHairStrands` AFTER EVERY BINDING CREATION**, and confirm which log
file is live first: `LandscapeLab.log` goes stale at each editor restart while
the running session writes `LandscapeLab_2.log`. Reading silence out of the
stale file is what let the wrong root cause reach this document.

**WHAT STILL HOLDS** (each measured in both directions, and kept because the
next attempt needs them): vendor-content grooms do not bind at all — bald with
no clump; vendor bindings render EXPLODED on our head; nothing reasserts over
a direct component write, proven by a property read 150,000 frames later.

**THE ROUTE THAT WORKS REMAINS WARDROBE SELECT -> ASSEMBLE.**

Kept in full, struck rather than deleted, because it is a complete and
plausible-looking procedure that a fresh session would otherwise re-derive and
re-trust — and because its REJECTED section is still correct.

**Status (historical): PROVEN** — five bindings, three renders above 42x the
repeat floor, two proven failures in the other direction. Narrative in `LESSONS.md`
2026-08-19 (overnight #2). This is the party-character groom path; the hero is
invocation #1, not the design.

### THE ONE-LINE RULE

**A groom must live in PROJECT content to be bindable, and every groom reaches
a character through a binding freshly built against THAT character's own face
mesh.** No exceptions, party-wide.

### THE PROCEDURE

    1  duplicate the groom into project content
           EditorAssetLibrary.duplicate_asset(vendor_path, /Game/Characters/
               <Name>/Grooms/<Char>_<Style>_vN)
       (an Alembic-imported groom is already project content; skip)
    2  read the TARGET FACE MESH off the placed actor, never by name
           the Face SkeletalMeshComponent's `skeletal_mesh`
    3  GroomLibrary.create_new_groom_binding_asset_with_path(
           bind_path, groom, face_mesh, 100, None, 0)
    4  component.set_groom_asset(groom); component.set_binding_asset(binding)
    5  release the game thread, let it converge, then gate on pixels

### EXACT VALUES THAT WORK

    num_interpolation_points        100      (matches the assembled bindings)
    source_skeletal_mesh_for_transfer  None  (the WORKING assembled binding
                                              has this null; see REJECTED)
    matching_section                0
    target mesh   /Game/Hero/Unpacked/MHC_AlpineHero/Face/
                      SKM_MHC_AlpineHero_FaceMesh
    bind cost     0.29 s at 7 MB, 3.43 s at 27 MB, 8.55 s at 100 MB
                  -- scales with ASSET SIZE, not curve count

    measured renders, 1.1 m framing, stability-masked
        Hair_M_BobMessy      unpacked    126,709 px   72.7x floor
        Hair_S_Messy         unpacked     73,970 px   42.2x
        Hair_BobMessy_Custom duplicate   155,153 px   87.2x

### VERIFICATION

`groom_presence.py` at the framing the result will be judged at. A binding
that assigns and does not draw reports PERFECTLY on every property, so the
only instrument that can tell the two apart is pixels.

## R-GROOMBIND REJECTED

- **BINDING A GROOM THAT LIVES IN THE VENDOR PLUGIN'S CONTENT.**
  `/MetaHumanCharacter/Optional/Grooms/GroomAssets/...` **Symptom:** the
  binding builds in under a second, `does_asset_exist` is true, the component
  read-back names the right groom AND the right binding, and the head is BALD
  at 60 s and still bald at 90 s. Assigning it also stops the OTHER grooms on
  the actor drawing, which reads as a wedged actor and is not — restoring an
  assembled binding recovers everything instantly. **Correct:** duplicate into
  project content first.
- **REACHING FOR `source_skeletal_mesh_for_transfer` TO FIX IT.** Vendor
  grooms are authored against `SKM_Groom_Head_Legacy01/02` and the vendor
  bindings record source == target == Legacy01, so passing the authoring head
  looks exactly right. It changes nothing, and the field-by-field diff shows
  the WORKING assembled binding has `source_skeletal_mesh` **null**.
  **Correct:** None, and if a render is bald the question is where the groom
  ASSET lives.
- **USING A VENDOR BINDING ON A PROJECT CHARACTER.** `Hair_X_Binding` under
  `/MetaHumanCharacter/.../Bindings/` targets `SKM_Groom_Head_Legacy01`, not
  your face mesh. **Symptom:** strands render EXPLODED across the face rather
  than absent — a different and more honest failure than the bald one.
- **CONCLUDING "WARDROBE ONLY" FROM A BALD DIRECT WRITE.** The property read
  after a wait separates reassertion from render failure in twelve seconds and
  costs nothing; the write is durable at 150,000 frames. Reading Blueprint
  construction logic first would have been an hour spent on a refuted premise.

## R-GROOMBIND2 — HOW A GROOM BINDING IS ACTUALLY BUILT (2026-08-20)

**Status: MECHANISM PROVEN FROM SOURCE, EXECUTION BLOCKED.** The recipe below
is what the MetaHuman assemble does, read out of the engine. It is not yet
runnable from remote Python: its final call fatals the editor. Supersedes the
struck R-GROOMBIND. Narrative: `LESSONS.md` 2026-08-20.

### THE RECIPE, from MetaHumanGroomEditorPipeline.cpp

    CharacterBinding = DuplicateObject(VendorBinding)   # ALREADY BUILT
    CharacterBinding.SetTargetSkeletalMesh(TargetFace)
    NewGroom = DuplicateObject(VendorBinding.GetGroom())
    FGroomRBFDeformer().GetRBFDeformedGroomAsset(...)   # NOT reflected
    CharacterBinding.SetGroom(NewGroom)
    CharacterBinding.SetSourceSkeletalMesh(None)
    CharacterBinding.Build()                            # <- fatals from Python

**THE HEADLINE: A BINDING IS NEVER CREATED FROM SCRATCH. It is a duplicate of
an already-built binding, retargeted and rebuilt.**

### WHAT IS REFLECTED, AND WHAT IS NOT

    reflected      groom, source_skeletal_mesh, target_skeletal_mesh,
                   num_interpolation_points, matching_section, group_infos,
                   build(completion_delegate)
    NOT reflected  FGroomRBFDeformer (plain C++), FGroomBindingCompilingManager

### THE ASYNC-COMPILATION CONTROLS, which DO work and are NOT the fix

    Editor.AsyncGroomBindingCompilation            0 = synchronous
    Editor.AsyncGroomBindingCompilationFinishAll   blocks until all done
    Editor.AsyncGroomBindingCompilationMaxConcurrency
    Editor.AsyncGroomBindingCompilationResume

Useful to know and worth nothing here: with async off there is no "Waiting for
groom bindings to be ready" line and the render is still SCALP-BALD.

## R-GROOMBIND2 REJECTED

- **`create_new_groom_binding_asset_with_path` FOR PUTTING A GROOM ON A
  CHARACTER.** It is not the call the pipeline uses. **Symptom:** binding
  builds in under 9 s, saves, validates, every property reads back correct,
  and the render is a BALD CROWN with a clump of strands hanging at the jaw —
  `crown 1%` against a working binding's `crown 66-81%`, while the broken one
  has the LARGER pixel count. **Correct:** duplicate an already-built binding
  and retarget it.
- **`GroomBindingAsset.build()` FROM REMOTE PYTHON.** **Symptom:**
  `Assertion failed: IsUnlocked() [BulkData.cpp:596]`, editor gone, connection
  reset mid-payload. Third MetaHuman/groom entry point to fatal this way after
  `request_auto_rigging(blocking=True)` and `conform_to_target_meshes` — it is
  the TRANSPORT, not the API. **Correct:** a `UFUNCTION` in
  `LandscapeLabEditor`, or an attended editor action.
- **RETARGETING WITHOUT REBUILDING.** Duplicate, `SetTargetSkeletalMesh`,
  `SetSourceSkeletalMesh(None)`, save, assign, skip `Build()`. **Symptom:**
  `SCALP-BALD, crown 1%`, reproduced at drift 0.2%. The `Build()` is
  load-bearing.
- **DISABLING ASYNC COMPILATION AS A FIX.** It genuinely makes the build
  synchronous and genuinely removes the waiting message. It does not change
  the render, because the wrong call was being made either way.

## R-GROOMBIND3 — PUTTING ANY GROOM ON ANY CHARACTER, WORKING (2026-08-20)

**Status: PROVEN BY RENDER.** Supersedes the struck R-GROOMBIND and completes
R-GROOMBIND2. Narrative: `LESSONS.md` 2026-08-20.

    Hair  215,647 px  139.7x floor  crown 35%  drift 0.4%   PRESENT
    before, every other approach:    crown  1%              SCALP-BALD

Evidence: `_verify/20260820_bindfix/before_after_rbf.png`.

### THE CALL

    unreal.LandscapeLabTools.build_groom_binding_for_mesh(
        source_binding,     # an ALREADY-BUILT binding (the vendor one)
        target_mesh,        # the character's face mesh, READ off the actor
        dest_binding_path,  # /Game/Characters/<Name>/Grooms/Bindings/BND_...
        dest_groom_path)    # /Game/Characters/<Name>/Grooms/<Char>_<Style>_vN
    -> (out_binding_path, out_groom_path, b_out_success, out_error)

**ASSIGN BOTH RETURNED ASSETS.** The deformation lives in the GROOM, not only
in the binding; assigning the vendor groom with the new binding is half the
fix and renders like a total failure.

Cost: **~15 s per groom**, no assemble, no editor restart.

### THE FOUR STEPS, ALL LOAD-BEARING

Each was measured by leaving it out:

    1  DUPLICATE an already-built binding      omit -> crown 1%, bald
    2  SetTargetSkeletalMesh + Build()         omit -> crown 1%, bald
    3  RBF-bake into a DUPLICATED groom        omit -> crown 1%, bald
    4  STRIP DECIMATION around the bake,       omit -> 3,353 px, crown 43%
       then restore it                                 (right place, no hair)

Step 4 looks like housekeeping and is not. The engine's comment:
*"The RBF deformer doesn't support decimation in the interpolation data."*

### WHY IT IS C++ AND NOT PYTHON

`GroomBindingAsset.build()` is reflected and FATALS the editor from remote
Python (`Assertion failed: IsUnlocked() [BulkData.cpp:596]`).
`FGroomRBFDeformer` is not reflected at all. Both are fine on the game thread
inside `LandscapeLabEditor`.

## R-GROOMBIND3 REJECTED

- **`create_new_groom_binding_asset_with_path`.** Wrong function for this job,
  full stop. **Symptom:** bald crown, clump at the jaw, `crown 1%` with a
  LARGER pixel count than the correct render.
- **THE RBF BAKE WITHOUT THE DECIMATION STRIP.** **Symptom:** 3,353 px at
  `crown 43%` — hair in the right place and almost none of it. Distinctive,
  and the only failure mode of the four that points at its own cause.
- **ASSIGNING THE VENDOR GROOM WITH THE NEW BINDING.** The deformation is
  baked into the groom copy. **Symptom:** looks exactly like the binding not
  working.
- **RELAUNCHING THE EDITOR WITHOUT MOVING `PackageRestoreData.json` ASIDE.**
  Cost ten minutes here: the editor sat at 2.86 GB with flat CPU and a Restore
  modal blocking the game thread, which is the only channel that could have
  reported it. It is in the handoff procedure for this reason; it is not
  optional when cycling the editor repeatedly.
- **SAVING ANYTHING AFTER A BIND, OR LETTING THE EDITOR SAVE ON QUIT.**
  The bind DIRTIES VENDOR CONTENT. Measured 2026-08-20 after a catalogue run:
  `get_dirty_content_packages()` returns **48 packages and all 48 are under
  `/MetaHumanCharacter/Optional`** — the source groom's own
  `<Style>_CardsMesh_Group0_LOD*` and `<Style>_Helmet_LOD*` static meshes.
  `DuplicateObject` does not deep-copy them, so the duplicate references the
  vendor's and the cards `PostEditChangeProperty` rebuilds them in place.
  **The symptom you will NOT see is any symptom at all.** The renders are
  correct and the gate passes; the damage exists only if something writes.
  Those packages live in Program Files, **outside both roots**, so a
  `Save All` or a save-on-quit breaks the never-edit-vendor-content floor AND
  standing rule 1 in one action.
  **Correct posture: DISCARD on every close.** A force-kill writes nothing and
  is the right answer here — which inverts the usual preference for a clean
  shutdown, and is worth stating because a clean shutdown is the habit.
  **Verified clean on disk, and the check that settles it is the mtime
  HISTOGRAM, not a `-newermt` cutoff:** all 1,387 vendor groom uassets carry a
  single date, 2026-08-15, the install date. `find -newermt 2026-08-01`
  returns every one of them and reads like a catastrophe; one date across
  1,387 files is the actual evidence.
- **CORRECTED IN PLACE, AND IT WAS MY OWN COMMENT.** The C++ read *"the cards
  and mesh descriptions are duplicated by the pipeline too, so the deformed
  groom does not share static meshes with the vendor asset."* Measured FALSE
  by the dirty list above. The comment now carries the measurement and the
  consequence. Non-negotiable 25 — and this one was load-bearing for a safety
  floor, which is the worst place for a comforting claim nobody re-checks.
- **`Hair_M_TwistedBraids` AND `Hair_S_BrushCut` ARE NOT REACHABLE BY THIS
  RECIPE, AND IT IS NOT A BUG.** The vendor pack ships **38 groom assets and
  36 bindings**; those two styles have a groom and no `<name>_Binding`
  sibling. R-GROOMBIND3 duplicates an ALREADY-BUILT binding, so a style with
  none has no input to duplicate. **Symptom:** `no vendor binding at
  /MetaHumanCharacter/Optional/Grooms/Bindings/Hair/<name>_Binding`.
  Recorded in the catalogue index as `NO VENDOR BINDING` with the count that
  proves it, not as a failure — an absence of input is not a failed bind.
  **The names came from convention and the disk disagreed**, which is the
  names-come-from-the-asset rule arriving a fourth time.
