## R-HAIRVOLUME — GIVING AN AUTHORED GROOM BODY WITHOUT STRIPPING THE SCALP (2026-08-21)

**Status: MEASURED IN BLENDER, RENDERED IN UE.** Informed by `LESSONS.md`
2026-08-21 ("VOLUME: the number rose 23% and the render did not change").

### THE MECHANISM

Volume is a clearance that GROWS along the strand, applied by the BVH drape in
`scripts/blender/author_hero_hair.py`:

    pos = drape(pos, drape_clearance + volume_cm * t * t)

`t` is 0 at the root and 1 at the tip. **The ramp is QUADRATIC and that is not
cosmetic.** A linear ramp holds the middle of every strand ~0.8 cm off the skin,
and on a convex skull pushing a point out along the surface normal spreads
neighbouring points apart as r², so the coverage cost is paid over the whole
strand instead of only at the tips.

### THE LOCKED VALUES, and what each one is worth

    hairline_frac      0.82        front hairline, fraction of head height
    len_top_cm         9.5
    lift_cm            2.50        strand stands off the scalp this far before
                                   gravity dominates -- the main volume lever
    back_bias          1.00
    front_sweep_gain   2.00
    out_bias           0.15        RAMPED, not signed -- see REJECTED
    volume_cm          1.60        layer thickness at the tips
    drape_clearance    0.20
    strands            48,000

### THE ACCEPTANCE NUMBERS — `scripts/blender/preview_hair.py`, ~40 s

               exposed%   midline%   front_px   height gain
    before        9.43       9.75      40,691       1.76 cm
    after         8.11       4.46      63,026       2.91 cm

- `scalp_exposed_pct` — % of scalp samples with no hair point within 8 mm.
  **Scalp is defined by the ROOTS** (a head vertex within 1.5 cm of one), never
  by a second copy of the hairline rule.
- `scalp_exposed_by_zone` — the same figure split at |x| < 3 cm. A parting and a
  thin nape are the same aggregate and different defects.
- `silhouette.<view>.hair_px` — difference render against the head alone
  through the same camera. This is the metric that matches the eye.
- `silhouette.front.height_gain_cm` — how much taller the hair made him.

**Any styling change is measured here BEFORE a UE round trip.** Blender: ~40 s.
UE round trip: ~4 minutes plus an editor.

### SWEEPING

Every `PARAMS` key is overridable for one run with `HAIR_<KEY>` in the
environment, and the effective values are written into the sidecar, so a render
traces to its numbers. Do not edit `PARAMS` to run a trial.

---

## R-HAIRVOLUME REJECTED

- **`shell_thickness` AS THE VOLUME GATE.** Wrong value: treating BVH
  nearest-surface distance as proof that volume landed. **Symptom:** tip shell
  2.627 → 3.235 cm (+23%) and a UE render indistinguishable from the one
  before it. **Why:** standoff is how far the layer sits OFF the skull and says
  nothing about whether the layer is THERE; measured, that +23% cost
  20.55 → 32.12% scalp exposure. **Correct:** gate on `scalp_exposed_pct` and
  the silhouette difference, and keep shell thickness as a descriptive number.

- **A LINEAR VOLUME RAMP.** Wrong value: `volume_cm * t`. **Symptom:** the mass
  leaves the head everywhere at once and the render reads *thinner*, not
  fuller. **Correct:** `volume_cm * t * t`, so the strand lies on the head
  through its first half.

- **`side = sign(root.x - mid)` FOR THE OUTWARD BIAS.** **Symptom:** a bald
  stripe down the centre of the crown in the front view; measured 29.21%
  exposure within 1.5 cm of the midline against 8.64% laterally. **Why:** a
  step function throws two strands born a millimetre apart a full bias-width in
  opposite directions. **Correct:** a ramp reaching ±1 at 35% of the head
  half-width, so a strand on the centre line has no outward push.

- **`out_bias` 0.85.** **Symptom:** two wings standing off the temples at
  eyebrow height, plus the midline parting above. **Correct:** 0.15. Body comes
  from the radial drape clearance, not from a lateral push.

- **TWO DEFINITIONS OF "FRONT-OF-HEAD" IN ONE FILE.** Wrong value: the hairline
  using `max((facing+1)/2, |n.x|)` while the sweep used `(facing+1)/2`.
  **Symptom:** strands hanging at the brow that no sweep setting removes —
  `front_sweep_gain` 1.2 → 2.4 moved the crossing figure 3.10 → 3.06%.
  **Why:** a TEMPLE is at the front of the head with a sideways normal; the
  hairline knew that and the sweep did not, so temple roots got half the
  backward drive. **Correct:** one expression, used by both.

- **SCALP DEFINED BY SURFACE NORMAL** ("above the nape and not strongly
  face-facing"). **Symptom:** 28.43 / 28.67 / 28.28 / 29.39% across a SIX-FOLD
  change in `back_bias` — a number that will not move. **Why:** cheeks,
  temples, ears and the back of the neck have lateral normals and are supposed
  to be bare, so they dominated the sample. **Correct:** scalp is where the
  roots are.

- **`tips_in_face_box`, THEN `strands_crossing_face_box`, AS THE OVER-THE-EYES
  GATE.** **Symptoms:** the first read 0.18 → 0.00% across five iterations that
  changed nothing in the render; the second read 3.08% through a 23% cut to
  side length AND a doubling of the sweep. **Why:** a tip census cannot see
  strands that cross with their middles; a nearest-surface-normal test cannot
  see strands hanging in the AIR beside the temple, because the nearest skin
  there is cheek and a cheek normal points sideways. **Correct for the front
  view:** count hair pixels landing inside the bare head's own silhouette in
  the eye rows — no normals involved.

- **READING `scalp_exposed_by_zone` AT |x| < 1.5 cm.** **Symptom:** 5.62 /
  12.36 / 14.44% across rising strand count — non-monotonic. **Why:** n = 178,
  so those are 10 vs 26 samples. **Correct:** |x| < 3 cm, n ≈ 2080, stable.
  State the denominator before quoting the percentage.

- **`fresh_bind_payload.txt` PASSING FOUR ARGUMENTS.** **Symptom:**
  `TypeError: build_fresh_groom_binding() required argument 'dest_groom_path'
  (pos 5) not found`, after 180 s of discovery window. **Why:** the C++
  (`LandscapeLabTools.h:639-650`) gained `DestGroomPath`/`OutGroomPath` and the
  committed payload was never updated; it also unpacked three outs where there
  are four. **Correct:** five in, four out
  `(OutBindingPath, OutGroomPath, bOutSuccess, OutError)`, and **assign the
  returned GROOM COPY**, not the original — R-GROOMBIND3's own headline.

### KNOWN OPEN, NOT FIXED BY THIS RECIPE

- Hair still hangs at the brow and temples: `hair_over_face_px` ≈ 17,400 in the
  front preview. A hide-the-hair control proves it is the groom and not the
  face mesh's eyelash geometry.
- Hair colour is vendor default. The authoring path clears
  `override_materials`; the ruled values are melanin 0.92 / redness 0.28 /
  whiteness 0.00.

## R-GROOMBIND4 — A FRESH BINDING FOR A GROOM AUTHORED ON ITS OWN TARGET (2026-08-21)

**Status: MECHANISM CORRECTED AFTER AN EDITOR FATAL.** Narrative in
`LESSONS.md` 2026-08-21 ("THE RBF BAKE KILLED THE EDITOR").

For a groom authored in Blender directly on the character's own exported face
mesh — not a vendor groom being retargeted — the binding is built fresh rather
than duplicated from a vendor one:

    unreal.LandscapeLabTools.build_fresh_groom_binding(
        groom, source_mesh_or_None, target_mesh,
        dest_package_path, dest_groom_path)
      -> (out_binding_path, out_groom_path, b_success, out_error)

**FIVE ARGUMENTS IN, FOUR OUT.** `LandscapeLabTools.h:639-650`.

**PASS `source_mesh = None` WHEN THE GROOM WAS AUTHORED ON THE TARGET.** Source
then defaults to target and the binding is an identity. This is a claim about
the groom, so it is passed explicitly and recorded in the output rather than
defaulted silently.

**ASSIGN THE RETURNED GROOM COPY, NOT THE ORIGINAL** — `out_groom_path`, not
the asset you passed in. R-GROOMBIND3's headline, and it applies here too.

**THE RBF BAKE RUNS ONLY WHEN SOURCE != TARGET**, and the module logs which
branch it took:

    LogLandscapeLab: BuildFreshGroomBinding: RBF bake SKIPPED (source IS the target).

---

## R-GROOMBIND4 REJECTED

- **CALLING `FGroomRBFDeformer::GetRBFDeformedGroomAsset` ON AN IDENTITY
  BINDING.** **Symptom:** the editor dies with
  `Assertion failed: RootDatas[GroupIndex].MeshPositions.IsValidIndex(MeshLODIndex)`
  at `GroomRBFDeformer.cpp:740`, on a 50,400-curve groom, after ~4 minutes of
  apparently healthy work at ~5 CPU-s per wall-s with no log growth.
  **Why:** the deformer computes `RootDatas` itself (`:670-683`) and `check()`s
  that mesh LOD 0 is present; an engine `check()` is a hard crash, not a
  refusal. **And the step is a no-op for this input** — an RBF deformation
  transfers strands from the authoring mesh to the target mesh, and here they
  are the same mesh. **Correct:** guard on `EffectiveSource != TargetMesh`.

- **CARRYING THE THREE-BINDING MEASUREMENT INTO THIS CASE.** Wrong reasoning:
  "three bindings produced the same picture, therefore the binding alone does
  not move strands, therefore always bake." **Why it does not apply:** that was
  measured on a groom authored on a DIFFERENT mesh. It shows the bake moves a
  TRANSFERRED groom; it says nothing about a groom already in the right place.
  A measurement's scope is part of the measurement.

- **`fresh_bind_payload.txt` PASSING FOUR ARGUMENTS AND UNPACKING THREE OUTS.**
  **Symptom:** `TypeError: build_fresh_groom_binding() required argument
  'dest_groom_path' (pos 5) not found`, one full remote window per attempt.
  **Why:** the UFUNCTION gained two parameters and the payload was never
  updated; nothing checks a payload against its UFUNCTION until it runs.
  **Correct:** five in, four out, and re-run the payload after ANY change to a
  signature it calls.

- **TRUSTING A COMMENT IN OUR OWN CODE.** The function opened with *"NO RBF
  BAKE HERE, DELIBERATELY"* forty lines above a block that bakes and whose own
  heading says it overturns that plan. The payload header repeated the false
  half into a second file. **Correct:** the stale comment is struck in place
  with the date, and the live rule sits at the code it governs.

### THE PROCEDURE AROUND A GROOM FATAL

1. The imported `GroomAsset` is saved before the bind, so a bind crash costs
   the binding and not the groom — check the `.uasset` before re-importing.
2. Copy the crash folder and `LandscapeLab.log` into `_verify/` **before**
   relaunching; the log is overwritten on start.
3. Move `Saved/Autosaves/PackageRestoreData.json` to `_trash/` before
   relaunching, or the next start raises a Restore modal that blocks the game
   thread and therefore blocks remote execution.
4. Rebuild the plugin while the editor is down — a module rebuild is ~18 s and
   cannot be done with it running.

## R-HAIRFACE — KEEPING AN AUTHORED GROOM OFF THE FACE (2026-08-21)

**Status: MEASURED ON TWO INDEPENDENT INSTRUMENTS.** Narrative in `LESSONS.md`
2026-08-21 ("THE HAIR OVER THE EYES WAS HAIR GROWING ON HIS BROW").

### THE RULE

**No root is placed in the front of the face below the brow, and the test is on
POSITION, not on a normal.** In `scripts/blender/author_hero_hair.py`:

    brow_z  = z_lo + face_zone_z_frac * height        # 0.80 = top of eye band
    y_frac  = (p.y - y_face_end) / (y_back_end - y_face_end)
    if y_frac <= face_zone_y_frac and p.z < brow_z:   # 0.28
        reject

`y_face_end` / `y_back_end` are measured over the SKULL only (`z >= nape_z`) so
the bust's shoulders do not stretch the range.

### THE VALUES

    face_zone_z_frac   0.80    the brow. ANATOMY, decoupled from the haircut
    face_zone_y_frac   0.28    front-of-head depth that counts as face
    face_reject_dot    0.95    nearly inert; see REJECTED
    hairline_frac      0.82
    lift_cm            3.50
    len_top_cm         12.0

### THE ACCEPTANCE NUMBERS — two instruments, no shared code path

    scripts/blender/diagnose_face_hair.py     over_face_pct   5.62 -> 0.76 %
    scripts/blender/preview_hair.py           hair_over_face  17,368 -> 1,689 px
                                              front silhouette 63,026 -> 72,443
                                              height gain      2.91 -> 3.41 cm

**The silhouette went UP while the hair came off his face.** That is the check
that separates a fix from a trim, and it is the one to repeat on any change
here.

**`diagnose_face_hair.py` REFUSES rather than reports** if its own control
fails: a point 3 cm in front of the face must score and one 3 cm behind the
skull must not.

---

## R-HAIRFACE REJECTED

- **REJECTING FACE ROOTS BY SURFACE NORMAL ALONE** (`face_reject_dot`, and the
  normal-driven `required_z` sweep). **Symptom:** a dark mass over both eye
  sockets that survives every styling change aimed at it. **Why:** a MetaHuman
  face carries eyelids, sockets and lash geometry at the brow whose normals do
  not point forward, so a brow vertex passes the face rejection, gets a low
  front-ness, has its required height dropped toward the nape, and becomes a
  legal root. **Correct:** a position-based face zone, which no normal can
  defeat.

- **`face_reject_dot` 0.45.** **Symptom:** a high, receding, balding hairline
  in every render of this groom. **Measured** with the position rule in place:

        0.45 -> 0.99   over-face 0.82 -> 0.77 %   front silhouette +45%

  It was removing the entire FOREHEAD, 22,600 silhouette pixels, and buying
  nothing. **Correct:** 0.95, kept only as a cheap pre-filter.

- **TYING THE FACE ZONE TO `hairline_frac`.** **Why:** lowering the hairline to
  bring hair forward would shrink the protection over the eyes — the two are
  not the same fact. **Correct:** `face_zone_z_frac`, the top of the measured
  eye band, which is a property of the head.

- **FIXING IT WITH `front_sweep_gain` OR `len_side_cm`.** **Symptom:** the
  over-face figure reads 17,463 -> 17,362 across a doubling of the sweep, and
  17,378 -> 17,378 across a 23% cut to side length. **Why:** the offending
  strands are rooted BELOW the hairline on the brow, so neither lever reaches
  them. **An input that moves nothing is not the input the defect is made of.**

### THE DIAGNOSTIC'S OWN REJECTED VALUES — it was wrong three times

- **Ray cast TOWARD the camera** to test "is this drawn over him". Symptom: 87%
  of offenders rooted at the nape, which is impossible. The ray must go AWAY
  from the camera.
- **Ray test without an outside-the-head test first.** Symptom: still 100%
  nape; 62.3% of flagged points sat at the BACK of the head. A point buried in
  the skull also has geometry between it and the far side. Require
  `(p - nearest).dot(normal) > 0` first.
- **Classifying roots by the nearest vertex NORMAL.** Symptom: brow roots
  reported as "back-facing", i.e. the corrupted normals that caused the defect
  also corrupted its diagnosis. Report the root's own POSITION.

**And note what the control did NOT catch.** The front/back control passed
while version 2 was still wrong. A control proves the test discriminates at the
extremes; it does not prove it is right in the middle. What caught version 2
was the distribution being anatomically absurd.

## R-HAIRSHAPE — BREAKING THE BOWL (2026-08-21)

**Status: GATED IN ENGINE.** Narrative in `LESSONS.md` 2026-08-21 ("THE BOWL
WAS TWO THINGS" and "A BALD RENDER, AND I BLAMED THE THING I HAD JUST
CHANGED").

### THE TWO MECHANISMS

**1. The ruled line across the forehead is made of ROOTS, not tips.**
`required_z` was a hard threshold, so root density went from full to zero
across one vertex. Fixed with a RAISE-ONLY lateral wave on the threshold:

    lobe = 0.6*sin(fx*7.3 + phase) + 0.4*sin(fx*17.1 + phase*2.1)
    required_z += hairline_wave_cm * 0.5 * (1 + lobe)     # in [0, w]

**RAISE-ONLY IS LOAD-BEARING.** A symmetric wave lowers the line in half its
columns, and at the TEMPLES — which the position-based face zone does not
cover, because a temple is not the front of the face — that puts roots below
the brow.

**2. `lift_cm` means different things in different places.** It sends a strand
along the scalp NORMAL, which is upward on the crown (height, the body that
made the volume fix work) and sideways on the temple (flare past the ears, the
dome outline). Scaled by how upward the root normal is:

    lift_eff = lift_cm * (lift_side_frac + (1 - lift_side_frac) * max(0, n.z))

### THE VALUES

    hairline_wave_cm     3.0     raise-only
    hairline_soft_cm     1.2     density fade below the line
    hairline_wisp_scale  0.55    fade roots grow shorter hair
    lift_side_frac       0.10    sideways roots get 10% of the lift
    layer_gain           0.30    length on the BACK -- see REJECTED
    fringe_tilt          0.18
    len_jitter           0.72 .. 1.28

### ACCEPTANCE

    diagnose_face_hair.py   hairline_profile.spread_cm   0.406 -> 0.965
    preview_hair.py         scalp_exposed_pct           13.63 -> 12.07
                            front silhouette            72,443 -> 77,697 px
                            over-face                    0.76 -> 1.08 %
    groom_presence.py       Hair PRESENT 18,633 px, 9.1x floor, crown 83%,
                            drift 2.8%, two passes at 1.7 m

**MEASURE THE HAIRLINE IN GEOMETRY, NOT IN THE RENDER.** Bin front-facing
roots by x and take the lowest root per bin. The render-side edge statistic
read 0.69–0.73 cm across a 0 → 0.70 change in `layer_gain`, a 0 → 3.5 change
in `hairline_soft_cm` AND a 0 → 2.2 change in `hairline_wave_cm` — it cannot
see any of them.

---

## R-HAIRSHAPE REJECTED

- **`layer_gain` AS THE FIX FOR THE FRINGE EDGE.** **Symptom:** 0 → 0.70 moves
  the edge spread 0.694 → 0.689 cm while the front silhouette grows 22%.
  **Why:** it scales length by how far BACK a root is, and forehead roots sit
  at back_frac ≈ 0. It lengthens the back of the head — a mullet, not a layer.
  **Correct:** it is kept at 0.30 FOR that effect, and its comment says so.

- **A SYMMETRIC HAIRLINE WAVE.** **Symptom:** over-face 0.74 → 4.94% at
  ±2.2 cm. **Why:** it lowers the line at the temples, outside the face zone's
  reach. **Correct:** raise-only, `w * 0.5 * (1 + lobe)`.

- **`hairline_soft_cm` ALONE.** **Symptom:** 0 → 3.5 moves the edge 0.691 →
  0.711 cm and costs over-face 0.74 → 2.89%. **Why:** a fade gives every
  column the same statistical treatment, so the boundary moves DOWN and stays
  level. It is kept small as a wisp generator, not as the edge fix.

- **THE RENDER-SIDE `fringe_edge_spread_cm` AS A GATE.** It is descriptive.
  Three mechanisms that demonstrably work in geometry moved it by nothing.

- **`flare_p95_ratio` AS EVIDENCE FOR THE LIFT CHANGE.** It moved the WRONG
  way (0.509 → 0.540 as side lift fell) and sits near 0.5, i.e. it reports the
  hair as narrower than the head where it was built to look. The lift change
  rests on the render and the mechanism. The number is left in the report
  labelled rather than quietly dropped.

### AND WHEN THE RENDER COMES BACK BALD

**RE-RUN THE LAST KNOWN-GOOD CONFIGURATION BEFORE DIAGNOSING THE NEW ONE.**
On 2026-08-21 v22 rendered bald, survived a fresh binding, and was cleared by
a new export validator — and then v21, put back on the same component, was
bald too. The component was carrying a binding that no longer applied.

On a freshly respawned actor the groom assigns and the binding reads back
NULL; call the assignment again and it sticks. Observed four times today
across three assets, sometimes succeeding first call. **Behaviour, not
mechanism.**

`scripts/blender/validate_groom_export.py` checks points-per-curve, root UVs,
radius and finite positions in ~40 s. Run it BEFORE an import.

## R-HAIRREAR — THE REAR RUBRIC, AND THE INPUTS IT CANNOT MEASURE (2026-08-21)

**Status: PROVEN ON THE REFERENCE, REFUSED-BY-INSPECTION ON AN IN-WORLD
RENDER.** Narrative in `LESSONS.md` 2026-08-21 ("THE RUBRIC MEASURED THE
FOREST, THEN MEASURED A HOLE").

`scripts/hero_face/likeness/rear_metrics.py` measures the back of a cut with
one implementation for the reference AND the candidate, which is the whole
point of it — a rubric with two measurement paths is two lists that must agree.
Every metric is scale-free or normalised by head height, so the 1375x768
portrait and a 2048 SceneCapture are comparable by construction.

### WHAT IT MEASURES, AND THE TARGET VALUES

Measured on `hero/reference/hero_example_pic_rear.jpg` at luma_max 70.0 /
sat_max 0.35, mask inspected as a PNG before the numbers were used. These are
declared in `characters/registry.json` and are the numbers to beat:

    mask_frac        0.1943
    taper_ratio      0.5533     nape width / crown width; a blunt bottom
                                edge reads near 1.0
    edge_roughness  27.9648     perimeter / sqrt(area), dimensionless
    crown_width_px     476.0
    nape_width_px      263.3
    width_profile    rises 0.38 -> 1.00 over the upper half, falls to 0.42

### THE PROCEDURE

    1  render the rear                    the hero turned 180 deg:
                                          place_hero_in_world.py --yaw-offset 90
                                          (the frontal default is -90)
    2  rear_metrics.py --dump-mask <png>  ALWAYS pass --dump-mask
    3  OPEN THE MASK                      before any number is quoted
    4  compare against the table above

**STEP 3 IS NOT OPTIONAL AND IT IS THE ONLY THING THAT CAUGHT THE FAILURES
BELOW.** The tool exits 0 on both of them.

### THE INPUT CONTRACT — this is what the REJECTED entries are about

The mask is `luma <= luma_max AND sat <= sat_max`. It is sound only where:

- **the background is separable by luminance** — hair must be the darkest
  thing touching the head silhouette; and
- **the subject is uniformly dark** — flat or diffuse light, so the whole hair
  mass sits under `luma_max`, not just its shadowed rim.

A flat-lit portrait on plain grey satisfies both. **A sunlit in-world render
satisfies neither, and there is no constant that fixes it.**

## R-HAIRREAR REJECTED

- **AN IN-WORLD RENDER WITH FOREST BEHIND THE HEAD.** **Symptom:** exit 0,
  `crown_width_px` 1322 in a 2048 frame, `edge_roughness` 283.3909 against the
  reference's 27.96, `taper_ratio` 0.3255. **Why:** the shadowed canopy is dark
  and unsaturated, so it satisfies both predicates, and it TOUCHES the head
  silhouette — so `_largest_component`, which exists to drop a dark background,
  keeps hair and forest as one blob. **Correct:** re-render with a background
  the mask cannot claim; do not raise the thresholds, which only trades this
  failure for the next one. Mask kept at
  `_verify/20260821_artdirect/rear_mask_render.png`.

- **A SUNLIT HEAD AGAINST SKY.** **Symptom:** exit 0, background cleanly
  excluded, `edge_roughness` 142.7551 — still 5x the reference — and
  `taper_ratio` 0.4072. **Why:** the mask is a hollow RING. The sunlit crown is
  brighter than `luma_max` 70, so only the silhouette rim and shadowed strands
  survive; area is understated and perimeter roughly doubled by the inner
  boundary. **The topology is wrong, not the threshold.** Correct: diffuse
  light on the whole hair mass. Mask kept at
  `_verify/20260821_artdirect/rear_mask_sky.png`.

- **`mask_frac` AS THE GUARD AGAINST EITHER OF THE ABOVE.** **Symptom:** the
  band `[0.005, 0.50]` passed both failures; the forest blob was 3.2% of frame
  and so is a plausible head of hair. **Why:** a gate on the EXTENT of a region
  cannot see whether it is the RIGHT region, and it is computed from the same
  mask as the metrics — check and checked share a source, so they cannot
  corroborate each other. **Correct:** the mask PNG, which is a different
  representation. The band is worth keeping as a floor against a fully
  degenerate mask; it is not evidence that a mask is the subject.

- **PITCHING THE CAMERA UP TO GET SKY BEHIND THE HEAD, AS A FIX.** It solves
  the background and creates a foreshortening caveat on a rubric whose whole
  value is that it is scale-free. Used here only to isolate the second failure
  mode. **Correct:** a flat-lit close rig against a plain background — the same
  instrument the eye-colour item has needed since 2026-08-19, serving three
  open items at once.

### WHAT THIS RUBRIC IS FOR, STATED NARROWLY

It answers *"is the back of this cut tapered, and how choppy is its edge"* —
the two things the frontal reference cannot see. **It does not judge a
haircut.** The 2026-08-21 art-direction pass found a difference of CLASS
between v22 and the reference (a short crop against a long layered shag) from
the pictures alone, with no rear number available at all. When the gross shape
is wrong, the rubric is not the instrument that tells you so.

## R-GROOMSEAT — LOCALISING A GROOM THAT DRAWS THE WRONG SHAPE (2026-08-21)

**Status: THE LADDER IS PROVEN; THE DEFECT IT LOCALISED IS OPEN.** Narrative in
`LESSONS.md` 2026-08-21 ("THE SHAPE DECIDED IN BLENDER IS NOT THE SHAPE UE
DRAWS").

A custom groom can be wrong in at least six places, and a picture cannot tell
them apart. This is the ordered set of controls that CAN, each moving one
thing. Run it in order and stop at the first disagreement — that rung is where
the shape is lost.

### THE LADDER

    1  re-author from PARAMS, preview in Blender     ~15 s
       Assert it reproduces the shipped .blend's silhouette px EXACTLY. If it
       does not, the baseline is a lookalike and every row below is void.
    2  preview the guide stack .blend                ~8 s
    3  read the groom ASSET in UE                    groom_geometry_probe.txt
       hair_groups_info[0].max_curve_length against the Blender strand max.
       These agreed to 0.9% here, which is what cleared import and export.
    4  read the component's HairGroupDesc            groom_groupdesc_probe.txt
       hair_length_scale + its OVERRIDE flag. A value without its override is
       inert and reporting one without the other is non-negotiable 17.
    5  standalone GroomActor, UNBOUND                unbound_groom_control.txt
    6  standalone GroomActor, BOUND                  same, --set BIND=<path>
       5 and 6 together separate the BINDING from the COMPONENT. Skipping them
       is how two days went into binding routes for a defect that is not in
       the binding.
    7  the real component, bound                     the shipping configuration
    8  the real component, unbound                   expected: nothing draws
    9  a KNOWN-GOOD vendor groom on the real component, same session

**RUNG 9 IS NOT OPTIONAL.** It is the difference between "this groom is wrong"
and "this session is wrong", and those have disjoint fix lists.

**PASS `/Game/...` ARGUMENTS THROUGH POWERSHELL, NOT GIT BASH.** msys rewrites
them into `C:/Program Files/Git/Game/...` and the payload refuses with a path
nobody typed. Cost one void frame here.

### WHAT THE LADDER FOUND, 2026-08-21

    rungs 1-6   agree: Blender, the guide stack, the asset, the component
                settings, and BOTH standalone renders carry the authored shape
    rung 7      the short cap
    rung 9      the vendor groom renders correctly, same session, same camera

So the defect lives in the MetaHuman GroomComponent path with a custom groom,
and NOT in the authoring, the export, the import, the asset or the binding.

### THE OPEN LEAD

    all SIX vendor HAIRS        enable_global_interpolation TRUE
    every custom groom          FALSE
    brows/stubble (1-2 cm)      FALSE and fine

`enable_global_interpolation` is documented as "RBF interpolation INSTEAD OF
THE LOCAL SKIN RIGID TRANSFORM". A rigid carry by a wrong root frame throws a
strand in proportion to its LENGTH, which fits the split exactly. **Not
demonstrated.**

## R-GROOMSEAT REJECTED

- **JUDGING A HAIRCUT ON A BLENDER PREVIEW.** **Symptom:** Blender draws a
  curtain to the jaw; UE draws a cap with bare ears, same asset, same day.
  **Why:** the two representations had never been photographed side by side,
  so no gate on either side could disagree with the other. **Correct:** one
  Blender preview and one UE render of the SAME asset, as the loop's first
  artefact. Four minutes.

- **`enable_global_interpolation` TRUE + A REBUILT IDENTITY BINDING, AS THE
  FIX.** **Symptom:** `build_fresh_groom_binding` returns a well-formed binding
  — right groom, right target, 100 interpolation points — and the component
  REFUSES it, four attempts, `binding_asset` reading back None each time.
  **Positive control:** the old binding re-assigns on attempt 1 immediately
  afterwards, so the setter works and the refusal is about this binding.
  **Suspected but unproven:** the RBF path needs a real SOURCE mesh and an
  identity source (source == target) gives it nothing to solve.

- **READING A REFUSED ASSIGNMENT AS THE INTERMITTENT ONE.** **Symptom:** the
  first assignment read back None, which this project has recorded as
  intermittent since 2026-08-21. **Why it is not:** it repeated 4 times and a
  different binding took on the first attempt in the same payload.
  **Correct:** retry, then run the positive control. An intermittent fault and
  a rejected input look identical on one attempt.

- **`source_skeletal_mesh` AS EVIDENCE OF HOW A BINDING WAS BUILT.** It reads
  **None** on our identity binding AND on every working vendor binding, which
  were built by the MetaHuman pipeline against an archetype. The property does
  not record what the build was given. **Correct:** treat it as unreadable
  provenance and compare RENDERS.

- **A 400-FIELD COMPONENT DIFF AS A ROOT CAUSE.** It returned exactly one
  substantive row, `attachment_name = FACIAL_C_FacialRoot`, which is shared by
  the vendor grooms that work. **A difference is not a cause until the working
  case lacks it.**

## R-GROOMSEAT, AMENDED 2026-08-21 (seating attempt) — TWO STAGES, NOT ONE

**Status: LOCALISED TO TWO STAGES, NOT FIXED.** Narrative in `LESSONS.md`
2026-08-21 ("ONE GROOM, THREE SHAPES").

### CORRECTION TO THIS RECIPE'S OWN LADDER — rungs 5 and 6 are WEAKER THAN WRITTEN

The ladder above says rungs 5–6 (standalone unbound / standalone bound)
**exonerate the binding**. They do not. **A standalone `GroomActor` has no
skinned mesh, so a binding's transfer data is never exercised.** Those rungs
prove only that the binding does not corrupt the ASSET, which is worth knowing
and is not what it was claimed to be.

They also say the standalone renders "the full authored shape". It renders full
**LENGTH** and a **DIFFERENT SHAPE**. Corrected in place because a rung that
over-claims is worse than a missing rung: it stops the next session looking.

**The rung that actually clears the binding subsystem is new and is now rung
6b:** build a binding for a KNOWN-GOOD VENDOR groom with our own builder and
render it on the real component. It came back indistinguishable from the
vendor's own binding.

### THE THREE SHAPES — the artefact that carries this

`_verify/20260821_artdirect/SHEET_three_shapes.png`

    1  Blender raw curves          a curtain hanging DOWN, fringe on the brow
    2  UE standalone, post-stack   swept BACK and up -- full length, different
                                   haircut. So stage one is the GUIDE STACK.
    3  UE bound on the hero        a short cap. So stage two is the BINDING-
                                   DRIVEN DEFORMATION on the skinned mesh.

### THE GUIDE STACK IS NECESSARY AND INSUFFICIENT — measured

    raw authored .abc, NO stack    imports at exactly 48,000 curves, binds,
                                   assigns (groom AND binding read back),
                                   renders BALD
    with the stack                 renders, collapsed
    a vendor groom, our builder    renders correctly

**Do not read the bald render as an import failure.** The assignment was
verified on the component before the frame was judged, which is the only thing
that separates "it drew nothing" from "nothing was there to draw".

## R-GROOMSEAT REJECTED — additions

- **IMPORTING THE RAW AUTHORED ALEMBIC TO SKIP THE STACK.** **Symptom:** clean
  import at the authored curve count, clean bind, verified assignment, and a
  completely bald render. **Why:** the stack's `Attach Hair Curves to Surface`
  is what gives the exported curves their surface attachment; without it UE has
  no roots to bind and draws nothing. **Correct:** the stack is required. The
  open question is which of its five nodes also moves the geometry.

- **`enable_global_interpolation` SET ON AN ALREADY-BUILT GROOM.** **Symptom:**
  the flag sets and survives a reload, the binding builds, and the component
  REFUSES the binding four times while the previous binding re-assigns on the
  first. **Note the discriminator:** the SAME builder produced an accepted
  binding for a VENDOR groom that carries the flag True, so the builder handles
  global interpolation. **Suspected:** flipping the flag after the groom is
  built leaves the groom without the interpolation data the binding then
  advertises.

- **DISMISSING A SILHOUETTE METRIC BECAUSE A NEIGHBOURING ONE DID NOT MOVE.**
  **Symptom:** `preview_hair.py` reported `height_gain_cm` 3.52 -> 0.05 between
  the authored blend and its guide stack, and I read it as a metric artefact
  because `hair_px` barely changed. **Why it looked safe:** the guide-stack
  blend contains a guide OBJECT, so hiding the hair does not produce a bare
  head and the difference render's control IS contaminated — the number is
  genuinely untrustworthy AND was pointing at a real 70x change. **Correct:**
  fix the control; never explain away a number you have just called
  untrustworthy.

- **READING `preview_hair.py`'s CENSUS AND SILHOUETTE AS ONE GEOMETRY.** The
  census walks RAW curve data; the silhouette comes from a RENDER, which
  evaluates modifiers. On a blend carrying a Geometry Nodes stack these are two
  different pieces of geometry, and the alembic that ships is the evaluated
  one. **Every root/scalp statistic taken this week describes the PRE-stack
  curves.** Correct: label each number with the representation it came from, in
  the report, beside the value.

### THE NEXT CUT, NAMED

Bisect the five-node stack. `Shrinkwrap Hair Curves` and `Attach Hair Curves to
Surface` are the two that can move geometry; `Attach` is required (its absence
is the bald render). **First cut: keep Attach, drop Shrinkwrap**, export,
import, bind, render, and compare against `SHEET_three_shapes.png` panel 2.

## R-GROOMSEAT, AMENDED AGAIN 2026-08-21 — THE WORKING CONFIGURATION

**Status: A CONFIGURATION THAT RENDERS THE AUTHORED HAIR ON THE HERO IS
PROVEN. THE UNDERLYING WEIGHTING DEFECT IS NOT REPAIRED.** Narrative in
`LESSONS.md` 2026-08-21 ("THE AUTHORED HAIR RENDERS ON THE HERO").

### THE WORKING ROUND TRIP

    1  author       author_hero_hair.py -- <out.abc> 48000 <seed> 0.035 0.012
                    <out.blend>
    2  guide stack  build_guide_stack.py -- <demo.blend> <stack.abc>
                    <stack.blend> 1          <-- GUIDE_EVERY 1, load-bearing
    3  import       import_groom_abc_payload.txt
    4  bind         fresh_bind_payload.txt   SOURCE_MESH empty (identity), for
                    a groom authored on the target's own head
    5  assign       BOTH the returned groom copy AND the binding
    6  render + gate

    result   Hair PRESENT, 29.6x floor, crown 91%, drift 0.6%, reproduced

**`guide_every 1` IS THE WHOLE FIX AND IT IS A WORKAROUND.** It costs 144,000
curves against 52,800. See REJECTED for why it is not a density setting.

### CORRECTIONS TO THIS RECIPE'S EARLIER AMENDMENT

- **"ONE GROOM, THREE SHAPES" IS WITHDRAWN.** `build_guide_stack.py` reports
  `evaluated_z` [158.645, 181.894] against the raw [158.633, 181.971] and
  `crown_delta_cm` 3.457 against 3.52 — **the stack does not move the
  geometry**. Panels 1 and 2 of `SHEET_three_shapes.png` are an ORTHOGRAPHIC

- **`Shrinkwrap Hair Curves` and `Attach Hair Curves to Surface` NEVER RUN.**
  They are Blender essentials assets absent from the demo .blend; the tool

### DISCOVERING THE SOURCE MESH FOR A THIRD-PARTY GROOM

A groom pack's own binding declares the head it was authored on, as BOTH its
`source_skeletal_mesh` and its `target_skeletal_mesh` — for
`GB_SC_Hairstyle_Male_11` that is
`/Game/Hero/Grooms/SC_Hairstyle_Male_11/GroomMesh/SKM_MH_Groom_Head`. **Read
it from the binding; do not guess it.**

## R-GROOMSEAT REJECTED — further additions

- **`guide_every` AS A DENSITY SETTING TO TUNE.** **Symptom:** 20 -> BALD,
  4 -> BALD, 1 -> FULL HAIR. **Why it matters:** a gradient would mean density
  and would invite tuning; a CLIFF at "every curve is its own guide" means
  CORRESPONDENCE — the only configuration in which each strand's nearest guide
  is itself and `Merge Guide and Weight it` cannot get the weights wrong.
  **Correct:** use 1 today, and treat the guide weighting as an open defect.
  **One point could not have told these apart** and would have read as
  "denser is better".

- **BISECTING NODES THAT ARE NOT IN THE STACK.** **Symptom:** a bisect plan
  naming `Shrinkwrap Hair Curves` and `Attach Hair Curves to Surface`, both of
  which the tool's own report lists as absent. **Correct:** read the report's
  `skipped` / `absent_after_append` / `modifiers` fields, which say exactly
  which three nodes ran.

- **ADDING A REPORT KEY THAT COLLIDES WITH AN EXISTING ONE.** **Symptom:** an
  env-override feature wrote `rep["skipped"]`, silently overwriting the field
  that records which stack nodes were absent — the one field that would have
  stopped the wrong bisect. **Correct:** `skip_requested`. A new key in a
  shared report is a namespace change; grep the report builder first.

- **A THIRD-PARTY GROOM ON AN IDENTITY BINDING.** **Symptom:**
  `SC_Hairstyle_Male_11` renders seated on the JAW with a bare scalp.
  **Why:** an identity binding asserts the groom was authored on the target's
  own topology. This one was authored on `SKM_MH_Groom_Head`, so its raw
  coordinates land wherever they fall on our face. **Correct:** pass
  `SOURCE_MESH`. **Not yet working:** doing so rendered bald, so the transfer
  path is UNPROVEN, not fixed.

## R-AIHAIR — the AI Hair Toolkit operator surface, enumerated

*Recorded 2026-08-22. Status: MEASURED (enumerated live, not inferred from
the UI).*

The documented fast path for CHARACTER N+1. Tonight's hero groom did NOT go
through it — see the lineage note below — but for a fresh character this is the
shortest route from a portrait to native Hair Curves.

### THE WHOLE SURFACE. Four operators, and NONE of them takes an argument.

    bpy.ops.aihair.generate_hair        Generate Hair
    bpy.ops.aihair.apply_optimization   Apply Optimization
    bpy.ops.aihair.first_run_setup      First-time Environment Setup
    bpy.ops.aihair.stop_server          Stop Server

    panel   AIHAIR_PT_main, N-strip category "AI Hair Toolkit"

### THE THREE FACTS THAT DECIDE WHETHER YOU CAN USE IT

1. THERE IS NO LOADER. No import, no open, not one filepath or directory
   argument anywhere in the namespace. Its ONLY input is `generate_hair`, which
   calls the live server. It cannot read an .npz off disk, so it cannot consume
   a hash-pinned payload from a previous session.
2. `apply_optimization` TAKES NO ARGUMENTS. It reads the panel's scene
   properties (Hair Count %, Curve Resolution) and acts on the session's current
   object. Scripting it headlessly means setting those properties, not passing
   them.
3. THE PANEL IS SERVER-GATED. It appears when the runtime server is warm on
   8765. A missing panel is a cold server, not a missing add-on.

### AND ITS DECIMATION HAS A MEASURED CAVEAT

The Hair Count % slider is the obvious lever and on the hero's data it did NOT
do what it looks like it does. Measured 2026-08-22: 33% → 100% of strands moved
rendered silhouette mass 0.4917 → 0.5345, nine per cent and not three times,
because `hair_area_over_face_area` measures the OUTLINE and strands added inside
the same envelope do not grow it. Curve Resolution is what actually carries a
reduction: 256 → 28 points is 89% fewer points at full strand count.
**Decimate POINTS, not STRANDS**, unless you have measured otherwise on that
character.

### LINEAGE, and why tonight's groom did not use this path

The canonical payload is the repo npz, hash-pinned. Since the add-on has no
loader, its path is bound to whichever generation is live in the session — a
second, different sample. Two generations must not blur into one lineage, and
here they cannot: only one route reaches the pinned payload.

### RELATED

`GroomExporter` is the other enabled add-on and it DOES take a filepath:
`bpy.ops.groom.buttonexport(filepath=..., groom_scale=1.0, ...)`. That is the
export path in use, and the one that writes `groom_root_uv` — whose absence put
every pack-derived groom on the hero's jaw.

## R-GROOMVALID — THE FORTY-SECOND GROOM DEGENERACY GATE (2026-08-22)

*Status: PROVEN IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. Passes two grooms that draw and one that
does not; refuses two manufactured defects at exit 7.*

`scripts/blender/validate_groom_export.py` now carries seven checks. Checks 1-4
(points-per-curve, root UVs, radius, finite positions) are unchanged. Checks 5-7
were added to kill the generative-hair degeneracy class in Blender in forty
seconds instead of in UE in four minutes:

    5  segment collapse   min consecutive-point distance, and the count of
                          segments of length EXACTLY zero
    6  strand collapse    min total curve length, and the count of strands of
                          length EXACTLY zero
    7  root collision     roots quantised and deduplicated; largest cluster

### RUN IT

    blender --background <groom.blend> --python scripts/blender/validate_groom_export.py

    exit 0   PASS      exit 7   REFUSE, with the reason in `refusals`

### THE BARS ARE LOOSE ON PURPOSE, AND THE CALIBRATION IS THE RECIPE

Only an EXACTLY-zero segment or an exactly-zero strand refuses. That looks
timid until the control is read:

    metric                     DiffLocks (BALD)   procedural (DRAWS)
    min consecutive-point d      0.0806 cm          0.0092 cm
    min segment / strand len     1.03e-2            1.84e-3
    roots sharing a position    24,564 of 100,943  46,789 of 48,000
    distinct root positions     76,379             1,211
    largest root cluster            10                166

**THE GROOM THAT RENDERS IS DIRTIER ON EVERY ONE OF THE THREE.** Its roots sit
in 1,211 distinct places for 48,000 strands — 2.5% distinct, because procedural
authoring grows clumps from guides — where the bald groom is 75.7% distinct. Any
bar tightened to "look strict" refuses the known-good groom, which is exactly
what `verify_export_bounds.py` was retired for on 2026-08-21.

### AND THE BARS ARE SCALE-FREE, WHICH IS NOT COSMETIC

Segment collapse is judged as a fraction of that strand's OWN length; the root
quantum is 1e-4 of the MEDIAN strand length. A fixed decimal place would call
every metre-authored groom degenerate and every centimetre-authored one clean —
a statement about the file's units, not about the groom. This project has
already paid for a units-shaped groom defect twice (`global_scale` 1.0 landing
at 1/100; `global_scale` multiplying `radius`).

### THE SEGMENT BUFFER HAS A BOUNDARY, AND IGNORING IT INVERTS THE RESULT

Points are stored flat. The last point of curve *i* and the first of curve *i+1*
are ADJACENT IN THE BUFFER AND ARE NOT A SEGMENT. A naive `diff` over the whole
buffer invents one large bogus segment per curve — 47,999 of them here — and the
histogram it produces hides every genuine short segment underneath. The check
masks `starts[1:] - 1` out before taking any statistic.

### PROVEN TO REFUSE

`hero/groomloop/scripts/corrupt_for_gate_test.py` writes a COPY of a good blend
with one manufactured defect. Both arms observed:

    zeroseg      1 coincident pair    verdict REFUSE, zero_segments 1,  exit 7
    zerostrand   one strand collapsed verdict REFUSE, zero_segments 11,
                                      zero_strands 1,                  exit 7

The 11 is the corroborating detail: a 12-point strand collapsed to a point has
ELEVEN internal segments, not twelve, so the boundary mask is doing its job.

## R-GROOMVALID REJECTED

- **A DEGENERACY BAR SET BY INTUITION.** **Symptom:** a threshold like "refuse
  any segment under 0.01 cm" or "refuse more than N roots sharing a spot".
  **What you will see:** the gate refuses `cr_g75.blend`, a groom measured
  rendering on the hero. **Correct:** refuse only the undefined cases (exactly
  zero), report everything else as a number beside the known-good groom's value.

- **`np.diff` OVER THE WHOLE POINT BUFFER.** **Symptom:** `min_segment` looks
  plausible and `segments_under_...` reads 0 on a groom that has short segments.
  **Why:** every curve boundary contributes a fake segment and dominates the
  statistic. **Correct:** mask `starts[1:] - 1`.

- **CALLING THE PER-GROUP SIMULATION FLAG AS A SUSPECT WITHOUT READING IT.**
  **Symptom:** a plausible theory that an unbound groom is being pushed through
  guide interpolation by a per-group `enable_simulation` defaulting on.
  **Measured 2026-08-22:** `hair_groups_physics[0].solver_settings.enable_simulation`
  is **False on both bald DiffLocks grooms AND on the procedural groom that
  draws**, and **True on the vendor groom, which also draws**. The field that
  differs between two grooms that both render is the same field that is identical
  between one that renders and one that does not. Per-group physics and
  interpolation are ACQUITTED, with a positive control inside the same reading.

## R-GROOMABC — WHAT THE GROOM EXPORTER ACTUALLY WRITES (2026-08-22)

*Status: MEASURED at source lines and verified by reading the written files.
Supersedes the assumption, held since 2026-08-21, that this pipeline's exports
carry root UVs.*

### THE HEADLINE

**Every groom this project has exported through the GroomExporter add-on ships
`groom_root_uv` as all zeros, or not at all.** Verified on the file, not on the
Blender arrays: `cr_g75.blend` holds 1,223 distinct real UVs and
`cr_g75_ue.abc` holds 48,000 rows of `V2f(0, 0)`.

**It is NOT why a groom renders bald** — the groom that draws has the zeros too.
It IS a live candidate for the jaw-seating failure on third-party grooms, since
UE's binding transfer consumes root UVs.

### THE FOUR SOURCE LINES

    ExporterOperators.py:26-28    GetCurvesObjects returns
                                  obj.evaluated_get(depsgraph) -- so every
                                  property the exporter reads comes off the
                                  EVALUATED copy, not the object you wrote to
    AlembicGroomExporter.py:282   the root-UV attribute is resolved by the NAME
                                  held in obj.GroomProperty.att_groom_root_uv
    ExporterOperators.py:42       `if att_name != "":` -- an unset pointer
                                  short-circuits, att_valid stays False
    AlembicGroomExporter.py:349   `if att_surface_uv_valid:` -- groom_root_uv is
                                  written ONLY here, silently skipped otherwise
    ExporterOperators.py:65-75    the FLOAT2 branch copies a flat (2n,) buffer
                                  into an (n,2) view without reshaping: raises
    ExporterOperators.py:53,79-97 out_type = type(out_array) is matched against
                                  the STRINGS "imath.V3fArray"/"imath.V2fArray".
                                  A type never equals a string; the match falls
                                  through with no default and the zero-filled
                                  array ships. Also hits FLOAT_COLOR/BYTE_COLOR.

### THE PROCEDURE — four steps, all in `export_hero_groom.py`

1. **POINT the exporter at the attribute.** `ob.GroomProperty.att_groom_root_uv
   = "groom_root_uv"`. A freshly built `bpy.data.hair_curves.new()` object has
   this at `""`; only the add-on's own operators set it.
2. **`ob.update_tag()`** so the write reaches the evaluated copy. Measured
   sufficient: evaluated pointer `""` -> `"groom_root_uv"`. Then assert on the
   EVALUATED object, not on `ob.data`.
3. **Convert FLOAT2 to FLOAT_VECTOR** (u, v, 0) in memory. FLOAT2 raises;
   FLOAT_VECTOR is the route `GroomText.py:47` names as supported.
4. **Monkeypatch `ExporterOperators.getAttributeArray`** on the module object so
   the FLOAT_VECTOR branch copies instead of falling through. Never edit the
   add-on on disk — it is outside both roots (standing rule 1).

### VERIFICATION — read the FILE, and read the VALUES

    abc_arb_params  ['groom_group_id','groom_group_name','groom_root_uv']
    abc_root_uv     n 100943  unique 1758  u [0.00285, 0.99715]
                                           v [0.29193, 0.99012]  all_zero False

matching the Blender-side attribute exactly. The exporter also prints
`[Att] uv setted`, which is absent on every failing run and is the cheapest
positive tell.

`hero/groomloop/scripts/abc_schema_dump.py` dumps ICurves schema, the topology
array and every geom param with scope, POD and length, for any ABC.

## R-GROOMABC REJECTED

- **CHECKING THAT AN ATTRIBUTE EXISTS BY THE NAME YOU GAVE IT.** **Symptom:** the
  export gate passes on every run and the ABC has no `groom_root_uv`.
  **Why:** the exporter resolves by a per-object pointer, not by your name.
  **Correct:** set the pointer, then assert what the exporter would resolve.

- **ASSERTING ON `ob.data.attributes`.** **Symptom:** the pointer resolves, the
  gate passes, the ABC is still empty. **Why:** the exporter reads the
  depsgraph-evaluated copy. **Correct:** `ob.update_tag()`, then assert on
  `bpy.data.objects[name].evaluated_get(dg)`.

- **STORING `groom_root_uv` AS FLOAT2.** **Symptom:** once the pointer resolves,
  `ValueError: could not broadcast input array from shape (2n,) into shape
  (n,2)` from `ExporterOperators.py:75`. **Note:** FLOAT2 is the semantically
  correct type for a UV, which is exactly why this trap is easy to walk into.
  **Correct:** FLOAT_VECTOR with w = 0.

- **CONCLUDING FROM `AlembicGroomExporter.py:282` THAT TYPE DOES NOT MATTER.**
  **Symptom:** the line accepts `["FLOAT2", "FLOAT_VECTOR"]`, so type looks
  irrelevant. **Why it is wrong:** it accepts both at the VALIDITY check and
  only one survives the ARRAY COPY. I recorded "the type theory is dead" on this
  reading and had to withdraw it two steps later. Read the consumer all the way
  through, not just the branch that mentions your value.

- **A PRESENCE CHECK ON A PACKED ARRAY.** **Symptom:** `groom_root_uv` is in the
  ABC and the groom still misbehaves. **Why:** the add-on ships a zero-filled
  array. **Correct:** read the values back out of the written file; refuse on
  fewer than two distinct UVs. This is non-negotiable 21's silent-channel class
  arriving in a different container.

- **TREATING ABSENT ROOT UVs AS THE CAUSE OF A BALD RENDER.** **Symptom:** the
  schema diff shows `groom_root_uv` present on the groom that draws and absent
  on the one that does not, which reads as decisive. **Measured:** the groom
  that draws carries 48,000 all-zero UVs, and the DiffLocks groom re-exported
  with 1,758 genuine ones still gates **Hair ABSENT, 3,940 px, 1.9x floor**,
  reproduced. **Root UVs are ACQUITTED as the render cause.**

## R-GROOMINTERP — WHY A GROOM BINDS, MEASURES CORRECTLY AND DRAWS NOTHING (2026-08-22)

*Status: MECHANISM ESTABLISHED AT FOUR SOURCE LINES AND ONE ENGINE ASSERTION.
The remedy is DESIGNED, NOT YET PROVEN — no render has been taken with
interpolation data present.*

### THE CHAIN

    GroomAsset.cpp:3835   NeedsInterpolationData(GroupIndex) is TRUE only if
                            IsSimulationEnable        || 
                            IsGlobalInterpolationEnable ||
                            GetEnableSimulationCache  ||
                            IsDeformationEnable
    GroomAsset.cpp:636    interpolation bulk data is built ONLY under that flag
    GroomBuilder.cpp:1752 BuildInterplationBulkData returns early when
                            PointCount == 0 || CurveCount == 0,
                          leaving Header.Flags at 0
    GroomBuilder.cpp:1758 otherwise Flags = DataFlags_HasData
    GroomResources.cpp:1919
                          FHairStrandsInterpolationResource's constructor
                            check(!!(Flags & DataFlags_HasData));

A groom built with simulation off AND global interpolation off has **no
interpolation bulk data at all**. Nothing warns; the asset imports, reports the
right curve counts, binds, and reads back correctly on every property.

### THE MEASUREMENT THAT PROVED IT, AND IT WAS A CRASH

Setting `enable_simulation` True on a groom whose interpolation data was already
built empty fatals the editor on that `check()`. The vendor groom, which ships
with simulation True, does not — so the assertion is a two-sided instrument:

    ours    enable_simulation True  ->  ASSERT   -> interpolation data ABSENT
    vendor  enable_simulation True  ->  renders  -> interpolation data PRESENT

### THE STATE OF EVERY GROOM ON THIS PROJECT

    groom                    renders   enable_simulation   curve/vertex decim
    DiffLocks k28              BALD         False              1.0 / 1.0
    DiffLocks k12              BALD         False              1.0 / 1.0
    procedural Clay_R4         BALD         False              1.0 / 1.0
    vendor SideSweptFringe     DRAWS        True               0.8 / 0.5

### THE REMEDY, AND WHY THE OBVIOUS FORM OF IT DOES NOT WORK

**The flag must be TRUE WHEN THE ASSET IS BUILT.** The DDC key includes
`bNeedInterpolationData` (`GroomAsset.cpp:2494, 2607`), so the bulk data is
produced per-key at build time. A post-hoc property write flips the flag on an
asset whose data was already built empty, and the next resource creation walks
into the `check()`. That is the crash above, and it is the FIRST thing anyone
will try.

So the flag goes on at IMPORT or REIMPORT, not afterwards. `GroomAsset.build()`
is NOT the route — `RECIPES.md` R-GROOMBIND2 records it fataling this editor on
`Assertion failed: IsUnlocked() [BulkData.cpp:596]`.

**UNPROVEN.** No render exists with interpolation data present. Do not record
this as the cause of the bald render until one does — the assertion proves the
data is absent, not that its absence is what stops the draw.

### THIS SUPERSEDES THE 2026-08-21 READING OF THE SAME CORRELATION

That entry recorded six vendor hairs at `enable_global_interpolation` TRUE and
every groom we ever made at FALSE, called it *"a correlation over five assets,
not a mechanism"*, and guessed the mechanism was RBF-versus-rigid transfer. The
correlation was right and the guessed mechanism was wrong:
`IsGlobalInterpolationEnable` is one of the three disjuncts above.

## R-GROOMABC, AMENDED 2026-08-22 (eyeball) — THE POINTER BUG IS A CLASS, NOT A FIELD

The 2026-08-22 entry above treats the empty `att_groom_root_uv` pointer as the
defect. It is one INSTANCE of the defect. All TWELVE exporter attributes resolve
through their own per-object pointer and every one of them skips in silence.

### THE FULL POINTER TABLE, MEASURED ON BOTH OBJECTS

    pointer                    clay (operator-built)   DiffLocks (hand-built)
    att_groom_width            'radius'      WRITE     ''   SKIP SILENTLY
    att_groom_root_uv          'groom_root_uv' WRITE   ''   SKIP SILENTLY
    the other ten              ''            SKIP      ''   SKIP

`hero/groomloop/scripts/groom_pointer_audit.py` reproduces
`ExporterOperators.getAttribute` against the EVALUATED attributes and prints
WRITE / SKIP SILENTLY per pointer. Run it before any export from a hand-built
Curves object.

### THE WIDTH INSTANCE IS THE ONE THAT COSTS A RENDER

`groom_width` is NOT an arb geom param. It feeds the ICurves schema's own
`widths`, so a skipped width still produces a full-length `widths` array -- of
zeros, from `AlembicGroomExporter.py:244`'s allocation, because
`getAttributeArray` returns at `ExporterOperators.py:51-52`.

    cr_g75_ue.abc          min 0.012  mean 0.0235  max 0.035  12 distinct
    difflocks_k12_ue.abc   min 0.0    mean 0.0     max 0.0     1 distinct
    difflocks_k12_full_ue  min 0.018  mean 0.018   max 0.018   (after the fix)

**A groom with zero width draws zero pixels.** The schema diff reported `widths`
present with the right LENGTH on both files, and that is exactly what a
zero-filled array looks like to a presence check.

### THE PROCEDURE, AMENDED — six steps now

1. `ob.GroomProperty.att_groom_root_uv = "groom_root_uv"`
2. **`ob.GroomProperty.att_groom_width = "radius"`** -- refuse if no FLOAT
   `radius` attribute exists, because the alternative is shipping zero widths
3. `ob.update_tag()` so both reach the evaluated copy; assert THERE
4. convert `groom_root_uv` FLOAT2 -> FLOAT_VECTOR in memory
5. monkeypatch `ExporterOperators.getAttributeArray` for the FLOAT_VECTOR
   fall-through
6. reopen the written ABC and refuse on all-zero widths OR fewer than two
   distinct root UVs

### AND THE SCHEMA CARRIES NO OTHER DIFFERENCE

Re-bucketed mechanically by `abc_diff_classify.py`: of 16 differing fields, 7
are root_uv rows, 8 are exactly (48000|576000) vs (100943|1211316), and the
last is **`name`** -- the ICurves object name.
`AlembicHairTranslator.cpp` reads attributes by the `groom_` prefix and has no
object-name logic, so `name` is benign. **Beyond root_uv presence and the width
values, the two files are structurally identical.**

## R-GROOMABC — FINAL (2026-08-22 closure). THE DEFECT IS CLOSED.

**Cause:** `att_groom_width = ''` on a hand-built Curves object -> the exporter
skips `groom_width` in silence -> the .abc ships a PRESENT, correct-length,
correctly-typed widths array of ZEROS -> that defeats the groom builder's
absent-width 1 cm fallback (an empty width is substituted, a zero width is
obeyed) -> zero pixels.

**The only substantive differences between the file that renders and the file
that does not were `groom_root_uv` PRESENCE and the width VALUES.** Everything
else in a 60-field schema comparison was count-driven or the object's own name.

**Proof, eyes on four solo arms with predictions pre-registered:**

    11_k12     widths all zero            PREDICT BALD    BALD
    12_rootuv  root UVs fixed, widths 0   PREDICT BALD    BALD
    13_full    widths 0.018, real UVs     PREDICT DRAWS   DRAWS
    14_clay    the working control        PREDICT DRAWS   DRAWS

**On the hero:** Hair PRESENT 46,080 px / 21.7x floor / crown 79%; after
colouring 88,840 px / 42.7x / crown 85%, drift 0.0%. Vendor on the same rig the
same day: 39,239 px / 19.5x / crown 74%.

### THE EXPORT PROCEDURE, FINAL — six steps, and step 2 is a LOOP

1. `att_groom_root_uv = "groom_root_uv"`
2. **Set EVERY `att_*` pointer from one declaration**, not case by case. The
   table lives in `export_hero_groom.py` as `(pointer, candidate source names,
   accepted types, ue_consumed)` and reports SET / NO SOURCE per row.
   `ue_consumed` is from `EHairAttribute` (HairAttributes.h:50-61): RootUV,
   ClumpID, StrandID, PrecomputedGuideWeights, Color, Roughness, AO, Width.
   Two hand-written cases is how this bug was found twice instead of once.
3. `ob.update_tag()`; assert on the EVALUATED object.
4. `groom_root_uv` FLOAT2 -> FLOAT_VECTOR in memory.
5. Monkeypatch `ExporterOperators.getAttributeArray` for the FLOAT_VECTOR
   fall-through, and STAMP the exporter's SHA-256 into the report — the add-on
   on disk still writes zeros and the patch dies with the process, so two .abc
   files with the same name can differ in whether the groom renders.
6. Reopen the written ABC: refuse on all-zero widths, or fewer than two distinct
   root UVs.

### THE VALIDATOR, FINAL — eight checks

Checks 1-4 presence; 5-7 degeneracy; **check 8 value variance on every resolved
attribute.** Calibrated backwards against clay, which renders:
`radius` min 0.012 / 12 distinct. So "distinct > 1" is NOT the bar — DiffLocks
is legitimately uniform at 0.018 and renders. The bar is `min <= 0` or
`all_zero`. Proven both directions: clay PASS, DiffLocks PASS, a deliberately
zeroed radius REFUSE at exit 7.

### UPSTREAM NOTE FOR THE ADD-ON AUTHOR (GroomExporter, Blender 5.2)

Two defects, both silent:

1. `ExporterOperators.py:65-75`, `case "FLOAT2"` — a flat `(2n,)` buffer is
   `np.copyto`'d into an `(n,2)` memoryview with no reshape.
   `ValueError: could not broadcast input array from shape (2n,) into shape
   (n,2)`. FLOAT2 is the natural type for a UV, so `groom_root_uv` as FLOAT2 can
   never export.
2. `ExporterOperators.py:53` sets `out_type = type(out_array)` — a TYPE object —
   and `:79-97` `match`es it against the STRING literals `"imath.V3fArray"` /
   `"imath.V2fArray"`. A type never equals a string, so no case matches, the
   `match` falls through with no default, the function returns None, and the
   zero-initialised array ships. Same bug reaches FLOAT_COLOR and BYTE_COLOR.
   Fix: `out_type = type(out_array).__name__`, or match on the class objects.

Suggested third: when a pointer does not resolve, warn. A silent skip that
produces a zero-filled array of the right length is indistinguishable from
success at every downstream check.

## R-GROOMINGEST — THE SIDECAR DRAW GATE (2026-08-22)

*Status: PROVEN IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. Refuses the pre-fix .abc at exit 2, passes
the fixed one, and the fixed one is on the hero at 41.9x floor.*

**The zero-width defect is invisible from both ends of the ingest.** Neither
side can be the gate:

    UE          `max_import_width` is NOT reflected on GroomAsset in 5.8.
                Measured: it RAISES. `hair_width` reads 0.01 on every groom --
                that is the asset default and carries no information about the
                per-point array that was imported.
    system py   PyAlembic ships inside the Blender add-on, built for Python
                3.13 (imathnumpy.cp313-win_amd64.pyd, boost_python313,
                PyImath_Python3_13). System Python is 3.12. That is an ABI
                mismatch, NOT a missing DLL -- os.add_dll_directory does not
                help. Reading the .abc at ingest would cost a 40 s Blender
                launch per call.

### THE SHAPE OF THE FIX

The exporter is the only process that can see the widths, so it records them.
`export_hero_groom.py` writes `<abc>.groomstats.json` carrying the widths and
root-UV statistics it verified **by reopening the file it just wrote**, the
sha256 of that file, the pointer table, and the SHA-256 of the two add-on source
files that produced it.

`ingest_groom.py` then refuses:

    no sidecar               -> exit 2. Every .abc predating the fix, produced
                                by an unpatched process, or by another tool.
    sidecar hash mismatch    -> exit 2. The file changed after it was gated.
    widths all_zero or max<=0 -> exit 2.

Escape: `--no-draw-gate`, documented as *"using it is a claim you own"*.

**Why a sidecar and not a check.** Non-negotiable 3 prefers an input that cannot
express the catastrophic value over a gate that rejects it. The export path now
cannot emit zero widths. The sidecar extends that as far as it goes: a file with
no provenance from the fixed path is refused by construction rather than
inspected.

### TO RUN

    blender --background <blend> --python hero/groomloop/scripts/export_hero_groom.py -- <out.abc>
      -> writes <out.abc> and <out.abc>.groomstats.json
    python scripts/hero_face/likeness/ingest_groom.py --style <S> --abc <out.abc>
      -> prints `draw gate : PASS widths max ..., root UVs N distinct, exporter <hash>`

### THE UE-SIDE GUARD IS DEMOTED, DELIBERATELY

`scripts/hero_face/likeness/groom_draw_guard.txt` refuses on unreadable
`max_import_width` -- which is ALL grooms, including the two that render. That
is correct fail-closed behaviour for a field that cannot be read, and it makes
the guard useless as a discriminator. It is kept for `num_curves` and
`max_curve_length` and is NOT the draw gate. **A guard that cannot see the
defect it was written for should say so and step aside, not be tuned until its
verdicts are agreeable.**

## R-HAIRLENGTH — LENGTHENING A RECONSTRUCTED CUT WITHOUT RESTYLING IT (2026-08-22)

*Status: L1 APPLIED AND GATED; awaiting operator judgment on the frame.*

    blender --background <in.blend> --python hero/groomloop/scripts/scale_strand_length.py
        -- <out.blend> <target_mean_cm> compressive

Each strand is scaled UNIFORMLY ABOUT ITS OWN ROOT, p' = root + k*(p - root).

### THE TARGET BAND, CORRECTED

**27.10 cm is NOT the target.** It is the vendor `Hair_M_SideSweptFringe`'s
reach — the groom ruled too long, sleek and curtained, and its length is why it
draped. The band is the clay family:

    cr_g75      11.56 cm max reach
    v22         20.44 cm max reach   (recorded 2026-08-21)
    vendor      27.10 cm             <- REJECTED as a target
    DiffLocks   14.91 -> 20.37 cm after L1

### COMPRESSIVE k, NOT A SINGLE MULTIPLIER

A global multiplier on a distribution spanning 2.68–14.91 stretches the LONGEST
strands furthest, and those already define the silhouette. `k_i` is graded by
rank so short strands gain proportionally more, then renormalised to hit the
target mean. Measured: k 1.366–1.764, and the max lands at 20.37 rather than
running past the v22 band.

### WHAT IT PRESERVES AND WHAT IT COSTS

Preserved exactly: each strand's DIRECTION and the SHAPE of its curl — the curve
is similar to itself. **Not preserved: curl SCALE.** A 1.56x strand has 1.56x
curl radius, and the reconstruction's curl is authored data.

The alternative — extrapolating each tip along its final tangent — keeps curl
size and welds a straight segment onto every strand, which reads as a wig. Of
the two ways to be wrong, similarity stays recognisable. **Prefer a modest k and
judge the frame; if the extended strands distort the cut's character, say so
with a frame rather than push further.**

### ROOTS ARE ASSERTED, NOT ASSUMED

`root_shift_max_cm` must be 0; the script exits 3 otherwise. The entire seating
proof rests on root positions, and a length op that shifted them silently would
void it without any downstream check noticing.

### MEASURED, L1

    metric      before    after
    mean         8.162    12.500
    p50          8.349    12.962
    p90         10.400    14.577
    max         14.913    20.373
    min          2.681     4.729
    gate    141,588 px  69.1x floor  crown 67%  drift 0.7%
    was      89,360 px  41.9x floor  crown 85%

Crown 85 -> 67 is the expected direction — longer strands put mass below the
crown band — and is recorded rather than read as a regression.

## R-HAIRJUDGE — THE NEUTRAL KEY LIGHT (2026-08-22)

*Status: PROVEN to be a different instrument. Used from cycle L1 onward.*

`scripts/hero_face/likeness/neutral_light.txt`, ACTION spawn | remove.

**WHY.** Alpine8K's sun sits at 12 degrees and R13 exposes for horizontal
terrain, so a vertical surface takes ~4.7x the ground's illuminance. Everything
is raking side light, which EXAGGERATES FLATNESS — a lifted groom and a slicked
one photograph alike under it. Judging volume on that frame is the clay-target
error applied to lighting: **an instrument with a one-way bias cannot adjudicate
the axis it is biased on.**

Two broad point sources at ±35° plus a low fill, spawned and removed by label
prefix `NEUTRAL_KEY_`. No asset writes.

**VERIFIED, not assumed** — a neutral frame that matched the alpine one would
mean the lights never took:

substitutes into `r"__PARAMS_JSON__"` and the JSON's own double quotes close
the literal. Standing rule 3's mechanism in a new costume.

### THE MECHANISM, AND IT IS WHY FIVE EARLIER CYCLES STALLED

**THIS MASTER HAS FOUR MELANIN LAYERS, NOT ONE.** Read off the asset by
`hair_color_probe.txt`, the state before this recipe was:

    hairMelanin        0.92   hairRedness        0.00   dye [0.5,0.58,0.72]
    HighlightsMelanin  0.28   HighlightsRedness  0.25   dye [1,1,1]

    RegionMelanin      0.28   RegionRedness      0.25   dye [1,1,1]

The base layer was already dark and neutral. The other three sat at a THIRD of
its melanin, with redness 0.25 and a neutral white dye — light and warm — and
the 2026-08-23 colour investigation moved only `hairMelanin`, `hairRedness`,
`WhiteAmount`, `hairDye` and `PaintColor`, leaving all three untouched across
five cycles. **Those three layers own the HIGHLIGHT, which is the zone that
measured warmest.** The search had been running inside one quarter of the
parameter space and concluding the space was empty.

**GENERAL RULE: A "GAMUT LIMIT" IS A CLAIM ABOUT THE SEARCH UNTIL THE
PARAMETER LIST CAME OFF THE ASSET.** The enumeration existed the whole time —
`hair_color_probe.txt` had already printed all four families — and was read as
a list of names rather than as a map of what had not been tried.

## R-HEROHAIR — THE WORKING MODEL, RULED (2026-08-23)

**Status: RULED BY THE OPERATOR 2026-08-23** — *"stick with Hair_M_SideSweptFringe
at length scale .75 as our working model it's our best one so far and all work
should be based off that."*

**THE HERO'S HAIR IS THE VENDOR GROOM. Every future change starts from this
configuration, not from a DiffLocks arm.**

    groom     /Game/Hero/Unpacked/MHC_AlpineHero/Grooms/Hair_M_SideSweptFringe
    binding   /Game/Hero/Unpacked/MHC_AlpineHero/Grooms/Hair_M_SideSweptFringe_Binding
    length    hair_length_scale 0.75, ENABLE FLAG SET
    colour    MI_AlpineHero_CustomHair, R-HAIRCOLOUR
    curves    37,520

    gated     Hair PRESENT 55,462 / 55,271 px, 26.9x floor, crown 80%,
              drift 0.3%, alpine at 1.1 m

### THE PAIR IS NOT GUESSABLE FROM THE NAME

`Hair_M_SideSweptFringe_RBF` + `BND_Hair_M_SideSweptFringe`, under
`Characters/AlpineHero/Grooms/CatalogueV2` and `.../BindingsV2`, read as a
matched pair by name and by folder. Mounted together they render **ABSENT at
3,843 px, 1.8x floor** — a binding carries per-strand root correspondence for
ONE specific groom copy, and these two are copies from different runs.

**Use the `/Game/Hero/Unpacked/...` pair above.** The Grooms folders hold 40+
groom assets, nearly all dead probes from the draw-defect hunt, and several
carry the string `SideSweptFringe`.

### THREE PIECES OF STATE, THREE DIFFERENT LIFETIMES — this is the whole recipe

| what | lives on | survives an editor restart? |
|---|---|---|
| groom + binding | the actor's external package | yes, once saved |
| colour | `MI_AlpineHero_CustomHair` asset | yes, saved when written |
| **`hair_length_scale`** | **the COMPONENT** | **only if the actor is saved** |

**The length scale is the one that gets lost.** It is component state, a Python
edit does NOT mark the owning package dirty, and `save_dirty_packages` then
returns True having written nothing. `save_hero_actor.txt` saves the actor's own
package BY NAME with `only_dirty=False` and prints the package path so the write
can be checked against the filesystem and `git status`, which is what actually
settles it.

Package for this hero: `/Game/__ExternalActors__/Alpine8K/6/ZH/V7LP6AQV5ROQ94X5HTGAW4`

### MOUNTING IT

`mount_groom.txt` swaps an already-built groom+binding pair with no ingest.
**RUN IT TWICE, from separate payload invocations.** Swapping `groom_asset`
triggers a rebuild that clears `binding_asset` AFTER an in-payload read-back can
see it, so the first call verifies its own success and is then undone. The
second call, with the groom already in place, holds — confirmed from a third
payload. An unbound groom draws nothing while every property still reports
correctly.

Then set the length scale, then verify from a payload that did neither.

### CLOSING THE EDITOR AFTER GROOM WORK

`dirty_census.txt` reads the dirty set and says WHERE it lives, because the
correct close is not constant:

- dirty set is **vendor/engine** content — those packages are in Program Files,
  outside both roots, so a Save All or save-on-quit breaks the vendor floor and
  standing rule 1 at once. **A force-kill is correct: it writes nothing.**
- dirty set is **ours** — a force-kill loses work; save first.
- **nothing dirty** — close cleanly.

Every asset write in the 2026-08-23 session used
`save_asset(only_if_is_dirty=False)` at the point of writing, so the census read
**0 total** and the clean close was the right one. Move
`Saved/Autosaves/PackageRestoreData.json` aside first regardless: a Restore
modal on the next launch blocks the game thread, which is the only channel that
could report it.

  authored DiffLocks groom mounted while the component still carried 0.75 — it
  is cut twice, once in Blender and once at render. **Correct:** the scale

## R-CITY — A SETTLEMENT AS A MASSING BLOCKOUT (2026-08-25)

**Status: PROVEN for the PLAN. The world placement of the repaired plan is
PENDING** — the 763 volumes standing in `/Game/Alpine8K` today were placed from
the SUPERSEDED plan and their streets do not join. Owed, and named here rather
than left to be discovered.

**This recipe was owed from 2026-08-24.** `recipes/city.json` shipped with its
own `_schema_status` field saying so. The new-element rule wants the recipe
before the session ends and it did not exist for a day, during which the
specification altitude of a real defect had nowhere to go.

**WHAT THIS PRODUCES, AND THE WORD MATTERS: A MASSING BLOCKOUT.** Volumes,
streets and plot footprints placed from measured terrain out of
`/Engine/BasicShapes` primitives. It answers where a town stands, how big it is,
and how it reads at range. **It does not answer what it looks like.** There is
no modular architecture kit on this machine — `KiteDemo/LevelContent/
Architecture` is a photo-studio lookdev kit (`SM_1Meter_01`,
`SM_AssetPlatform_02`, `SM_CycRoom_01`), verified.

### THE CHAIN

    1  site      scripts/find_city_site.py     ranks by LARGEST INSCRIBED
                                               CIRCLE, not by area
    2  plan      scripts/plan_city.py          offline, seeded, deterministic
    3  check     scripts/measure_city_connectivity.py   is it ONE network?
    4  draw      scripts/draw_city_plan.py     top-down plan render
    5  place     scripts/city_place_payload.txt
    6  verify    scripts/city_verify_payload.txt   counts IN THE LEVEL and
                                                   re-grounds with a FRESH trace
    7  save      external actor packages, one per volume

**Steps 2 and 6 must not share an instrument.** The placer returned `ok:true`
with its output truncated by a 763-entry actor list, so "it worked" arrived with
no numbers attached.

### THE SITE, MEASURED NOT CHOSEN

    centre (-210800, 278800) cm   usable radius 184.2 m   area 109.8 ha
    elevation 187 m of a terrain spanning 0 .. 1552.5 m
    slope mean 6.25 deg, p90 10.32
    evaluated at cell_m 8.0   <- flatness at the scale a CITY occupies

**The slope bar was ruled from the frontier, not tuned until it passed:**
6 deg -> 82.4 m usable radius, 8 -> 108.8, 10 -> 169.7, **12 -> 184.2**,
15 -> 237.9. 15 was rejected because a 27% street grade is not a street.

**The foothill constraint was NOT binding** — identical usable radius at
elevation percentile 40, 60 and 80. So `WORLD_VISION.md:303` is corroborated by
measurement rather than imposed.

### STREETS — THE TWO GATES, AND WHAT EACH ONE IS ABOUT

    max_street_slope_deg    8.0    END-TO-END GRADE, rise over run
    max_street_cut_fill_m   1.8    max deviation of natural ground from the
                                   straight run joining the two ends
    street_join_tol_m       7.0    centrelines within this are JOINED

**BOTH ARE REQUIRED AND NEITHER IS SUFFICIENT.** Grade alone accepts a segment
that dives into a gully and climbs out level at the far side — its two ends are
level, so its grade is zero. Cut/fill alone accepts a uniform 30% ramp.

**A street is gated the way a building pad is**, because it is the same kind of
object: a levelled surface cut into a slope. `max_street_cut_fill_m` is a
SEPARATE key from `buildings.max_pad_cut_fill_m` and starts at the same 1.8 m
deliberately — an earthmoving allowance is an ENGINEERING choice, not a physical
constant, and non-negotiable 19's own test is whether the quantity is physical.
An angle of repose would have to be shared; how much digging we will pay for
does not.

### THE NETWORK IS PRUNED TO THE PLAZA'S COMPONENT

Gating segments one at a time punches holes in a lattice, and a lattice with
holes is not a network. Whatever survives in a piece that cannot be walked to
from the centre is a road to nowhere: it would be placed, rendered, and would
lie to anyone reading the town from a ridge.

**KEEP THE PLAZA'S COMPONENT, NOT THE LARGEST ONE.** See REJECTED.

**ONE DEFINITION OF CONNECTED**, in `measure_city_connectivity.py`, imported by
the planner that prunes and by the gate that checks. Two copies would be two
lists that must agree (non-negotiable 24). **Note precisely what that does not
buy:** the gate re-reading the plan proves only that the pruner ran. The
independent check is the one taken IN THE WORLD from placed actor transforms —
same definition, different source.

**CONNECTIVITY IS GEOMETRIC, NOT AN ENDPOINT GRAPH.** Rings sit at
`core + i*spacing`; spokes are cut at `plaza + (R-plaza)*k/14`. A spoke CROSSES a
ring mid-segment and the two share no endpoint, so an endpoint graph reports
~459 components — an artefact of the representation, not a fact about the town.

### THE NUMBERS THAT SAY IT WORKED

    lattice generated              1342 segments
    refused on grade                323
    refused on cut/fill              46
    pruned as unreachable           135
    SHIPPED                         838 segments, 15,001 m, ONE network
    town centre                     in it

    buildings 303   landmark 1   pads spanning 44.7 m of relief
    plan sha256 ac215d1a...   re-runs byte-identical

Tolerance sensitivity, because a count that moves with the knob is about the
knob: components at tol 200/350/500/700/1000/1500 cm = 4/1/1/1/1/1.

### THE GATES, AND ALL OF THEM RUN BEFORE THE WRITE

    min_buildings          40    below this it is a hamlet
    min_street_segments   200    a floor on the CONNECTED network
    streets_are_one_network      ASSERTED by re-deriving the component count

Proven in three directions 2026-08-25: `min_street_segments 2000` REFUSES
exit 1 writing nothing; `max_street_slope_deg 1.0` collapses to 10 segments,
REFUSES exit 1 writing nothing; the good recipe exits 0 and writes.
