## R-CITY REJECTED

**`street_slope_deg` AS THE MAX OF SIX SUB-INTERVAL DIFFERENCES.**
*Symptom you will see:* `streets_rejected_slope` in the high hundreds against a
few hundred kept, and a street network that renders as disconnected stubs.
Measured: **883 of 1342 rejected, 155 disconnected pieces, largest holding 9.2%
of segments, the town CENTRE stranded in a 22-segment fragment.** It read
**p50 10.54 deg** over a basin surveyed at **mean slope 6.25 deg** — it rejected
the median segment of ground already certified flat enough to hold a town.
*Why:* that is a ROUGHNESS statistic, not a grade; one rough 2.5 m sub-interval
anywhere condemns the whole segment. **The bar was right and the measurand was
wrong.** *Correct value:* end-to-end grade, p50 3.84 deg on the same lattice.
*Reference:* `LESSONS.md` 2026-08-25.

**"KEEP THE LARGEST CONNECTED COMPONENT" AS THE CONNECTIVITY FIX.**
Proposed in the 2026-08-24 commit message as the remedy. *Symptom:* it deletes
91% of the streets AND the town centre with them, because on the shipped plan
the largest component held 42 of 459 segments and did not contain the plaza.
*Correct value:* keep the component containing the PLAZA — the centre is what a
town is organised around, so the centre defines the network. *Why it was
wrong:* it was authored against a mental picture of a mostly-good network with
frayed edges, by a session that had not measured it. **A remedy designed against
an unmeasured defect is a guess wearing a plan's clothes.**

**GATES RUNNING AFTER THE PLAN IS WRITTEN.**
*Symptom:* a refused run exits 1 **and leaves the refused plan on disk**, at
exactly the path `city_place_payload.txt` reads. Measured 2026-08-25: a run
refused at 10 street segments had already written all 10. *Why it is worse than
no gate:* the exit code is transient and lives in one shell; the bad file is
durable and is what the next step consumes. This is Division 3's "a refusal that
mutated and saved before printing REFUSE", found in our own planner.
*Correct form:* every gate runs before the write, and the refusal message says
"Nothing was written." The previous good plan stays on disk, which is a state a
caller can recover from.

**`main()` AT MODULE SCOPE IN `plan_city.py`.**
*Symptom:* `import plan_city` — to reuse its terrain sampler — REWRITES THE
PLAN as a side effect. *Correct form:* `if __name__ == "__main__":`. The
alternative was a second copy of the heightmap sampler, non-negotiable 19.
*Regression proof for any future refactor of a seeded generator:* the plan must
re-run BYTE-IDENTICAL. The guard was proven inert that way.

**`Paths.project_saved_dir()` AS AN ABSOLUTE PATH** (capture path, 2026-08-24).
It returns a RELATIVE path and the editor's working directory is the ENGINE
BINARIES folder. *Symptom:* a watcher reports "no new screenshot appeared" over
a shot that was written correctly. Wrap in `convert_relative_path_to_full`.

**A 120 s WATCHER ON A HighResShot AT MULTIPLIER 2.** On a 4064x2546 viewport
that shot takes OVER TWO MINUTES on this machine. *Symptom:* the watcher gives
up on a shot that lands a few seconds later.

## R-NAVBUILD — AMENDED 2026-08-26: THE AGENT, AND WHAT THE QUERY DOES TO THE ANSWER

**Status: PROVEN for two 1024 m-class volumes.** The town volume was added and
built; the spawn volume reproduced its recorded package sizes exactly.

### THE AGENT COMES FROM THE PAWN, NOT FROM THE WORLD

    recipes/character.json  navigation.agent_profile   "walk"    44.765083
    recipes/character.json  movement.profile           "climb"   70.0
    recipes/alpine_8k.json  world.primary_movement_mode "mount"  35.0   (UNUSED
                                                                         by the
                                                                         navmesh)

Ruling 19 compares the navmesh agent against the **PAWN's** movement profile.
It previously compared against `world.primary_movement_mode`, which is a
world-scale declaration about how the region is crossed and is NOT what slides.

**MEASURED COST OF THE OLD COMPARAND:** a navmesh built for a horse under a town
whose consumers walk. 19 of 60 street points unreachable from the town's own
plaza; the basin rim climbs 186.7 → 333 m and fragments at 35°.

### VALUES (amended)

    tile_size_uu                           1600.0
    average_layers_per_tile                1.5
    max_simultaneous_tile_generation_jobs  16
    min_region_dimension_uu                400.0
    data_gathering_mode                    "lazy"
    chunk_grid_size_cm                     102400
    builder_loading_cell_size_cm           102400
    AgentMaxSlope                          44.765083   DERIVED from the pawn

### MEASURED, TWO VOLUMES (1040 m town + 1024 m spawn)

    wall clock      34.0 s        bar 30 min
    peak commit     19.9 GB       bar 200 GB
    new packages    8, 21.59 MB
    warnings        ZERO RegistrationFailed_AgentNotValid

The dense-town cost concern did not materialise: 1,446 collision volumes and
~3,700 trees cost 34 s against the empty forest cell's 30 s.

### THE QUERY IS PART OF THE MEASUREMENT, IN BOTH DIRECTIONS

    +-20 m extent    7/25 on a navmesh that reads 25/25 at +-120 m   (recorded)
    120 m extent     the plaza spawn "projects" to a polygon 116.7 m away
    500 cm extent    the same point projects at 0.0 cm lateral

**A LARGE EXTENT DOES NOT MERELY WIDEN THE SEARCH -- IT CHANGES THE ANSWER.**
Gate on a tight extent and report the generous one alongside it if at all.

### PROJECTION IS NOT REACHABILITY

`project_point_to_navigation` says a polygon is underfoot. `get_path_length`
says a path exists. The town's streets project 838/838 and reach 653/838.
**Only the path query separates "navmesh exists here" from "you can get here".**

### API SHAPES THAT COST A FALSE FINDING

    project_point_to_navigation(world, point, nav_data, filter_class, extent)
        FIVE args. Four puts the extent into filter_class and leaves the extent
        [0,0,0] -- a zero-extent projection that misses nearly everywhere.

    get_path_length(world, start, end, nav_data, filter_class)
        -> (NavigationQueryResult, float). Compare == SUCCESS explicitly:
        INVALID=0, ERROR=1, FAIL=2, SUCCESS=3, so truthiness INVERTS the gate.
        BOTH ENDPOINTS MUST BE PROJECTED FIRST -- a point 42 m away at the
        wrong z returns (ERROR, 0.0); at its projected z, (SUCCESS, 5702.7).

## R-NAVBUILD REJECTED — additions 2026-08-26

**Two `+SupportedAgents` entries to get two different max slopes.** SYMPTOM: two
navdata instances that differ in radius/height/step and are IDENTICAL in slope.
CAUSE: `AgentMaxSlope` is not part of `FNavDataConfig`; it lives on the
RecastNavMesh class config, and per-actor writes revert via `PostLoad`
(already a REJECTED entry above). CORRECT: one agent, chosen for the consumers
that actually use the navmesh.

**Building a navmesh at the `climb` profile (70°) to cure fragmentation.**
SYMPTOM: none at build time; NPCs pathfind up cliff faces at runtime. CAUSE:
climb is the PLAYER's traversal reward, not an AI pathing surface. CORRECT:
`walk`. Written into `character.json` so nobody raises it to "fix" a
fragmented navmesh.

**Reading a reachability result without a POSITIVE control.** SYMPTOM: 0 of 40
street points and both negative controls also 0 -- indistinguishable from a
town with no navmesh. CORRECT: a point known to project (the PlayerStart)
carried in the same run; if it fails, the verdict is COULD NOT LOOK.

**Querying a building's CENTRE to ask whether it is reachable.** SYMPTOM: 0 of
303 buildings reachable. CAUSE: the centre is inside the solid volume the
navmesh is carved around. CORRECT: sample the DOORSTEP, just outside the
footprint -- 253 of 303.


**Adding a navmesh VOLUME to make ground reachable.** SYMPTOM: the build is
clean by every bar it carries — 10 chunk actors, 35.18 MB, 36.0 s, 20.0 GB peak,
zero `RegistrationFailed_AgentNotValid` — and the reachable island does not move.
A directed probe every 50 m to 1400 m projects at ALL 28 points and is reachable
at 6. CAUSE: a volume declares where Recast MAY build; it cannot join two
regions the terrain separates. CORRECT: **measure connectivity BEFORE sizing a
volume**, with a path query and not a projection. A volume is the right fix for
a COVERAGE gap and no fix at all for a CONNECTIVITY gap, and the two are
indistinguishable from a coverage number.

**Judging a slope against the agent bar at convenient sample spacing.** SYMPTOM:
the gradient at the reachability flip reads **35.71°** — under the 44.765° bar —
which points the diagnosis at coverage or `MinRegionArea`, both fixable, and
away from the terrain. CAUSE: 5 m spacing averages 26 Recast cells. At 0.5 m
the same ground reads **51.34°**: a 1.25 m rise over 1 m. CORRECT: sample at or
near the consumer's own evaluation scale — `CellSize` is ~19 cm here — or state
the spacing beside the number. A gradient without its denominator is not a
slope.

**Reporting the FIRST unreachable sample along a ray as the region boundary.**
SYMPTOM: bearing 0 reads 244 m at 2 m spacing and 322 m at 0.5 m, on the same
navmesh. CAUSE: isolated dropouts exist (324.5 m reads reachable among
unreachable neighbours), and a first-flip scan stops at the first one it meets,
so the statistic moves with sampling. CORRECT: scan the WHOLE ray and take the
FURTHEST reachable point, which no single dropout can move. Applies to any
"where does X stop" probe, not only navigation.

**Distinguishing the three barrier mechanisms** — worth keeping because they
have three different fixes and one shared symptom (a reachability flip):

    no polygon at all        fails to PROJECT           coverage, fixable
    discarded thin strip     projects, gradient under   MinRegionArea, fixable
    real slope step          projects, gradient over    terrain, not fixable
                                                        without an edit

Report `projects` and the LOCAL GRADIENT beside every reachability result, or
the probe locates a barrier without identifying it.


**Reading `get_path_length` FAIL as "no path exists".** SYMPTOM: a coherent,
reproducible, completely wrong map of a sealed basin -- 24 bearings, furthest
reachable 252-504 m, median 360. CAUSE: a path query has a finite search budget
and FAILS when it exhausts it; from a single call that is indistinguishable from
disconnected ground. It also returns a PARTIAL LENGTH on failure (424 m), so a
caller reading the length without checking the result gets a plausible number.
CORRECT: **a relay.** Query from the nearest point already known reachable;
reachability over a navmesh is transitive when every leg is a real path.
`scripts/city_path_chain_payload.txt` is the three-leg discriminator (A plaza to
far FAIL, B mid to far SUCCESS, C plaza to mid SUCCESS).

**Reading a UNIFORM reachability profile as a uniform barrier.** SYMPTOM: "the
best bearing is only 1.4x the median, so there is no natural pass." CAUSE: a
roughly circular limit centred on the QUERY START is the shape a budget makes;
terrain barriers are irregular. CORRECT: uniformity across bearings is evidence
the boundary does NOT depend on the terrain. Check the anchor before the ground.

**Trusting a single-source instrument because it REPRODUCES.** SYMPTOM: stable
numbers across sampling intervals, across bearings, and across two navmesh
builds. CAUSE: the answer was a property of the query, so of course it
reproduced. Non-negotiable 0 with one instrument asked many times, which is not
corroboration at all.

**Reading "projects everywhere, reachable nowhere" as two instruments agreeing.**
CAUSE: they answer different questions. It is one instrument saying the ground
is fine and another saying the search stopped -- which is the ANSWER, not
agreement that something is wrong with the ground.

**A model that scores well on one axis and badly on another, read as "roughly
right".** MEASURED: the offline walk model agrees with the built navmesh 91.5%
on PROJECTS and 48.9% on REACHABLE. CORRECT: that gap is a statement about WHAT
the model is for -- it predicts the surface and does not attempt connectivity --
and it was the loudest available clue that reachability was not about slope.
`scripts/calibrate_walk_model.py` scores it against a measured grid.

**A slope model on a heightmap, two ways to get it wrong, both permissive.**
(1) PER-AXIS: testing dz/dx and dz/dy separately passes a quad rising 0.9 m in
each, which is 1.27 m over 1 m = 51.8 deg; understates by up to sqrt(2).
(2) CENTRAL DIFFERENCES (`np.gradient`): halves a one-cell step, smoothing away
exactly the sub-metre risers under investigation. CORRECT: forward differences
per QUAD, gradient MAGNITUDE -- `design_pass.quad_slope_deg`. Both errors make
ground look flatter than the agent finds it.

**Sub-metre sampling of a 1 m heightmap.** SYMPTOM: bearing 315 reports 1
blocking segment at 1 m spacing, 4 at 0.5 m and 7 at 0.25 m, the new ones 0.2 m
long. CAUSE: bilinear interpolation between 1 m vertices -- artefacts of the
sampler, not steps in the ground. CORRECT: work on the grid the terrain has.

**A negative control placed AFTER the headline computation.** SYMPTOM: the run
reports `ok: false` with "136 recovered" already in the payload, from an
`IndexError` on `loc_cm[2]` -- `loc_cm` is `[x, y]`. CORRECT: a number that
arrives without its control is not a result, and a run reporting `ok: false` has
not produced one however complete the output looks.


**A "ground" line trace that excludes only foliage.** SYMPTOM: 17 town streets
trace 12.9 m above their planned height and read as unreachable, reproducibly,
while still projecting. CAUSE: the trace lands on a BUILDING ROOF, and a navmesh
projection from roof height finds no reachable polygon. CORRECT: ignore foliage
AND every actor tagged `LandscapeLab.City`. A trace answers "what is above this
point", not "where is the ground", and the difference only appears where
something is standing there. With the exclusion: 136 gained, 0 lost -- a strict
superset, which is what a correct relay must produce.

**A reachable region sampled only from town features.** SYMPTOM: an encounter
rule of the form "OUTSIDE the settlement AND near reachable ground" yields ZERO
available area, and the zero looks like a fact about the terrain. CAUSE: every
row in the sidecar is a street midpoint or a building doorstep, so
`near_reachable` is True only inside the town and the two clauses are disjoint
BY CONSTRUCTION. CORRECT: a LATTICE over the whole built navmesh
(`city_reachable_lattice_payload`), measured by grid BFS -- a cell joins when a
path exists from an already-reachable 4-neighbour, so every query is one lattice
step and none approaches the search budget. 1261 of 1431 cells over 2.163 km2,
1557 queries.

**A verifier that inherits the defect it verifies.** SYMPTOM:
`city_encounter_verify_payload` reported all 6 encounters unreachable on a plan
whose own gate had passed them. CAUSE: it asked ONE query from the spawn.
CORRECT: try direct, then relay off the nearest measured lattice point; only a
failure of BOTH is unreachable. All 6 then verify, ALL VIA RELAY -- which is
itself evidence the budget was the limit.

**Reporting one field for two differently-derived quantities.** SYMPTOM:
`path_len_m` 15.2-60.0 m for encounters sited outside a 940 m town. CAUSE: a
relay length is only the last leg, from an anchor one lattice step away; a
direct length is the walk from the PlayerStart. CORRECT: record WHICH leg
answered on every row, count them in the summary, and name the summary field
`path_len_m_DIRECT_ONLY`. A number whose meaning depends on a branch must carry
the branch.

**Explaining a zero instead of doubting it.** SYMPTOM: "the basin cannot hold
encounters" was written up with a `WORLD_VISION` citation about remoteness
explaining why the zero was not merely correct but desirable. The zero was an
artefact of the sample. CORRECT: a satisfying explanation for a measurement is
not evidence the measurement is right -- it makes the measurement harder to
doubt, which is the opposite of what is wanted. Check the denominator's
PROVENANCE before reasoning about its value.

## R-CITY — AMENDED 2026-08-26: THE TOWN IS 78% REACHABLE, AND THAT IS AUTHORED DATA

**A settlement's extent must be gated on WHOLE-NETWORK reachability, not on
per-structure pads.** The town's extent was drawn by cut/fill and pad slope,
each building judged alone. Every building passed and the town reaches onto
ground unreachable from its own plaza.

    streets    653 of 838 reachable (77.9%)
    buildings  253 of 303 reachable at the doorstep (83.5%)
    agent      walk, 44.765 deg
    artefact   city/alpine_basin_town_reachable.json

**THE REACHABLE REGION IS AUTHORED, VERSIONED DATA**, in the same spirit as unit
8's ruling that the navigable area is recipe data rather than an emergent
accident. It is BOUND to the agent, the resident chunk count, the PlayerStart
and the query extent, because a reachability claim is true for exactly ONE
navmesh build.

**The unreachable districts are declared, not hidden.** Dead ground NAMED as
dead is honest; dead ground silently available to the next placement tool is the
trap — the encounter planner has already tried to put five encounters in it.

~~**OWED:**~~ **DISCHARGED 2026-08-26, both halves.** `plan_city` now carries a
whole-network building gate — every building within `max_building_to_street_m`
of the CONNECTED street network, measuring **292 of 303, 11 orphaned (3.6%)** —
and the shared infrastructure the 4a escalation required is
`scripts/reachability.py`, one implementation consumed by `plan_city`,
`plan_encounters` and every future placement tool. The private copy
`plan_encounters` had already grown was deleted rather than patched; an
individually-patched reachability check in a planner is a REJECTED pattern from
here.

**~~`max_orphan_building_fraction` IS PROVISIONAL AND NEEDS A RULING.~~
RATIFIED AT 0.05 BY THE OPERATOR, 2026-08-27.** Kept struck rather than
rewritten, because HOW it was chosen is the part worth carrying: it was set at
0.05 against a first measurement of 3.6% — **a bar chosen to pass the number it
first saw**, which is non-negotiable 2's untested gate, and it had never refused
anything.

**What the ratification does and does not settle.** It settles that 0.05 is the
VALUE, so the bar is now a decision rather than an accident. It does not convert
the value into a derivation: nobody has costed what an orphaned building
actually means to a player, and if that is ever measured the bar should move to
follow it rather than being defended because it is written down.

**The MACHINERY is separately proven**, and that is what makes ratifying a
post-hoc value acceptable rather than merely convenient: `prove_city_gates.py`
drives this gate to a refusal at 0.0 and asserts the refusal WROTE NOTHING, so
the gate is known to be reachable and known to fail closed. A ratified bar on an
unproven gate would be worth much less.

## R-CITY REJECTED — additions 2026-08-26

**Computing an encounter density target over the whole area box.** SYMPTOM: a
target of 5 in a box where 0.69–8.49% of the ground is actually available, and
a planner refused for failing to find encounters in the settlement. CAUSE: the
denominator is the ground a candidate can OCCUPY — outside the settlement,
outside the spawn-safe radius, connected to the player, near measured reachable
ground — not the box. CORRECT: measure availability on the same grid, applying
exactly the tests a candidate must pass. Non-negotiable 22.

**A CONSTANT floor as the encounter-count gate.** SYMPTOM: the density curve
produced a target of 5, the floor was 6, and the planner hit its target EXACTLY
and was refused. CAUSE: a bar satisfied by lowering the bar tests nothing.
CORRECT: relative to target (`min_fraction_of_target`), which catches what can
actually go wrong — exclusions or separation eating a plan.

**Tuning the offline heightmap connectivity model until it agrees with the
navmesh.** SYMPTOM: none — it would pass. CAUSE: fitting a model to an answer.
The model passed five encounters the navmesh refused at two different agents.
CORRECT: leave it optimistic, label it a PREFILTER, take the measured
reachable-region sidecar as the INPUT and the built-navmesh check as the
authority.


**Placing a deliberately-broken COPY of a repo script outside `scripts/` to
positive-control a prover.** SYMPTOM: the control reports the expected FAILED
verdict, and every case fails — including the positive control, which the
injected defect does not predict. CAUSE: `plan_city.py` derives `REPO` from its
own `__file__`, so a copy elsewhere resolves neither `recipes/` nor its sibling
imports and dies before reaching a gate; a dead planner and four working gates
produce the same table. CORRECT: write the control copy BESIDE the original,
remove it in a `finally`, and assert its absence afterwards. **Then assert the
control's failures land where the injected defect predicts** — a control that
fails everywhere is an instrument fault until proven otherwise.

**Ticking off a positive control on its VERDICT LINE.** SYMPTOM: none — the
prover is recorded as positive-controlled and every later PASS inherits the
credential. CAUSE: "FAILED" is the expected output of a working control AND of
a control that cannot run. CORRECT: read WHICH rows moved. With the orphan gate
dead, exactly the two cases routed through it must fail and the other three
must still pass.

**Proving a gate refuses without also proving the refusal WROTE NOTHING.**
SYMPTOM: none at test time; later, a refused plan sits at exactly the path the
placer reads. CAUSE: an exit code cannot distinguish "refused before writing"
from "wrote, then refused". CORRECT: assert the output file DOES NOT EXIST on
every refusal case. `scripts/prove_city_gates.py` does, on all four.

**A gate whose threshold was chosen to pass the first number it saw.**
SYMPTOM: it never refuses. `max_orphan_building_fraction` = 0.05 against a
first measurement of 3.6%. NOT A FIX, A DECLARATION: it is marked PROVISIONAL
and RULING NEEDED in R-CITY rather than left reading as ratified, and the
prover exercises it by mutation so the machinery is at least known to work.


**Leaving a plan on disk after its producer's method changes.** SYMPTOM: none.
`encounters/alpine_8k_all.json` reads as a valid plan — well formed, seeded,
naming its recipe and world — and its producer now REFUSES to generate it. The
artefact says `target_count: 5`; the corrected availability denominator computes
0. CORRECT: `python scripts/check_plan_freshness.py --reproduce` before
consuming any plan, and re-derive or explicitly retire a plan whose producer
will not reproduce it.

**Reading a plan's freshness off the plan.** SYMPTOM: cannot be done — these
artefacts carry their inputs' PATHS, not their HASHES. CAUSE: non-negotiable
20's live pointer. "What IS the plan" is then answerable only by re-running the
producer, whose own inputs may have moved. CORRECT (OWED): stamp every plan with
the SHA-256 of each declared input at write time, so staleness is a fact on
disk rather than a re-derivation.

**Judging staleness from git history alone.** SYMPTOM: a good plan condemned.
`city/alpine_basin_town_plan.json` has THREE inputs committed after it — the
planner, its recipe and the world recipe — and is byte-identical, `65ab655e`
both ways. CAUSE: a commit touching a producer is not a change to its output.
CORRECT: history answers "could this have changed"; only re-derivation answers
"did it". Report the suspicion, then settle it.

**An emoji on a diagnostic's FAILURE branch.** SYMPTOM: `UnicodeEncodeError:
charmap codec can't encode character` on cp1252 stdout, AFTER every passing row
printed cleanly and BEFORE the summary. CAUSE: the failure branch carried a
character the success branch did not. CORRECT: ASCII markers on any branch that
has to survive, asserted by scanning the file for non-ASCII. **A tool that
cannot print its own worst verdict reports success by omission** — and it fails
in the one direction nobody audits.


**Shipping a planner whose SUCCESS path has never executed.** SYMPTOM: none --
every run refuses, correctly, and the gates look well tested. CAUSE: a world
that legitimately admits no rows exercises only the refusal half.
`plan_encounters` was in this state all day. CORRECT:
`python scripts/prove_encounter_plan.py` -- a SYNTHETIC world, in a COPY of the
recipe, that permits placement, plus a negative control that must still refuse.
Same class as the first-ever call of `create_landscape_from_heightmap` and
`build_landscape_nanite`.

**Believing a planner's own report that its plan is valid.** SYMPTOM: none;
every internal assertion passes because the code that placed the rows is the
code that checks them. CORRECT: re-derive every invariant from the OUTPUT plus
the RECIPE, in code that did not place them -- per-pair separation, settlement
containment rebuilt from the city plan, spawn radius, elevation eligibility,
slope bar, party size, count. Non-negotiable 8.

**A count gate that names the wrong bar when it refuses.** SYMPTOM:
`REFUSE: 0 encounters against a target of 0 -- below 80% of target (need 3)`.
80% of 0 is 0, so the FRACTION was not binding; `min_encounters_floor` was. The
operator is pointed at the wrong knob. CORRECT: `need = max(floor, ceil(frac *
target))` must report WHICH term won, and print all three numbers. Both branches
are now exercised -- the real basin takes the floor branch, the prover's
negative control takes the fraction branch.

**Reading a synthetic-world proof as a statement about the world.** SYMPTOM: a
capability proof quoted as "the basin can hold 66 encounters". CAUSE: the prover
widens the area box and relaxes the proximity prior to make placement possible.
CORRECT: the tool prints SYNTHETIC WORLD as its first line and says the real
basin's refusal is the right answer. Keep the label attached to the number.


**A verifier that re-types the plan's contents instead of deriving them.**
SYMPTOM: `world count does not match the plan`, counted 1446 against a planned
1142, on a CORRECT town. CAUSE: `city_verify_payload.txt` summed three hardcoded
terms (buildings + streets + landmark); roofs and a spire were added to the
planner afterwards, and the plan's own `counts` already declared both.
Non-negotiable 24. CORRECT: derive the expectation from the plan's own
geometry — a section carrying `loc_cm` is a placement — so the next kind is
covered the day it is planned. **Adding roofs to the hardcoded list is NOT the
fix**; it reproduces the defect one kind later.

**Using `plan['counts']` as the expectation.** SYMPTOM: would refuse on
`streets_rejected_grade` and `streets_pruned_disconnected`. CAUSE: `counts`
mixes placements with diagnostics. CORRECT: the placement sections themselves.

**Grounding a city over ALL its actors.** SYMPTOM: `base_above_ground_cm max
883.1` — an actor apparently floating 8.8 m. CAUSE: it is a ROOF, and tracing a
roof's base to the terrain measures the height of the building under it. Roofs
and spires sit on other actors BY DESIGN. CORRECT: sample ground-sitting kinds
only (buildings, streets, landmark), declare which kinds and how many in the
output. Re-measured that way: **p50 -0.0, max 0.0 cm over 60 fresh traces, 0
misses.** Non-negotiable 22 — a grounding statistic is meaningful only
conditioned on what is supposed to be on the ground.

**Verification form for a placed city, PROVEN IN BOTH DIRECTIONS 2026-08-26:**

    positive   the committed plan vs the live world
               ok true, 5 kinds exact, grounding max 0.0 cm
    negative   a COPY of the plan with one building removed and the whole
               `spire` section deleted, same world
               REFUSE: buildings planned 302, in world 303;
                       spire planned None, in world 1

The negative arm catches a MISSING KIND, which a hardcoded sum cannot. An empty
recognised-placement set fails closed as COULD NOT LOOK, never as a match.


**A plan that names its inputs by PATH and not by HASH.** SYMPTOM: staleness is
undetectable from the file; the only check is re-running the producer, whose own
inputs may have moved. CAUSE: non-negotiable 20's live pointer. CORRECT: stamp
`_input_sha256` at write time, after every gate, via `scripts/plan_stamp.py`.
`plan_city` and `plan_encounters` write it; `check_plan_freshness` reads it.

**Three copies of the INPUT_KEYS list.** SYMPTOM: none, until an input key is
added to a producer and not to the checker -- which then reports MATCHES over an
unhashed input. CAUSE: non-negotiable 24. CORRECT: `plan_stamp.INPUT_KEYS` is
the single declaration and `check_plan_freshness` imports it rather than
re-typing it.

**A stamp that skips an input it could not read.** SYMPTOM: verifies clean later
against a plan built from something else. CORRECT: `plan_stamp.stamp()` RAISES
on a declared-but-absent input, and `verify()` returns UNREADABLE rather than
folding it into MATCHES. Unknown is never yes.

**Quoting the cheapest of three green checks as though it were the strongest.**
The ranking is: HISTORY suspects (a commit touching a producer is not a change
to its output); the STAMP is a fact on disk about the INPUTS; REPRODUCE is
decisive about the OUTPUT. A stamp cannot catch a producer whose behaviour
depends on something it does not declare. State the ordering wherever all three
are reported.

**Adding a key to a committed plan the placer reads, on the assurance that it is
harmless.** CORRECT, and it is cheap: regenerate to a TEMP path, strip the new
key, re-serialise both, require BYTE-IDENTITY, then re-run every consumer.
Measured 2026-08-26: `47abfa61 == 47abfa61` with the stamp stripped, and the
live world still verifying `ok true`, `mismatch {}`, grounding max 0.0 cm.
Restore point tag `pre-plan-stamp-20260826`.


**Recording a binding and enforcing only part of it.** SYMPTOM: none. The
reachable sidecar's `_bound_to` records the agent, the PlayerStart, the query
extent and `nav_chunk_actors_resident`; `reachability.py` refused on the agent
and never compared the chunk count. The east extension took the world 8 -> 10
chunks and the sidecar went on declaring 8. CAUSE: non-negotiable 25 -- a claim
in a docstring that nothing re-checks. CORRECT: every field a binding records is
either ASSERTED or explicitly declared unenforceable, with the reason at the
check. `expect_nav_chunks=None` now means UNCHECKED and says so.

**Assuming an unenforceable check is a passing check.** SYMPTOM: an offline
caller loads a sidecar and believes the whole binding was verified. CAUSE: the
live chunk count is an editor query and offline callers cannot supply it.
CORRECT: name the limit where the check is, not in a signature default.
Unknown is never yes.

**Re-measuring the reachable region after ANY navmesh build.** The sidecar's own
header prescribes it; it had not been done after the east extension. Procedure:
`scripts/city_reachable_region_payload.txt` with `__PLAN__` and `__OUT__`
substituted, then diff the new file against the committed one FIELD BY FIELD
before installing it. Measured 2026-08-26: exactly one field moved
(`nav_chunk_actors_resident` 8 -> 10) and **zero of 1141 rows flipped** -- a
second, independent confirmation that coverage is not connectivity.

## R-NAVGRID — THE REGION'S NAVMESH AS ONE DECLARATION (2026-08-27)

**Status: PROVEN** — executed end to end on `/Game/Alpine8K`, 72 volumes, 64
chunk actors, and verified by an instrument that never saw the recipe.

New element type: a navmesh **tile grid**. `R-NAVBUILD` covers BUILDING a
navmesh; this covers deciding WHERE it exists, which unit 8 ruled to be
authored, versioned recipe data and `PHASE2_PLAN:250` left as "a decision, not
a plan".

### 1. PRECONDITIONS

- UE **5.8.1-56057345+++UE5+Release-5.8**.
- Plugins: `LandscapeLabEditor` (for `load_all_world_partition_regions`),
  `LandscapeLabGameplay`. Both `EnabledByDefault`, no `.uproject` entry.
- `recipes/alpine_8k.json` validates, and its `navigation` block already
  declares `tile_size_uu` **1600.0**, `average_layers_per_tile` **1.5**,
  `chunk_grid_size_cm` **102400**, `min_region_dimension_uu` **400.0**,
  `data_gathering_mode` **"static"**.
- `recipes/character.json` `movement.profile` and `navigation.agent_profile`
  both present; ruling 19 compares the AGENT against the **PAWN**, never
  against `world.primary_movement_mode`.
- At least one bounds volume already declared and BUILT, to anchor the grid.
  Here `NavBounds_Town`, min `[-262400, 227200, 11600]`, max
  `[-158400, 331200, 45000]`.
- `terrain/alpine_8k.png`, 8129², 1 m/vertex, and collision known to agree
  with it: `check_collision_truth` p50 0.011 / p90 0.039 / max 0.168 m over
  500 points.
- Free RAM ≥ 16 GB (`resource_guard.py`), no editor running for the build.

### 2. EXACT VALUES

| Parameter | Locked | Range | What it affects |
|---|---|---|---|
| `TILE_CM` | **104000.0** (1040 m) | multiples of `TileSizeUU` | volume count and per-tile voxel cost |
| `MARGIN_BELOW_CM` | **1100.0** | 0–5000 | how far under terrain the volume reaches |
| `MARGIN_ABOVE_CM` | **2000.0** | 0–10000 | headroom above the tallest ground in the tile |
| `MIN_TILE_FRAC` | **0.30** | 0.05–1.0 | drops clipped EDGE slivers; see REJECTED |
| `--min-walk-frac` | **0.05** | 0.0–1.0 | skips tiles too steep to be worth a volume |
| agent bar | **44.765083°** | — | DERIVED from `character.json` `agent_profile` = `walk`; never typed |

Measured result on this region: **72 tiles kept, 9 slivers dropped, 0 tiles
below the walk floor**, 77.88 km² of volume over 49.27 km² of walkable terrain.
Union side 812800 cm → **388,622** navmesh tiles against the **1,048,576** hard
limit.

**Z comes from the HEIGHTMAP and the recipe says so in every generated `basis`.**
The two originally hand-authored volumes used 625 collision traces each and are
carried through UNCHANGED. Describing a heightmap-derived z as "measured"
without naming the instrument is the derived-record trap.

### 3. ORDERED STEPS

1. `python scripts/measure_walkable_extent.py` — how much of the region is
   walkable at all. Navmesh over ground the agent cannot stand on is build time
   spent on nothing. *(Prefilter: its CLOSED verdicts are trusted, its OPEN ones
   are not.)*
2. `python scripts/plan_navmesh_tiles.py` — report only. Read the printed
   bounds. **The sliver defect was caught here by eye, not by a gate.**
3. `python scripts/plan_navmesh_tiles.py --write`.
4. Validate: `import_heightmap._validate_recipe` must return zero errors. The
   tile-budget check runs here and REFUSES over the hard limit.
5. **CALIBRATE before committing to the campaign.** Apply ONE representative
   tile — full canopy, not a cleared one — with
   `apply_navigation_config.py --world --volumes <NAME> --go`, save, close the
   editor, build, and record MB / wall / peak commit / **reachable ground
   gained**.
6. `python scripts/save_level.py --recipe <world> --save`. *Load-bearing: the
   builder reads packages on DISK, not the editor's memory. Unit 6's collision
   reached PIE as `NoCollision` for exactly this reason.*
7. Read the dirty list; it must be EMPTY. Close the editor. Move
   `Saved/Autosaves/PackageRestoreData.json` aside so the next launch cannot
   raise a Restore modal — a modal blocks the game thread, which is the only
   channel that could report it.
8. `python scripts/resource_guard.py`, then
   `python scripts/build_navmesh_chunk.py --go --max-minutes 30
   --max-commit-gb 90`.
9. Relaunch and re-measure the reachable region AND the lattice. **Both are
   bound to the navmesh build and are now stale** — `reachability.py` will
   refuse a mismatched chunk count, which is the guard working.
   ⭐ **AMENDED 2026-09-19b: the lattice ground trace MUST ignore
   `WorldPartitionHLOD` actors.** Since the 2026-09-14 4096 rebuild the HLOD
   proxies carry collision at/above the landscape; a trace that stops on a
   proxy returns a wrong height and the nav projection below it misses,
   reading a plausible collapse (reachable 2802 vs 9810 correct on Brief-4
   T6). `city_reachable_lattice_payload.txt` now adds them to the trace
   ignore-list beside foliage + city-tagged; the landscape stays resident
   via `load_all_world_partition_regions`. Any NEW nav-vs-ground trace on
   this world inherits the same requirement.

### 4. VERIFICATION

**Independent instrument (non-negotiable 8):** the relay sweep and the reachable
lattice are editor path queries against the BUILT navmesh, which is

## R-ENCOUNTER — AN ENCOUNTER SITE, FROM DENSITY CURVE TO VERIFIED ROW (2026-08-27)

**Status: PROVEN for PLANNING AND VERIFICATION. NOT PROVEN for PLACEMENT —
nothing has ever been spawned.** Said first because the rest of this recipe
reads like a complete pipeline and one end of it has never run.

New element type: an **encounter site**. `PHASE2_PLAN` units 9 and 10.

### 1. PRECONDITIONS

- UE **5.8.1-56057345+++UE5+Release-5.8**; `LandscapeLabGameplay` loaded, with
  `EncounterMarker` and `EncounterDirectorSubsystem` reflected (verify on a

  the reachability gate cannot measure produces rows nobody can verify.

  re-described in the encounter recipe; it derives from `city/<id>_plan.json`'s
  own geometry, tested as oriented rectangles — the SAME test the foliage clear
  uses (non-negotiable 19, one declaration two consumers).
- A **reachable LATTICE** over the built navmesh, not just the town sidecar.
  The sidecar samples street midpoints and building doorsteps, all INSIDE the
  settlement, which makes "outside the settlement AND near reachable ground"
  unsatisfiable by construction.
- `recipes/character.json` `navigation.agent_profile` — the slope bar is
  DERIVED from it, never typed.

### 2. EXACT VALUES

| Parameter | Locked | Range | What it affects |
|---|---|---|---|
| `density.base_per_km2` | **4.68** | > 0 | encounters at the reference elevation |
| `density.reference_elevation_m` | **187.0** | — | the basin floor, measured |
| `density.per_100m_above_reference` | as declared | ≥ 0 | the foothill→peak gradient, `WORLD_VISION:305` |
| `exclusions.max_distance_from_reachable_m` | **30.0** | < lattice step | see REJECTED — 60 against a 60 m lattice admits a full cell of error |
| `exclusions.player_start_safe_radius_m` | as declared | > every leash radius | or an encounter reaches the spawn |
| `settlement.building_margin_m` | as declared | > the largest aggro radius | or an encounter aggros from inside the town |
| `gates.min_fraction_of_target` | **0.8** | 0–1 | RELATIVE, not a constant floor |
| `gates.min_encounters_floor` | **3** | ≥ 0 | backstop when the target is itself near zero |
| lattice step | **6000 cm** (60 m) | — | the resolution of "reachable"; the proximity radius must be well inside it |
| director `ActivateRadiusCm` | **12000.0** | — | config, not C++ |
| director `DeactivateRadiusCm` | **20000.0** | **must exceed activate** | hysteresis; asserted at runtime |
| director `NavProjectExtentCm` | **500.0** | — | CALIBRATED: a large extent changes the answer, it does not widen the search |

Separation between two encounters is `aggro + leash` of the **LARGER of the
pair**, computed PER PAIR. One global radius cannot express that two scavengers
may sit closer than a scavenger and a highland beast.

### 3. ORDERED STEPS

1. Measure the reachable lattice in the editor —
   `scripts/city_reachable_lattice_payload.txt`, grid BFS. *Load-bearing: every
   query is between ADJACENT cells so none approaches the pathfinder's search
   budget. A single long query from the spawn returns FAIL when it exhausts that
   budget, which is not "no path exists".*
2. `python scripts/stamp_plan.py city/<lattice>.json`.
3. `python scripts/plan_encounters.py` — offline, seeded, byte-identical across
   runs. Writes `encounters/<region>_all.json`, stamped.
4. Verify in the editor: `scripts/city_encounter_verify_payload.txt` with
   `__LATTICE__` and `__ROWS_OUT__`. It tries the direct query then RELAYS off
   the nearest measured lattice point, and records WHICH leg answered.
5. `python scripts/adopt_verified_encounters.py --rows <rows> --write` →
   `encounters/<region>_verified.json`, stamped against BOTH sources.
6. Re-verify the ADOPTED file. It must come back with **0 unreachable**.
7. **PLACEMENT — NOT RUN.** Spawning wilderness content is behind
   `WORLD_VISION` item 4's POI tripwire, which reserves reconfirmation to the
   operator.

**Independent instrument:** the planner reads the HEIGHTMAP; the gate reads the
BUILT NAVMESH, which is collision-derived. Checking reachability against the
heightmap would be one source checked twice — precisely how this project
rendered `alpine_heightmap_v2` while COLLIDING v1 for three days with every gate
green.

|---|---|---|
| available ground | 109,307 of 256,027 cells = 27.87 km² | > 0 |
| placed | 320 of target 320 | ≥ `max(floor, 0.8 × target)` |
| by archetype | scavenger 210, raider_camp 82, highland_beast 28 | all archetypes reachable at their elevations |
| separation | per-pair, tightest above requirement | 0 violations |
| in-editor verify, plan | 317 of 320 reachable | — |
| in-editor verify, ADOPTED | **317 of 317, 0 unreachable** | 0 |
| controls | positive reaches, a point 50 km out does not | both must hold |
| determinism | byte-identical across two runs | exact |

Offline proof that the SUCCESS path works at all, in a synthetic world:

from the OUTPUT by code that did not place the rows, plus a negative control
(separation ×60) that must REFUSE and write nothing.

**A REFLECTED CLASS IS NOT A WORKING FEATURE.** `AEncounterMarker` and the
director are reflected and their properties read back on a cold boot. No marker
actor exists in any level, the director has never ticked against one, and unit

speed, nav data resident before the marker — HAS NOT RUN.

### 5. REJECTED

## R-SURFACE — WHAT AM I STANDING ON, ON THE CPU (2026-08-27)

**Status: PROVEN, with one pair explicitly NOT separated.** The acceptance
clause is met for Snow against both other layers, by a render -- a different
representation from the weightmap the lookup and the material share. **Rock
against Grass is corroborated only by PROVENANCE**, differing by 0.0124 in mean
luma inside a 0.10-0.12 standard deviation. `PHASE2_PLAN` unit 11.

New element type: a **CPU surface-type lookup** — for footstep audio, movement
modifiers and VFX, answered without asking the renderer.

### 1. PRECONDITIONS

- `textures/<biome>_weights.png` exists, baked by `make_layer_weightmap.py`.
  **It is the material's own source and must not be re-derived here.**
- The recipe declares exactly **three** `material.layers`, in channel order
  R, G, B. `make_layer_weightmap` refuses at four for the same reason: RGB has
  three channels and there is no fourth.
- numpy, Pillow. No editor. No plugins.
- Every layer carries a `surface` key naming its photogrammetry set, or the
  query can report a layer and not a material.

### 2. EXACT VALUES

| Parameter | Locked | Range | What it affects |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--samples` | **20000** | ≥ 1000 | size of the positive control |
| `--seed` | **20260827** | any | which points the control draws; printed so any run is reproducible |
| blend-boundary threshold | **dominance < 16** | 0–255 | what the query calls `on_blend_boundary` |
| R channel | dominant layer index, recipe order | 0..N-1 | the answer |
| G channel | dominance = winner − runner-up | 0..255 | blend depth |
| B channel | **0, DECLARED INERT** | — | non-negotiable 21 |

Measured on `alpine_8k`: Snow **21.3758%**, Rock **37.3012%**, Grass
**41.3230%**; dominance p10 167 / p50 255 / p90 255; genuine blend boundary
**1.04%** of the map.

**DOMINANCE IS BLEND DEPTH, NOT CONFIDENCE.** The material blends; it does not
choose. A cell at dominance 4 is genuinely half rock and half grass, and a
consumer wanting one answer there is asking a question the world does not have.
The query returns the weights so the caller can decide.

### 3. ORDERED STEPS

1. `python scripts/bake_surface_lookup.py` — report only. Read the layer shares
   against expectation before writing anything.
2. `python scripts/bake_surface_lookup.py --write` — writes
   `textures/<biome>_surface.png` and its sidecar. **Both controls must pass or
   nothing is written.**
3. `python scripts/stamp_plan.py textures/<biome>_surface.json`.
4. `python scripts/surface_query.py --selftest`.
5. Query: `python scripts/surface_query.py --at X_CM Y_CM`.

### 4. VERIFICATION

| Check | Measured | Bar |
|---|---|---|
| POSITIVE control — N points re-derived straight from the weightmap by code that did not build the arrays | **20000 of 20000** | 100% |
| NEGATIVE control — the same lookup shifted ONE ROW must stop agreeing | **9.86% disagree** | > 1% |
| round trip — R channel survives the PNG write | equal | exact (PNG is lossless) |
| inert B reads back zero | zero | exact |
| selftest — a TAMPERED sha256 in the sidecar is REFUSED | refused | must refuse |
| selftest — 50 km off the landscape returns **None** | None | not a surface |
| sanity — the town plaza reads Grass at dominance 255 | Grass 255 | a town is sited on meadow |

**THE ACCEPTANCE CLAUSE, MET BY A DIFFERENT REPRESENTATION.** Every check above
compares the lookup to the material's INPUT -- the same weightmap -- and
non-negotiable 0 says instruments sharing a source are one measurement. A
top-down RENDER is the material's OUTPUT.
`python scripts/verify_surface_against_render.py --frame <top-down png>`:

    samples 30,000   usable 10,881 (36.3%)   off the landscape 19,006
    Snow  0.7703      Rock  0.7064      Grass  0.6940   (mean linear luma)
    Snow brighter than Rock  +0.0638      than Grass  +0.0763   bar 0.02

**⛔ AND ROCK AGAINST GRASS IS NOT SEPARATED BY IT** -- 0.0124 apart against
standard deviations of 0.10-0.12, inside the noise. The tool deliberately does
not assert that pair. So Snow is corroborated by two representations and the
Rock/Grass distinction rests on PROVENANCE alone; separating it would need
chroma rather than luma, or a flat-lit rig.

Only 36.3% of samples are usable, because a 90 deg frame from 9 km covers
16.9 x 10.6 km against an 8.1 km landscape. Reported, not hidden -- the tool
refuses below 20%, because a filter that removes most of the data cannot
support a conclusion.

### 5. REJECTED

- **Painting landscape layers to get this.** It forks the surface definition —
  the painted layers and the baked weightmap become two sources for one physical
  fact. `PHASE2_PLAN` unit 11 names it; non-negotiable 19 is the general rule.
- **Deriving the surface from slope and height at query time.** That is a SECOND
  implementation of the selection the weightmap already encodes, and it would
  drift the moment a band moved.
- **Reading `dominance` as confidence in the lookup.** It is a property of the
  WORLD, not of the bake. Low dominance means "the material draws both here".
- **Asking this for WALKABILITY.** `IsWalkable` reads
  `HitComponent->GetWalkableSlopeOverride()`, a **PER-COMPONENT** override, and
  one landscape component here is 254 m square. "Scree is unwalkable" is
  gameplay logic on top of the query, never a landscape setting.
- **Leaving the B channel unwritten.** A channel nobody assigns carries whatever
  the allocator left, reads like data, and is sampled by something eventually
  (non-negotiable 21). It is written zero AND the code says so.

## R-CITY — AMENDED 2026-08-27: THE SLABS ARE SEATED, AND THE SAVE DELETES

**Status: PROVEN.** Two additions to the procedure, both measured.

### SEATING A STREET SLAB

`plan_city.street_seat(T, cx, cy, yaw_deg, len_cm, width_cm)` fits a plane
through the slab's four corners and returns `(pitch_deg, roll_deg)`. ONE helper,
called by both the ring and the spoke branch.

    over all 838 streets    centre gap        worst corner gap
    flat                    p50   0.3 cm      p50 67.9  p90 141.5  max 442.0
    seated                  p50  -0.0 cm      p50 10.9  p90  55.9  max 185.9
    corners over 50 cm      558  ->  107

**ROLL IS NEGATED IN THE PLACER, NOT IN THE PLAN.** The plan stores the ground
plane's slope in the plane fit's own right-handed sense — a physical fact. UE is
left-handed with Z up, so `city_place_payload` passes `-roll_deg` and
`+pitch_deg` into `Rotator(ROLL, PITCH, YAW)`.

The residual after seating is the terrain's CURVATURE across the slab, which a
flat box cannot follow at all. Removing it needs conforming geometry or shorter
segments and is NOT what this does.

### THE SAVE IS PART OF THE PROCEDURE, AND IT IS `save_level.py`

A commit run destroys the prior tagged actors and places new ones.
**Destroying an actor does NOT remove its package.** Measured after one
re-place: 4,713 packages on disk against 3,266 live actors — 1,447 orphans. A
cold boot would have drawn the town and every encounter marker twice.

`get_dirty_content_packages()` returns **0** for a package pending deletion, so
it cannot be used to decide this. `save_level.py --save` enumerates the world's
own package list, names the deletions as OWNED, and commits them. After it:
3,266 on disk, 3,266 in world.

### VERIFICATION

| Check | Measured | Bar |
|---|---|---|
| plan reproduces byte-identically | `13ad8ee53319ffac` over three runs | exact |
| city verify against the live world | ok true, 1446 by kind, mismatch {} | no mismatch |
| grounding, ground-sitting kinds | p50 -0.0, max 0.0 cm over 60 traces | < 5 cm |
| street corner gap, from PLACED transforms | p50 10.9 cm | was 67.9 |
| disk packages == live actors | 3266 == 3266 | exact |

## R-CITY REJECTED — additions 2026-08-27

**Judging slab grounding from a trace under the actor's ORIGIN.** SYMPTOM:
`base_above_ground max 0.0 cm` on a town whose streets visibly float, with
daylight under the edges in an eye-level frame. The reading is TRUE and about a
point; a slab is not a point (non-negotiable 22). CORRECT: trace the four
CORNERS of the oriented rectangle, over every street, not a resample.
REFERENCE: measured p50 67.9 cm at the corners against 0.3 cm at the centre, on
the same 838 slabs.

**Measuring the seating fix from the PLAN's centre Z.** SYMPTOM: byte-identical
corner-gap statistics before and after a fix that had demonstrably reached the
world (838 of 838 actors carrying a tilt, max 22.69°). The quantity — ground
height at a corner minus the slab's CENTRE height — is invariant under rotating
the slab, so the instrument could not have moved. CORRECT: compute the corner's
slab-surface height from the ACTOR'S OWN transform (location, rotation, scale)
read out of the world, and carry a positive control on the input so a run with
no tilt anywhere cannot be read as a clean result.

**Deriving the engine's roll/pitch signs by reasoning.** SYMPTOM: an analytically
correct plane fit that seated the slabs on paper (p50 14.1 against flat's 45.9)
and barely moved the placed world (60.0 against flat's 67.9). CORRECT: apply
each candidate convention to the PLACED actors and re-trace — rotating in place
costs one payload where re-placing 1,142 actors per variant costs four
placements. Adopted `p+ r-` at p50 10.9; the other three scored 60.0, 85.6 and
130.6, and two of them were WORSE than flat. REFERENCE: `unreal.Rotator` is
(ROLL, PITCH, YAW) and has been got wrong three times in this project; this is
the fourth and the first settled by measurement.

**Trusting `get_dirty_content_packages()` to decide whether a placement
persisted.** SYMPTOM: `ok true`, `counted_in_world 1446`, 0 dirty packages, and
1,447 orphaned files on disk that would have doubled the town on a cold boot.
CORRECT: `save_level.py --save`, which enumerates the world's package list
including pending DELETIONS, and verify against the filesystem — `git status`
and a package count — never against the editor's reply.

## R-CITYSHOT — CAPTURING THIS WORLD FROM THE EDITOR VIEWPORT (2026-08-27)

**Status: PROVEN, with one unresolved editor fault declared.**
`scripts/city_shot_payload.txt`. Two frames delivered:
`_verify/20260827_kit/CITY_oblique_seated.png` and `PLAZA_eyelevel.png`.

### THE PROCEDURE

1. **`ShowFlag.Volumes 0`** before anything else. This world carries 72
   `NavMeshBoundsVolume` actors and they DRAW in the editor viewport — the
   2026-08-27 oblique has orange wireframes across its entire sky. It is an
   editor artefact, not the world, and it ruins any frame taken for review.
   `ShowFlag.Navigation 0` alongside it.
2. **Trace the ground under an ad-hoc camera before using it.** Measured
   18671.8 cm at the PlayerStart; eye level is that + ~175.
3. Foreground the editor.
4. Run the shot. **Nothing else touches the editor while it runs.**
5. **Judge by a NEW FILE ON DISK, never by the payload's verdict** — see below.
6. Check the frame is tonally non-trivial (mean, std, blown, black) BEFORE
   reading anything into it, then OPEN it.

### VALUES THAT WORK

    oblique      loc (-208000, 272000, 24500)  rot (0, -14, 62)   mult 1
    eye level    loc (-210800, 278800, 18850)  rot (0,  -3, 35)   mult 1
    output       1242 x 1322 at mult 1
    oblique      luma mean 0.4864  std 0.2294  blown 0.000%
    eye level    luma mean 0.2660  std 0.2037  blown 0.000%

### ⛔ THE WATCHER'S DEADLINE IS A BUDGET, NOT A VERDICT

**BOTH frames of 2026-08-27c landed AFTER their payload had given up**, each at
the same 841 s deadline including its 240 s grace, each exiting 1 and reporting
`ok` false. Three of three across two sessions: the watcher has never once been
right about whether a frame exists.

The world gained 72 nav volumes, 64 chunk actors and 317 markers on 2026-08-27
and the payload's budget predates all of it. The camera itself is not in doubt —
the payload's own read-back reports `max_loc_err_cm` 0.0 and `max_rot_err_deg`
0.0, so it fails only on the WAIT.

**Poll for a file newer than the last known frame; do not trust the reply.**

### ⛔ AND A COMPLETED SHOT WEDGES THE EDITOR — UNRESOLVED

Three captures, two sessions, same ending every time: the frame is written, then
the editor drops to **0.01–0.02 CPU-seconds per wall-second** with
`Responding=False` and stops serving remote execution. Not a render stall (the
frame exists). Not a modal (every visible window enumerated all three times:
only `UnrealWindow` and the console).

**IT RECOVERS AFTER 630 SECONDS.** Measured 2026-08-27c by polling `bootstrap.py`
until remote execution answered. An earlier draft of this recipe said "after
some hours" — inferred from a PID being healthy at the start of a later session,
which is an interval CONTAINING the recovery rather than a measurement of it.
The difference matters operationally: 10.5 minutes is a wait, hours is a
session-ender.

**Consequence for planning: take editor measurements FIRST and render LAST** —
or budget ~11 minutes of dead channel after each frame. Both carry-over checks
deferred by the wedge on 2026-08-27c ran clean once it lifted.

## R-CITY — AMENDED 2026-08-27d: THE PLAZA CLEARS AS A DISC, AND THE SPAWN CONE IS A TRACE

**Status: PROVEN.** Two additions.

### THE PLAZA CLEAR

`city_clear_foliage_payload.txt` gains `PLAZA_MARGIN_M`, from
`recipes/city.json` → `foliage_clearing.plaza_margin_m` = **6.0**.

    dry run    16 instances inside the disc
               Norway spruce 5 · Scots pine 3 · spruce_half 4 · spruce_small 4
    committed  removed 16 · mismatches [] · still_inside_after 0
    on disk    ONE package changed — all four components live in the single
               foliage actor covering the plaza
    control    PLAZA_MARGIN_M 0.0 removes nothing; the per-structure clear is
               idempotent and unchanged

**THE DISC IS DERIVED, NEVER DECLARED TWICE.** The cleared radius is
`plan.plaza_radius_cm + plaza_margin_m`. A `plaza_clear_radius_m` field would be
a second number for the plaza's size and would diverge the first time the plaza
was resized (non-negotiable 19). This required `plan_city` to EMIT
`plaza_radius_cm`, a value it already used to reject buildings and never
recorded; the payload REFUSES if the plan lacks it rather than defaulting,
because a guessed radius cuts a differently-sized hole and reports success.

**WHY A DISC IS CORRECT HERE AND NOWHERE ELSE IN THIS RECIPE.** The block's own
warning — *"IT FOLLOWS THE TOWN SHAPE, NOT A RADIUS"* — is about the town
EXTENT, whose true shape is the terrain's, and it stands. The plaza is a
DECLARED CIRCLE, so clearing it as one matches its geometry rather than imposing
one. Both readings sit together in the recipe so the exception is documented
where the rule is.

### THE SPAWN CONE

`scripts/spawn_cone_payload.txt`. 61 rays, ±45°, 30 m, eye height 175 cm above
TRACED ground, on the PlayerStart's own yaw.

    CLEAR          48 of 61
    blocked        13, ALL the same actor
    that actor     City_Landmark — confirmed by label and tags
    nearest        25.5 m (the tower's near face; centre 29.2 m)
    FOLIAGE HITS   ZERO

**Its polarity is the OPPOSITE of every other trace here.** The grounding traces
EXCLUDE foliage and city actors because they ask where the LANDSCAPE is. This
asks what stands in front of the player, so foliage is included — and landscape
hits are tallied SEPARATELY so rising terrain cannot inflate the blocked count.

**It refuses unless there is exactly one `PlayerStart`**: UE picks among several
unpredictably, so a cone measured at one of them is not the cone the player gets.

**Expecting the per-structure clear to reach the plaza.** SYMPTOM: a conifer
3–4 m in front of the PlayerStart after the clear had run twice and reported
success both times — and both reports were TRUE. The clear tests instances
against BUILDINGS, STREETS and the LANDMARK; the plaza is DEFINED as ground with
no structures on it, so nothing inside it was ever a candidate, and no margin
reaches it because a margin grows outward from a structure. CORRECT: the plaza
needs its own disc, derived from the plan's declared radius. REFERENCE: a rule
scoped to the PRESENCE of a thing is blind exactly where that thing is ABSENT,
and the blind spot is invisible to the rule.

**Reading the "not a radius" warning as a ban on discs everywhere.** SYMPTOM:
none yet — recorded before it cost anything. The warning is about the town
EXTENT and is correct there. Applying it to the plaza would leave the spawn
facing a trunk in deference to a rule about a different shape. CORRECT: a
warning written against one shape must say which shape, and an exception belongs
beside the rule rather than in a commit message.

**Answering "is the spawn clear" with a render.** SYMPTOM: ~840 s per frame on
this world plus a ~630 s remote-exec wedge afterwards, for a judgement rather
than a number, that cannot be re-run cheaply after a foliage change. CORRECT: a

## R-CITY — AMENDED 2026-08-29: `storey_m` IS A QUANTISATION STEP, AND IT IS NOW THE KIT'S COURSE

**Ruled by the operator 2026-08-29: `buildings.storey_m` 3.2 -> 2.0.** The kit's
wall modules are all 2.00 m tall, measured live on 15 meshes
(`Free/_measured/kit_medievalvillage.json`), so the town now stands a whole
number of courses and can be built from the kit without a cut top course.

### THE VALUE, AND WHY IT IS NOT WHAT IT LOOKS LIKE

`storey_m` is **NOT a floor height multiplied by a fixed storey count.** It is a
**quantisation step**. `plan_city.py:392-395`:

    f       = d / R_cm
    h       = (hc + (he - hc) * f) * 100      # CONTINUOUS, 14.0 m -> 6.5 m
    storeys = max(1, int(round(h / (storey_m * 100))))
    h       = storeys * storey_m * 100        # snapped

The planner holds the HEIGHT and derives the COUNT. Changing `storey_m`
re-quantises the same continuous heights onto a finer grid.

### MEASURED EFFECT — the whole town, before and after

    heights   6.4 / 9.6 / 12.8 m      ->  6 / 8 / 10 / 12 m
    counts    51 / 164 / 88           ->  19 / 73 / 113 / 98
    courses   3.20 / 4.80 / 6.40      ->  3 / 4 / 5 / 6      EXACT
    mean      9.99 m                  ->  9.91 m             -0.8%
    max snap error vs the declared falloff   1.59 m -> 1.00 m   HALVED
    distinct heights                          3 -> 4

**It is strictly CLOSER to what `height_m` already declares** (centre 14.0,
edge 6.5), not further.

### WHAT DID NOT MOVE — the control that mattered

    building XY          identical, 303 of 303
    building FOOTPRINT   identical, 303 of 303   <- reachability depends on this
    building yaw, pad_z  identical
    streets, landmark, spire, counts   identical
    roofs                XY identical, z moved on all 303 (they sit on walls)

Only `buildings`, `roofs` and `_input_sha256` differ at the top level.

### VERIFICATION

- Positive control BEFORE the change: heights reconstructed from building
  positions reproduced the shipped plan **exactly, 0 mismatches of 303**. That
  is what makes the predicted after-state trustworthy rather than arithmetic.
- `check_plan_freshness --reproduce`: the plan REPRODUCES, stamp MATCHES.
- The reachability sidecar carries a DECLARED, NARROW `_stamp_waiver` (below).

### REJECTED

- **WRONG VALUE TO FEAR: that `storey_m` -> 2.00 cuts the town 33%**, taking
  2/3/4-storey buildings from 6.4/9.6/12.8 m to 4/6/8 m. SYMPTOM: the ruling
  refused on a cost that does not exist. ROOT CAUSE: reading `storey_m` as a
  per-floor height with the STOREY COUNT held fixed; the planner does the
  opposite. CORRECT: the mean height falls **0.8%**. REFERENCE:
  `_verify/20260828_kit/COVERAGE.md` correction banner, 2026-08-29.
- **WRONG: annotating a recipe "for free".** Writing notes into
  `recipes/city.json` moves its SHA-256 and invalidates every downstream stamp.
  SYMPTOM: `city/alpine_basin_town_reachable.json` reports STAMP DIFFERS, and
  refreshing it needs an in-editor payload. CORRECT: batch recipe annotations
  with a change that moves the hash anyway, or keep them out of the hashed file.

### THE WAIVER MECHANISM (new, `check_plan_freshness.py`)

`check_plan_freshness`'s refusal has always said *"Re-run the producer, or
record why the artefact is kept"* — **and there was nowhere to record it**, so
the only way to keep a green suite was to excuse the whole exit code, which
masks the next genuine staleness in the same tool.

A plan may now carry `_stamp_waiver` = `{inputs, why, recorded, retire_when}`.
It is deliberately narrow, and **proven to refuse in four directions** by
`--self-test`:

    waiver naming the differing input      -> WAIVED
    ...but NOT a second, unnamed input     -> STALE
    waiver naming the WRONG input          -> STALE
    waiver with no reason given            -> STALE
    no waiver at all                       -> STALE

It never applies to `UNREADABLE` (that is *"I could not look"*) and never to a
failed `--reproduce`. It prints its reason in full on every run, so it cannot
rot quietly.

**A WAIVER IS A GATE TURNED OFF. It gets the same treatment every other gate
here gets: prove it says NO before trusting it when it says yes.**

## R-KIT — TAKING IN A VENDOR PACK BY DEPENDENCY CLOSURE (2026-08-29)

**Status: LOCKED for the file-level half, UNPROVEN in engine.** New import path,
so it earns a recipe under the new-element rule. First worked example: the
Medieval Village Megascans Sample, 15 modules, 106 packages, 942.7 MB out of a
22.6 GB pack.

### THE PROBLEM THIS SOLVES

A vendor pack is far larger than the part you need, and the part you need is not
a folder — it is a **closure**. Copying a folder gets too much and still misses
the shared master material two directories away. Copying "the meshes" gets a
mesh whose material reference dangles, which **loads well enough to measure
bounds and draws as the default checkerboard.** This project shipped a
checkerboard landscape once already.

### ORDERED STEPS

1. **R-ASSET step 1 first: source, licence and role in `ASSETS.md`.** Before any
   copying. Cheapest moment to discover you may not ship it.
2. **Seed from what you actually need** — here, the 15 measured modules.
3. **Walk every `/Game/` reference to a FIXED POINT.** A `.uasset` name table
   contains the package paths it imports, as length-prefixed strings, readable
   with no editor. `scripts/intake_kit_closure.py` and the closure walker.
4. **`DANGLING REFS: 0` IS THE ACCEPTANCE CRITERION FOR THE CLOSURE.** A closure
   that still names something missing is not closed, and the number is the
   evidence that the set is complete rather than merely large.
5. **Cost it before copying it** — packages, bytes, and which are SHARED versus
   per-item. Log free RAM and disk (pipeline rule 5).
6. **PRESERVE PACKAGE PATHS.** Copy to `Content/<same relative path>`. This is
   not cosmetic: references are by package path, so a flat copy dangles.
7. **REFUSE on any pre-existing destination.** Vendor trees overlap
   project-owned ones (`Content/Materials`, `Content/Meshes` here hold 49
   tracked files of ours). Overwriting one is a loss that looks like an import.
8. **SHA-256 both ends per file**, manifest committed as the derivative
   (NN20 — hash-proven at adoption). Source stays gitignored.
9. **`.gitignore` the vendor subtrees NARROWLY** — never a shared parent.
10. **Verify resolution offline**: every `/Game/` reference in every copied
    package resolves inside `Content`. `scripts/verify_kit_closure.py`.
11. **R-ASSET steps 6–7: spawn and RENDER before `verified in engine` flips.**

### VERIFICATION — what was actually run

    closure walk        106 packages, 0 dangling            fixed point reached
    dry run             0 missing at source, 0 collisions
    collision gate      PROVEN: a planted decoy -> exit 3 even with --go
    copy                106 files, 942.7 MB, hash-checked both ends
    independent check   sha256sum (a DIFFERENT tool from the copier's hashlib)
                        on the largest texture -> match
    filesystem          106 files, 942,685,655 bytes -- counted, not reported
    resolution          294 /Game/ refs, 0 dangling
    gitignore           0 vendor files visible to git

### REJECTED

- **WRONG: copying meshes to a flat folder.** SYMPTOM: bounds and triangle
  counts read fine, so a measurement probe succeeds — and the material
  reference points at the pack's original path and resolves to nothing.
  CORRECT: preserve package paths. REFERENCE: the `_probe/` copy of 2026-08-28,
  retired 2026-08-29.
- **WRONG: `.gitignore`ing `Content/Materials/` or `Content/Meshes/` wholesale**
  to cover vendor content landing inside them. SYMPTOM: 49 tracked
  project-owned files silently untracked. CORRECT: ignore only the subtrees the
  closure creates.
- **WRONG: assuming a pack's per-item texture sets are uniform.** SYMPTOM: a
  material audit or a planner that indexes `<mesh>_N` finds nothing for some
  items and reports a defect that is the vendor's data. MEASURED here: 12 of 15
  modules carry `_A _MRF _MaskRGB _N`; two carry a separate `_R` instead of the
  packed `_MRF`; and **`Wall2x2MH` ships NO NORMAL MAP AT ALL** — its MI
  references none, so its only normal comes from the shared blend layer.
- **WRONG: applying R-ASSET's ORM-unpack rule to an adopted vendor material.**
  That rule governs SOURCE maps wired into OUR material declaration. `_MRF` and
  `_MaskRGB` arrive as imported textures wired by the vendor's own master, which
  is adopted whole; unpacking would mean rebuilding it. Recorded so the absence
  of an unpack step reads as a decision.
- **WRONG: trusting a copy report.** 942.7 MB copied and double-hashed in 1.3 s
  is fast enough to distrust. CORRECT: count the files and bytes on the
  FILESYSTEM afterwards, and re-hash with a different tool.

### R-KIT — VERIFIED IN ENGINE 2026-08-29, and R-ASSET steps 6–7 are now CLOSED

    master material   M_GlobalRGB_Blend  recompile -> 0 ERRORS
    bindings          15 of 15 bound to their own MI; 0 bound to a DEFAULT
    live read-back    the SPAWNED COMPONENT's material compared to the asset's
    frames            _verify/20260829_kit/KIT_row.png (materials),
                      KIT_row_seated.png + CROP_seated_contact.png (contact)
    tonality          mean 0.5264 / 0.3592, std 0.2213 / 0.2355, 0% blown
    provenance        all 106 packages re-hashed AFTER the session: 0 mismatches

**`bound_to_default` is compared BY PATH against the engine defaults, not merely
checked non-null.** `WorldGridMaterial` IS non-null and IS the failure — a
null-check would pass the exact state it exists to catch.

**NOTHING WAS SAVED, DELIBERATELY.** `recompile_material` dirties the master.
Saving it rewrites bytes the closure manifest has SHA-256'd, so the save would
destroy the provenance the intake was built on. Left dirty in memory; the world
was restored (15 eval actors destroyed, 1,446 city actors unhidden) and every
package re-verified against the manifest afterwards.

### R-KIT REJECTED — additions 2026-08-29

- **WRONG: a ground trace with an EMPTY ignore list.** SYMPTOM: the trace
  SUCCEEDS, returns a plausible Z, and stands 15 modules **27 metres in the
  air** — measured 2717.7–2815.4 cm. It hit the forest canopy; conifers here are
  17–33 m. Nothing refuses, because a trace that hits the wrong thing is
  indistinguishable from one that hits the right thing unless you ask WHAT it
  hit. CORRECT: trace PER item, ignoring foliage, the city and the items being
  placed — and better still, place on ground that cannot have a canopy over it.
  REFERENCE: the same class cost 17 streets a 12.9 m roof trace on 2026-08-27;
  that entry says "exclude `LandscapeLab.City` too", which reads as advice to
  someone who already HAS an ignore list. **An empty ignore list is a defect,
  not a default.**
- **WRONG: judging float from the whole frame.** SYMPTOM: modules against a
  mountain look fine; "how high is that" has no reference at that scale. CORRECT:
  crop to the base. The float was obvious only with sky and trees visible UNDER
  it, and then it was measured rather than estimated.
- **WRONG: taking the shot payload's verdict.** It exited 1 with `ok: false` over
  a 5,019 KB frame that existed. **Fourth of four** — see R-CITYSHOT. Dispatch
  the shot and POLL FOR A NEW FILE beside it; never let the verdict be
  load-bearing.

## R-DERIVEMAT — AN ALBEDO-ONLY SURFACE SET BECOMES A UE MATERIAL (2026-08-30)

**Status: PROVEN for the C0 donor house.** Seven roles, ten mesh slots, 21
textures, one master, seven instances, compiling clean with 0 orphans and 3 of
3 samplers agreeing with the engine's own `AutoSetSampleType`.

**The problem this solves:** an albedo is all you get. The C0 donor zip ships
seven Poly Haven maps and every one is a diffuse; the operator's generated
replacements are diffuses too; and Phase C1's concept-derived materials will
be diffuses as well. **Everything else has to be derived, and the derivation
must be honest about which of its outputs is a measurement.**

### THE THREE KINDS OF CLAIM, AND THEY ARE NOT INTERCHANGEABLE

    MEASURED   the normal-map CONVENTION
    DERIVED    the normal itself, from albedo luminance as a height field
    AUTHORED   the roughness base

`scripts/derive_material_maps.py` prints `roughness_is_authored: TRUE` on every
run and `recipes/c0_materials.json` carries the split in a `_measured_vs_authored`
key. A roughness map presented as a measurement is a number with no ground
truth, and this project has a rule about those.

### THE PROCEDURE

1. **Gate the albedos for tiling first** (`verify_tileable.py`), repair what
   fails (`repair_tileable.py`), re-run the gate on the OUTPUT. A non-tiling
   albedo produces a non-tiling normal and a non-tiling roughness, so this is
   the step that must not move.
2. **`derive_material_maps.py --calibrate` BEFORE deriving anything.** It must
   report 10 of 10 and a positive red control. This is a precondition, not a
   report.
3. Author `roughness_base` and `normal_strength` per role in the manifest.
4. `derive_material_maps.py --manifest <recipe>` -> `<role>_N.png`, `<role>_R.png`.
5. Import at the settings below; **read every one back**.
6. Build ONE master, mint N instances; **read every texture parameter back off
   the instance**.
7. **Capture `recompile_material`'s returned error list and REFUSE on it.**
8. Run `audit_material_connectivity` and `audit_material_samplers` — different
   code, different question.

### VALUES THAT WORK

    kind       srgb    compression        sampler                address
    albedo     True    TC_DEFAULT         SAMPLERTYPE_COLOR      TA_WRAP
    normal     False   TC_NORMALMAP       SAMPLERTYPE_NORMAL     TA_WRAP
    roughness  False   TC_MASKS           SAMPLERTYPE_MASKS      TA_WRAP

    convention          DX (green DOWN)
    highpass sigma      0.06 of the short axis for the normal's height field
                        0.02 for the roughness detail term
    normal_strength     5 (plaster) .. 12 (rock, roof tiles)
    roughness_base      0.65 (worn floor) .. 0.90 (plaster)

    master              M_C0_House: TexCoord x Tiling -> three
                        TextureSampleParameter2D -> BaseColor/Roughness/Normal
                        6 expressions, 6 reachable, 0 ORPHANED

### ⭐ THE CONVENTION IS MEASURED AGAINST THE VENDOR'S OWN LABELS

ambientCG ships `_NormalDX` AND `_NormalGL` beside one `_Displacement` for five
surfaces — ten files whose correct answer is written on them. The test never
sees the filename.

**The RED channel is the control and it is not decoration.** Red tracks
`-dH/dcol` under BOTH conventions, so it has the same expected sign either way;
green is the only discriminator. A red reading that is not strongly positive
means the instrument is broken and no verdict about green may be issued. It
caught two separate faults in one session.

### R-DERIVEMAT REJECTED

**`Image.open(p).convert("L")` ON A 16-BIT MAP.**
→ Symptom: the map reads as a CONSTANT. Ground037's displacement, real range
18770..59293, comes back **all 255**; every correlation against it is 0.000 and
the convention test reports an instrument fault.
→ Correct: `texture_16bit.load_float(path)`. It lives in the module that
already owns `DEFECT_MODES`; **a private copy in the caller is REJECTED in its
own right** (non-negotiable 4a).
→ Reference: `texture_16bit.py:38`, which stated the defect before this
happened, and its selftest, which now reproduces it.

**`corr(G, dH/drow) > 0` READ AS DIRECTX.**
→ Symptom: all ten vendor-labelled files classified backwards, with a red
control at +0.53 to +0.90.
→ Correct: **GL is the positive one.** Image rows increase downward, so
`y_up = -row` and `-dH/dy_up = +dH/drow`. DX is negative.
→ Note: the asset-intake skill states the opposite sign. The ten labelled
files outrank it, and CLAUDE.md's protocol says the lookup wins.

**TRUSTING `set_material_instance_texture_parameter_value`'s RETURN VALUE.**
→ Symptom: it returns **False on all 21 writes while all 21 land**. Second
occurrence; the first was 2026-08-16's hero face bake, six instances with
`"bound": []`.
→ Correct: `get_material_instance_texture_parameter_value` and compare names.
The setter's return is evidence in neither direction.

**DELETE-THEN-CREATE THE MASTER.**
→ Symptom: works the FIRST time; the second run returns None from
`create_asset` because the instances still reference the master, so the delete
cannot complete and the name stays taken. The message points at creation, the
cause is deletion.
→ Correct: load-if-present, then total clear. Idempotent by construction, and
what pipeline rule 3 asks for.

**SCANNING ue_exec's STDOUT FOR THE `__LL__` LINE.**
→ Symptom: "NO RESULT FROM THE EDITOR — that is 'could not look'" over a run
that entirely succeeded. `ue_exec.py:155` has already consumed the marker and
pretty-printed the payload.
→ Correct: take the outermost JSON object.

## R-CITYSHOT — AMENDED 2026-08-30: THE RECIPE SAID `ShowFlag.Volumes 0` AND THE PAYLOAD NEVER DID IT

R-CITYSHOT's step 1 has read **"`ShowFlag.Volumes 0` before anything else"**
since 2026-08-27, and `scripts/city_shot_payload.txt` — the one payload every
editor render of this world passes through — **never issued the command.**
CURRENT STATE says the same thing twice more, as "every future editor render of
this world needs it".

So the requirement existed in three places in prose and in none in code, and
the next render would have carried the orange nav wireframes exactly as the
2026-08-27 oblique did. **This is non-negotiable 24 between a RECIPE and its
TOOL:** two places that must agree, no single declaration, and the drift is
invisible because the prose half keeps reading correctly.

Now issued in the payload, before the streaming warm-up loop.

**And the amendment cost a wasted round trip to prove a second point.** The
first edit put the command at the wrong indent level, silently splitting a
`for` body, and the payload died with `IndentationError` at line 110 — 25 s
gone. `python -c "ast.parse(...)"` on the substituted payload costs nothing and
now precedes any render. **A payload is a call site with no compiler; give it
one.**
