## R-AIGATE — AN ASSET THAT MAY NOT BE FED TO A MODEL (2026-08-30)

**Status: PROVEN.** Guard discriminates 5 refused / 4 passed; wired into both
generation scripts ahead of the model load; register, document and guard
cross-checked; both checks in the offline suite.

**The problem this solves.** A Fab listing can say **"Allows usage with AI:
No"**. That is a licence term, and it has a property almost nothing else in
this project has: **its violation cannot be detected after the fact.** A
generated mesh carries no provenance — no hash of its inputs, no manifest, no
trace. There is no artefact to inspect afterwards and nothing to revert. The
only moment the check can work is *before the model runs*.

### THE PROCEDURE

1. **Record the restriction in `recipes/ai_restrictions.json`** — the single
   machine-readable source. Four kinds of path, because the operator's ruling
   covers all four: `source_globs`, `packages`, `levels`, `render_globs`.
2. **Never write the rule into a document as its only home.** ASSETS.md carries
   the human-readable row; `check_ai_restrictions.py` asserts the two agree.
3. **Call `ai_input_guard.py --strict <input>` at the top of every generation
   script**, under `set -e`, so a refusal aborts before the model loads.
4. **Both checks go in the offline suite**, so the guard is exercised on every
   run and not only when someone edits the register.
5. **Prove the retrospective case too**: run the guard over every input that
   has already reached a model, and record the result.

### VALUES THAT WORK

    exit 0   cleared          exit 2   no input given (not a pass)
    exit 3   REFUSED          exit 4   guard does not discriminate

    self-test    5 restricted refused, 4 legitimate passed
    live proof   WSL, mounted paths, the exact call the scripts make:
                 restricted FBX -> exit 3 (aborts the run)
                 concept-art crop -> exit 0

### ⛔ FAIL CLOSED, AND WHY THAT IS RIGHT **HERE** SPECIFICALLY

`--strict` refuses anything not positively cleared, not merely what matches a
restriction. Everywhere else this project says a broken gate must report *"I
could not measure"*; here it must additionally **decline to proceed**, because
the costs are asymmetric: a false refusal costs a re-run and a question, a
false pass costs an irreversible, undetectable licence violation.

### R-AIGATE REJECTED

**PUTTING THE RESTRICTION ONLY IN `ASSETS.md`.**
→ Symptom: nothing happens. The rule is enforced by whoever remembers to read
the document, which is the same class as R-CITYSHOT specifying
`ShowFlag.Volumes 0` in prose that the payload never issued for three days.
→ Correct: the register is the source, the guard reads it, a checker asserts
the document matches.

**GUARDING ONLY THE SCRIPT YOU ARE WORRIED ABOUT.**
→ Symptom: `run_control.sh` uses a bundled MIT example and "obviously" needs no
check, so it gets none — and the next script copied from it inherits the gap.
→ Correct: guard every generation entry point. A guard that runs only where
someone remembered to put it is not a guard.

**READING A `0` IN A SPARSELY-POPULATED RECORD AS A FINDING.**
→ Symptom: the Fab DB's `is_ai_forbidden` reads 0 for the Medieval Village kit,
which looks like "AI permitted". The row has an empty description, no tags, no
formats and 0 reviews, so the 0 is indistinguishable from an unset default.
→ Correct: record it as an OBSERVATION, not evidence. NN21 — an inert field
reads exactly like a set one.

**TREATING AN ABSENT LAUNCHER RECORD AS A LICENCE ANSWER.**
→ Symptom: `medieval_houses_10` is not in `listings_v1.db`, which invites
"so it is not in the library". The DB caches only launcher downloads — the C0
donor is legitimately absent too, and it *is* owned.
→ Correct: report UNKNOWN, and restrict precautionarily where the author's
other work carries an AI prohibition.

## R-CITYSHOT — AMENDED 2026-08-30b: THE WATCHER BLOCKS THE THREAD IT IS WATCHING, AND THE WEDGE IS THE SAME EVENT

**Status of the old text: two of its three unexplained faults are now one
explained fault.** R-CITYSHOT has carried, since 2026-08-27, a "watcher deadline
is a budget not a verdict" section and a separate "⛔ AND A COMPLETED SHOT WEDGES
THE EDITOR — UNRESOLVED" section. **They are not two phenomena.**

### THE MECHANISM

`city_shot_payload.txt` waits for its own screenshot in a
`_time.sleep(1.0)` loop. That payload runs inside the editor via
`MODE_EXEC_FILE`, **on the game thread**. `HighResShot` does not render
synchronously — it sets a flag, and the tiled capture completes over
**subsequent engine ticks**.

**A blocked game thread cannot tick, so the frame cannot be written until the
watcher gives up.** The watcher is waiting for an event that its own waiting
prevents. It is structurally incapable of ever observing success.

### THE MEASUREMENTS THAT ESTABLISH IT

**Six for six**, across four sessions, the frame lands ~1 s AFTER the payload
declares it absent:

    2026-08-30 iter0   issued 19:11:58.122   gave up 19:25:59.442 (841.3 s)
                       frame written 19:26:00.244    -- 0.8 s later
    2026-08-30 iter1   issued 19:52:40.780   gave up ~20:06:41    (841.0 s)
                       frame on disk 20:06:43         -- ~2 s later

**The log itself is the independent instrument.** `LogEOSSDK` writes a
heartbeat on a ~320-355 s schedule (the line states its own
`Update Interval`). During a capture block there is **no log line of any
kind**:

    heartbeats 19:31:59 / 19:37:26 / 19:43:10 / 19:49:31, then NOTHING
    for the 14 minutes from `Cmd: HighResShot 1` to the payload's return

A missing periodic heartbeat is a measurement of a stalled game thread, taken
with an instrument that has nothing to do with the payload or its client.

### ⛔ THE FOREGROUND HYPOTHESIS IS DISCONFIRMED — LOGGED AS LOUDLY AS IT WOULD HAVE BEEN PROMOTED

R-CITYSHOT step 3 says "Foreground the editor." It was proposed that a
BACKGROUNDED editor throttles its tick rate and that this explained the ~14
minute captures. **Tested directly and it does not.**

    iter0   backgrounded   editor 0.017 cpu-s/wall-s   841.3 s   848 s to disk
    iter1   FOREGROUNDED   editor ~2.2  cpu-s/wall-s   841.0 s   ~843 s to disk

**A 100× difference in editor CPU and opposite window focus produced a ~5 s
difference in a ~845 s wait**, inside the measuring poller's own 3 s
resolution. Duration is set by **the payload's deadline**, not by render cost
and not by focus. Foregrounding remains in the recipe as good practice; it is
**not** the explanation for anything, and no before/after numbers should be
cited for it.

### THE FIX, NOT YET APPLIED

Do not wait for the frame **on the game thread**. Issue `HighResShot`, return
from the payload immediately, and poll the screenshot directory **from the
host**, where sleeping costs the editor nothing. The client already knows how —
every session has ended up doing it by hand.

### AND THE `OUTDIR` COPY HAS NEVER ONCE RUN

`city_shot_payload.txt:233` copies the frame to `OUTDIR/NAME.png`. It sits
**after** the `raise RuntimeError(...)` on the absent-frame path. Since the
watcher has never succeeded, **the copy is dead code** and every frame in
`_verify/` this project owns was placed there by hand. A self-banking step
that has never executed reads, in the source, exactly like one that works.

## R-CITYSHOT REJECTED — ADDITIONS 2026-08-30b

**WAITING FOR THE SCREENSHOT INSIDE THE EDITOR.**
→ SYMPTOM: `"ok": false, "no new screenshot appeared ... after 841 s"` over a
frame that lands ~1 s later; the editor appears "wedged" at 0.01-0.02
cpu-s/wall-s with a frozen log for the whole interval; ~14 minutes of dead
remote-exec channel per frame.
→ CAUSE: `_time.sleep()` in the payload blocks the game thread; the tiled
`HighResShot` needs ticks it cannot get.
→ CORRECT: return from the payload after issuing the command and poll from the
host.
→ REFERENCE: six occurrences, 2026-08-27 through 2026-08-30; the `LogEOSSDK`
heartbeat gap; iter0 vs iter1 with focus inverted and duration unchanged.

**EXPLAINING THE CAPTURE DURATION BY WINDOW FOCUS OR TICK THROTTLING.**
→ SYMPTOM: a plausible before/after CPU table that measures nothing — the
"after" column was a foregrounded viewport redrawing, not a blocked render.
→ CORRECT: the deadline governs. Test focus by holding it constant and varying
nothing else, as was eventually done.
→ REFERENCE: iter0 848 s backgrounded vs iter1 843 s foregrounded.

**PASSING A RENDER-SIZED `--timeout` TO `ue_exec.py`.**
→ SYMPTOM: nothing happens for the full timeout — no `CONFIRM` line, no
`ShowFlag`, no `HighResShot`, client idle at 0.09 CPU — and it reads exactly
like a wedged editor.
→ CAUSE: `--timeout` is the **discovery window** and is spent in full
(`ue_exec.py:174`). It has nothing to do with how long the payload runs.
→ CORRECT: **12-25.** The payload's own duration is not governed by this flag.
→ REFERENCE: 2026-08-30, `--timeout 1200` cost 20 minutes; the tool printed its
NOTE and the warning was swallowed by a `| tail` on a backgrounded command.

**FILTERING THE OUTPUT OF A COMMAND WHOSE WARNINGS ARE WHY IT IS SAFE.**
→ SYMPTOM: an empty output file read three times as evidence about the editor.
→ CORRECT: never `| tail` / `| head` / `| grep` a long-running or backgrounded
command that prints guards at the point of use. Let it print.
→ REFERENCE: LESSONS.md 2026-08-30, the `--timeout` entry above.

**RESIZING THE EDITOR WINDOW BETWEEN SHOTS IN A SERIES.**
→ SYMPTOM: two frames of the same subject at 2032×1273 and 1263×1349 that
cannot be diffed — `highres_shot.py` calls that a different CALIBRATION CLASS.
→ CAUSE: `ShowWindow(h, SW_RESTORE)` while foregrounding resized the viewport;
`HighResShot` captures the active viewport.
→ CORRECT: park the viewport size before a series, or do not touch the window
between its frames.
→ REFERENCE: 2026-08-30 concept iter0/iter1 pair.

## R-CITYSHOT — AMENDED 2026-08-30c: THE WAIT IS ON THE HOST NOW, AND `scripts/shoot.py` IS THE ENTRY POINT

**Status: BUILT, self-tested, NOT YET PROVEN AGAINST A LIVE EDITOR.** The fix
approved after the 2026-08-30b diagnosis. It is locked as a PROCEDURE only
once a real frame comes back through it — frames 3 and 4 of the render batch
are that proof.

### THE NEW PROCEDURE

    python scripts/shoot.py --name <name> \
        --loc " x,y,z" --rot "roll,pitch,yaw" --fov <deg|0> --mult 1 \
        --outdir _verify/<dated dir>

**Do not call `ue_exec.py` on `city_shot_payload.txt` by hand any more.** The
payload now returns the instant it has issued `HighResShot`, so calling it
directly gets you an `ok:true` and no frame.

**`ok` means two different things on purpose:**

    payload   ok = ISSUED      the console command was accepted
    shoot.py  ok = ON DISK     a new png appeared and its size settled

The old defect was a tool issuing a verdict about a file it could not observe.
The names now say which question is being answered.

**A leading space in a negative `--loc`** (`--loc " -4500,0,900"`) stops
argparse reading it as a flag.

### WHAT CHANGED IN THE PAYLOAD

The `_time.sleep()` watch loop, the 240 s grace pass, the
`raise RuntimeError("no new screenshot appeared...")` and the `OUTDIR` copy
are **all gone**. The payload now hands back `shots_dir` and `before` — the
directory listing taken in the editor immediately before the command — so the
host diffs against that exact listing rather than re-deriving it and racing an
unrelated capture.

Everything BEFORE the shot is unchanged and still mandatory: `ShowFlag.Volumes
0` / `Grid 0` / `Navigation 0`, the camera read-back assertion, the FOV
read-back, the ground trace, and the selection clear.

### VALUES THAT WORK

    ue_exec --timeout        25      DISCOVERY window, spent in full
    shoot.py --deadline    1800      HOST-side, costs the editor nothing
    MIN_FRAME_BYTES       10000      one declaration, poller and caller
    self-test              7 cases, in the offline suite

## R-CITYSHOT REJECTED — ADDITIONS 2026-08-30c

**AN INNER WAIT LOOP THAT DOES NOT CHECK THE OUTER DEADLINE.**
→ SYMPTOM: the poller runs forever on a test whose longest deadline is 15 s.
Nothing is logged; it simply never returns, and from outside it looks exactly
like the editor problem it was written to fix.
→ CAUSE: `poll_for_frame`'s settle loop was `while True` with the exit
condition `cur == size and cur > 10000`. A file that settles BELOW the floor —
a truncated or empty capture, which is exactly what lands in a screenshot
directory — satisfies the first half forever and the second never.
→ CORRECT: bound every wait on EVERY path out, with the same deadline the
caller passed; and fold a settled-but-too-small file into `before` so the next
sweep looks past it instead of re-picking the same dud.
→ REFERENCE: found by `shoot.py --self-test` on its first run, 2026-08-30,
before any live shot. LESSONS.md, same date.

**SHIPPING A REPLACEMENT INSTRUMENT WITHOUT A POSITIVE CONTROL.**
→ SYMPTOM: the new tool is trusted because the old one's defect is understood.
→ CORRECT: three directions — it FINDS the thing, it REFUSES what is not the
thing, and it REFUSES TO CLAIM EARLY. Understanding a failure class does not
immunise the code written to fix it; the replacement here shipped with a
non-terminating loop written by someone who had just root-caused the original.
→ REFERENCE: `check_plan_freshness.py` is currently failing its own positive
control while all nine of its mutation cases pass — the state this entry
exists to prevent repeating.

**Status: PROVEN.** 12 self-test cases, positive control first, standalone.
`python scripts/check_plan_freshness.py --self-test` -> exit 0.

### THE PROCEDURE

    --self-test   proves the INSTRUMENT. Synthetic fixture in a temp tree.
                  STANDALONE -- never touches the corpus. Exit 0 = the tool

    (no flag)     audits the corpus by HISTORY + stamp.  Exit 3 = something

**Two suite entries, two questions.** "Does this tool work?" and "is the corpus
fresh?" must never share an exit code.

### VALUES THAT WORK

    fixture       temp tree, files written then stamped then verified in the
                  same call -- MATCHES by construction, nothing can move
                  between the stamp and the check
    cases         12: positive control, hash corrupted, ONLY that input named,

                  with a missing input, and 5 waiver directions
    live plan     REPORTED in the self-test output, never asserted on

## R-STAMP REJECTED

**A LIVE ARTEFACT AS THE POSITIVE CONTROL.**
→ SYMPTOM: `POSITIVE CONTROL (unmutated) -> DIFFERS, want MATCHES` while all
nine mutation cases pass. Reads as "the instrument is broken" and casts doubt
on every verdict it ever issued.

MATCHES. RULING 4 changed `recipes/city.json` and `scripts/plan_city.py` one
commit after the plan was stamped, so `verify` correctly returned DIFFERS. The
control and the artefact under test were the same object — never two
measurements (non-negotiable 0).

positive control must be INERT** — unable to change for reasons unrelated to

## R-CITYSHOT — AMENDED 2026-08-30d: PROVEN, AND EDITOR SPRITES JOIN THE SHOWFLAG LIST

**Status of 2026-08-30c: PROVEN.** Three levels, four shots, host-side wait.

    issued -> on disk, payload waiting on the game thread   848 s, 843 s
    issued -> on disk, wait moved to the host                 4 s, 4 s, 4 s

**The render was never slow.** ~14 minutes per frame became 4 seconds. Wall
time per shot is now 31 s, of which 25 s is `ue_exec`'s discovery window.

### STEP 1 GAINS TWO FLAGS

    ShowFlag.Volumes 0        ShowFlag.Grid 0        ShowFlag.Navigation 0
    ShowFlag.BillboardSprites 0        ShowFlag.LightRadius 0

Names verified in `ShowFlagsValues.inl` — `BillboardSprites` :213,
`LightRadius` :291.

### RESOLUTION IS PINNED IN THE COMMAND

`HighResShot` takes EITHER `WxH` OR a multiplier — `UnrealClient.cpp:2459`
parses argument 0 with `ParseResolution()` and falls back to `Atof()` only if
that fails. `shoot.py` pins **2032x1273** by default so a series is one
calibration class.

### BETWEEN LEVELS

Scratch levels need `launch_editor.ps1 -Map`. **Wait for ZERO editors before
launching the next**, then query the loaded level before shooting.

## R-CITYSHOT REJECTED — ADDITIONS 2026-08-30d

**LEAVING EDITOR BILLBOARD SPRITES ON.**
→ SYMPTOM: a DirectionalLight's editor sprite and blue arrow rendered over the
CENTRE subject of a 3-variant comparison and hid it completely. Every tonal
check passed — mean 0.6049, std 0.1873, 0.000% blown — because a sprite is

→ SYMPTOM: two editors serving the same project; discovery may answer from
either, so a shot can be taken in the wrong level and look entirely plausible.
→ CAUSE: `CloseMainWindow()` was not honoured within 20 s and the launch went
ahead anyway.

LEVEL before shooting.

→ SYMPTOM: left-to-right in the frame was assumed to be ascending X, and the
labels came out reversed — which would have reported two same-material
variants as differing MORE than a different-material one.
→ CAUSE: UE's right-vector at yaw 90 is −X, so the image mirrors the layout.
→ CORRECT: ask the level for actor positions and materials. A camera
convention is not a thing to infer from a picture.

## R-CITYSHOT — AMENDED 2026-08-30e: RENDERS ARE NO LONGER SCARCE

**Ryan, 2026-08-30, on the 848 s -> 4 s result: renders are no longer scarce,
and that changes planning.**

### THE RULE THAT RELAXES

    OLD   "Measurements and commits FIRST, renders LAST."
          A render cost ~14 minutes of dead remote-exec channel, so a batch
          was assembled and fired once, at the end, and a shot fired mid-queue
          cost 75 minutes on 2026-08-30.

    NEW   "RENDER FREELY. WEDGE-CLASS MYSTERIES ARE RETIRED."
          A frame costs 4 s of rendering (31 s wall, of which 25 s is
          ue_exec's discovery window). Three frames across three levels cost
          ~16 s of rendering in total.

**What this permits, and it is the point of the change:** a concept loop may
now take a frame PER ITERATION instead of batching to the end. The Phase B loop
was split into an "arithmetic half" precisely because "a render costs the
editor for a quarter of an hour" — that sentence is in `concept_loop.py`'s own
docstring and it is now FALSE. The loop's judgement half is affordable.

**What does NOT relax:**

* **Commit before a render** still stands — it is about having a restore point,
  not about cost.
* **The preamble and the read-back assertions** still run on every shot. Cheap
  frames make it *easier* to ship a wrong one, not harder.
* **Standing rule 11** — zero editors, then ask which level. A cheap wrong
  frame is still a wrong frame, and it is now cheap to make many of them.

### WHAT WAS RETIRED, AND IT WAS NEVER A MYSTERY

The "unexplained 630 s post-capture wedge", the watcher wrong 6 times of 6, and
a never-executed `OUTDIR` copy were **one defect**: the payload slept on the
game thread, and `HighResShot` needs ticks. Do not budget for a wedge, do not
schedule around one, and do not attribute a slow frame to the editor before
checking what is holding the game thread.

## R-FORGE — GENERATING AN ASSET, TEN STAGES (2026-08-30)

**Status: PROVEN on the church.** `python scripts/forge.py --asset <key>`.
Ratified by Ryan together with the ABSOLUTE acceptance rule.

    1  check_generation_input.py     measured input floors        PROVEN
    2  ai_input_guard.py --strict    BEFORE weights load          PROVEN
    3  generate                      TRELLIS, formats=["mesh"]
    4  retopo / decimate             MANDATORY, headless Blender
    5  pivot to base-centre
    6  UV state (established if absent)
    7  measured intake
    8  ASSETS.md row
    9  FORGE_LOG.md cost line
   10  REAL-WORLD SCALE              orientation gate, declared scale, read back

### VALUES THAT WORK — the church, 2026-08-30

    inputs        4 views, 192k-308k subject px vs a 150k floor
    generate      190,562 v / 381,364 f  thin/long 0.4317  watertight
                  load 21.4 s  inference 5.5 s  VRAM peak 10,082 MiB
    retopo        381,364 -> 60,000 tris  (hero_prop ceiling 60,000)
    UVs           none -> 1 channel, smart_project (MACHINE unwrap)
    in engine     1341.3 cm top, 11.2 x 5.8 m footprint, 2.50x silhouette
    total         44 s end to end

### VALUES THAT WORK — the wood stack, 2026-08-30 (SECOND asset, prop_small)

    inputs        4 views, PASSED PER SET -- az090/az180 are 751/785 px on the
                  longest side, UNDER the 800 px per-image floor, and pass as
                  rotations (ground +1.1% / +0.1% vs the master az035)
    generate      1,400,074 v / 2,801,712 f  thin/long 0.617  watertight
                  load 21.3 s  inference 55.7 s  VRAM peak 14,870 MiB
    retopo        2,801,712 -> 15,000 tris  (prop_small ceiling 15,000)
    UVs           none -> 1 channel, smart_project (MACHINE unwrap)
    genus         392 -> 392   (decimation preserves topology, as designed)
    total         133.3 s end to end, exit 0

⚠ **TWO NUMBERS HERE ARE NOT COMFORTABLE, AND NEITHER IS A REFUSAL.**

**VRAM peak 14,870 MiB against 15,045 MiB free = 175 MiB, a 1.2% margin.**
VRAM fit is one of the four ratified ABSOLUTE floors and this cleared it by
less than measurement noise. A pass at 1.2% and a pass at 40% print
identically. Anything heavier than this asset should be assumed not to fit
until measured. Reporting headroom, and warning below a threshold, is
BACKLOGGED.

**Genus 392 at a 15,000-tri budget** — 6.4x the church's genus against a
quarter of its ceiling, from 7.3x the vertices. Partly honest: a stacked cord
of firewood really is full of tunnels. **The forge cannot tell a real tunnel
from reconstruction noise**, so this is recorded, not adjudicated. See the
`tri_within_budget` note above.

### ⛔ THE FORGED `.fbx` IS THE ARTEFACT OF RECORD. KEEP IT; NEVER REGENERATE ON DEMAND.

**The forge is NOT bit-reproducible, and a fixed seed does not make it so.**
Two runs, identical inputs, identical seed 20260830, identical sampler params,
identical model repo:

    standalone   190,498 v   381,228 f   chi -116   genus 59
    forge run    190,562 v   381,364 f   chi -120   genus 61

CUDA and spconv are not bitwise deterministic; the seed fixes the sampling
PATH and not the RESULT. **Pipeline rule 3 is amended for generated assets**
(Ryan, 2026-08-30): the VERDICT is reproducible -- `thin_over_long` 0.4317 on
both runs, watertight on both -- and the MESH is not.

Consequence, and it is operational: the `.fbx` is committed and kept. A
downstream fix, a material, a placement or a measurement refers to THAT file.
Re-running the forge produces an equivalent asset, never the same one, so
"just regenerate it" silently substitutes a different mesh for the one that
was reviewed.

### ⛔ SCALE IS DECLARED OR THE FORGE REFUSES

A generated mesh carries **no units**. TRELLIS normalises its output, so the
church imported **39.5 cm tall** and rendered perfectly. The triangle budget,
the watertight check, the pivot and the UV pass are ALL scale-invariant --
nothing in stages 1-9 could ever notice.

Every asset in `recipes/forge.json` declares `scale`: either `height_cm`, or
`ratio_against` + `ratio` + `reference_cm`. **Missing scale is a refusal, in
the same class as missing views, and it is checked BEFORE the GPU runs.**

    church      ratio 2.5 x reference 536.5 (chalet_silhouette_cm) = 1341.25
    wood_stack  height_cm 120.0

### `tri_within_budget` IS A TRIANGLE CLAIM, NOT A TOPOLOGY CLAIM

Named that way deliberately. The church met a 60,000 ceiling at **genus 61
with every handle intact** -- collapse decimation preserves topology. A field
called `within_budget` beside a decimation report reads as "cleaned up"; it
means "made smaller". A real retopology stage (voxel remesh -> decimate, with
a genus target) is BACKLOGGED as stage 4b and is NOT authorized.


### ⭐ STAGE 10 IS GENERAL AS OF 2026-08-30, AND PROVEN ON BOTH ASSETS

It used to MEASURE LIKE A CHURCH whatever it imported. Now:

    keys      raw_height_cm / top_cm / base_cm / footprint_cm  (was church_*)
    label     Forge_<Asset>, passed in
    level     /Game/Scratch/ForgeScale_<Asset> -- PER ASSET, because
              `new_level` OVERWRITES and one shared level meant the second
              asset destroyed the first's staged scene
    ratio     OPTIONAL. Reported only when the recipe declares
              `ratio_against`. A ratio is a RULING and only the church has one.
    checked   top_cm is compared to the declared target: height_error_cm and
              height_within_1pct, because "set_actor_scale3d did what it was
              told" is a claim like any other

**The orientation gate was already general and is unchanged** -- it compares
UE's per-axis extents to the exported Blender bbox and refuses on mismatch.

### VALUES THAT WORK — the wood stack in engine, 2026-08-30

    imported   /Game/Scratch/ForgeWoodStack/SM_WoodStack_Forge
    tris       14,996 in engine  (15,000 out of Blender -- the FBX round trip
               welds; the ceiling is 15,000 and it is UNDER, not at)
    UVs        1 channel
    orient     PASSED -- shape ratios [0.6176, 0.7577, 1.0] expected AND
               measured, identical to 4 dp
    scale      1.59478 from a raw 75.245 cm to the declared 120.0 cm
    read back  top 120.0 cm, base 0.0 cm, ERROR 0.00 cm
    footprint  158.4 x 97.8 cm
    companion  chalet silhouette 536.5 cm, MEASURED not scored -- this asset
               declares height_cm, so there is no ruled ratio
    frames     woodstack_beside_kit.png, woodstack_closeup.png

**Stage 10 IS reproducible**, unlike generation: run twice, identical numbers.
The non-reproducibility is in TRELLIS, not in the placement.

### RECORDING IT IS A SCRIPT, NOT A RETYPE

`scripts/forge_record_stage10.py --asset <key> --from <transcript>` folds the
payload's JSON into `forge_report.json` and flips the ASSETS.md
verified-in-engine column. **It refuses `ok:false` and refuses
`orientation_ok:false`** -- both verified. Stage 10 runs through `ue_exec`, so
its result arrives on stdout and lands nowhere; retyping it by hand is exactly
the stage-8 defect one stage later.

## R-FORGE REJECTED

**SCALING A MESH BEFORE CHECKING ITS ORIENTATION.**
→ SYMPTOM: `church_top_cm` 1341.3 and `church_over_chalet` 2.5 -- the ruled
height hit exactly and a perfect score for ruling 1 -- on a church lying on
its side. Only the footprint (26 x 31 m for a 13 m building) disagreed.
→ CAUSE: the FBX round trip rotates -90 about X; UE's Y held Blender's Z.
Scaling to a target on the wrong axis will always report success, because the
scale is computed FROM the axis it is applied to.
→ CORRECT: an orientation gate BEFORE the scale step, comparing UE's per-axis
extents to the exported Blender bbox and refusing on mismatch.
→ REFERENCE: 2026-08-30 first forge run; LESSONS.md same date.

**TRUSTING `replace_existing=True` TO RE-IMPORT.**
→ SYMPTOM: the FBX was re-exported three times with different content -- mtime
and sha256 both changed -- and UE returned byte-identical bounds every time,
reporting success and handing back the stale asset.
→ CORRECT: delete the destination first, guarded to `/Game/Scratch/`.
→ REFERENCE: same run.

**`bpy.ops.object.transform_apply` IN BACKGROUND MODE.**
→ SYMPTOM: the report logged the rotation as applied; the exported file was
unchanged.
→ CORRECT: write the vertex coordinates directly, and ASSERT the extents
changed before exporting.
→ REFERENCE: same run.

**GATING SET CONSISTENCY ON BBOX HEIGHT.** (stage 1, `--set`)
→ SYMPTOM: `wood_stack_az090` REFUSED at 8.6% "off the master", and the forge
blocked, on a set whose camera never moved. Measured: ground line spread
**1.1%**, top-edge spread **22.5%**, bbox-height spread 9.3%.
→ CAUSE: bbox height = ground line + top edge. The top edge moves whenever the
silhouette changes, which is exactly what azimuth does; the noise term is
larger than the signal term, so NO tolerance separates a camera move from an
honest rotation.
→ CORRECT: gate the **GROUND LINE** at ±3% (`GROUND_TOL`). Keep height at ±15%
(`HEIGHT_TOL`) REPORTED ALWAYS but gating only when the ground line has also
failed — it still catches a rescale that holds the ground line.
→ REFERENCE: ruled 2026-08-30 (operator, option 1); LESSONS.md same date;
`_verify/20260830_bakeoff/GENERATION_VIEW_SPEC.md`.

**A "FURTHER AWAY" FIXTURE BUILT BY SCALING THE WHOLE FRAME.**
→ SYMPTOM: the negative control reported a pass while measuring a ground delta
of **0.6%** — it was not simulating distance at all.
→ CAUSE: pasting a 0.75x copy of the entire frame onto a canvas leaves a
rectangular seam; `subject_mask` locks onto the SEAM, not the subject.
→ CORRECT: composite **only the subject's masked pixels**, scaled about the
frame centre, as a projection behaves. The rebuilt fixture measures y=792 vs
the master's y=890 = 11.0% and is refused.
→ REFERENCE: same date. A fixture that does not construct the condition it
names is worse than no fixture.

**ASSERTING REFUSAL BY SEARCHING THE FAILURE MESSAGE FOR A PHRASE.**
→ SYMPTOM: `any("bbox HEIGHT" in f ...)` went on reporting a PASS after the
gate moved to the ground line and stopped emitting that phrase.
→ CAUSE: absence of a searched-for string is indistinguishable from absence of
a problem. The message is the most likely thing to be reworded.
→ CORRECT: match a stable token both sides reference, and verify the control
FAILS when it should — a green that survives the message changing is not a
control.
→ REFERENCE: same date.

**`subprocess.run(..., text=True)` WITH NO `encoding`, ON A CHILD THAT EMITS UTF-8.**
→ SYMPTOM: `UnicodeDecodeError` traceback from `Thread-4 (_readerthread)`
mid-forge, and the run completed anyway. Measured on the same bytes:
`text=True` alone gives rc 0 with **stdout None and `__FORGE_GEN__` NOT
found**; adding `encoding="utf-8"` gives rc 0, 423 chars, marker found.
→ CAUSE: `text=True` decodes with the LOCALE codec (cp1252 here). TRELLIS
emits tqdm bars; U+258F `▏` is `E2 96 8F` and **0x8F is undefined in cp1252**,
so the reader thread dies. **An exception in a thread does not fail the
process** — it returns None, and stage 3's defensive `(p.stdout or "")` turns
that None into a confident "could not look" over a good 56 s GPU run. It
survived only because tqdm defaults to STDERR.
→ CORRECT: `encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"` on the helper. Decode
explicitly whenever a child's output is EVIDENCE; the locale codec is a
property of the machine, not the data.
→ REFERENCE: 2026-08-30 wood-stack forge; LESSONS.md same date. 20+ other
`text=True` sites in `scripts/` share the defect and are BACKLOGGED, not swept
blind.

**A STAGE THAT COMPUTES ITS ARTEFACT AND STASHES IT IN THE REPORT.** (stage 8)
→ SYMPTOM: wood_stack forged exit 0, `FORGE_LOG.md` gained its line, and
`ASSETS.md` gained NOTHING. `forge_report.json` held a perfectly good
`assets_row` that was never written anywhere.
→ CAUSE: stage 8 built the row and assigned it to `report["assets_row"]`;
only stage 9 called an append. The church's row had been written BY HAND, so
the register looked right and the defect had no first victim. `ASSETS.md`'s
preamble claims "scripts/forge.py writes the row" and that was false from the
start — non-negotiable 9, on our own artefact.
→ ALSO: the dead row had SEVEN fields against the table's SIX columns.
**Output with no destination cannot be caught being wrong**, so it drifts.
→ CORRECT: `_append_assets_row` writes into the forge table and REPLACES any
row for the same asset — a REGISTER is one row per asset, unlike
`FORGE_LOG.md`, which is a run log and appends per run. Verify in three
directions: adds, is idempotent, replaces without duplicating.
→ REFERENCE: 2026-08-30 wood-stack forge; LESSONS.md same date.

**HARDCODING `DEST`/`NAME` IN A PAYLOAD WHOSE OTHER PARAMETERS ARE TEMPLATED.**
→ SYMPTOM: the stage-10 command printed at the end of the WOOD STACK forge
pointed at `DEST=/Game/Scratch/ForgeChurch`, `NAME=SM_Church_Forge`. The
payload deletes `DEST + "/" + NAME` before importing, so running the emitted
line would have DESTROYED the forged church — the artefact of record, and not
reproducible.
→ CAUSE: partial parameterisation. `SRC`/`TARGET_CM`/`EXP_*` were templated,
which made the command read as fully recipe-driven. **The two parameters left
hardcoded were the ones selecting what gets overwritten.**
→ CORRECT: template `DEST`/`NAME` and pass them from `forge.py`
(`_dest_path()` = `/Game/Scratch/Forge<CamelKey>`). Keep the
`DEST.startswith("/Game/Scratch/")` guard — an unsubstituted `__DEST__` fails
CLOSED on it, verified both directions.
→ STILL NOT GENERAL: the payload emits `church_top_cm` / `church_over_chalet`
and scores ruling 1's 2.5x. `forge.py` now prints a NOT-GENERAL warning for
any non-church asset. Stage 10 has NOT been run for the wood stack.
→ REFERENCE: same run.

**RUNNING THE EMITTED STAGE-10 COMMAND FROM GIT BASH.**
→ SYMPTOM: `REFUSE to delete outside /Game/Scratch/:
C:/Program Files/Git/Game/Scratch/ForgeWoodStack`. The guard fires and nothing
is imported.
→ CAUSE: MSYS2 argument conversion rewrites any argument that looks like an
absolute POSIX path against the Git install root. Measured: `--set
DEST=/Game/Scratch/ForgeWoodStack` arrives as
`DEST=C:/Program Files/Git/Game/Scratch/...`. `LEVEL` is mangled identically.
The church never hit it because `DEST`/`LEVEL` were HARDCODED IN THE PAYLOAD —
generalising them is what moved them onto a command line.
→ CORRECT: run it from PowerShell (the project's primary shell), or prefix
`MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1` in Git Bash. Do NOT "fix" it by relaxing the
`/Game/Scratch/` guard — that guard is what caught it.
→ REFERENCE: 2026-08-30 wood-stack stage 10; LESSONS.md same date.

**LETTING STAGE 10 WRITE ITS LEVEL TO ONE SHARED PATH.**
→ SYMPTOM: none yet -- caught before running. `LEVEL` was a hardcoded
`/Game/Scratch/ForgeScale` and `new_level` OVERWRITES, so staging the wood
stack would have destroyed the church's staged scene, the level the committed
`church_beside_kit.png` was framed in.
→ CAUSE: the same partial-parameterisation shape as the hardcoded `DEST`. A
name that silently keeps working for the asset it was written for.
→ CORRECT: `/Game/Scratch/ForgeScale_<Asset>`, passed in. The church's
original `ForgeScale.umap` is left untouched.
→ REFERENCE: 2026-08-30 stage-10 generalisation.

## R-EDITOR-CLOSE — THE EDITOR THAT WILL NOT CLOSE (2026-08-30)

**Status: PROVEN once.** Ruled by the operator after `CloseMainWindow()` went
unhonoured for 180 s while the editor answered `ue_exec` normally.

    1  census   scripts/dirty_package_census_payload.txt
                content and map packages queried SEPARATELY -- "I couldn't
                look" is not "nothing is dirty"
    2  quiet    newest mtime under LandscapeLab/Content, HOST-side.
                Older than 120 s = no write in flight.
    3  RETRY    CloseMainWindow again. Do this BEFORE killing.
    4  kill     authorized ONLY if 1 is clean AND 2 is quiet.
                If dirty or writing: wait, do not kill.

### WHY STEP 3 EXISTS, AND WHY IT IS NOT OPTIONAL

Conditions 1 and 2 measure THE EDITOR HAVING FINISHED ITS WORK, which is also
the condition under which it will accept a close. Measured 2026-08-30:
0 dirty, newest write 552.6 s old, retry closed it in **10 s**. The kill was
authorized and turned out to be unnecessary.

A busy editor and an unresponsive one look identical from outside -- same
process, same RSS, and a successful remote round trip, because remote
execution is serviced between tasks. **The mtime is what separates them**, and
it is a host-side observation the editor was never asked to self-report.

### REJECTED

**READING "ANSWERS A ROUND TRIP" AS "IS IDLE".**
→ SYMPTOM: an editor declared deaf after 180 s, on the evidence that it
returned a correct level from `ue_exec` the whole time.
→ CAUSE: the round trip proves the process is ALIVE, not that it is FREE. The
first close was issued moments after an import, several level saves and four
HighResShots, with Nanite and shader work still draining.
→ CORRECT: measure quiescence host-side (Content mtime), then retry the close.
→ REFERENCE: 2026-08-30; LESSONS.md same date.

**FORCE-KILLING ON THE FEAR OF TRUNCATION, OR REFUSING TO ON THE SAME FEAR.**
→ Both are the unquantified version. The risk is a kill DURING A WRITE, which
the 120 s mtime window measures directly. Dirty packages are a different and
lesser matter: killing loses unsaved in-memory changes, it does not corrupt
what is already on disk.

### R-EDITOR-CLOSE — THE DIRTY-MODAL DEADLOCK (2026-09-09)

**The rule can deadlock, and it did.** Step 4 says the kill is authorised only
if the census is CLEAN and the window is quiet, and "if dirty or writing:
wait, do not kill". That assumes DIRTY RESOLVES OVER TIME, which is true of a
write in flight and false of a save prompt.

Measured 2026-09-09 after a session that deliberately never saved:

    census        4 dirty  (__ExternalActors__ packages for the 4 lighting
                            actors apply_lighting had mutated)
    quiet         4,363 s  -- far past the 120 s threshold
    close         unhonoured
    RETRY close   unhonoured, window title unchanged
    ue_exec       "no editor nodes answered discovery"

The last line is the diagnosis. A modal blocks the GAME THREAD, and remote
execution is serviced on the game thread, so **an editor that answers nothing
while its window title looks normal has a modal up** — a save prompt, which is
a CHILD window and therefore invisible to `MainWindowTitle`.

Waiting cannot clear it. The dirty state is what RAISED the prompt, and there
is no operator to click it.

**RULE: when the census is dirty AND two closes go unhonoured AND the editor
has stopped answering, the kill is authorised** — provided the quiet window
passes, which is the condition that actually measures the risk (a kill DURING
A WRITE). Enumerate the dirty packages first and say why losing them is
acceptable. Here all four were lighting actors fully re-derivable by re-running
`apply_lighting` from the recipe, which is the whole point of hard rule 2.

**Do NOT read this as "kill when dirty".** The quiet window still gates it, the
packages still get enumerated, and both closes are still tried first.

### R-EDITOR-CLOSE — FOURTH OCCURRENCE: DEADLOCK AT 0-DIRTY (2026-09-10)

**The dirty-modal explanation is one mechanism, not the mechanism.**
Census CLEAN, quiet 2,132 s, first close ACCEPTED and destroyed the
window — and the process wedged idle (0.1 s CPU/10 s, 12 GB RSS, remote
exec dead) for 9+ minutes. Retry returned False: no window left to
close. Kill per the ORIGINAL step 4 (clean AND quiet, both closes
tried): clean outcome, EMPTY PackageRestoreData, no post-kill writes.

→ RULE UNCHANGED: census → quiet → close → retry → kill-if-clean+quiet.
It has now produced the correct outcome under both mechanisms. A
wedged-idle process with a clean census and an empty restore file loses
nothing; do not diagnose the hang from outside — the gate already
measures everything the decision needs.
→ REFERENCE: LESSONS 2026-09-10d.

### R-EDITOR-CLOSE — AMENDED 2026-09-11: CPU IS NOT THE QUIET SIGNAL, FLAT RSS IS

**The quiet gate could not be satisfied, and the close worked anyway on
the first attempt.** Measured 2026-09-11 after a material rebuild and
three 4K captures: **~4.4 cores for 9 minutes straight** — 18 consecutive
samples between 124 and 211 CPU-seconds per 30–45 s wall — with
`Responding=True`, remote execution answering, census CLEAN, zero
ShaderCompileWorkers, and **RSS pinned at exactly 13.6 GB the whole
time**.

That is not work in flight. It is a FOREGROUND EDITOR VIEWPORT rendering
an 8129² Nanite/Lumen world at an uncapped framerate, which it will do
for as long as it is open. Waiting for CPU to fall is waiting for
something that does not happen.

→ **The quiet window's PREMISE is "CPU activity means an unfinished
write".** The discriminator that actually carries that meaning is
**flat RSS + clean census + responsive**, not the CPU number. A
shader/asset build GROWS memory; a rendering viewport does not.
→ RULE, refined: census → **RSS flat and census clean** → close → retry
→ kill-if-clean+quiet. `CloseMainWindow()` returned True and the process
was gone within 30 s; PackageRestoreData ABSENT.
→ AND THE GENERAL FORM: a gate whose signal has two causes will block on
the benign one forever. This one had been read as "the editor is busy"
for four occurrences without anyone asking *busy doing what*.

### R-EDITOR-CLOSE CONFIRMED A SECOND TIME — 2026-08-30

    census   0 dirty     quiet 146.4 s     retry closed in 10 s

Same result as the first application: the kill was authorized by both
conditions and was again not needed. Two for two on the retry. The ordering
(census, quiet-window, RETRY, then kill) stands.

## R-BRIEFLOOP — ITERATING STAMP PLACEMENTS AGAINST A LAYOUT BRIEF (2026-08-31)

**Status: PROVEN once**, on the degraded coast demo
(`_verify/20260831_brief_loop/`): the recipe was reverted to its original
defective state (carves before the cliff ADD, cove at 140 m carve relief)
and `scripts/brief_loop.py` reproduced the entire manual fix chain of the
2026-08-31 coast benchmark on its own — lint refusal on ordering, reorder
under the explicit flag, then amplitude 140 -> 42 -> 30.2 -> 27.2 m,
slope 20.8 -> 4.6 deg, ALL CHECKS PASS in 4 iterations, exit 0.

### THE PROCEDURE

    python scripts/brief_loop.py --selftest        # 15 checks, three directions
    python scripts/brief_loop.py --recipe <recipe> --brief <brief>
    # lint refusal on carve-buried-by-ADD? decide, then: --reorder

The brief carries machine-checkable `acceptance` entries (kinds:
`flat_site`, `peak`) keyed to placement ids. The loop composites, probes
the STAMPED output with the compositor's own origin
(`landscape.location_cm` — NEVER a centred formula), adjusts ONE bounded
knob per failing check, and repeats. Cap 6 iterations; **a cap hit is exit
3 and a REFUSAL — do not widen tolerances to make it pass.**

**MAX-plateau rule (added 2026-09-03, forge duskhighland):** a
`flat_site` whose placement is `blend: MAX` takes its OWN branch — the
single knob is the plateau height (`anchor_m + amplitude_m`), set to
`max(box elev_max + 3 m, band mid)` clamped to the band top. Flank
topping out above the band, or a plateau already at target and still
failing, are GEOMETRY refusals (no mutation). Selftest carries 4 derived
cases (24 checks total).

**IT NEVER ADOPTS.** `heightmap.source` is untouched; adoption stays the
R-STAMP hash-proven manual step.

### R-BRIEFLOOP REJECTED

**A CENTRED ORIGIN FORMULA (-res*spacing/2) FOR THE PROBE.**
-> SYMPTOM: none on the coast recipe — it is numerically identical there,
which is exactly the danger. On (n-1)-centred recipes (alpine_8k,
location_cm -406400) it probes HALF A CELL OFF: a plausible, slightly
shifted measurement nothing downstream can detect.
-> CORRECT: origin from `landscape.location_cm`, the same source
`composite_stamps.py:461` uses. One declaration.
-> REFERENCE: audit 2026-08-31 F3, `_verify/20260831_brief_loop/audit_verdict.md`.

**TRUSTING THE SELFTEST OVER THE DOCUMENTED RULE.**
-> SYMPTOM: `--selftest` asserted anchor 10.0 where the rule it tests
yields 0.0 (floor). The tool was right; the TEST was the broken
instrument, and a green run would have locked a false invariant.
-> CORRECT: when a selftest and the documented rule disagree, derive the
expected value from the rule by hand before touching either.
-> REFERENCE: audit B2.

**SYSTEM %TEMP% FOR A SELFTEST SPECIMEN.** Out of both roots, and its
context-manager cleanup is a recursive delete (standing rules 1-2).
Specimens live under the repo and are removed as single files.

**PRESENCE-ONLY VALIDATION.** Direction 3: malformed `at_m`/`box_m`/bands
crashed mid-loop instead of refusing at the gate. Shape AND type first.

**THE ADD/MIN KNOB RULES APPLIED TO A MAX PLACEMENT.**
-> SYMPTOM: slope-fail on a MAX plateau reduced amplitude — which lowers
the plateau INTO the flank. Measured 2026-09-03 (forge duskhighland):
amplitude driven 130 -> 5 across six iterations while slope sat at the
raw flank's 15.8 deg; the loop converged on a no-op and hit the cap.
-> CORRECT: the MAX branch above — plateau height is the only knob, and
it moves UP, above the box's measured elev_max.
-> REFERENCE: LESSONS 2026-09-02 (carve-form) + brief_loop selftest
`MAX too low -> plateau raised above box max`.

# R-ANGBUDGET — DERIVING A CULL OR LOD DISTANCE FROM PIXELS (2026-09-05)

**Status: PROVEN OFFLINE, INCLUDING AGAINST ENGINE SOURCE.** The pixel
projection is exact and independently re-derived. The `ScreenSize` column
was **VERIFIED against UE 5.8 source on 2026-09-05 and FOUND WRONG BY 2x;
it is now corrected** — see R-ANGBUDGET SCREENSIZE below. It is verified
against SOURCE but **not yet against the RUNNING ENGINE**: the second
instrument (an editor read-back of one mesh's LOD ScreenSize at a known
distance) is still outstanding and is carried into the Task 3 editor
session. Until that lands, treat a ScreenSize written into a recipe as
source-verified only, and say so where it is written.

Informed by: LESSONS 2026-09-05 (this session) and LESSONS 2026-08-04
("THE LOD SWITCH DISTANCE MATCHES THE REPORT, AND I COULD NOT MEASURE THE
POP") — the defect that entry identified correctly and could not measure,
because it reached for a renderer when the quantity was a projection.

## WHAT IT IS FOR

Answering "at what distance may this object stop being drawn?" without
typing a number in metres. Visibility is angular; metres are correct for
exactly one FOV and one resolution. The engine already thinks this way
(LOD switching is keyed on projected bounding sphere, not distance);
`cull_distance_m` was the one distance-denominated knob left in the chain,
and it is the one that pops.

## PRECONDITIONS

- `height_m` MEASURED, citing a `Free/_measured/*.json` row — never a
  remembered or handed-over figure (see R4 REJECTED, 2026-09-05).
- For a Nanite mesh, know which bound you are holding: `RENDER_DATA` is
  the FALLBACK PROXY and overstates. Prefer a `SOURCE_MODEL` measurement.
- Instance scale from the placed `foliage/<biome>_<species>.json` list,
  not from the recipe's `scale_range` — the range is the sampling domain,
  the list is what is actually standing in the world.
- The camera is the RULED judgement camera, not the capture camera of the
  day: **3840x2160 at 90 deg horizontal** (Ryan, 2026-09-05), with
  2560x1440 as the floor. 8K is inspection only.

## EXACT VALUES

    thresholds_px    vanish 1.5    silhouette 6    detail 40
    declared camera  fov_h 90.0    res 3840x2160  (floor 2560x1440)
    derived          fov_v 58.7155 deg            42.67 render px/deg
                                                  1.406 arcmin/render px

At 90 deg / 3840 the render resolves 42.67 ppd against a 27" 1440p
reference display's ~45 ppd: **the RENDER is the limiting instrument, not
the eye.** Thresholds are therefore correctly stated in RENDER pixels, and
every distance in this recipe must be re-derived if the declared camera
changes. Pass `--display-ppd` and the tool names which side limits.

The projection, verified by independent hand derivation (four cases,
delta 0.00e+00, and `dist_for_pixels` round-trips `pixels_tall` to 1e-6):

    fov_v      = 2*atan(tan(fov_h/2) * H/W)
    px_tall    = h / (2*D*tan(fov_v/2)) * H
    D_at_px    = h*H / (2*px*tan(fov_v/2))

## ORDERED STEPS

    1. python scripts/lod_silhouette_check.py --selftest    # PASS
       python scripts/temporal_stability.py --selftest      # PASS
       (angular_budget.py ships no --selftest; check its projection by
        hand against the three formulae above before trusting a run)
    2. Assemble heights + placed scale stats into a provenance JSON with
       one cited source per row (pattern:
       _verify/bench/2026-09-05/species_heights.json)
    3. python scripts/angular_budget.py --fov-h 90 --res 3840 2160
         --object <Name> <h_m> ...  --cull <Name> <d_m> ...
         --display-ppd 45 --out _verify/bench/<date>/angular_budget_<...>.json
    4. Re-run at 2560 1440 (the floor) and at BOTH the typical (p50) and
       worst-case (max) placed height. Four runs; a verdict that flips
       between them is a finding, not a rounding error.

## THE RULE THE OUTPUT FEEDS

**A cull may only sit at a band boundary where the NEXT band exists.**
Culling to nothing is legal only below 1.5 px. Choose the threshold by
what takes over:

    imposter / HLOD exists for the species   ->  cull at `detail`
    nothing takes over                       ->  cull at `vanish`
    silhouette, with nothing behind it       ->  NEVER

## R-ANGBUDGET REJECTED

**A CULL DISTANCE AUTHORED IN METRES.**
-> SYMPTOM: see R4 REJECTED 2026-09-05 — 14.9 to 62.9 px objects deleted
in one step, four species of them above the 40 px detail threshold.
-> CORRECT: derive from height, declared camera and threshold.
-> REFERENCE: `_verify/bench/2026-09-05/angular_budget_2026-09-05_SUMMARY.json`.

**A HEIGHT TAKEN FROM A HANDOFF, A RECIPE COMMENT OR MEMORY.**
-> SYMPTOM: every derived distance scales linearly with the error, and the
result still looks like a well-formed table. BRIEF section 0a got all seven
heights wrong, all but one in the direction that UNDERSTATES the defect —
which reads as agreement and so is never rechecked.
-> CORRECT: one cited `Free/_measured/` row per height, in a provenance
file committed beside the run.

**A `RENDER_DATA` BOUND ON A NANITE MESH.**
-> SYMPTOM: 29.313 m against the source model's 27.317 m, +7.3%, silent.
The fallback proxy overstates Z by 6.6% and X by 36%
(`recipes/alpine_8k.json` Conifer `collision.capsule.basis`).
-> CORRECT: SOURCE_MODEL via
`GeometryScript_AssetUtils.copy_mesh_from_static_mesh`.

**THE MESH HEIGHT ALONE, IGNORING INSTANCE SCALE.**
-> SYMPTOM: understates the worst case by up to 60% — SpruceSapling is a
4.529 m mesh placed at up to 1.600x, so the object being culled at 180 m
is 7.246 m and 77.3 px, not 4.529 m and 48.3 px.
-> CORRECT: p50 and max from the placed instance list; report both.

**WRITING THE TOOL'S `ue_screen_size` COLUMN INTO A RECIPE TODAY.**
-> SYMPTOM: would be an unverified constant factor — the tool's own
docstring flags it VERIFY-pending and the multiple could be off by 2x.
-> CORRECT: Task 2 first — open `SceneManagement.cpp`
`ComputeBoundsScreenRadiusSquared` / `ComputeBoundsScreenSize`, cite the
line, and confirm against a second instrument (a read-back of one mesh's
LOD ScreenSize at a known distance) before any recipe consumes it.

**`/tmp` IN A TOOL THAT RUNS ON THIS MACHINE.**
-> SYMPTOM: `lod_silhouette_check.py --selftest` died with
`FileNotFoundError: '/tmp/_lod_l0.png'` at its line 126 (PIL
`Image.py:2706` opens the path directly). Windows has no `/tmp`.
-> CORRECT: `tempfile.mkdtemp()` plus explicit cleanup. Run an incoming
tool's selftest BEFORE its first real use — it was the cheapest possible
place to find this.

## R-ANGBUDGET SCREENSIZE — the verified formula (2026-09-05, Task 2)

**Source of truth, opened and cited, UE 5.8:**

    Engine/Source/Runtime/Engine/Private/SceneManagement.cpp
      :966  ComputeBoundsScreenSize(BoundsOrigin, SphereRadius, ViewOrigin, ProjMatrix)
      :968    Dist           = FVector::Dist(BoundsOrigin, ViewOrigin)
      :971    ScreenMultiple = FMath::Max(0.5f * ProjMatrix.M[0][0],
                                          0.5f * ProjMatrix.M[1][1])
      :974    ScreenRadius   = ScreenMultiple * SphereRadius / Max(1.0f, Dist)
      :977    return           ScreenRadius * 2.0f

    Engine/Source/Runtime/Core/Public/Math/PerspectiveMatrix.h
      :102-105  TPerspectiveMatrix(HalfFOV, Width, Height, MinZ, MaxZ)
                  M[0][0] = 1 / tan(HalfFOV)                  (HalfFOV is HORIZONTAL)
                  M[1][1] = (Width / Height) / tan(HalfFOV)

    tan(vFOV/2) = tan(HalfFOV) / aspect   =>   M[1][1] = 1 / tan(vFOV/2)

**THE VALUE:**

    aspect >= 1  =>  ScreenMultiple = 0.5 / tan(vFOV/2)
    ScreenSize   = 2 * ScreenMultiple * R / D
                 =     R / (D * tan(vFOV / 2))

    inverse (engine's own, SceneManagement.cpp:980-989):
    D = ScreenMultiple * R / (ScreenSize * 0.5)

`ScreenSize` is the bounding-sphere **DIAMETER** as a fraction of screen
**HEIGHT**. Confirmed at the CONSUMING end, not merely restated from the
producing one: `SceneManagement.cpp:1042` (and `:1004` on the temporal
path) select a LOD with `Square(MeshScreenSize * 0.5f) > ScreenRadiusSquared`
— the authored per-LOD ScreenSize is halved before comparison against a
screen RADIUS.

**Units:** the engine works in centimetres and clamps `Max(1.0f, Dist)`,
i.e. below 1 cm. R and D in the tool are both metres; the ratio is
unitless and the clamp is unreachable at any distance this project
measures.

## R-ANGBUDGET SCREENSIZE REJECTED

**`ScreenSize = 2*R/(D*tan(vFOV/2))`** — the formula `angular_budget.py`
SHIPPED WITH, inherited from the research handoff.
-> SYMPTOM: every ScreenSize exactly 2x the engine's, and every distance
derived from an authored ScreenSize exactly 2x too far. Silent: the value
is dimensionless and plausible at both scales, and the pixel columns
beside it are correct, so the report looks internally consistent.
-> CORRECT: `R / (D * tan(vFOV/2))`. Fixed in `ue_screen_size`,
2026-09-05; the module docstring and the report's own
`_ue_screen_size_note` field were carrying the wrong formula too and were
fixed in the same commit (a wrong claim in an artefact WE emit is the
contamination path standing rule 9 exists for — fix the seed and the
copies).
-> REFERENCE: SceneManagement.cpp:971 and :977 above; LESSONS 2026-09-05.

**`ScreenMultiple = 0.5 * ProjMatrix[1][1]`** as a statement of what the
engine does.
-> SYMPTOM: none on our camera, which is the danger. The engine takes
`Max(0.5*M[0][0], 0.5*M[1][1])`; for aspect >= 1 the Max IS the [1][1]
term, so the claim is accidentally true at 16:9 and wrong in general. It
would mis-predict on a portrait or square viewport, and a check run only
at 16:9 would "confirm" it.
-> CORRECT: state the Max. A claim that is accidentally true in the only
case you tested is indistinguishable from a true one until the case
changes.

**VALIDATING A CORRECTED FORMULA WITH THE ENGINE'S OWN INVERSE.**
-> SYMPTOM: `ComputeBoundsDrawDistance` round-trips to 1.1e-13 against
either the right formula or the wrong one, because it SHARES A SOURCE
with the forward function. Non-negotiable 0: instruments sharing a source
are ONE measurement. It proves transcription, not correctness.
-> CORRECT: an identity between two INDEPENDENT code paths. ScreenSize
must equal `pixels_tall(2R, D) / H`, which the tool computes without
touching `ue_screen_size`. Exact on all five test rows for the corrected
form; **off by exactly 2 on every row for the shipped form** — meaning
this defect was detectable offline, from the tool's own two columns,
before the engine was ever opened. When a tool computes one physical
quantity two ways, make them agree as a standing check; it is a free
instrument.

**CALLING THE FORMULA "PROVEN" ON SOURCE ALONE.**
-> The acceptance for Task 2 asks for a SECOND INSTRUMENT: an editor
read-back of one static mesh's LOD ScreenSize at a known distance
(place a spruce at a measured distance, read the LOD screen sizes and the
active LOD). **NOT DONE — carried into the Task 3 editor session.**
Source verification settles what the engine COMPUTES; it does not settle
that our camera, aspect and bounds match what we assumed we were feeding
it. Say "source-verified" until the read-back exists.

## NOTED, NOT ACTED ON — a LOD-chain defect this exposed

Running `spruce_half_01`'s own editor-read chain
(`[1.0, 0.99, 0.60, 0.35, 0.17]`, `Free/_measured/pn_spruce_forest.json`)
through the corrected formula at the judgement camera:

    LOD0 1.00 ->  15.6 m     LOD3 0.35 ->  44.7 m
    LOD1 0.99 ->  15.8 m     LOD4 0.17 ->  92.0 m
    LOD2 0.60 ->  26.1 m

The chain BOTTOMS OUT AT 92 m against a 730 m cull: LOD4, the imposter
card, is the active representation across the whole 92–730 m range and
takes over while the tree is still **349 px tall**, ~9x above the 40 px
detail threshold. Orthogonal to the cull defect — fixing the cull does
not fix this. Belongs to Task 8 (LOD chains by silhouette).

# R-BENCHSTATION — DERIVING A CAMERA STATION BY MEASUREMENT, NOT BEARING (2026-09-05)

**Status: DERIVED OFFLINE, NOT YET CONFIRMED IN THE EDITOR.** The tool is
`scripts/bench_station_derive.py` (selftest: 12 checks, three directions, PASS).
**No station here is locked.** Each must be confirmed by a real render at that
camera before it is used to judge anything — non-negotiable 8, verify with a
different instrument than the one that made the claim. This tool proposes; the
editor disposes.

## THE DEFECT THIS EXISTS TO PREVENT

`recipes/perf_budgets.json` derived its four stations from BEARINGS —
*"treeline at 1.25x the town extent radius"*, *"vista at 2.6x extent on the
opposite side, looking back over the town to the peak"*. Correct positions,
**occlusion never traced**. The first renders ever taken there
(`_verify/20260905_stations/STATIONS_READ.md`, 2026-09-05) showed `treeline` as
a near-vertical rock face filling ~85% of frame and `vista` showing neither the
town nor the peak.

**A bearing tells you where a thing is. It does not tell you whether anything
is in the way.**

Worse, both frames are *stable and reproducible*, which is why nothing
downstream ever flagged them: a camera pressed into a hillside gives a
beautifully repeatable measurement of a hillside.

## WHAT THE TOOL MEASURES

Ray-marches the **same heightmap the landscape was imported from** and projects
the **same placed instance lists the world was built from**:

    pct_sky / pct_terrain / pct_canopy
    pct_near_terrain_lt100m      the "pressed against a rock face" number
    by_distance_m                canopy% and terrain% in 0-100, 100-300,
                                 300-1k, 1k-1.5k, 1.5k-3k, 3k-8k, 8k+
    shape_band                   canopy inside a species' px band, BOTH as a
                                 share of whole frame AND as a share of the
                                 frame that lies in the band at all
    ridge_silhouette             terrain beyond 3 km with sky directly above,
                                 and how many columns carry it

## THE CROSS-CHECK THAT LICENSED IT

Before choosing anything it was pointed at the two stations already known bad,
and independently reproduced the human verdict:

    treeline  report "near-vertical rock face ~85% of frame"
              tool   90.56% terrain within 100 m, 0.0% sky,
                     0.00% canopy in the 6-40 px band, ridge 0/240 cols
    vista     report "near-field conifers and rock; no town, no peak"
              tool   84.2% within 100 m, 0.05% beyond 1 km,
                     0.02% canopy in the band, ridge 0/240 cols

A heightmap raycast and a person looking at a PNG are genuinely different
instruments (non-negotiable 0). Their agreement is what licensed the tool.

## THE DERIVED STATIONS (offline; editor confirmation OUTSTANDING)

    near_ground  -210800.0,278800.0,<TRACED>,-2.0,-12.8,0.0   KEPT (plaza)

`mid_slope` at ground 632.8 m is the only candidate with **continuous** canopy

elevation: two stations measuring the same thing is worse than one station
measuring less.

**All percentages in this recipe are at probe resolution 320x180** unless
stated. The probe is a subsample of the frame, so figures shift by a few tenths
between resolutions (the same station reads 14.92% / 85.1% at 240x135). Quote
the probe res with the number, or two runs of the same station will look like a
change in the world.

`vista` at ground 763.8 m sits **above the conifer band** (placement stops at
640 m), so its near field is terrain only. Ridge silhouette in 104 of 320
columns (32.5%); the 1-3 km band is 10.83% of frame.

**The town is NOT in the vista frame, and that was a trade, not an oversight.**
Of 542 elevated positions 1.2-4.5 km from the plaza, only **14** have clear

trees (the best has 73.1% of frame within 100 m), and above the treeline only

under the bar. The ridge was a MUST and the town was conditional, so the town

## THE PERF-BUDGET CONSEQUENCE

`treeline` and `vista` in `perf_budgets.json` now carry `basis_invalidated:
true`. Their GPU and Game budgets were **ratified 2026-08-30 against the OLD
camera** and now describe a viewpoint that no longer exists. `check_perf.py`
returns **NO VERDICT** for those zones — never PASS, never RED — until they are

applies when a read-back disagrees by >0.05°.

to retune a budget.

(8.0 ms) and its camera renders almost nothing — a frame full of near geometry
is cheap. The budget may be measuring occlusion rather than the zone it names.

the depth-band breakdown beside the millisecond number.
-> STILL OPEN: `main_street`'s root cause was never established (2026-09-05
ruled out inside-a-building, under-a-roof, underground, fixed-by-height; the
leading candidate is a foliage instance and the settling probe was never run).
**Its station was NOT re-derived — the operator ruled on treeline and vista.**

**ASSERTING AN EXTREMUM OVER A SAMPLE AS A PROPERTY OF THE WORLD.**
-> SYMPTOM: this session claimed, and COMMITTED (efe804ce), that *"the maximum
fraction of frame lying beyond 1 km from any ground-level camera in this world
is 9.36%"*, and used it to argue the operator's 30% requirement was
geometrically unsatisfiable. **Falsified within the hour:** a local refinement
found **28.18%** far-band and **20.64%** canopy-in-band — 3x better, within
600 m of a point the coarse scan had already visited.
-> ROOT CAUSE: a 150-200 m grid with 15° yaw steps over an 8 km world does not
establish a maximum. It establishes what that grid found.
-> CORRECT: report "best found over N cameras was X" and stop there. An
extremum over a sample is a property OF THE SAMPLE; reporting it as a property
of the world converts *"I did not find better"* into *"better does not exist"* —
the same class as reporting a failed measurement as a measurement
(non-negotiable 6).
-> WHAT SURVIVES: the 30% requirement is still not met (best 20.64%), and the
geometric reason high values are hard is unchanged — from eye height 1.75 m
everything past 1.15 km sits in a narrow wedge below the horizon, 0.15% of
frame on FLAT ground, lifted only by relief. But "hard" is not "impossible",
and no ceiling is asserted.

**JUDGING A VISTA ON NEAR *TERRAIN* ALONE.**
-> SYMPTOM: the first vista gate checked `pct_near_terrain_lt100m` and passed a
camera standing inside the forest with **73.1%** of frame within 100 m — 39.8%
of it tree trunks. A vista buried in near canopy fails for exactly the reason a
rock face does, and the gate could not see it.
-> CORRECT: gate on near-field TOTAL (terrain AND canopy). The failure mode is
"cannot see out", and what blocks the view is irrelevant to that.

**A REFINEMENT JOB THAT PRINTS ONLY AT THE END.**
-> SYMPTOM: a 686-camera sweep ran 25 minutes with an empty output file, so
there was no way to tell progress from hang, and no partial result to salvage

-> CORRECT: a long search flushes per result. A job you cannot abandon
informedly is a job you will either kill blind or wait out blind.

## THE API FACTS, VERIFIED AGAINST 5.8 SOURCE

    UMoviePipelineConsoleVariableSetting::CVars is ScriptNoExport
      (MoviePipelineConsoleVariableSetting.h:129) -- INVISIBLE to Python.
      Use add_or_update_console_variable(name, value).
    mrq.temporal_samples is NOT a console variable. It is
      UMoviePipelineAntiAliasingSetting::TemporalSampleCount
      (MoviePipelineAntiAliasingSetting.h:59).
    job.map / job.sequence are SoftObjectPath; job.get_configuration()
      returns the MoviePipelinePrimaryConfig; settings come from
      find_or_add_setting_by_class.

## THE REAL CVAR READ-BACK IS THE ENGINE LOG

MRQ applies its variables when a shot starts and RESTORES them when it ends, so
nothing read from Python afterwards is the render's state. The during-render
values are in `Saved/Logs/LandscapeLab.log`:

    LogMovieRenderPipeline: Applying CVar "sg.ShadowQuality"
        PreviousValue: 1.000000 NewValue: 1.000000

`bench_capture` records the log byte offset immediately before starting, then
parses forward, so it cannot pick up an earlier run.

## R-BENCHCAPTURE — TRUTH RUNS THROUGH MRQ (2026-09-09, first PASS)

**The truth instrument runs through MRQ, not the editor.** Corrected
2026-09-09 after the editor route was found unusable and the MRQ route was
found to have never been connected.

    python scripts/bench_capture.py --profile target --truth \
        --load-all-regions --tag <tag> --stations near_ground mid_slope

    near_ground  PASS  expected 808  resident 3477  missing 0
    mid_slope    PASS  expected 20   resident 3420  missing 0

### THE GRID NAME IS `MainPartition`, NOT `MainGrid`

This world's hash is `UWorldPartitionRuntimeHashSet`;
`WorldPartitionRuntimeHashSet.cpp:269` names the default partition
`MainPartition`. `wp.Runtime.OverrideRuntimeLoadingRange` is an EXACT FName
lookup with NO wildcard (`WorldPartitionSubsystem.cpp:563-571`). A wrong name
does not warn — it silently does nothing.

### `--truth` MUST SUPPRESS THE DERIVED RANGE

Both blocks name the same grid, and the derived append lands AFTER the truth
command in one `start_console_commands` list. Last writer wins, so 12 km was
being overwritten by 256 m on the same grid, in the same list.

### DISCOVERY WINDOWS ARE NOT DEADLINES

`ue_exec.run` passes `timeout` to `_select_verified_node` ONLY;
`remote.run_command` takes no timeout, so payload EXECUTION is unbounded. Use
25. Callers passing 120-900 "to be safe" bought nothing and spent it all:
900 s before every truth capture, 600 s before every `--load-all-regions`.

## R-BENCHCAPTURE REJECTED — additions 2026-09-09

**A GATE DECIDED BY COMPARING TWO DIFFERENT INSTRUMENTS.**
→ SYMPTOM: Task 0's skyline-IoU acceptance reported FAIL at 0.887; the same
player frame against a SAME-DAY, same-pipeline truth frame reads 0.970 PASS.
→ CAUSE: an MRQ player frame was compared against an editor/HighResShot truth
frame from two days earlier, and the difference was called residency.
→ THE TELL WAS IN THE OUTPUT: `player_land_truth_sky` must be ~0 — the player
cannot show MORE world than the fully-loaded frame — and it read 0.70%
against 0.10% for the same-day pair. That term measures the instrument gap.
→ CORRECT: same instrument, same pipeline, same session, or WITHHOLD the
verdict. Annotating the caveat and letting the verdict stand is not enough.
→ REFERENCE: LESSONS 2026-09-09d.

**A NULL RESULT FROM A LEVER THAT WAS NEVER CONNECTED.**
→ SYMPTOM: 2026-09-06 concluded "PIE cannot be force-loaded" from three
measured levers, and the truth instrument was rebuilt on the editor because
of it — where `HighResShot` then would not complete above ~960x540 against a
force-loaded world, leaving no working truth capture at all.
→ CAUSE: one of the three levers named a grid that does not exist.
→ THE TELL: the `derived` block of the SAME benchmark.json had already
discovered `MainPartition` and written its provenance. Two declarations in
one artefact named the same engine object differently and nothing compared
them.
→ CORRECT: before concluding a lever does not work, prove it was CONNECTED —
read back its effect, not just its command.
→ REFERENCE: LESSONS 2026-09-09d.

**`render_queue_with_executor(CLASS)` WHEN THE EXECUTOR NEEDS CONFIGURING.**
-> SYMPTOM: it CONSTRUCTS AND STARTS in one call, so
`set_is_rendering_offscreen(True)` on the returned object lands after the render
is under way. Observed 2026-09-05: `Job 1/3, 0% Completed` indefinitely, 50
shader jobs queued with `Num Already Dispatched: 0`, zero ShaderCompileWorker
processes, editor responding, CPU ~6% of one core.
-> CORRECT: `new_object(MoviePipelinePIEExecutor)`, configure it, then
`render_queue_with_executor_instance(executor)`.
-> **NOT PROVEN AS THE CAUSE OF THE STALL.** It is a real ordering defect found
while diagnosing, and the first thing to eliminate. The shader-dispatch stall
itself is UNEXPLAINED.

**POLLING RENDER PROGRESS THROUGH REMOTE EXEC.**
-> SYMPTOM: silence. Remote-exec Python runs on the GAME THREAD and MRQ owns
the game thread while rendering, so the polls never execute -- not one
`LogPython` line appeared in the engine log for the whole render. The poller
would have reported failure on a SUCCESSFUL capture just as readily.
-> CORRECT: instruments that do not need the game thread -- the engine log's
size and mtime, the frames arriving on disk, and the editor's MAIN WINDOW
TITLE, which MRQ updates with `[Job n/N Total] Current Job: P% Completed.` The
window title is what diagnosed this stall.
-> GENERAL: when instrumenting a long operation, check that the instrument runs
on a different thread, process or machine than its subject.

**A TIMEOUT WHERE A STALL GATE BELONGS.**
-> SYMPTOM: a render that dies in its first minute is indistinguishable from a
slow one until the full 3600 s timeout expires, and then reports the wrong
thing.
-> CORRECT: refuse when the engine log has been idle 600 s with the render
unfinished, and say STALL.

**LAUNCHING A LONG RENDER WITHOUT LINE-BUFFERED STDOUT.**
-> SYMPTOM: twenty minutes of empty output file; progress and hang look
identical. Second occurrence of this defect IN ONE SESSION.
-> CORRECT: fixed at the source -- `bench_capture` calls
`sys.stdout.reconfigure(line_buffering=True)` itself so no caller has to
remember `-u`. Make the defect unrepresentable rather than remembered.

### R-EDITOR-CLOSE — THIRD OCCURRENCE, and the first CLOSE cancels a render (2026-09-05)

The recipe held, and the sequence had a wrinkle worth recording.

    1  census   0 dirty, level /Game/Alpine8K            CLEAN
    2  quiet    newest Content write 3826 s old          QUIET
    3  retry    CloseMainWindow issued TWICE             unhonoured
    4  kill     authorized by 1 + 2; editor gone         DONE

**THE FIRST `CloseMainWindow()` DID NOT CLOSE THE EDITOR — IT CANCELLED THE
STALLED MRQ RENDER.** The window title went from
`Movie Pipeline Render (Preview) [Job 1/3 Total] Current Job: 0% Completed.` to
`LandscapeLab - Unreal Editor`, the game thread came free, and remote exec
started answering again (the dirty census then ran in 30 s, having been
impossible moments earlier).

That is worth knowing in both directions:

- **A close request against a rendering editor is a render cancel, not a
  close.** If a capture has to be abandoned, this is the lever; it does not
  require a kill.
- **And "the close was ignored" may mean "the close did something else".**
  Counting close attempts without watching what CHANGED would have read this as
  two failures when the first one worked and did something useful.

After the render was cancelled the editor entered a genuine shutdown that did
not finish: working set fell 17.3 -> 12.8 -> 11.3 GB and then sat there for
~20 minutes, CPU advancing ~1 s per 30 s, `Responding: True`, window title
empty. Both preconditions were re-verified at that point, so step 4 applied.

**The step-2 mtime is what makes the kill safe, and it earned its place again:**
the newest Content write was over an hour old and was `Bench_Still_vista.uasset`
— an asset this session had saved and verified — so nothing was in flight.

## R-BENCHCAPTURE — RESIDENCY IS A DECLARED, READ-BACK PRECONDITION (2026-09-06)

**Status: THE GATE IS PROVEN; FORCE-LOAD IS NOT SOLVED.** Residency is declared
in `benchmark.json`, applied by `bench_capture`, and read back from inside PIE.
It refuses correctly on real data. Making the whole world resident for a truth
frame **does not work yet** and the cause is unexplained.

### THE THREE PARTS, AND ALL THREE ARE REQUIRED

    DECLARED   benchmark.json residency{}: expect_landscape_components 1024,
               engine_warm_up_frames 180, require_probe, near_field{}, truth{}
    APPLIED    UMoviePipelineAntiAliasingSetting.engine_warm_up_count, with
               use_camera_cut_for_warm_up FALSE -- EngineWarmUpCount is gated
               behind that EditCondition (AntiAliasingSetting.h:100), so it is
               set explicitly and read back, never assumed
    READ BACK  scripts/payloads/bench_residency_probe.py, run ON THE PIE GAME
               THREAD by MRQ's end_console_commands as `py "<path>"`

### WHY THE PROBE NEEDS ITS OWN CHANNEL

Remote exec runs Python on the game thread, and MRQ owns the game thread for
the whole render — proven 2026-09-05, when not one `LogPython` line appeared
during a capture. `PythonScriptPlugin.cpp:1057-1060` handles **`PY`** as a
runtime exec command, so MRQ's own console hooks can run Python where remote
exec cannot. `end_console_commands` fires after the shot's frames and before
PIE tears down; during a static shot residency only grows, so it is a LOWER
BOUND on what the frame saw — the safe direction for a gate.

The census is `measure_frame_cost`'s, moved to the game world via
`UnrealEditorSubsystem.get_game_world()`. Components come from
`get_components_by_class(LandscapeComponent)` and **never** the
`landscape_components` UPROPERTY, which reads 0 on a fully loaded world
(R-FRAMECOST REJECTED).

### THE VERDICT KEEPS THREE OUTCOMES APART

    full census, at or above the declared figure       PASS
    short                                             FAIL
    no probe line / probe errored / unreadable        NO VERDICT, never PASS

"I could not look" is not "it was there", and the unreadable case says
*could not count*, not *absent*.

### THE MEASURED STATE OF THIS WORLD, 2026-09-06

    near_ground   12 of 1024 components    2,781 foliage instances
    mid_slope     16 of 1024                 265
    vista         16 of 1024                 265

Every bench frame ever taken here was rendered on a ~1.4% resident world.

### NEAR-FIELD MODE, AND WHY IT EXISTS

`--near-field` judges residency **within a declared radius of the camera**
(`residency.near_field`: 600 m, 16 components) instead of over the whole world.
Demanding all 1024 of a dolly through the town refuses work that is genuinely
correct — the near field IS resident — and **a gate that refuses correct work
is a gate that gets switched off**. A near-field PASS licenses nothing about
the 1–3 km bands, and the declaration says so in as many words.
