and the lookup is an exact FName match (`WorldPartitionSubsystem.cpp:563-571`).
-> **UNEXPLAINED.** The obvious next diagnostic,
`wp.Runtime.DumpWorldPartitions`, produces no log output in either the editor
or PIE, so it needs solving before it can be used.

**WARM-UP FRAMES AS A CURE FOR MISSING DISTANT CELLS.**
-> SYMPTOM: 180 and then 300 warm-up frames, read back, changed nothing.
-> CAUSE: warm-up buys TIME. Cells outside the loading RANGE are not late,
they are not requested. Time does not fix range.

**TREATING "NOTHING BEYOND 1 KM" AS A STREAMING BUG.**
-> It is the absence of HLOD. `Alpine8K_HLODLayer_Instanced` / `..._Merged`
exist as layer DEFINITIONS and **no built `WorldPartitionHLOD` actor package
exists anywhere** under `Content/`. Beyond the streaming range World Partition
shows a proxy if one was built and nothing if not.
-> CORRECT: build HLOD (Task 7) before judging anything in the shape or blob
bands. This is why the operator moved Task 7 ahead of imposters.

## R-BENCHCAPTURE REJECTED — additions 2026-09-06 (the dolly)

**A DOLLY SCORE TAKEN WITH AUTO-EXPOSURE LIVE.**
-> SYMPTOM: `temporal_stability` scored 0.66877 on the first dolly. Mean luma
drifted 0.3486 -> 0.2749 across the 8.4 m walk and 15.2% of pixels changed by
more than 0.10 between CONSECUTIVE frames, which are 4.7 cm apart. The tool
Weber-normalises to LOCAL luminance, so a global exposure ramp survives
normalisation and dominates the residual. A LOD pop would be invisible inside
it.
-> CAUSE: `benchmark.json` said `"lighting": "... exposure manual"` in prose and
NOTHING APPLIED OR READ IT BACK.
-> CORRECT: `r.DefaultFeature.AutoExposure 0` (SceneView.cpp:183) and
`r.EyeAdaptationQuality 0` (PostProcessEyeAdaptation.cpp:361), expressed as
PROFILE CVARS so they travel the path that already reads back from the engine's
own `Applying CVar` log lines. **APPLIED 2026-09-06, NOT YET VERIFIED** -- the
dolly must be re-captured and the luma drift shown gone before any score is a
baseline.
-> THE PATTERN, THIRD INSTANCE IN THREE DAYS: perf stations declared no FOV;
residency was declared for the perf tool and not the capture tool; exposure was
declared in prose and never applied. **A parameter that reads like a setting
and polices nothing is worse than an absent one**, because it answers "is this
controlled?" with a yes.

**POPULATING A NEW FIELD WITH THE OLD QUESTION'S ANSWER.**
-> SYMPTOM: `near_field.expect_components_within_radius` was declared 16. The
capture measured 8 within 600 m and refused. 16 was the WHOLE-WORLD component
count from the same probe output — the exact figure the distance-aware census
was built to stop using.
-> CORRECT: a near-field threshold must come from a near-field measurement.
-> AND NOTE THE TRAP IN THE REPAIR: changing 16 to 8 to make it pass is
indistinguishable from widening a tolerance. It is legitimate only because the
original was never evidence about the near field, and the replacement must be
labelled as a REGRESSION TRIPWIRE derived from observation, not as a justified
correctness floor. Not changed this session; the refusal stands in the artefact.

## R-HLOD — GIVING A WORLD PARTITION WORLD ITS HLOD LAYER (2026-09-08)

**Status: the ASSIGNMENT half is PROVEN and locked. The BUILD half is not yet
in this recipe** — see R-HLOD PENDING at the end. Do not read the locked half
as licence to assume the build works.

### The one thing to know

**You almost certainly do not need to assign an HLOD layer to any actor.**
A World Partition world has a world-level default, and the engine applies it to
every actor that has none, at streaming-generation time, without writing to a
single external actor package.

    UWorldPartition::DefaultHLODLayer      WorldPartition.h:610-612
                                           UPROPERTY(EditAnywhere,
                                           DisplayName "Default HLOD Layer")
      -> WorldPartitionStreamingGeneration.cpp:1384
             MainContainerCollectionInstance.HLODLayer =
                 FSoftObjectPath(WorldPartitionContext->GetDefaultHLODLayer())
      -> :1425   ResolveHLODLayer(...)
      -> :868-875
             if (!GetHLODLayer().IsValid()
                 && GetIsSpatiallyLoaded()
                 && GetActorIsHLODRelevant())
                     SetRuntimeHLODLayer(ParentHLODLayer);

`SetRuntimeHLODLayer` (:549-553) writes the streaming-generation VIEW. The
persisted value lives at `WorldPartitionActorDesc.cpp:153` and is left alone.

### The procedure
> STATUS: SUPERSEDED-BY B3.21 — the HLOD landscape-layer procedure example preceded the B3.21 rework

    payload  scripts/payloads/hlod_save_world_default.py
    run      python scripts/ue_exec.py scripts/payloads/hlod_save_world_default.py \
                 --set LAYER=/Game/Alpine8K_HLODLayer_Landscape
    probe    scripts/payloads/hlod_route_discovery.py    (read-only, no edits)

**The route, and every hop is a casualty of guessing:**

    world = UnrealEditorSubsystem.get_editor_world()
    ws    = world.get_world_settings()                  METHOD ON WORLD
    wp    = ws.get_editor_property("world_partition")
    wp.set_editor_property("default_hlod_layer", load_asset(LAYER))
    LevelEditorSubsystem.save_current_level()

### MEASURED COST, on Alpine8K — 3,269 actors, 1,093 IFA, 256 proxies, 1,446 SMA

    set                0.005 s
    save               0.520 s
    Alpine8K.umap      13,755 -> 13,915 bytes, mtime moved
    actor packages     ZERO written
    read-back          correct, chain re-resolved from the world

Against the alternative, measured 2026-09-07: 2,796 actors assigned, 843.7 s to
assign, and a save that had not finished after 90 minutes and was killed.

### Verification is the file, not the return value

`save_current_level()` returning `True` proves the call ran. Capture the
`.umap` size and mtime **before and after** and report the delta. Standing
rule 12 — the read-back comes from the artefact, and the re-read of
`default_hlod_layer` must come from a chain resolved afresh out of the world,
never from the object you just wrote to.

### Choosing the layer, since the world may already have a wrong one
> STATUS: WRONG — WRONG (B3.21): recommends a layer the same doc's later measurement shows inert

Alpine8K already had `default_hlod_layer` set — to `Alpine8K_HLODLayer_Instanced`,
INSTANCING, `loading_range` 76800 cm. **A default HLOD layer whose loading range
is INSIDE the World Partition streaming range does nothing you want**: the mesh
is still streamed at that distance, so the HLOD never gets to be the thing you
see. Its parent `Merged` was worse — range 51200, shorter than its own child,
and `is_spatially_loaded` false.

    rule   the HLOD loading range must EXCEED the WP streaming range
           (~1 km on this world), and a parent layer must outlive its child

Current: `Alpine8K_HLODLayer_Landscape`, MESH_MERGE, cell 25600, range 200000,
spatially loaded, no parent.

## R-HLOD REJECTED

**Assigning `hlod_layer` per actor across the world.** Symptom: the assignment
call itself returns cleanly (843.7 s for 2,796 actors, read-back correct) and
then the SAVE does not complete — 90 minutes, killed; reproduced once with
`save_dirty_packages()` and once with a per-package loop, so the save API is
NOT the variable. Correct approach: set `DefaultHLODLayer` on the
`UWorldPartition`, above. Reference: LESSONS 2026-09-07 (two entries) and
2026-09-08.

**Concluding "nothing points at the layers" from a per-actor `hlod_layer: None`
census.** Symptom: you will believe HLOD cannot build and go assign 2,796
actors. `hlod_layer: None` is the NORMAL state of an actor in a world that has
a default — `ResolveHLODLayer` supplies it at generation time. Correct check:
read `world.get_world_settings().get_editor_property("world_partition")
.get_editor_property("default_hlod_layer")` FIRST. On Alpine8K it had been set
the whole time. Reference: LESSONS 2026-09-08.

**Judging an editor "spinning" from an absolute CPU-core reading.** Symptom:
5–6.6 cores with a silent log, no files and flat DDC reads as a hang, and all
four signals agree. Alpine8K's editor IDLES at **8.19–8.28 cores** with a
byte-identical log and no `ShaderCompileWorker` children — higher than the
reading taken as the defect. Correct approach: take the idle baseline in the
same session, on the same loaded world, before attributing any CPU figure to
anything. Reference: LESSONS 2026-09-08.

**`unreal.GameplayStatics.get_world_settings`** — does not exist in 5.8.
Symptom: `AttributeError: type object 'GameplayStatics' has no attribute
'get_world_settings'`. Correct: `World.get_world_settings()`, a method on the
world object.

**`world.get_editor_property("persistent_level")`** — symptom: `Exception:
World: Failed to find property 'persistent_level' ... on 'World'`, *despite*
`UWorld::PersistentLevel` being `UPROPERTY(Transient)` at `World.h:952-953`.
Being a UPROPERTY in C++ is not sufficient for the Python attribute to exist.
Correct: `World.get_world_settings()` reaches WorldSettings directly.

**`Package.set_dirty_flag` / `Package.is_dirty`** — both `AttributeError`.
Symptom: the set succeeds and the save line raises, leaving the value live and
unsaved. Correct: do not touch the dirty flag; `set_editor_property` marks the
package, and `LevelEditorSubsystem.save_current_level()` writes it. Verify by
the `.umap` mtime, not by the flag.

**Looking for the WorldSettings actor in `EditorActorSubsystem.get_all_level_actors()`**
— symptom: zero hits across 3,269 actors, and a probe that reports `null` for
the whole chain. Correct:
`GameplayStatics.get_all_actors_of_class(world, WorldSettings)`, or the
`get_world_settings()` method.

**Assuming `dir(obj)` is the property contract.** `default_hlod_layer` does not
appear in `dir(world_partition)`; `get_editor_property("default_hlod_layer")`
returns it correctly. Absence from `dir()` is not absence from the reflected
surface.

## R-HLOD — AMENDED 2026-09-08b: A LAYER IS VALID BECAUSE A RUNTIME PARTITION REGISTERS IT

**This amendment supersedes the layer-choice advice in the locked half above.**
That advice said to pick a layer by loading range. Correct, but second — the
FIRST question is whether the world will accept the layer at all, and this
world rejects every layer it does not register.

### The rule

    an HLOD layer is NOT valid because the asset exists
    NOT valid because actors point at it
    NOT valid because it is the world default
    VALID only if a runtime partition lists it in
        RuntimePartitions[].HLODSetups[].HLODLayers

`IsValidHLODLayer` has three implementations that disagree, and which one runs
depends on the world's runtime hash CLASS:

    UWorldPartitionRuntimeSpatialHash   WorldPartitionRuntimeSpatialHash.h:326
                                        returns literal TRUE -- anything passes
    UWorldPartitionRuntimeHash (base)   WorldPartitionRuntimeHash.h:225
                                        returns literal FALSE
    UWorldPartitionRuntimeHashSet       WorldPartitionRuntimeHashSet.cpp:377-380
                                        the only REAL one; delegates to
                                        ResolveRuntimePartitionForHLODLayer
                                        (:388-435)

**`/Game/Alpine8K` is a `WorldPartitionRuntimeHashSet`** — read back from
`...WorldSettings.WorldPartition_0.WorldPartitionRuntimeHashSet_0`. So this
world enforces registration and a SpatialHash world would not. Check the class
before reusing any of this on another map.

### THE REGISTRY IS NOT REACHABLE FROM PYTHON

`RuntimePartitions` is `EditAnywhere` but **`private:`**
(`WorldPartitionRuntimeHashSet.h:262-263`), and `FRuntimePartitionDesc` /
`FRuntimePartitionHLODSetup` are bare `USTRUCT()` without `BlueprintType`
(:27-29, :55-57). `get_editor_property("runtime_partitions")` fails.

    CONSEQUENCE, and it is the standing instruction:
    DO NOT AUTHOR NEW HLODLayer ASSETS FOR THIS WORLD.
    Reuse a registered one and tune THAT asset's own fields, which ARE
    reachable: layer_type, cell_size, loading_range, is_spatially_loaded.

Registration itself is a World Settings panel edit or a C++ change.

### WHAT THIS WORLD REGISTERS, read back 2026-09-08
> STATUS: SUPERSEDED-BY B3.21 — the registration snapshot preceded the B3.21 rework

    /Game/Alpine8K_HLODLayer_Instanced   runtime grid MainPartition:HLODLayer_Instanced
    /Game/Alpine8K_HLODLayer_Merged      runtime grid MainPartition:HLODLayer_Merged

and NOTHING else. `Alpine8K_HLODLayer_FoliageApprox` and
`Alpine8K_HLODLayer_Landscape`, both created 2026-09-07, are registered by
nothing and are inert.

### THE MEASUREMENT, single variable
> STATUS: SUPERSEDED-BY B3.21 — the instanced-actors result is overtaken by B3.21

    world default = Alpine8K_HLODLayer_Landscape
        0 HLOD actors, 2,775 "invalid HLOD layer" errors, execution 1.41 s
    world default = Alpine8K_HLODLayer_Instanced
        2,230 HLOD actors, 25 errors, execution 2.84 s

Nothing else changed between the two runs. External actor packages for this
world went 3,269 -> 5,499.

### THE LABEL GRID, after Setup and before Build

`-BuildSingleHLOD=` matches the actor LABEL exactly
(`WorldPartitionHLODsBuilder.cpp:1134`), and labels are only knowable after
Setup. **Do not try to pick a cell by proximity: before Build, every HLOD actor
desc reports zero-extent bounds at the origin** — the actors exist, the
geometry does not, so there is nothing to be near. Read the labels instead;
they carry `<source>_L<level>_X<i>_Y<j>`.

Measured grid, cell size DERIVED from the observed index span against the
812,800 cm world extent rather than assumed from the layer asset's `cell_size`:

    grid                              level  cells  derived cell
    MainPartition:HLODLayer_Instanced   L0     217     12700 cm
    MainPartition:HLODLayer_Instanced   L1     736     25400 cm
    MainPartition:HLODLayer_Instanced   L2     252     50800 cm
    MainPartition:HLODLayer_Merged      L0     773     25400 cm
    MainPartition:HLODLayer_Merged      L1     252     50800 cm
                                            -----
                                             2230

Note the derived sizes are 12700/25400/50800, NOT the 25600 the layer assets
declare. Tool: `scripts/payloads/hlod_label_grid.py`.

### THE ORDER

    1  read the runtime hash CLASS            hlod_hash_by_name.py
    2  set the world default to a REGISTERED layer, save
                                              hlod_save_world_default.py
    3  -SetupHLODs                            creates the actors, no geometry
    4  read the label grid, pick a cell       hlod_label_grid.py
    5  -BuildHLODs -BuildSingleHLOD=<label> -AllowCommandletRendering
    6  verify the built actor has NON-ZERO bounds and a mesh

Step 6 is the read-back and it is not optional: step 3 produces 2,230 actors
that look like success and contain nothing.

the label's `_L<level>_X<i>_Y<j>`, and derive the cell size from the observed
index span rather than the layer's declared `cell_size` — they differ here
(25400 vs 25600).

`MainPartition:HLODLayer_Instanced` and `MainPartition:HLODLayer_Merged`, not

elimination can be re-judged. → REFERENCE: REGISTER, "three levers".

## R-HLOD — AMENDED 2026-09-08c: THE BUILD STEP IS NOT YET PROVEN, AND `-BuildSingleHLOD` IS A TARGET NOT A TOTAL

### `-BuildSingleHLOD` pulls its dependency chain

Asking for one Merged L0 cell produced:

    #### Building 6 HLOD actors ####
    [1 / 6] Building HLOD actor Alpine8K_HLODLayer_Instanced/Alpine8K_MainPartition_L0_X-20_Y22...

A Merged cell is built FROM the Instanced cells beneath it, so the builder
resolves and queues the sources too. Budget for the chain, not for one actor,
and do not read a count greater than one as a filter failure.

### STATUS: WEDGED, cause bounded but not established

The run stalls immediately after queueing material shadermap compiles:

    LogMaterial: Missing cached shadermap for .../spruce_half_01_MA
                 in PCD3D_SM6 ... compiling.        (~15 such lines)
    LogAssetRegistry: Asset registry cache written as 159.5 MiB
    <nothing further>

    60 s window   0.044 cores, log bytes IDENTICAL, 0 ShaderCompileWorker
                  processes, 6.1 GB working set flat

**Not a spin — a wedge.** See the CPU-baseline entry in R-HLOD REJECTED
(2026-09-08): this world's EDITOR idles at 8.2 cores, so 0.044 is a real stop
rather than a busy process being misread.

Do not brute-force it. Next attempts, cheapest first, are listed in
LESSONS 2026-09-08c; the first is simply to re-run once the shader work is warm.

### Killing a stalled BUILD COMMANDLET is safe, and R-EDITOR-CLOSE does not apply

`SaveHLODPackage` writes per actor as each one completes
(`WorldPartitionHLODsBuilder.cpp:751-759`). If no actor has completed, nothing
is half-written. Verified after killing this run: working tree clean apart from
the log, external actor count still 5,499 -- the 2,230 Setup packages intact and
zero build products.

R-EDITOR-CLOSE's census/quiescence/retry ceremony exists because the EDITOR
holds unsaved in-memory state. A commandlet holds none. Applying the editor
ritual to a commandlet costs a diagnosis and buys nothing.

## R-HLOD — AMENDED 2026-09-08d: IT BUILDS. `-noxgecontroller` IS MANDATORY ON THIS MACHINE

**Supersedes R-HLOD PENDING and the 2026-09-08c wedge status.** The build half
is now PROVEN, and the read-back is on record.

### The one line that must be on every HLOD commandlet

    -noxgecontroller

Without it, on this machine, the run wedges forever. With it, the same command
finishes in 80 seconds. Single variable, measured both ways:

    without   0 ShaderCompileWorker | 0.044 cores | never completes
    with     14 ShaderCompileWorker | 0.44 cores  | Built 6 HLOD actors, 1:20

### WHY, from source — and it is deliberate engine behaviour, not a fault

`r.XGEController.AvoidUsingLocalMachine` defaults to **1**, documented at
`XGEControllerModule.cpp:74-80` as *"Avoid spawning tasks on the local
(initiator) machine **except when running a commandlet** or -buildmachine is
passed"*. The implementation (:97-111):

    return !bForceUsingLocalMachine && !GIsBuildMachine && !IsRunningCommandlet();

So:

    EDITOR      IsRunningCommandlet() false -> avoid local -> falls back to
                LOCAL ShaderCompileWorkers -> compiles fine
    COMMANDLET  IsRunningCommandlet() true  -> DOES use local XGE -> hands the
                jobs to IncrediBuild -> they never return -> wedge

The two log lines differ by one word and that word is the whole diagnosis:

    editor      "XGE tasks will not be spawned on this machine."
    commandlet  "XGE tasks will be spawned on this machine."

IncrediBuild is installed here — `docs/environment.md` records it because its
`Manager.exe` holds port 8000 — but it does not service these jobs.

Switches, `XGEControllerModule.cpp:153-161`: `-noxgecontroller`,
`-noxgeshadercompile`, `-noshaderworker` all set `Enabled = 0`. **Use
`-noxgecontroller`** — `-noshaderworker` reads as though it would also suppress
the local worker being fallen back to, so it is the wrong lever even though it
sets the same variable.

### THIS APPLIES TO EVERY COMMANDLET, NOT JUST HLOD

Both `-SetupHLODs` runs on 2026-09-07/08 **also hung — on the way out.** Each
logged `Engine exit requested ... result 0`, did all its work correctly, and
then sat at 0.005 cores holding 2.1 GB and 4.5 GB until killed an hour later.
`FShaderCompilingManager` drains on shutdown and jobs dispatched to XGE never
drain.

    RULE: a commandlet that prints "Engine exit requested" has NOT exited.
    Check the process list, not the log line. Every commandlet run gets a
    post-run process check.

With `-noxgecontroller` the Setup rerun exited on its own.

### MEASURED BUILD COST, warm (the first actor pays a one-off shader compile)

    Instanced L0    0.02 s each      (instance transform lists, 56-115 KB)
    Instanced L1    4.9 s
    Merged L0      11.7 s            (merged mesh + baked textures, 13.9 MB)
    first actor    62.7 s one-off    material shadermaps for the foliage set

### ACCEPTANCE READ-BACK — `hlod_verify_built.py`

Cell `Alpine8K_HLODLayer_Merged/Alpine8K_HLODLayer_Instanced_L0_X-10_Y11`:

    bounds        26544 x 27092 x 9052 cm, NON-ZERO
                  (after Setup alone every HLOD desc reads zero extent)
    triangles     329,364      vertices 951,468      LODs 1
    nanite        FALSE
    material      MI_Alpine8K_HLODLayer_Instanced_L0_X-10_Y11
                  MaterialInstanceConstant, baked into the actor package
    package       130 bytes -> 13,959,833 bytes

The bounds contain the target point the cell was chosen for, which independently
confirms the label-grid cell-size derivation in the 08b amendment.

**Do not accept a package size as evidence of geometry.** Bytes grew for the
Setup stubs too. Count triangles.

## R-HLOD — THE FULL BUILD IS NOT YET AUTHORISED, AND THE REASON IS DISK

Extrapolating the measured per-actor costs to the 2,267 actors now set up:

    time   roughly 4-5 hours       -> DETACHED / overnight, not single-session
    disk   roughly 15-20 GB NEW    -> and `LandscapeLab/Content` IS TRACKED IN GIT

**`__ExternalActors__` mixes HLOD packages in with real actors under the same
hash-bucketed GUID paths**, so they cannot be separated by a `.gitignore`
pattern. A full build therefore adds on the order of 15-20 GB of DERIVED,
regenerable binary content to a 41 GB repository that already carries an
unresolved 1.2 GB history-bloat item.

**Resolve the git strategy BEFORE running the full build.** Running it first
and deciding afterwards is the expensive order.

## R-HLOD — AMENDED 2026-09-08e: THE FULL BUILD, AND KEEPING ~17 GB OF IT OUT OF GIT

### ⚠ A FRESH CLONE HAS NO HLOD AT ALL — NOT EVEN THE STUBS. THIS IS NOT A BUG.

**Standing the project up from a clone requires `-SetupHLODs` then `-BuildHLODs`,
both with `-noxgecontroller`, before anything beyond the ~1 km streaming range
will render.** The HLOD packages are untracked build products; git carries the
layer assets and the world settings and nothing else. So a clone renders a void
past the streaming range, `mid_slope` and `vista` come back featureless, and
every one of those symptoms is identical to the 2026-09-05-through-09-07 defect
that cost three sessions. It is not that defect. It is an unbuilt world.

    clone -> -SetupHLODs -> -BuildHLODs   both with -noxgecontroller
    ~45 min. Until then, distance is EMPTY BY DESIGN.

### The command

    UnrealEditor-Cmd.exe <uproject> /Game/Alpine8K \
      -run=WorldPartitionBuilderCommandlet \
      -Builder=WorldPartitionHLODsBuilder -BuildHLODs \
      -noxgecontroller -AllowCommandletRendering \
      -unattended -nosplash -nopause -abslog=<repo>/_verify/hlod/<date>/build_full.log

`-noxgecontroller` is not optional here — see the 08d amendment. `-BuildHLODs`
without `-RebuildHLODs` skips cells that are already built, so the command is
resumable: re-running it after an interruption continues rather than restarting.

### WRITE THE START MARKER FIRST, BEFORE LAUNCHING

    _verify/hlod/<date>/BUILD_START_MARKER

Its **mtime** is what `scripts/hlod_gitignore.py` compares against to tell this
build's output from packages already on disk. A wall-clock string would have to
be parsed and time-zone reasoned about; a file's mtime is compared directly
against other files' mtimes in the same clock. Write it in the same step that
launches the build, or the reference is wrong.

Tag a restore point in the same breath — this is a risky-op checkpoint by the
letter of the rule (bulk write across ~2,267 packages).

### MEASURED COST — 8129 m world, 2,267 HLOD actors

    rate      ~51-59 actors/min, blended        total ~45 min
    disk      ~7.6 MB/actor blended             total ~17 GB
    memory    7.1 GB at launch -> 12.5 GB by 7 min, watch it
    exit      the process EXITS on its own with -noxgecontroller

**DO NOT EXTRAPOLATE COST FROM THE FIRST FEW HUNDRED ACTORS.** The builder does
not write cells in a representative order: early ones are cheap `Instanced`
cells (~0.02 s, tens of KB), later ones are `Merged` cells (~11.7 s, up to
13.9 MB). A projection from the first 202 packages gave 5–6 GB and was wrong by
3x. Either wait for a blended sample or state the figure as provisional.

### THE GIT STEP, AND ITS ORDER IS THE WHOLE POINT

**The packages are ALREADY TRACKED** — `-SetupHLODs` created them as ~130-byte
stubs and those were committed. `-BuildHLODs` inflates them in place. So:

    .gitignore ALONE DOES NOTHING. Ignores do not apply to tracked paths.
    Adding 2,267 entries succeeds, changes nothing, and the 17 GB still
    enters the next commit.

The operation is `git rm --cached` **and** the ignore entry, and it must happen
**BEFORE the first commit after the build**:

    committed then untracked   17 GB in history forever
    untracked then committed   17 GB never in history

    python scripts/hlod_gitignore.py           # dry run, writes nothing
    python scripts/hlod_gitignore.py --apply    # manifest + rm --cached + ignore

Then commit **the manifest and `.gitignore` only**. History keeps the 130-byte
stubs, ~300 KB in total.

### MEMBERSHIP IS BY CONTENT SIGNATURE (standing rule 8)

World Partition hash-buckets HLOD packages into the SAME GUID directories as
landscape proxies and foliage, so the path says nothing and `git rm --cached`
on a real actor would be a real defect. A package is HLOD **iff its bytes
contain `WorldPartitionHLOD`** — 3–7 hits in a built HLOD package, 0 in a
`LandscapeStreamingProxy`. It appears within the first 16 KB even in the
13.9 MB cell, so a 1 MB head read decides it, with a full-file fallback when
the head is inconclusive.

All three conditions required: under `__ExternalActors__`, mtime newer than the
marker, and carrying the signature.

### VERIFICATION IS BOTH DIRECTIONS, and the script exits non-zero otherwise

    POSITIVE  first/middle/last manifest entries are ignored AND absent from
              `git ls-files`
    NEGATIVE  the four HLOD layer assets, `Alpine8K.umap`, the manifest itself
              and a sample of surviving tracked actors are NOT ignored and
              REMAIN in the index; no untracked files left under
              `__ExternalActors__`

A one-directional check passes just as happily with `*` in `.gitignore`.

## R-HLOD REJECTED — additions 2026-09-08e

**Adding `.gitignore` entries for build output without checking whether it is
tracked.** → SYMPTOM: no error, a correct-looking 2,267-line diff,
`git check-ignore` still reports a match, and the content lands in the next
commit regardless. The failure is invisible until the repository is 17 GB
heavier and only a history rewrite will help. → CAUSE: ignores do not apply to
tracked paths, and `-BuildHLODs` rewrites tracked stubs rather than creating
files. → CORRECT: `git rm --cached` plus the ignore entry, before any commit.
→ REFERENCE: LESSONS 2026-09-08f.

**Letting a tool silently perform an operation that has no effect.**
→ SYMPTOM: as above — the whole class. → CORRECT: when a tool can do something
inert, make it REFUSE and REPORT. `hlod_gitignore.py` sorts candidates into
tracked and untracked and declines to write ignore entries for the tracked
ones; that single decision is what surfaced the defect, in one line of output,
before anything was committed.

**Extrapolating a bulk job's cost from its first slice.** → SYMPTOM: 5–6 GB
reported to the operator, actual ~17 GB. → CAUSE: the first 202 packages were
cheap `Instanced` cells; the builder's write order is not representative.
→ CORRECT: blended sample, or say "provisional" out loud.

## R-HLOD — AMENDED 2026-09-08f: THE PROXY BUDGET COMES FROM THE BLOB BAND, AND `MeshMerge` CANNOT PRODUCE ONE

### The structural mistake in the first build

`Alpine8K_HLODLayer_Merged` was `EHLODLayerType::MeshMerge`. **`FMeshMergingSettings`
has NO triangle-reduction field.** `LODSelectionType`/`SpecificLOD` choose WHICH
SOURCE LOD to merge; `MaterialSettings` controls the bake; nothing decimates.
**MeshMerge concatenates.** One 254 m cell came out at 329,364 triangles because
that is the sum of its sources.

So this was never a settings tweak — it is a LAYER TYPE change. Of the types
that can reduce (`HLODLayer.h:31-38`):

    Instancing / MeshMerge   cannot reduce
    MeshSimplify             FMeshProxySettings -- ScreenSize / VoxelSize,
                             no direct triangle target
    MeshApproximate          FMeshApproximationSettings -- SimplifyMethod +
                             TargetTriCount, the control the budget is
                             expressed in

### THE BUDGET, derived

    4K/90 deg = 42.67 ppd            REGISTER, PROVEN (B1.3)
    blob band = 1.5-6 px             Brief 1's four-band ladder
    Merged L0 cell = 254 m           derived label grid, R-HLOD 08b

A proxy triangle should be no finer than the smallest feature that reads at the
distance where the proxy IS the representation. For N triangles as a grid,
quad edge = 254 / sqrt(N/2) m, and its angular size is
`(edge/d) * 57.2958 * 42.67` px:

    N = 4,000    edge 5.68 m   6.9 px @2km   3.5 px @4km   1.7 px @8km
    N = 329,364  edge 0.63 m   0.77 px       0.38 px       0.19 px

**4,000 puts the quad edge inside the blob band across 2-8 km. The built proxy
was SUB-PIXEL at every distance it is ever seen** — 82x too dense by count.

    TEXTURE 512^2 over 254 m = 0.50 m/texel = 0.61 px/texel at 2 km, already
            finer than the pixel grid. 1024^2 = 0.30 px/texel pays 4x memory
            for detail below the sampling limit. 512 is the target, 1024 the
            ceiling.
    NANITE  NOT enabled. It earns its cost on dense meshes; at 4,000 triangles
            a plain static mesh is cheaper, and Nanite adds a fallback mesh
            whose own RT representation is the thing being removed.

### RAY TRACING: THE DEFAULT IS THE DEFECT

`FMeshApproximationSettings::bSupportRayTracing` **defaults to TRUE**
(`MeshApproximationSettings.h:211`; `FMeshMergingSettings` carries the same
field at line 135). That default gave all 2,267 proxies an acceleration
structure. Measured, single variable:

    r.RayTracing on    peak VRAM 12,434 MiB   crashed DEVICE_HUNG, 2 of 2
    r.RayTracing=0     peak VRAM    812 MiB   opened in 90 s, 0 crashes,
                                              0 compile warnings (vs 558+)

**An HLOD proxy standing in for objects at 1.5-6 px never needs to be ray
traced. Set `support_ray_tracing` FALSE.**

`bForceRayTracingFarField` on the LAYER (`HLODLayer.h:154-155`) is an opt-IN
that ADDS spatially-loaded HLOD to the RT far field. It is not the lever and is
left alone.

### THE VALUES, applied and read back 2026-09-08

    layer_type            MESH_APPROXIMATE      was MESH_MERGE
    simplify_method       FIXED_TRIANGLE_COUNT
    target_tri_count      4000
    support_ray_tracing   false                 was true (engine default)
    generate_nanite_enabled_mesh  false
    texture_sizing_type   USE_MANUAL_OVERRIDE_TEXTURE_SIZE
    texture_size          512 x 512
    cell_size             25600      loading_range 51200   (unchanged)

Tool: `scripts/payloads/hlod_set_proxy_budget.py` — read back from a FRESHLY
LOADED asset, not the object written.

### PYTHON STRIPS THE LEADING `b` FROM BOOLEANS

`b_support_ray_tracing` raises "Failed to find property";
`support_ray_tracing` works. Same rule as `bIsSpatiallyLoaded` ->
`is_spatially_loaded`. Probe with `hlod_probe_approx_fields.py` rather than
guessing one round trip at a time.

### CHANGING `layer_type` SWAPS THE SETTINGS OBJECT, and it does so from Python

`HLODBuilderMeshMergeSettings` -> `HLODBuilderMeshApproximateSettings` on the
`set_editor_property("layer_type", ...)` call, verified by re-reading
`hlod_builder_settings` immediately afterwards. **It also invalidates every
dependent HLOD mesh**, and an open editor will start recompiling them
immediately — which will make the remote-exec node stop answering (`ue_exec`
exit 3) while it works. That is the editor being BUSY, not dead: check
`MainWindowTitle` and CPU before concluding anything.

## R-HLOD REJECTED — additions 2026-09-08f

**`MeshMerge` for a distance proxy.** → SYMPTOM: 329,364 triangles per 254 m
cell, 10.46 GB across the world, and the world stops opening. → CAUSE:
`FMeshMergingSettings` has no reduction field; MeshMerge concatenates its
sources. → CORRECT: `MeshApproximate` with `SimplifyMethod =
FixedTriangleCount` and a `TargetTriCount` derived from the band the proxy
serves. → REFERENCE: LESSONS 2026-09-08h; this amendment.

**Leaving `bSupportRayTracing` at its default on HLOD proxies.** → SYMPTOM:
peak VRAM 12,434 MiB of a 15,235 MiB budget, `DXGI_ERROR_DEVICE_HUNG` with a
page fault on `StaticMesh_Alpine8K_HLODLayer_Merged_0`, reproduced 2 of 2.
→ CAUSE: the field defaults to TRUE, so every proxy builds an acceleration
structure. → CORRECT: false — a 1.5-6 px blob is never a ray-tracing target.
→ EVIDENCE: `r.RayTracing=0` opened the same world at 812 MiB peak VRAM.

**Choosing a proxy triangle count by eye, or by "what looks like a reasonable
reduction".** → CORRECT: derive it. Quad edge = cell_size / sqrt(N/2); require
its angular size to sit inside the band the proxy serves at the distances the
proxy is seen. The arithmetic is three lines and it produced 4,000 from first
principles.

## R-HLOD — AMENDED 2026-09-08g: APPROXIMATION ACCURACY IS DERIVED FROM THE QUAD SIZE, NOT LEFT AT DEFAULT

### The cost of MeshApproximate is the VOXEL GRID, not the triangle target

`TargetTriCount` is what the SIMPLIFIER aims at — it governs the mesh that
comes out. The expensive step happens before that: MeshApproximate voxelises
the cell's contents, and the voxel resolution is
`FMeshApproximationSettings::ApproximationAccuracy`
(`MeshApproximationSettings.h:73-75`):

    /** Approximation Accuracy in Meters, will determine (eg) voxel resolution */
    meta = (DisplayName = "Approximation Accuracy (meters)", ClampMin = "0.001")
    float ApproximationAccuracy = 1.0f;

**Lowering `TargetTriCount` does not make the voxelisation cheaper.** Measured
at the default accuracy of 1.0 m: 265 cells in 52.4 min = **5.06 actors/min,
11.86 s/actor**, all of them `Merged L0`.

### ⚠ THE UNITS ARE METRES. A VALUE OF 150 IS NOT 150 cm.

`ApproximationAccuracy = 1.5` means a 1.5 m voxel. Setting `150` would mean
150-METRE accuracy on a 254 m cell — about two voxels across — which destroys
the proxy rather than accelerating it, and would do so without erroring.
`hlod_set_approx_accuracy.py` REFUSES any value above 10.0 for exactly this
reason.

### THE DERIVATION

    quad edge   4,000 tris on a 254 m cell = 254/sqrt(2000) = 5.68 m
    voxel       a quarter of the quad edge = 1.42 m, taken as 1.5 m

A voxel at roughly a quarter of the quad edge resolves everything the
simplifier can keep and nothing it must discard: detail finer than a
quarter-quad cannot survive decimation to 5.68 m quads, so paying to voxelise
it is pure waste.

Cross-checked against the band the proxy serves: at 2 km a 1.5 m voxel subtends
`1.5/2000 rad = 1.8 px`, already under the 6 px shape threshold. The voxel grid
is not resolving anything a viewer could read as shape.

    accuracy 1.0 m -> 254 voxels across the cell
    accuracy 1.5 m -> 169 voxels across      (~3.4x fewer in 3D)

**MEASURED 2026-09-08i, AND THE COST PREDICTION ABOVE IS WRONG.** Like-for-like
sustained runs gave 5.06 actors/min at accuracy 1.0 and 5.62 at 1.5 -- a 3.4x
reduction in voxel COUNT bought **1.11x** of wall time. Voxel resolution is not
the dominant cost of MeshApproximate on this content; what is remains
unmeasured. Set the accuracy from the quad size because it is the RIGHT value,
not because it will be fast.

`ClampVoxelDimension` is 1024 (`:79`, max 1290), so 169 is nowhere near the
clamp — the accuracy value governs rather than being silently limited. **Check
that**: an accuracy fine enough to exceed the clamp is capped without warning,
and the setting then means something other than what it says.

### VERIFIED ON ONE CELL BEFORE ANYTHING WAS LAUNCHED

`-BuildSingleHLOD=..._L0_X-10_Y11 -RebuildHLODs -noxgecontroller
-AllowCommandletRendering`, then read back from the built mesh:

    triangles          3,988          target 4,000   (was 329,364)
    vertices           7,299                         (was 951,468)
    bounds             26697 x 27101 x 9989 cm, NON-ZERO
    mesh_support_ray_tracing   FALSE  <- the layer setting reached the OUTPUT
    nanite             false
    package            1,455,802 B                    (was 13,959,833)
    material           1 x MaterialInstanceConstant

**`UStaticMesh::bSupportRayTracing` on the BUILT MESH is the read-back that
matters** (`StaticMesh.h:1385`). The layer's builder setting is an INPUT;
whether the emitted mesh carries an acceleration structure is the thing that
cost 12,434 MiB of VRAM and hung the GPU twice. `hlod_verify_built.py` reads
the output.

### THE TIMING COMPARISON THAT WOULD HAVE BEEN WRONG

That single cell took **57.8 s**, against 11.86 s/actor for the accuracy-1.0
run. It is tempting to read that as five times SLOWER. **It is not a valid
comparison and must not be recorded as one:**

    accuracy 1.0   WARM process, 265th-ish cell, in-process caches hot
    accuracy 1.5   COLD process, FIRST Merged cell of the run, one-off costs

Two variables. A like-for-like figure needs a sustained run at the new accuracy
sampled the same way — same instrument, same warm state — which is what
`build3_acc15.log` is for.

## R-HLOD REJECTED — additions 2026-09-08g

**Lowering `TargetTriCount` to make MeshApproximate faster.** → SYMPTOM: the
output mesh gets smaller and the build takes just as long. → CAUSE: the cost is
the voxel grid, sized by `ApproximationAccuracy`; the triangle target only
shapes what comes out of it. → CORRECT: derive the accuracy from the quad size
the triangle budget implies.

**Reading `ApproximationAccuracy` as centimetres.** → SYMPTOM: a value of 150
is accepted silently and yields a proxy built from ~2 voxels across a 254 m
cell. → CAUSE: the field is METRES, default 1.0. → CORRECT: 1.5 for a 1.5 m
voxel; the tool refuses anything above 10.

**Comparing a cold single-cell build against a warm sustained rate.**
→ SYMPTOM: 57.8 s vs 11.86 s/actor reads as a 5x regression from a change that
strictly reduces work. → CAUSE: process warmth and first-cell one-off costs are
a second variable. → CORRECT: sample the new setting the same way the old one
was sampled, over a sustained window.

## R-HLOD — AMENDED 2026-09-08: BATCHING IS BY BUILD MANIFEST, AND THE SKIP THE BATCH PLAN RESTED ON DOES NOT WORK

**Supersedes the cost argument for option (c) in LESSONS 2026-09-08i.** The
batching mechanism is confirmed and better than that entry guessed. The "skip"
that made it cheap is not real.

### THE BATCH FLAG EXISTS — the builder carries distributed-build sharding

That entry said "if there is no batch flag". There is one, and it works on a
single machine:

    STEP 1, generate the shards -- READ-ONLY, writes nothing under Content/
      -SetupHLODs -ReportOnly -BuildManifest=<abs>.ini -BuilderCount=12

    STEP 2, run one shard per FRESH process
      -BuildHLODs -RebuildHLODs -BuildManifest=<abs>.ini -BuilderIdx=<i>

    plus, on every run: -noxgecontroller -AllowCommandletRendering
                        -unattended -nosplash -nopause -abslog=...

    MEASURED: 12 sections, 185-191 cells each, 2,267 total, generated in
    0.4 min. Read-back: 0 of 2,267 packages changed in (size, mtime_ns).

    WorldPartitionHLODsBuilder.cpp:176-178  the three switches are parsed
    :1062-1095   with a manifest the actor list comes ONLY from section
                 [HLODBuilder<idx>], key `+HLODActorGuid`
    :68          section name = FString::Printf("HLODBuilder%d", idx)
    :580-586     GenerateBuildManifest runs inside the SETUP step
    :1418, 1236-1262   the split keeps each hierarchy group WHOLE and
                 child-before-parent
    :1426-1427   writes [General] BuilderCount and EngineVersion
    :287-310     a build run REFUSES without -BuilderIdx, on a missing file,
                 and on an EngineVersion mismatch -- three loud failures
    :1325-1412   ValidateWorkload requires every child EARLIER in the same
                 batch, which is why the shards must be the ENGINE's partition
                 and never a hand-rolled "next 200 by package size"

`-ReportOnly` is what makes step 1 safe: it gates both write paths in this
world's generator, `WorldPartitionRuntimeHashSetHLODGeneration.cpp:541` (the
save) and `:659` (the destroy-unreferenced pass).

### `-RebuildHLODs` IS MANDATORY HERE. Do not rely on the skip.

Measured 2026-09-08, batch 0, 191 cells, no `-RebuildHLODs`: **approve 0,
reject 191, 30 seconds, nothing changed** — including 77 cells whose own saved
build report reads `LayerType: MeshMerge(1)` against a layer asset that is now
`MeshApproximate`. Detail and the source chain: LESSONS 2026-09-08.

Forcing costs almost nothing here and the figure is measured, not assumed: only
**115 of 2,267** cells have ever been built under the MeshApproximate layer, and
the 1,225 Instancing cells rebuild at 0.02 s each.

### HOW TO TELL WHETHER A CELL IS STALE — not by size, not by triangles

    python scripts/hlod_report_census.py

Reads `AWorldPartitionHLOD::HLODBuildReport`, a saved `UPROPERTY() FString`
(HLODActor.h:232, assembled HLODActor.cpp:830-850, delimited
`### HLOD_REPORT_BEGIN ###` at :738). Per cell it gives the label, the
**LayerType the build actually ran with**, the build time, and the full command
line of the build that wrote it. No editor, no commandlet.

    THE WORLD, 2026-09-08      Instancing(0)        1,225
                               MeshMerge(1)           927   <- stale
                               MeshApproximate(3)     115   <- rebuilt

## R-HLOD REJECTED — additions 2026-09-08

**Trusting `-BuildHLODs` without `-RebuildHLODs` to rebuild cells that are
stale because the LAYER changed.**
→ SYMPTOM: a batch of 191 finishes in 30 s, logs
`HLODRebuildPolicyHashCompare -> RejectRebuild` for every cell, prints
`#### Built 191 HLOD actors ####`, and changes nothing. 77 of those cells
record `LayerType: MeshMerge(1)` while the layer asset reads
`EHLODLayerType::MeshApproximate`.
→ CAUSE: the decision is `OldHash != NewHash`
(`HLODRebuildPolicyHashCompare.cpp:33`) and the hashes compare EQUAL. **Why
they are equal is NOT established** — see the LEAD in LESSONS 2026-09-08, which
is recorded there precisely because it fails its own prediction.
→ CORRECT: pass `-RebuildHLODs` and bound the exposure with the manifest
shards instead. Verify the result from `scripts/hlod_report_census.py`, never
from the run's own log.
→ REFERENCE: LESSONS 2026-09-08.

**Reading `#### Built N HLOD actors ####` as a count of cells rebuilt.**
→ SYMPTOM: "Built 191" over a run with 191 rejections and zero geometry
written. Reads as a complete, successful batch.
→ CAUSE: `BuiltHLODActors++` is incremented once per loop iteration,
unconditionally, without consulting `BuildHLOD`'s return value
(`WorldPartitionHLODsBuilder.cpp` build loop). It counts cells VISITED.
→ CORRECT: it is a COMPLETION marker — the loop reached the end — and nothing
more. For "did anything get built", count `ApproveRebuild` decisions in the log
AND confirm against the cells' recorded LayerType afterwards.
→ REFERENCE: LESSONS 2026-09-08. Same shape as 08d's "Engine exit requested ...
result 0" printed by commandlets that had not exited.

**Using package size, or triangle count, to decide which cells are stale.**
→ SYMPTOM: two proxies disagree (705 packages over 5 MB vs 468 cells at
>= 100k triangles) and BOTH are wrong. `..._Merged/..._Instanced_L1_X-4_Y-2`
holds 8,449 triangles in a 19,071,154-byte package and is MeshMerge output.
→ CAUSE: a package also carries its baked textures, and a higher-level
MeshMerge cell falls under any triangle threshold worth picking. Both proxies
are downstream of the same event — the geometry a build emitted — so their
agreeing would not have made either right (non-negotiable 0).
→ CORRECT: `scripts/hlod_report_census.py`, which reads the settings the build
was CONFIGURED with rather than the geometry it produced. It puts the stale
count at 927, not 705.
→ REFERENCE: LESSONS 2026-09-08.

**Treating a commandlet's non-zero exit code as a failure on this machine.**
→ SYMPTOM: every successful HLOD run ends `Failure - 2 error(s), 2 warning(s)`
and exits non-zero, so a loop that retries on `rc != 0` retries every batch.
→ CAUSE: IncrediBuild's `Manager.exe` holds port 8000
(`docs/environment.md`), so `LogHttpListener: Error: HttpListener unable to
bind to 127.0.0.1:8000` is logged twice on EVERY commandlet regardless of the
work. Confirmed on the two runs that produced the accepted cell:
`build_one_cell_noxge.log:2420` / `:2435` and
`build_onecell_acc15.log:2192` / `:2207`.
→ CORRECT: record `rc` as data; judge the run on the log's error COUNT against
that baseline of 2, plus the artefact.
→ REFERENCE: LESSONS 2026-09-08.

LayerType each cell was actually BUILT with, plus the full command line of the

    DONE looks like:  Instancing(0) 1225   MeshApproximate(3) 1042
                      MeshMerge(1) 0       packages over 5 MB 0

### A GPU FAULT IN A SHARD IS SURVIVABLE, and may not even be a failure

Shard 9 faulted twice (signature 2: `DRIVER_INTERNAL_ERROR` /
`CreateReservedResource`), both times at its LAST cell, in fresh processes, at
**9,359 MB and 7,403 MB** of UE's `Local Used`. **Its work completed anyway** —
`approve 188, reject 0, written 188, torn 0`, artefact moved by its full −78 —
and the retry correctly reported `-0` because there was nothing left to do.

So: on a fault, re-run the shard; if the census shows its cells already
current, move on. Cost was one hour against build 3's whole run.

## R-RTFENCE — PENDING, NOT RUN: the Electric Dreams RT culling fence, and TWO OF ITS THREE VALUES DO NOT DO WHAT THE PLAN ASSUMES

**Status: PENDING.** Recorded 2026-09-08 as an operator contingency for a Phase
B step that has not run. **Nothing here is proven and none of it has touched
the editor.** It is written down because the values are specific and would
otherwise be lost, and because verifying them found a defect.

### THE RULING, verbatim in intent

If the RT-on open crashes again with the light proxies, do **not** fall back to
RT off. Keep hardware ray tracing and fence it instead:

    r.RayTracing.Culling=3
    r.RayTracing.Culling.Radius=70000     (700 m, the 4K detail band)
    r.RayTracing.Culling.Angle=2

applied as a profile cvar, **read back**, then ONE bounded retry. If it opens,
record it as the instrument and note the change in `bench_run.json`. Intent:
"the water reflections stay, the far BLAS goes."

### ⚠ WHAT THE SOURCE SAYS, and it contradicts the plan on two of three

`RayTracingInstanceCulling.cpp:22-49`, UE 5.8, declared defaults:

    r.RayTracing.Culling          default 3
    r.RayTracing.Culling.Radius   default 30000.0   (300 m)
    r.RayTracing.Culling.Angle    default 1.0       (degrees)

and this project sets **none** of them — no `RayTracing.Culling` line exists in
any `LandscapeLab/Config/*.ini`, and the live editor's log records no override.
So the engine defaults are what is running.

    Culling=3   ALREADY THE DEFAULT. Setting it changes nothing.
    Radius=70000  LOOSENS the fence, 300 m -> 700 m. The cvar culls objects
                  OUTSIDE the radius, so a LARGER radius keeps MORE far
                  geometry, not less. This is the opposite of "the far BLAS
                  goes" measured against what is running today.
    Angle=2     tightens correctly: culls anything under 2 degrees projected
                instead of 1.

**Only the Angle change reduces BLAS.** As written the fence would INCREASE
far ray-tracing geometry relative to the current state.

### WHY THE PLAN READS THE WAY IT DOES — an engine doc-string bug

`RayTracingInstanceCulling.cpp:24-29` declares the default as `3` and then
describes it as:

    " 0: Culling disabled (default)\n"

The help text says culling is off by default. **The declared value is 3.** Any
plan built from the documentation will assume RT culling is disabled and that
enabling it is a tightening; on this engine it is already on, at 300 m.

This is non-negotiable 9 in its purest form — a derived record (the help
string) contradicted by the artefact (the initialiser three lines above it).

### IF IT IS RUN ANYWAY, the corrected shape

To actually shrink the far BLAS from today's state, the radius must go DOWN,
not up. 700 m is defensible as a *design* target — it is the conifer detail
boundary at 4K (BRIEF 1: 706 m) — but it is a WIDENING here, and that must be
a deliberate choice rather than an accident:

    keep water reflections + honour the 4K detail band -> Radius 70000, and
        accept MORE far BLAS than the 300 m default. State this out loud.
    shrink the far BLAS from today -> Radius BELOW 30000, e.g. 20000 (200 m),
        with Angle 2.

Either way: apply, **read back from the live editor** (rule 12 — a cvar that is
not read back is prose), then one bounded retry.

### NOT VERIFIED HERE

Whether the fence helps at all. The RT-on open **succeeded** on 2026-09-08
without any fence (LESSONS 2026-09-08i), so the contingency's trigger has not
fired and there is no measurement of the fence's effect on this world.

## R-BENCH — EXPOSURE IN A BENCH CAPTURE IS OWNED BY THE VOLUME, AND ONE CVAR TAKES IT AWAY (2026-09-08)

**Locked on a measured three-point chain**, same station, same profile, same
tool, same resolution, one variable:

    no exposure cvars in the profile     luma 0.3477  (2026-09-06)
    r.DefaultFeature.AutoExposure=0      luma 0.9485  (2026-09-07)
    cvars dropped again                  luma 0.3468  (2026-09-07)

### THE RULE

**Exposure for a bench capture is owned by the level's PostProcessVolume**
(`AEM_MANUAL`, `auto_exposure_bias` from `recipes/alpine_8k.json`
`lighting.exposure.compensation_ev`), applied by `apply_lighting.py:333-345`.
**No profile in `benchmark.json` may set `r.DefaultFeature.AutoExposure`.**

Verify it with `python scripts/ue_exec.py scripts/payloads/exposure_probe.py`
before trusting any frame's luma. Expected on `/Game/Alpine8K`:

    volume_count 1, unbound true, enabled true,
    override_auto_exposure_method true, AEM_MANUAL,
    override_auto_exposure_bias true, -1.923

### HOW TO TELL A BLOWN FRAME FROM A BRIGHT ONE

`mean_luma` alone cannot: a correct sunlit vista sits at 0.71. Read the
histogram extrema off the PNG instead.

    correct   min 0,   max 240,  pure-255 fraction 0.0000
    blown     min 255, max 255,  pure-255 fraction 1.0000   (mid_slope)
    blown     min 100, max 255,  pure-255 fraction 0.4173   (near_ground)

A frame whose MINIMUM is 221 has nothing dark in it anywhere, which no exterior
with shadows can be.

## R-CULLDERIVE — CULL DISTANCES ARE DERIVED FROM A DECLARED CAMERA, NOT AUTHORED (2026-09-08)

**Locked. Every instance byte-identical at the same seed; only `cull_cm`
changed.** Supersedes `cull_distance_m` as the source of truth for tree
species. BRIEF 1 measured that every authored cull deleted its object while it
was still 15–63 px tall, four of them inside the DETAIL band.

### THE COMMAND — and the flag that is NOT optional

    python scripts/place_foliage.py --recipe recipes/alpine_8k.json

**`--recipe` IS MANDATORY.** `DEFAULT_RECIPE` is `recipes/alpine.json`
(`place_foliage.py:81`) — the pre-8K world `CLAUDE.md` calls HISTORY. Running
without the flag re-plans the wrong world and overwrites `foliage/alpine_*`.
Confirm from the run's own second line before trusting it:

    8129 x 8129 cells, 8128 m span   the 8K world
    2017 x 2017 cells, 8064 m span   HISTORY, stop

### THE INPUTS

    recipes/alpine_8k.json  perception.declared_camera  90 deg, 3840x2160,
                                                        floor 2560x1440
                            perception.thresholds_px    1.5 / 6 / 40
                            perception.cull_threshold   detail
    _verify/bench/2026-09-05/species_heights.json
                            mesh_height_m + placed_height_p50_m per species,
                            each citing a Free/_measured/ row

**`height_m` ON A SPECIES IS THE ELEVATION BAND, NOT THE PLANT.** Conifer
`[120, 640]` m above sea level. The plant's height is `mesh_height_m` in the
measured file. Writing one into the other destroys the placement band and
raises nothing.

### THE MEASURED RESULT

    species        authored   derived 4K   derived 1440p   applied
    Conifer           730.0       1148.6           765.8   derived
    ConiferPine       730.0        875.0           583.4   derived
    SpruceSub         730.0        743.5           495.7   derived
    SpruceSapling     180.0        238.3           158.8   derived
    Meadow             50.0         18.6            12.4   AUTHORED
    Blueberry          45.0         22.8            15.2   AUTHORED

    counts unchanged: 63,981 / 47,261 / 55,004 / 53,413 = 219,659

### GROUND COVER IS EXCLUDED, DELIBERATELY

A cull may sit at a band boundary only WHERE THE NEXT BAND EXISTS (BRIEF 1
§4). Trees have one — imposters plus 1,042 HLOD proxies. Ground cover does
not: HLOD activates only beyond the 256 m streaming range
(`RuntimePartition.cpp:27`), so culling Meadow at 18.6 m opens a 237 m gap
with nothing in it. The exclusion is the named `GROUND_COVER` set in
`place_foliage.py`, and `check_derived_culls.py` requires it to be EXPLICIT
rather than an accident of missing height data.

**RULED 2026-09-08 by Ryan: ground cover KEEPS its authored culls** — Meadow
50 m, Blueberry 45 m. The question of whether `silhouette` would serve it
better is CLOSED, not deferred: Meadow's silhouette boundary is 123.8 m, still
inside the 256 m streaming range, so it would narrow the gap without closing
it. Ground cover needs a REPRESENTATION in the band below, not a different
cull; that is a separate piece of work and BACKLOG carries it. Until it
exists, the authored values stand and `check_derived_culls.py` keeps asserting
that the exclusion is explicit.

### THE DERIVATION IS WRITTEN INTO EVERY PLAN

`cull_derivation` in each `foliage/alpine_8k_*.json`: threshold, threshold_px,
fov, res, vfov, mesh_height_m, placed_height_p50_m, the height's source
citation, the derived value, the 1440p floor value, and — when the authored
value is kept — WHY. A derived number whose working is not recorded is just a
different magic constant.

### THE GATE

`scripts/check_derived_culls.py`, in `run_offline_suite`. Refuses a missing or
incomplete `perception` block, and any non-ground-cover species that falls
back to an authored cull. Three-directions tested: passes as shipped; refuses
with `perception` removed, with `thresholds_px.detail` removed, and with a new
tree species that has no measured height.

## R-PLANSTALE — WHAT TO DO WITH A PLAN `check_plan_freshness` CALLS STALE (2026-09-08)

**Locked. Applied to 18 stale plans on 2026-09-08: 3 restamped, 15 waived, 1
of those 15 also carrying a divergence note.** A stale plan has FOUR possible
correct outcomes and only one of them is a waiver. Choosing between them is a
MEASUREMENT, not a judgement call.

### THE DECISION, IN ORDER — DO NOT SKIP STEP 1

    1  RUN THE PRODUCER TO A TEMP PATH and compare the PAYLOAD
       (all keys except _input_sha256, _stamp_waiver, _divergence_note)

       payload identical      -> RESTAMP: re-run the producer to its real
                                 path. No waiver. This is the common case.
       payload differs        -> is the difference intended?
            yes -> adopt the new output (that is a content decision, and it
                   may need a ruling -- a town rebuild is not a freshness fix)
            no  -> _divergence_note {why, retires_when}. STAYS RED BY LAW.
       producer cannot run    -> _stamp_waiver, naming every differing input
       artefact is FROZEN     -> _stamp_waiver saying so (see BACKLOG:
       (evidence, a dead world)   `_frozen` is the real fix)

**AMENDED 2026-09-16 (R5, E-4) — the table gains three outcomes ABOVE the
waiver rungs; the original text stands as history:**

    0  CHECK THE CONSUMED VERDICT FIRST. A plan carrying a
       `_consumed_sha256` stamp whose consumed subset still matches reads
       MATCHES_CONSUMED and is FRESH — no producer run, no waiver; the
       edit touched only fields the producer does not read.
    1a CONSUMED subset DIFFERS on a JSON input of a plan that CAN
       reproduce -> step 1 as written (temp-run + payload diff).
    1b CONSUMED subset DIFFERS on a GATED plan (regeneration ruled off,
       e.g. R-TOWNEXCL foliage) -> the difference is real and a waiver
       may bind to the CONSUMED pair (`granted_for` kind "consumed"),
       expiring only when a consumed field moves again.
    1c the differing input is the PRODUCER SCRIPT of an
       EXPECTED-UNREPRODUCIBLE plan -> `granted_for` kind "ruled"
       {ruling, retires_when}: the justification (no producer edit
       alters committed rows) is change-independent, so it binds to the
       RULING, prints every run, and retires when regeneration un-gates
       (D-4/X-1). REFUSED on JSON inputs and on plans without the ruled
       class.
    FROZEN row: superseded — dead-world plans are ARCHIVED to
       `foliage/_archive/` (R5 4b, reversible git mv), which delivers
       what the parked `_frozen` flag was meant to; the waive-forever
       form is rejected.
    1e (2026-09-16, same session) REPRODUCE'S VERDICT JUDGES THE
       PAYLOAD: whole-content identity is still reported, but the
       REPRODUCES/DIFFERS verdict compares payload_sha12 (every key
       except the four metadata keys). The stamp block records moving
       input hashes BY DESIGN, so a producer edit ripples metadata
       through every downstream plan while the plan itself is
       byte-identical — three such ripples in one evening each
       re-reddened payload-identical plans. A payload-identical,
       metadata-drifted reproduction prints "[metadata-only drift]"
       and reads REPRODUCES.
    1d (R6-Q1, 2026-09-16) the "STAYS RED BY LAW" rung is AMENDED:
       a --reproduce DIFFERS stays red UNLESS the divergence is ITSELF
       RULED — `_divergence_note` carrying a ruling id, a retires_when,
       AND `bound_to` {committed, fresh} equal to the OBSERVED
       content-hash pair — in which case the checker reports
       DIVERGENT-BY-RULING: its own verdict, never counted fresh,
       printed in full (ruling, retires_when, pair) on every run, and
       EXPIRING the moment either hash moves. PRODUCER REFUSES is never
       ruled-divergent. "Suite fully green" means exit 0 with every
       ruled divergence printed loud.

**A `_stamp_waiver` belongs ONLY on a plan that cannot be reproduced.** If the
producer runs, the answer is a restamp or a divergence note.

### THE PROBE THAT MAKES STEP 1 CHEAP

`--reproduce` prints ONE whole-file hash, and that hash cannot distinguish
"the rows changed" from "only the stamp moved" — opposite situations needing
opposite responses. Run the producer to a temp path yourself and diff the
parsed documents key by key. 30 lines. On 2026-09-08 it turned a blanket
18-waiver commit into 3 restamps and 15 waivers.

    city/alpine_basin_town_plan_roofbias.json   payload identical -> RESTAMP
    encounters/alpine_8k_all.json               payload identical -> RESTAMP
    encounters/alpine_8k_verified.json          payload identical -> RESTAMP
    city/alpine_basin_town_plan.json            303 -> 348 buildings -> NOTE

### ORDER — EVERY EDIT TO A STAMPED INPUT LANDS FIRST

Finish every edit to every recipe and producer BEFORE stamping or waiving.
`granted_for` binds a waiver to the hash pair it was granted against, so
editing a named input afterwards expires it immediately — correctly. Editing
a shared recipe also re-stales every plan already stamped against it,
including ones fixed minutes earlier.

### THE WAIVER'S OWN CONTRACT

`waiver_covers` requires every differing input NAMED, a non-empty `why`, and
`granted_for {path: {from, to}}` so it expires by itself. **Write the `why`
programmatically from the same rows that produce the binding.** A hash typed
into prose is a hash that will be wrong.

**And the `why` must be TRUE, not merely present.** Where the change is
material, say so — 15 of the 18 granted here are waived because the artefact
is FROZEN EVIDENCE, not because the change is inert, and each says which.

### INSERT TEXTUALLY, AFTER THE OPENING BRACE

Plans range from a 2 MB single-line compact foliage plan to a 23,035-line
pretty-printed city plan. `json.dump` reformats all of them into an
unreviewable diff. Insert `"_stamp_waiver": {...},` after the first `{`,
preserving BOM and line endings, then re-parse and compare the parsed document
against HEAD: it must be identical apart from the added key.

### VERIFY

    python scripts/check_plan_freshness.py              # stamp + HISTORY
    python scripts/check_plan_freshness.py --reproduce  # what the suite runs

The default run returning exit 0 does NOT mean the suite will pass. HISTORY
also compares COMMIT ORDER, so a correctly restamped plan reads STALE until it
is committed.

## R-PLANSTALE REJECTED — 2026-09-08

**Waiving a stale plan without first running its producer.**
→ SYMPTOM: a waiver that reads fine and passes the default gate, sitting
permanently on a plan that a five-second re-run would have made genuinely
fresh. 2 of 3 reproducible plans on 2026-09-08.
→ CAUSE: treating "stale" as one condition when it is four.
→ CORRECT: reproduce to a temp path and compare the PAYLOAD first.
→ REFERENCE: LESSONS 2026-09-08m.

**Inserting a `_stamp_waiver` into a plan whose producer CAN be reproduced.**
→ SYMPTOM: default gate exit 0, and `--reproduce` reports DIFFERS — the state
the waiver was meant to address, now caused by the waiver.
→ CAUSE: `sha12_content` hashes the WHOLE FILE; a freshly produced plan has no
`_stamp_waiver`, so the inserted key guarantees a mismatch. A waiver never
applies to `--reproduce` by law.
→ CORRECT: restamp it, or use `_divergence_note`.

→ SYMPTOM: the reason cites `c2c160f9168b -> f5ffe94d8f12` while the file
actually reads `9d6a5439bc7a`. `granted_for` is right; the prose is not.

`granted_for`.

**Stamping or waiving before all edits to stamped inputs have landed.**
→ SYMPTOM: waivers expire the moment they are written; freshly stamped plans
go stale again; the same producer has to be re-run twice.
→ CAUSE: `granted_for` binds to a hash pair, and a recipe is a SHARED input.
→ CORRECT: finish every edit first, then stamp and waive once.
→ REFERENCE: LESSONS 2026-09-08m.

**Reconstructing a past stamp by hashing `git show <commit>:<path>`.**
→ SYMPTOM: an implausible archaeology result — "33 of 34 plans were already
stale" — produced by comparing git's LF blobs against stamps taken over
working files with CRLF.
→ CAUSE: the representation trap `reproduce()` documents in its own comment.
→ CORRECT: use a real checkout (a worktree), or rest the claim on commit
ancestry, which needs no hashing.

## R-UEEXEC — PASSING DATA TO AN EDITOR PAYLOAD (2026-09-08q)

**Locked.** `ue_exec.py --set NAME=VALUE` substitutes VALUE **raw** into the
payload text, and the payload is then syntax-checked BEFORE the editor is
contacted. That check is the cheapest instrument in the loop — one second
against a 25 s round trip — and it is easy to defeat by accident.

### DO NOT SEND STRUCTURED DATA THROUGH `--set`

**PowerShell strips embedded `"` from arguments to native executables.** A
JSON value read correctly from disk arrives at `ue_exec` with every quote
gone, and nothing at the call site shows it.

    on disk     [["Conifer", "/Game/Meshes/Trees/SM_PVE_Norway_Spruce_01_A"]]
    at ue_exec  [[Conifer, /Game/Meshes/Trees/SM_PVE_Norway_Spruce_01_A]]

**A PAYLOAD THAT NEEDS A LIST SHOULD READ IT FROM DISK ITSELF.** The editor
process can read the repo:

    _root = os.path.dirname(os.path.normpath(_u.Paths.project_dir().rstrip("/")))
    _recipe = os.path.join(_root, "recipes", "alpine_8k.json")

Nothing crosses the shell boundary, so nothing can be rewritten in transit,
and the payload reads the same source of truth its producer does.

`--set` is fine for a SCALAR with no quotes, no spaces and no `/Game/` path.
Follow the `chalet_silhouette_probe_payload.txt` convention and put the quotes
in the TEMPLATE (`PKG = r"__ROOF_PKG__"`) — but see the REJECTED entry below
before reaching for that on a value the shell has already damaged.

### `--timeout` IS A DISCOVERY WINDOW AND IS SPENT IN FULL

`ue_exec` prints this on every run. **12-25 is right.** A query that answers
in seconds costs the whole window if you pass 240.

## R-UEEXEC REJECTED — 2026-09-08q

**"Fixing" a pre-flight syntax refusal by making the payload parse.**
→ SYMPTOM: run 1 refused in ~1 s with a clear SyntaxError showing the
substituted text. Wrapping the placeholder in `r"""..."""` makes run 2 pass
the check, reach the editor, and fail there with `JSONDecodeError` after
**240 s**. Same defect, later and more expensively.
→ CAUSE: the wrapper changed the payload's SYNTAX without changing the VALUE,
which was already damaged by the shell. A raw triple-quoted string is valid
Python whatever it contains, so the check had nothing left to catch.
→ CORRECT: fix the VALUE. If a change makes a refused payload parse without
changing what it means, it has DEFEATED the check, not satisfied it — the
tell is that it touches syntax and not content. Best of all, remove the
channel: read the data from disk inside the payload.
→ REFERENCE: LESSONS 2026-09-08q.

**Passing a `/Game/...` path or JSON through Git Bash.**
→ SYMPTOM: the argument arrives prefixed with the Git install directory, and
the tool reports the asset missing — a misdiagnosis wearing a plausible error
message.
→ CAUSE: MSYS path mangling.
→ CORRECT: the PowerShell tool, or `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1`. A `.claude/hooks`
guard already refuses this one. Note that PowerShell fixes the PATH mangling
and introduces the QUOTE stripping above.
→ REFERENCE: the `msys-game-path` hook; LESSONS 2026-08-05, 2026-09-08q.

## R-LODSILHOUETTE — RENDERING A MESH ON A FLAT KEY COLOUR, AND JUDGING ITS LOD CHAIN (2026-09-08)

**Locked.** Eleven smoke frames were spent getting a tree onto flat magenta,
and **nine of them reported success at the API level**. Every value below was
bought.

### THE COMMAND

    python scripts/lod_silhouette_capture.py

Drives `scripts/payloads/lod_capture_scene.py` (stage + force + read back) and
`scripts/shoot.py` (capture), then `scripts/lod_silhouette_check.py` (judge).
Every child process is invoked with an argv LIST -- see R-UEEXEC for what the
shell does to arguments otherwise.

### THE SCENE — VALUES THAT WORK

    backdrop mesh     /Engine/BasicShapes/Cube, scale (1, 500, 500)
                      NOT a Plane: the opaque key material is two_sided FALSE,
                      so a plane is invisible whenever its facing is wrong. A
                      cube always presents a face.
    backdrop material BUILT, not borrowed: MSM_UNLIT, BLEND_OPAQUE,
                      two_sided, Constant3Vector -> MP_EMISSIVE_COLOR
    emissive gain     5000x. Emissive 1.0 and 40.0 both render near BLACK --
                      exposure and the filmic tonemapper apply. Overshoot is
                      free; the channel clips at the key colour.
    view mode         LIT. `viewmode unlit` visualises BASE COLOR, and an
                      MSM_UNLIT material has none -- it renders pure black.
    editor overlays   LevelEditorSubsystem.editor_set_game_view(True), which
                      has a GETTER. ShowFlag.Sprites 0 does NOT remove them.
    rotators          KEYWORD arguments only: Rotator(roll=, pitch=, yaw=).
    framing           D = H / (2 * fill * tan(fov/2)), fill 0.80, fov 45,
                      camera aimed at the mesh's BOUNDS CENTRE, not its pivot
    nothing saved     actors spawned into the loaded level and destroyed; the
                      key material built in memory. World Partition writes
                      external actors on SAVE only.

### THE KEY COLOUR IS MEASURED, NEVER DECLARED

A saturated magenta backdrop measures **(211, 0, 199)**, not (255, 0, 255).
At the checker's threshold of 60 the distance between those is 71, so keying
on the declared colour classifies the BACKGROUND AS SUBJECT and inflates
coverage. The driver samples four corners, requires them to agree, and passes
the measured colour as `--key`.

### THE PIXEL MATHS

    px at a switch     px = res_h * S * H / (2 R)
    proposed S for px  S  = 2 R px / (res_h * H)

with S the LOD ScreenSize, H the mesh height, R its bounding sphere radius,
res_h the DECLARED camera's vertical resolution. Independent of FOV, so the
capture camera and the judged camera need not agree.

### JUDGE EVERY LOD TWICE

Once at the size it switches at TODAY, once at the silhouette size. A last LOD
that FAILS the first and PASSES the second indicts **the switch, not the
mesh** -- and the fix is a ScreenSize, which the sidecar records as a
PROPOSAL. Judging only at the current switch cannot tell "this billboard is
bad" from "this billboard is shown too early", and those have opposite fixes.

### NANITE IS OUT OF SCOPE, AND MUST BE STATED

`r.ForceLOD` does not govern a Nanite mesh, which does its own cluster LOD and
has no discrete switch. Conifer (nanite_enabled true, 1 LOD, screen size 2.0)
is recorded in the sidecar's `skipped` block WITH the reason. A Nanite mesh
reporting "1 LOD" reads exactly like a missing LOD chain.

## R-LODSILHOUETTE — AMENDED 2026-09-08s: THE CAPTURES MUST BE RGB, AND SHAPE MUST BE JUDGED SEPARATELY FROM TONE

### FILE THE CAPTURES AS RGB. NOT RGBA.

`lod_silhouette_check.load_mask_and_luma` branches on the image mode:

    if im.mode == "RGBA":  mask = alpha > 127
    else:                  mask = distance from key > 60

**HighResShot writes RGBA with alpha = 255 everywhere**, so an RGBA capture
masks the ENTIRE FRAME and the key colour is never consulted. The whole
magenta backdrop is bypassed by a branch on the file's mode.

    symptom   coverage_ratio 1.000, silhouette_iou 1.000, edge_error_px NaN
              on EVERY row of EVERY species

Convert with `Image.open(src).convert("RGB").save(dst)` when filing, and again
as a guard at judge time so an earlier capture cannot revive it.

### A METRIC PINNED AT ITS PERFECT VALUE IS A DISCONNECTED INSTRUMENT

1.000 on 13 of 13 rows should alarm exactly as much as 0.000. `edge_error_px`
NaN is the corroborating tell: a mask with no boundary has no edge to measure.

### READ THE CHECKER'S OUTPUT AS A LIST

It returns `{"thresholds": {...}, "lods": [ ... ]}`, indexed from the FIRST
comparison -- LOD0 is the reference and has no row. Reading it as `lod0`/`lod3`
keys yields `{}`, and `startswith("FAIL")` on an empty string is False, so a
MISSING measurement renders as a PASS. Emit "NOT JUDGED" when the row list is
empty.

### JUDGE SHAPE AND TONE SEPARATELY

`verdict` is one string that fails if any threshold fails, and `luma` fails
far more readily than `coverage` or `iou`. Pooling them indicts meshes whose
measured shape is fine.

    geometric verdict   coverage >= 0.85 AND iou >= 0.80   <- the audit's question
    tonal candidate     luma_delta_weber vs 0.03           <- reported, not ruled

**`luma_delta_weber` normalises by mean luma**, so a dim or backlit capture
inflates it. It is not a verdict until the lighting is controlled.

### THE MEASURED RESULT — 2026-09-08, /Game/Alpine8K

    species        LODs  last-LOD tris  coverage  IoU    geometric verdict
    ConiferPine       4             32     0.993  0.921  HOLDS
    SpruceSub         5              6     1.001  0.948  HOLDS
    SpruceSapling     4            326     1.141  0.825  HOLDS
    Conifer           1           2335     --     --     NANITE, excluded

**No ScreenSize proposal is warranted.** The rule is "fails at its current
switch AND passes at the silhouette size => the switch is wrong"; no species
fails geometrically at its current switch, so the antecedent never holds.

**A low triangle count does not imply a lost silhouette.** A 6-triangle LOD is
an alpha-masked billboard whose shape comes from the texture. Do not reason
from triangle count to silhouette.

Every failing row failed on LUMA alone, monotonically rising with LOD index on
all three species -- corroborating `measure_lod_materials.py`'s recorded
"trunks beyond ~50 m go uniformly pale". Recorded as a candidate; BACKLOG.

## R-PERFSTANDALONE — MEASURING FRAME COST WITH THE EDITOR GONE (2026-09-08)

**Locked.** Three runs were void before one was valid, and all three returned
plausible milliseconds.

### THE COMMAND

    python scripts/perf_standalone.py            # all four ratified stations
    python scripts/perf_standalone.py --only plaza --dry-run

Writes `_verify/perf/standalone_<date>/perf_standalone.json` plus one CSV per
zone. **It does not re-ratify anything**; `recipes/perf_budgets.json` is law
and is untouched.

### THE VALUES THAT WORK

    launch      UnrealEditor.exe <uproject> /Game/Alpine8K -game -windowed
                -ResX/-ResY -nosplash -NoLoadingScreen -AbsLog=<per-zone>
    ExecCmds    r.setRes <W>x<H>w , BugItGo <x> <y> <z> <pitch> <yaw> 0 ,
                CsvProfile frames=60000
    dwell       SETTLE_S 60 + MIN_WINDOW_S 25 + MARGIN_S 20, then terminate
    window      the TAIL of the capture, MIN_WINDOW_S long
    reduction   measure_frame_cost._reduce(skip_frames=N) -- extended, NOT
                copied (non-negotiable 4a)

**`-ResX/-ResY` DOES NOT SET THE RESOLUTION.** Config wins: the log shows
`LogConfig: Set CVar [[r.setres:1280x720]]`. `r.setRes` in ExecCmds runs after
config and does win. **Read it back from the CsvProfiler's
`systemresolution.resx/resy` metadata** and record `config_setres_seen`
beside it so the override is visible.

**DO NOT POLL FOR THE CSV TO EXIST.** The profiler writes INCREMENTALLY; a
size>0 check catches a partial file within seconds and terminating then
truncates the capture to the level load. Dwell a fixed wall time instead.

**DO NOT BOUND THE CAPTURE BY FRAME COUNT.** A frame budget that expires
mid-run ends the capture wherever it happens to be -- `frames=1600` yielded
823 frames of startup. Let the DWELL bound it.

### CAMERA PLACEMENT CANNOT BE VERIFIED IN-PROCESS

`getall PlayerController Location` prints NOTHING -- `Location` is not a
UPROPERTY on the controller. Do not add a check that always passes.

**Verify sideways, by cross-station GPU variation.** If BugItGo moved
nothing, all stations are one view and their GPU cost matches. Measured
2026-09-08: GPU p90 5.58 to 8.33 ms, a **49% spread** -> PASS. A flat GAME
thread across stations is not the failure signature; the GPU is the tell.

### THE MEASURED RESULT — 2026-09-08, /Game/Alpine8K, 3840x2160

    zone         GPU p90  Game p90   GPU budget  Game budget
    plaza          8.33     3.98        12.0        12.0
    main_street    5.95     4.05         8.0        13.0
    treeline       5.58     3.96        10.0        13.5
    vista          6.99     3.85        12.5        13.0

**THE EDITOR'S FrameTime p50 IS 16.67 ms AT EVERY STATION** -- a 60 Hz cap,
not a cost -- and its GameThreadTime tracks the cap (13.90-14.15) rather than
the content. That is REGISTER's "pinned at 13.9-14.15 regardless of content".
`check_perf`'s RED on plaza Game 14.00 is that cap.

### THE GPU COLUMNS ARE NOT LIKE-FOR-LIKE

`_verify/perf/20260905_fov90.json` records `viewport_size: null` for all four
zones -- it never captured the resolution it ran at, and a GPU figure is
resolution-bound. Treat GPU comparisons as INDICATIVE. The game-thread
comparison does not depend on resolution.
