## R-BENCHDOLLY — CAPTURING A DOLLY, AND KNOWING WHEN IT IS FINISHED (2026-09-08)

**Locked.** Four runs were needed for one capture, and one of them reported
**OK over a third of a render**.

### THE COMMANDS

    python scripts/pick_sunlit_heading.py            # MEASURE first, see below
    python scripts/ue_exec.py scripts/payloads/bench_make_dolly.py \
        --set SEQ_NAME=Bench_Dolly_Sunlit --set SECONDS=3.0 --set YAW=<deg>
    python scripts/bench_capture.py --profile target --dolly --dolly-only \
        --dolly-seq Bench_Dolly_Sunlit
    python scripts/check_dolly_sunlit.py \
        --dir _verify/bench/<date>/target/dolly --out <sidecar>.json

`SEQ_NAME`, `SECONDS` and `YAW` are REQUIRED. The builder DELETES AND REBUILDS
the asset it is named, so a variant must be given its own name or it destroys
the ratified `Bench_Dolly`.

### `YAW` — RE-HEAD THE WALK WITHOUT MOVING THE STATION (added 2026-09-08)

    YAW=actor     the camera's own read-back yaw -- the ratified behaviour,
                  bit-for-bit, and what `Bench_Dolly` must always be built with
    YAW=<deg>     travel on a chosen heading instead

**It does not touch the level.** The sequence POSSESSES the camera and keys
Rotation.X/Y/Z itself, so its keys drive the actor during playback. Rotating
`Bench_near_ground` for real would need a restore step afterwards, and
`Bench_Dolly`, the station shots and the perf stations all read that actor's
transform. A restore step is a thing that can be skipped; this has none.

**Pitch and roll are NEVER overridden** — they always come from the actor. E4
re-heads the walk, it does not re-frame the shot, and this project has set a
-25 deg ROLL believing it was pitch three times.

**The heading is a DECISION, not an output.** `pick_sunlit_heading.py` stands
the camera where the walk would END on each candidate and reports the lit
share there; it prints a table and picks nothing. Do not compute the heading
from `lighting.sun.azimuth_deg`: the azimuth->yaw convention is exactly what
caused the three roll-for-pitch errors, and `sun_exposure.py` marches the
HEIGHTMAP, so it is blind to the canopy shadow that actually dapples this
meadow.

### COMPLETION IS A COUNT, NOT A PRESENCE

    if a.dolly: return ok and len(fresh(dolly/*.png)) > 0     # WRONG

MRQ writes frames lazily and keeps flushing after the window title clears.
That test passes on the FIRST frame: the run printed "dolly 17 frames" and OK
and wrote its sidecar while 73 more were still being written.

**Assert the expected count**, derived from the sequence's own declaration
(`benchmark.json dolly.seconds x fps`; MRQ renders playback [0, N), so N
frames numbered 0..N-1). And before analysing, confirm independently: the
full range present, none missing, and the count STABLE across several polls.

### `--dolly-only` MUST REACH EVERY CONSUMER OF `stations`

There are four, and each omission fails differently:

    jobs                 a wait on files never scheduled
    completion check     the same, one layer up
    residency pre-check  refuses on a station this run never captures
    judging              KeyError AFTER a successful render

`--dolly-only` exists to PROTECT EVIDENCE, not to save time: the station jobs
write to `_verify/bench/<date>/<profile>/<station>.png`, which is where the
Phase C stills live.

### THE SUNLIT CHECK, AND WHY NOT MEAN LUMA

A frame half dark buildings and half lit grass has the same mean as an evenly
dim one. Direct sun makes a bright POPULATION; its SIZE is the discriminator.

    sunlit_fraction   share above 0.20 linear luma, GROUND HALF only
    load-bearing      FIRST vs LAST, not the absolute value

The upper half is sky, buildings and canopy, whose brightness says nothing
about whether the camera stands in shadow. The absolutes move with the
level's lighting and exposure, which the ruling forbids touching.

### THE MEASURED RESULT — 2026-09-09, yaw -67.5 (RULED), 3.0 s, 419.99 cm

    frame_0000   75.4% of the ground half lit
    frame_0089   60.6%
    floor        59.6% (t=0.75)   walk .755 .751 .709 .596 .606
    verdict      STAYS sunlit -- -19.6%, against SUNLIT_MIN 0.15, DROP_MAX 0.50

Captured at the PLAYER instrument (PIE via MRQ, 3840x2160, temporal x8), 90
frames, range 0..89 complete, count stable across three polls. NOT SCORED.
Sidecar `_verify/bench/2026-09-09/dolly_sunlit_yaw-67.5.json` carries the
heading's baseline (floor 0.646, first->last +0.068) and the walk profile.

### THE MEASURED RESULT — 2026-09-08, near_ground, 3.0 s, 419.99 cm

    frame_0000   41.1% of the ground half lit
    frame_0089   17.7%
    verdict      does NOT stay out of canopy shadow (-57%)

Both frames are partly lit: this is DAPPLED shadow across the meadow, not a
solid edge. **A 4.2 m walk was predicted to stay in the lit foreground and
does not.** Do not infer shadow coverage along a path from one still.

## R-BENCHDOLLY REJECTED — 2026-09-08

**`len(frames) > 0` as a dolly completion test.**
→ SYMPTOM: "dolly 17 frames" and OK, sidecar written, while 73 frames were
still being written. A shadow check run then would have treated frame_0016 as
the last frame of the walk.
→ CAUSE: presence of output proves rendering BEGAN.
→ CORRECT: assert the expected count from the sequence, then confirm the
range is complete and the count stable before analysing.
→ REFERENCE: LESSONS 2026-09-08u.

**Adding a scope flag to the job list only.**
→ SYMPTOM: four runs, four unrelated-looking failures — a silent 13 minute
wait, a refusal at an uncaptured station, and a KeyError after a successful
render.
→ CAUSE: `stations` computed once and consulted by four independent
consumers that each assumed it described this run.
→ CORRECT: derive what is judged from what was captured.
→ REFERENCE: LESSONS 2026-09-08u.

**TREATING AN EDITOR-STILL BASELINE AS A PREDICTION FOR A PIE CAPTURE.**
→ SYMPTOM: the heading's probe said the walk BRIGHTENS (0.646 -> 0.714,
+0.068); the capture on that same heading FELL (0.755 -> 0.606, -0.148).
Direction reversed, start 0.11 brighter and end 0.11 darker — systematic, far
outside the session's +/-0.03 drift.
→ CAUSE: `shoot.py` shoots the EDITOR world; the dolly renders PIE through
MRQ. Different worlds — and Q12 records 7 InstancedFoliageActors absent from
PIE while in range, so canopy present in one is missing in the other, by an
amount that varies with where the camera stands.
→ CORRECT: a baseline is a baseline FOR ITS OWN INSTRUMENT. Record it for
attribution, never as an expected value for a different instrument, and say
so in the sidecar rather than in a commit message.
→ REFERENCE: LESSONS 2026-09-09a; Q12.

**OMITTING `--dolly-seconds` FOR A VARIANT OF A DIFFERENT DURATION.**
→ SYMPTOM: completion waits for 180 frames while the sequence renders 90, so
a finished render never satisfies the wait.
→ CAUSE: the default comes from `benchmark.json dolly.seconds`, which is 6.0
and describes the RATIFIED dolly, not the 3 s sunlit variant.
→ CORRECT: pass `--dolly-seconds` matching the SEQ_NAME being rendered. It
does not change the sequence; it tells completion what to expect.
→ REFERENCE: 2026-09-09 E4 run.

**READING A ONE-MINUTE-OLD RUN AS A STALL.**
→ SYMPTOM: a quiet editor log during the residency round trip, called a stall
on the strength of this recipe's own "trigger followed by SILENCE" entry.
→ CAUSE: the run was ~60 s old and inside a remote payload with a 240 s
timeout. A Python round trip is not a render and logs nothing.
→ CORRECT: check ELAPSED TIME before applying the stall test. The silence
entry assumes a run old enough for silence to mean something.
→ REFERENCE: LESSONS 2026-09-09a.

**ASSUMING A RENDER DIES WITH THE SCRIPT THAT LAUNCHED IT.**
→ SYMPTOM: the driving python was killed mid-run; the output directory sat
empty and the render looked lost.
→ CAUSE: MRQ runs PIE INSIDE THE EDITOR PROCESS. The driver only waits.
→ CORRECT: check the editor log and the frame count before re-triggering — a
re-trigger over a live render is the expensive mistake here. All 90 frames
completed cleanly after the driver died.
→ REFERENCE: LESSONS 2026-09-09a.

**Reading a stalled run as a slow render.**
→ SYMPTOM: 13 minutes of no output, indistinguishable from a big render.
→ CAUSE: the completion condition could never be met.
→ CORRECT: read the editor log. A trigger followed by SILENCE is an idle
editor, not a busy one — the mirror of R-EDITOR-CLOSE's "answers a round trip
is not is free".
→ REFERENCE: LESSONS 2026-09-08u.

## R-CENSUS — READ-ONLY CENSUS OF A REFERENCE PROJECT (2026-09-08)

**Locked.** Four projects attempted, three censused, five maps.
`research/census/CENSUS_ROLLUP.json` is the consolidated result and every
number in it carries a STATUS.

### THE COMMANDS

    python scripts/census_project.py --project <P> --skip-shots
    python scripts/survey_shots.py --project-root <abs> --tag <t> \
        --outdir research/census/shots/<P> --stations-out <...>.stations.json

### NAME THE MAP. ALWAYS.

Three of the four projects open on a LOADING map:

    CitySample       EditorStartupMap /Game/Map/Startup
    ValleyOfTheAncient                /Game/AncientContent/Maps/Startup
    ElectricDreams                    /Game/Levels/Startup
    DarkRuins                         /Game/Main  <- the only exception

An editor opened without an explicit map censuses the loading screen and
reports `ok: true`. The first City Sample pass did exactly that and wrote
141 KB describing nothing. **Confirm `current_world` in the output before
trusting any census** — and name the artefact for the world it ACTUALLY
describes (`CitySample__Startup.json` is kept under that name).

### A ZERO NEEDS A TRACE

`_assets_of` must search the class's OWN package. `UPCGGraph` is
`/Script/PCG`, `UFoliageType` is `/Script/Foliage`; asking `/Script/Engine`
returns an empty list and throws nothing. That produced THREE false zeros,
including zero PCG graphs on the PCG reference project.

Every census records `asset_lookup_trace` (package hit, count found). A zero
without a trace is `ZERO_UNAUDITED`, not an absence.

### SHOTS: REMOTE EXECUTION, NOT -ExecCmds

`-ExecCmds` fires every command in one batch at startup, so `HighResShot`
lands before the teleport reaches the rendered view. Four attempts across two
projects, `r.HighResScreenshotDelay` 8 -> 900 -> 1200 plus `ghost` no-clip:
the delay fixed the CAPTURE (0 -> 1 -> 5 filed) and never the CAMERA.

The route that works is `bRemoteExecution=True` in the sample's config plus
`shoot.py`, which drives the editor viewport and waits HOST-SIDE so the editor
stays alive and ticking. Proven on Electric Dreams far-range: five genuinely
distinct frames.

    stations   from the LIVE world's bounds, actors >2 km excluded (a sky
               sphere put the first cameras 20 km up)
    ground     traced PER STATION, bTraceComplex=TRUE (False uses simple
               collision and sat 12.4 m under the visible surface)
    refusals   shoot.py's "camera is N m BELOW the ground" is NEVER
               suppressed -- an underground frame looks like content

**It does not always work and the cause is unknown.** Electric Dreams
close-range wedged after one shot; Dark Ruins issued shots and wrote no
frames. Two different failure shapes, both with fresh editors. Recorded as
open in the rollup with untested candidates; no cause claimed.

### RESTORING A SAMPLE PROJECT

Back up before editing — `enable_sample_remote_exec.py` and
`patch_sample_target.py` both copy the original into THIS repo first and both
take `--revert`.

**BACK UP WHAT THE TOOL MIGHT TOUCH, NOT ONLY WHAT YOU MEAN TO EDIT.**
Invoking a build on Valley deleted its shipped
`UnrealEditor-AncientGame.pdb` and overwrote `AncientGameEditor.target`.
Neither was backed up, because neither was a file I intended to change.

## R-CENSUS REJECTED — 2026-09-08

**Opening a sample project without naming the map.**
→ SYMPTOM: `ok: true`, a well-formed JSON, and world-scoped sections
describing a loading screen.
→ CAUSE: three of four projects set `EditorStartupMap` to a loading map.
→ CORRECT: pass the map explicitly and check `current_world` in the output.
→ REFERENCE: LESSONS 2026-09-08v.

**Reading a section's entry count as a measurement.**
→ SYMPTOM: `world_partition: 1` reported as a captured target, twice. The one
entry was `{"_error": ...}`.
→ CORRECT: count what the entries ARE. Carry a STATUS per value.
→ REFERENCE: LESSONS 2026-09-08v.

**Asking `/Script/Engine` for a class that lives elsewhere.**
→ SYMPTOM: `pcg_graphs: 0` on the PCG reference project; `foliage_types: 0`
across three censuses. No exception, no error record.
→ CORRECT: search the class's own package first; record
`asset_lookup_trace` so the zero is decidable.
→ REFERENCE: LESSONS 2026-09-08v.

**Taking survey shots with `-ExecCmds`.**
→ SYMPTOM: five frames of one viewpoint that differ enough (shader compile
recolouring between launches) to pass a naive difference check.
→ CORRECT: `bRemoteExecution` + `shoot.py`, host-side wait.
→ REFERENCE: LESSONS 2026-09-08v; R-LODSILHOUETTE for why the difference
metric cannot arbitrate.

**Backing up only the files you intend to edit.**
→ SYMPTOM: a shipped `.pdb` deleted and a `.target` overwritten by a build,
neither recoverable.
→ CORRECT: a build writes wherever its target directory points. Back up the
directory, or accept and RECORD the loss.
→ REFERENCE: LESSONS 2026-09-08v.


## R-FETCH — SOURCING CC0 GROUND SURFACES WITHOUT AN OPERATOR (LOCKED 2026-09-12)

**Locked.** RULED BY RYAN 2026-09-12: the agent sources its own
materials. The motivation was not speed — it was that picking packs by
eye kept landing on ones that are subtly wrong, and all three failure
modes had already happened here.

### THE COMMANDS

    python scripts/fetch_surface.py --selftest
    python scripts/fetch_surface.py --search rock terrain
    python scripts/fetch_surface.py --fetch polyhaven:forest_floor --dry-run
    python scripts/fetch_surface.py --fetch polyhaven:forest_floor

### A DOWNLOAD IS NOT FINISHED UNTIL IT HAS PASSED THE GATE

Everything lands in `Free/_staging/` and is **promoted to `Free/` only on
a pass**. A refused pack stays in staging beside a `REFUSED.json` saying
why, so it can never be mistaken for an intaken asset. Nothing is ever
deleted (standing rule 2).

Three refusals, each bought with a real defect on this project:

    NO HEIGHT MAP   Dry_Fallen_Leaves ships B/N/ORM and no _H at all
    8-BIT HEIGHT    Megascans ships Displacement as JPEG; six refused
    A DECAL         PineNeedles001 passed the height gate at 96.7%
                    TRANSPARENT -- a height gate does not test coverage

`--selftest` proves all three refusals plus the legitimate case plus an
empty folder, with no network.

### POLY HAVEN IS PREFERRED, AND THE REASON IS MEASURABLE

    polyhaven   dimensions published in mm  -> STRETCH IS COMPUTABLE
    ambientcg   dimensionX/Y/Z = 0 from its own API -> never computable

Poly Haven also exposes per-map format (`Displacement` as png/exr/jpg)
and separate `nor_dx` / `nor_gl`, so 16-bit height is REQUESTED rather
than discovered afterwards. 129 textures carry the `terrain` category.

Measured on the first fetch: `forest_floor`, 2.14 x 2.14 m stated,
derived tile 5.03 m, **stretch 2.35x** — the first stretch figure this
project has ever been able to compute.

### FAB CANNOT BE AUTOMATED, AND THIS IS NOT A PERMISSIONS PROBLEM

`Bridge`, `Fab` and `MegascansPlugin` ship **ZERO Python** — they are C++
around an authenticated embedded browser. There is no scriptable
download surface and no permission grant creates one. Recorded so the
question is not reopened.

### PNG THROUGHOUT

Height because the gate must read it without OpenEXR installed. The rest
because these are shipping material inputs that are ALSO MEASURED, and a
lossy albedo feeds the albedo-band table that rulings are made from.

## R-FETCH REJECTED — 2026-09-12

- **NAMING FETCHED MAPS BY ROLE** (`forest_floor_color_4k.jpg`).
  **Symptom: the pack passes the gate, and `scan_surface_stats` then
  reports "no colour map found" and both normals "absent" on an asset
  that is completely fine.** Correct: the ambientCG convention every tool
  in `scripts/` already reads — `_Color`, `_Displacement`, `_NormalDX`,
  `_Roughness`, `_AmbientOcclusion`. A second naming convention is a
  second list that must agree with the first (NN24). The fetcher conforms
  to the existing dialect rather than teaching every downstream tool a
  new one.
- **A MAP FINDER THAT ACCEPTS ONLY `.png`.** `find_map` skipped every
  other container, so a JPEG colour map reported as ABSENT — a file that
  was present, readable and sitting right there. **A finder that silently
  declines to look at a container reports absence for something it never
  examined**, the same class as the cvar getter that could not tell
  "zero" from "absent". Now accepts png/jpg/jpeg/tif/tiff.
- **JPEG FOR ALBEDO** to save bandwidth. It is lossy and it feeds the
  albedo-band table; the 22 MB saving is not worth a measured number
  being slightly wrong. PNG throughout.
- **`Remove-Item -Recurse -Force` AS ERROR HANDLING** when a parking
  directory already existed. Refused by the `no-force-delete` hook.
  Standing rule 2 has no exception for defensive cleanup — that is
  precisely how it was broken before. Move to `_trash/`; both `_trash/*`
  and `Free/*` are gitignored, so parking costs the repo nothing.


## R-LAYERS5 — FIVE LAYERS FROM FOUR CHANNELS (Brief 3 Task 3, 2026-09-12)

**Status: OFFLINE HALF LOCKED. The material has NOT been rebuilt in the
editor** — see WHAT IS NOT DONE. Supersedes R-LAYERS' v1 `--collapse`
mapping, whose own docstring deferred per-layer surfaces to "Task 3's
scans". They arrived.

### THE CONTRACT

    R = Snow        G = Rock        B = Scree       A = ForestFloor
    Grass (meadow)  = 1 - (R+G+B+A), DERIVED IN THE SHADER

**LAYER ORDER IS CHANNEL ORDER, and the remainder layer must be LAST.**
Reordering `material.layers` silently repaints the world.

**THE REMAINDER IS NOT STORED.** A fifth channel would be a fifth number
obliged to agree with four others, and 8-bit quantisation guarantees it
sometimes would not (NN24). Derived in the shader, the masks sum to 1 by
construction rather than by assertion.

### THE COMMANDS

    python scripts/derive_layer_weights.py --expand
    python scripts/bake_surface_lookup.py --write
    python scripts/surface_query.py --selftest

`--expand` asserts three things, each able to fail (the assertions live
in the pure `_expand_check`, so the selftest drives all three failure
directions without writing PNGs):

    sum(stored) <= 1        else the shader remainder goes NEGATIVE and
                            that layer renders as a black bruise
    remainder == wet_shore  ALL the non-stored layers fold into the
      + dirt_path + gravel  remainder, checked against the OTHER file, not
      + meadow (from w8b)   asserted in prose. AMENDED 2026-09-19 (Brief 4
                            T4): wet_shore was added to this sum -- dropping
                            it false-passes only while wet_shore==0, so the
                            amendment is load-bearing
    dirt_path still         it has no mask (streets are actors); if that
      identically 0         stops being true the omission must be
                            re-decided, not carried. wet_shore is NO LONGER
                            required zero -- it is a real derived ring now

Coverage: snow 9.92, rock 42.30, scree 11.97, forest_floor 10.63,
meadow-remainder 25.17% (= meadow 24.65 + gravel 0.52), pre-Brief-4.
wet_shore folds into the remainder (byte-identical shipped PNG), so these
stored-channel figures are unchanged by T4.

### ONE DECLARATION, TWO CONSUMERS

`WEIGHTMAP_CHANNELS` and `mask_plan()` live in
`make_landscape_material.py`. The payload's `_chan` is INTERPOLATED from
it; `bake_surface_lookup` and `surface_query` IMPORT it. None of the
three spells the mapping out again — two copies would disagree silently
and **the shader would paint scree where the footstep audio played
grass**, with nothing to compare them against (NN24, NN19).

### WHAT IS NOT DONE

    the 5 surfaces are NOT imported into UE (/Game/Surfaces/T_<id>_<role>)
    the material graph is NOT rebuilt -- the editor was never opened
    no render, no coverage check against a frame
    wet_shore is DERIVED (Brief 4 T4) but NOT a stored surface -- it folds
      into the shader remainder (renders as grass) at blockout. Promoting
      it to its own layer needs a 6th stored channel (a 2nd weightmap
      texture; the RGBA is full) + a shore SURFACE asset + a material
      rebuild == a MATERIAL-PASS item, not off-disk work

### WHY ONLY FIVE

`dirt_path` is **identically zero** (R-LAYERS): it has no mask because
streets are ACTORS. A sampler and a blend for a mask that is always zero
is cost for nothing — the concavity gate was rejected for exactly this.
`gravel` at 0.52% and (as of Brief 4 T4) `wet_shore` fold into the meadow
remainder rather than buying a second weightmap texture; `wet_shore` is a
real derived ring but has no shore SURFACE asset yet, so at blockout it
renders as grass. Promoting either to a stored layer is a one-line recipe
change plus the material rebuild once a surface exists (WHAT IS NOT DONE).
`--expand` still REFUSES if `dirt_path` stops being zero (its zero is a
structural fact, not a pending mask), but ALLOWS a non-zero `wet_shore`.

### THE FEATHER (Brief 7 Phase 1, 2026-09-24) — REQUIRED, not optional

**Symptom it cures:** the composite `alpine_8k_weights.png` was NEAR-BINARY
(~83–98% of texels pure 0/255 per channel), so two surfaces met on a HARD
~1 m mask edge and the terrain SHATTERED into ~1 m blocks under minification
(`research/brief7/p1_block_diff.md`, `feather_handoff.md`). The mip filter
(SIMPLE_AVERAGE) and `height_blend.k` are NOT the lever — the hard FULL-RES
mask is.

`--expand` now applies a **Gaussian σ = `material.weightmap_feather_sigma_px`
texels (1.5 → ~3 m ramps)** to the four stored channels
(`feather_stored_channels`), then RENORMALISES so the per-texel stored sum
≤ 1 (the shader meadow remainder must stay ≥ 0). 1 texel = 1 m here.

- The **source-contract `_expand_check` runs on the UNFEATHERED channels**
  (its assertion 2, `remainder == wet+path+gravel+meadow`, is a claim about
  the w8 SOURCE decomposition that the feather deliberately breaks); a
  separate post-feather guard asserts remainder ≥ 0 on the feathered result.
- **`weightmap_feather_sigma_px` is REQUIRED when `material.weightmap` is set**
  — an absent field is the retired near-binary path, so `_validate_material`
  refuses it (schema v1.29). `expand()` refuses too. Inert without a
  weightmap → also refused.

**Invariants:** `check_weightmap_feather.py` (in `run_offline_suite`) — (1)
feathered ≥ 25% in a ±ceil(3σ) band at each channel boundary AND ≥ source+0.25
(the pre-feather ramp is the negative control: measured feathered 0.88–0.96 vs
source 0.06–0.27); (2) Σ(stored) ≤ 255; (3) snow-line registration — the
**aspect** discrimination (`hillshade_snow_check.score` on the FEATHERED snow)
stays PASS (measured ratio 28.5, lit 0.68%), and the 50%-isoline altitude drifts
< 30 m (½ the derivation's 60 m vertical feather; measured 16.4 m — thin low
snow slivers erode, the line holds).

Coverage after feather (σ=1.5): snow 9.92, rock 42.30, scree 11.97,
forest_floor 9.53, meadow-remainder 26.27%. **Post-merge:** re-import the
weightmap → rebuild k=0 → re-bake surface → re-shoot (the world run).

## R-LAYERS5 REJECTED — 2026-09-12 (+ Brief 4 T4, 2026-09-19)

**Feather-verification rejections (Brief 7 P1, 2026-09-24 — hit as real
failures while authoring `check_weightmap_feather.py`; the feather itself was
correct, the instruments were not):**

- **SNOW REGISTRATION AS A PER-TEXEL IoU OF THE 50% ISOLINE.**
  → SYMPTOM: IoU 0.767 on a correct feather, reading as a big FAIL. → CAUSE:
  the snow mask is DAPPLED (per-aspect + slope-gated), so a σ=1.5 blur churns
  thousands of thin boundary texels while the LINE holds; per-texel IoU is far
  too sensitive to fine-structure change. → CORRECT: test the snow LINE, not
  the texels — `hillshade_snow_check.score` on the feathered snow (aspect
  discrimination: shaded/lit ratio, lit ceiling) PLUS a bounded mean-altitude
  drift. The aspect test PASSED (ratio 28.5) where IoU screamed.
- **NEGATIVE CONTROL = "the pre-feather SOURCE is < 25% feathered at the
  1-texel boundary ring".** → SYMPTOM: the source measured 0.573 feathered at
  the ring, "disproving" that it was near-binary. → CAUSE: the SMOOTH w8a
  source already has a 1–2 texel smoothstep ramp at the immediate edge; the
  near-binary property is a GLOBAL one (the vast interior), and at the 1-texel
  ring both source and feather look intermediate. → CORRECT: measure in a
  DILATED ±ceil(3σ) band (where the source's narrow ramp fills a small
  fraction and the feather fills most) and make the load-bearing claim
  "feathered ≫ source" (the ramp WIDENED), not an absolute source floor.

**wet_shore design-time rejections (Brief 4 T4, 2026-09-19 — rejected at
design, not hit as failures; recorded so a fresh session does not do the
naive thing):**

- **wet_shore AS A GLOBAL `|h - level| <= band` ELEVATION BAND.**
  → SYMPTOM: every mountainside, ridge saddle and unrelated basin at the
  lake's elevation lights up as "shore" — Lake A at 180 m would paint a
  contour line clear across the map. → CAUSE: proximity to the water
  SURFACE is not proximity to the water BODY. → CORRECT: gate the vertical
  band by ADJACENCY to the lake's CONNECTED footprint (a dilation of the
  footprint), so only the actual shore qualifies. The selftest's `far`
  region (same elevation, far from the lake → zero) is the discriminator.
- **RE-FLOOD-FILLING THE FOOTPRINT AT 8129 inside `derive_layer_weights`.**
  → SYMPTOM: a second lake-extent derivation that need not reproduce the
  hydro figures — connectivity at the fine grid can split or merge basins
  the 2033 analysis fixed, and nothing would notice. → CAUSE: two
  derivations of one physical fact (NN24). → CORRECT: reuse
  `hydro_derive.level_slice` on the committed 4x heightmap (the tool of
  record) and upsample nearest to 8129 (vertex-aligned: 8129=4*2032+1); the
  footprint is only an ADJACENCY LOCALIZER, the precise damp band is cut
  from the shipped 8129 heightmap. A POSITIVE CONTROL refuses if the
  footprint area drifts from water.json's area_ha.
- **FOLDING wet_shore SILENTLY INTO THE REMAINDER WITHOUT UPDATING THE
  `_expand_check` IDENTITY.** → SYMPTOM: `--expand` refuses with "remainder
  disagrees with gravel+meadow" the moment wet_shore is non-zero, OR (if
  the wet_shore==0 assertion were simply deleted) the shoreline renders as
  grass with no record of the re-decision. → CAUSE: the remainder is
  `1-(stored 4)` = wet+path+gravel+meadow; the old identity named only
  gravel+meadow. → CORRECT: add wet_shore to the identity AND keep dirt_path
  required-zero AND record in the recipe that promotion to a stored surface
  is a material-pass item. → REFERENCE: `derive_layer_weights._expand_check`.

- **KEEPING THE `forest_floor` TINT ALONGSIDE THE NEW LAYER.** Both are
  driven by the SAME alpha channel, so the canopy would be counted
  twice — tinted AND surfaced. The tint existed only because no litter
  scan had ever passed the 16-bit height gate. Block DELETED, not
  retained "in case".
- **STORING MEADOW AS A FIFTH CHANNEL.** See the contract: it is a fifth
  number that must agree with four others under 8-bit quantisation.
- **`convert("RGB")` ON THE WEIGHTMAP.** → SYMPTOM: `IndexError: index 3
  is out of bounds for axis 2 with size 3` in `surface_query`, and a
  bare `REFUSE: the recipe declares 5 layers` in `bake_surface_lookup`.
  → CAUSE: both dropped the alpha and assumed exactly three layers.
  → CORRECT: `convert("RGBA")`, then `mask_plan()` to decide how many
  are stored and whether the last is the remainder.
- **A SECOND COPY OF THE CHANNEL MAPPING** in each consumer. The shader
  and the CPU lookup answer the same physical question and must not be
  able to differ.

## R-TOWNEXCL — KEEPING THE FOREST OUT OF THE TOWN (2026-09-12b)

**Status: PROVEN once**, on `/Game/Alpine8K`: 219,659 → 2,557 removed →
217,102, zero tree instances inside the footprint, every survivor an
IDENTICAL row, and `buildings whose dominant layer is ForestFloor`
43.23% → 0.00%.

### THE PROCEDURE

    python scripts/town_exclusion.py --selftest        # 12 checks
    python scripts/place_foliage.py --recipe <r> --exclude-only
    python scripts/derive_layer_weights.py             # 8 layer PNGs
    python scripts/derive_layer_weights.py --expand    # -> RGBA weightmap
    python scripts/check_weightmap_fresh.py            # BEFORE any capture

The exclusion is declared in `foliage.settlement_exclusion` and names
ONLY the plan. **The margins are read from
`recipes/city.json:foliage_clearing`** (building 3.0 m, street 2.0 m,
plaza 6.0 m) where they were measured by sweep, never restated.

`--exclude-only` constructs NO generator: it filters committed plans in
place, so no position can move. Full `place_foliage` applies the same
exclusion as a POST-FILTER after the rows are built.

### REJECTED

**PUTTING THE EXCLUSION IN THE SAMPLER, OR BELIEVING IT CANNOT GO IN THE
RECIPE AT ALL.**
→ SYMPTOM: either the whole forest moves, or the exclusion is left in an
editor-side clear that the weight derivation never sees.
→ CAUSE: `plan()` draws yaw, pitch, roll and scale from the SAME
generator that placed the points, sized by how many points survived the
keep-mask. Filtering before the row build changes those sizes and shifts
every subsequent draw. `recipes/city.json` generalised that correctly-
observed hazard into "it cannot be in the foliage recipe", which is
false for a post-filter.
→ CORRECT: filter AFTER the rows are built (or use `--exclude-only`),
and ASSERT the survivors are the original rows. The assertion is one
line and the claim had gone untested since 2026-08-25.
→ REFERENCE: LESSONS 2026-09-12d; `recipes/city.json:128`.

**READING THE WEIGHTMAP AS RGB UNDER THE FIVE-LAYER CONTRACT.**
→ SYMPTOM: `IndexError: index 4 is out of bounds for axis 2 with size 3`
from `place_foliage`, OR — with four declared layers instead of five —
NO error and a plausible, wrong forest planted off the alpha channel.
→ CAUSE: four layers are STORED channels; the fifth is the shader
remainder `1-(R+G+B+A)` and has no channel. `Grass` is that remainder,
and every tree species is keyed to it.
→ CORRECT: `convert("RGBA")`, and resolve the layer through
`mask_plan` imported from the material builder — never a restated index.
Sample the remainder PER CHANNEL at the sample points; bilinear is
linear, so that equals the full-grid form and allocates nothing.
→ REFERENCE: LESSONS 2026-09-12d.

**GATING THE PLAZA DISC ON A NON-ZERO MARGIN.**
→ SYMPTOM: `plaza_margin_m: 0.0` clears NO plaza, rather than clearing
the plan's own 22 m radius.
→ CAUSE: `city_clear_foliage_payload` tests
`if _pc and float(PLAZA_MARGIN_M) > 0.0`, contradicting `city.json`'s own
declaration that the disc is `plan.plaza_radius_cm` PLUS the margin.
Inert at the shipped 6.0 m, which is why it survived.
→ CORRECT: build the disc whenever a centre exists; the margin only
SIZES it. `town_exclusion.build` does, and its selftest exercises the
margin production never uses.
→ REFERENCE: LESSONS 2026-09-12d.

**⛔ REGENERATING THE FOLIAGE FROM SCRATCH — BLOCKED, DO NOT RETRY BLIND.**
→ SYMPTOM: 152 instances where the plans carry 219,659; per-species
acceptance 0.0%.
→ CAUSE: NOT the exclusion. A jittered lattice at `cells=534`
(spacing 15.22097 px) sampling the REMAINDER layer returns 0.13153
against a whole-map mean of 0.25174 — a stratified sample, which is
unbiased by construction, coming back 48% low. Generator uniformity,
block independence, field smoothness and index coverage were all
measured and are clean; `cells` 400/512/813/1000 and five other seeds
are unaffected.
→ CORRECT: use `--exclude-only` until it is explained. A fix that
restores the count without explaining the bias plants a forest by an
unexplained mechanism.
→ REFERENCE: LESSONS 2026-09-12d, with a four-line repro.

## R-METER — MANUAL METERING AND RENDER WARM-UP (2026-09-13)

**Status: PROVEN.** The card lands in band for the first time.

### THE PROCEDURE

    python scripts/import_layer_textures.py --recipe <r>   # if maps moved
    python scripts/check_weightmap_fresh.py                # gate, pre-capture
    python scripts/apply_lighting.py --recipe <r>          # applies + SAVES
    python scripts/bench_capture.py --profile target --stations near_ground --linear
    python scripts/exr_card.py --exr <exr> --station near_ground --sidecar <json>

Metering is `AEM_MANUAL`, clamp pinned 1.0/1.0, Apply Physical Camera
Exposure **off**, all three with their `override_` companions TRUE and
all read back from the volume. Render warm-up is ON by default; use
`--no-render-warm-up` only to reproduce the pre-2026-09-13 state.

    compensation_ev  -14.2554   card 0.179812   band [0.171, 0.189]  PASS
    white_tint       -0.0139    R/G 1.0221  B/G 1.0091  band 0.97-1.03

### REJECTED

**SETTING A WARM-UP COUNT WITHOUT ITS ENABLING BOOL.**
> STATUS: HISTORY — anti-spec: the warm-up-bool / slope rejects
→ SYMPTOM: none. The sidecar records `"warm_up_frames": 300`, the count
reads back as set, and every capture renders ZERO warm-up frames.
→ CAUSE: `render_warm_up_count` defaults to 32 and
`render_warm_up_frames` — the bool that gates it — defaults to FALSE.
The 300 that was being set is `engine_warm_up_count`, which ticks the
GAME thread and renders nothing.
→ CONSEQUENCE, MEASURED: the card moved 0.180 -> 0.216851, about
+0.27 EV, so every exposure solve before 2026-09-13 was made against a
frame the engine had not settled.
→ TWO MECHANISMS, NOT ONE (AUDIT P1-2, added 2026-09-15). The pre-09-13
caveat must name BOTH, because a reader who fixes only one still gets an
unsettled frame: (1) EYE ADAPTATION — with render warm-up off, auto
exposure had not converged when the frame was taken; (2) SKY LIGHT
REAL-TIME CAPTURE IS TIME-SLICED across frames (Sky Light real-time
capture updates a fraction of the cubemap per frame), so on frame zero
the sky lighting is only partially built and the fill is wrong. The
+0.27 EV is the sum; the render warm-up (32 rendered frames) settles
both. Naming only eye adaptation would leave the sky-light half
un-diagnosed.
→ CORRECT: set and READ BACK all three —
`render_warm_up_frames` True, `render_warm_up_count` 32,
`engine_warm_up_count` 300.
→ REFERENCE: LESSONS 2026-09-13a; AUDIT P1-2.

**READING THE 0.7598 log-log SLOPE AS A PPI0 QUANTITY (AUDIT S-7, added
2026-09-15).**
→ The exposure transfer slope 0.7598 (which corroborates the 0.731
measured 2026-09-11) is a property of the LOOK chain, measured on the
tone-curve-carrying FinalImage. On PPI0 — upstream of the tonemap — a
requested EV delivers ~1.000 (the pass is linear in exposure by
construction, R-PPSPLIT). So the 0.7598 slope MUST NOT enter a PPI0-based
solve: doing so would apply the look chain's compression twice. It is
recorded beside the PPI0 numbers, never inside them.
→ REFERENCE: AUDIT S-7.

**READING `disable_tone_curve_readback` AS PROOF THE CURVE IS GONE.**
→ It reads the MRQ property that was just written. Under rule 12 that
proves the SETTER ran, not that the tonemapper honoured it.

**CLOSING Q12 ON A CANDIDATE WITH THE RIGHT SHAPE.**
→ SYMPTOM: "colour grading contrast is a power law, contrast is 0.95,
done."
→ CAUSE: the residual log-log slope is 0.723. 0.95 is not 0.723, and
0.95 x film_slope 0.88 = 0.836 is not either. The grade is a FACTOR.
→ CORRECT: MRQ residual stages stand, enumerated from the config:
DeferredPassBase, ImageSequenceOutput_PNG/_EXR, ColorSetting (ocio
disabled), AntiAliasing, GameOverride, ConsoleVariable, Output;
`disable_multisample_effects` False.
→ REFERENCE: `scripts/payloads/mrq_stages_probe.py`, `grade_probe.py`.

it compared shadowed TERRAIN to lit TERRAIN so its denominator moved
with ground albedo (the card read the light neutral while it reported

### R-EDITOR-CLOSE — AMENDED 2026-09-13: `-RenderOffScreen` HAS NO WINDOW

`CloseMainWindow()` returns **False** on an editor launched with
`-RenderOffScreen`, twice, because there is no main window. Census clean,
quiet 926 s, `PackageRestoreData` Packages `[]` — the kill was authorised
on the original step 4 and was clean.

→ **A LAUNCH FLAG CAN REMOVE A GATE'S INSTRUMENT.** Launch offscreen and
the graceful-close path does not exist; plan to end on the kill and
prove safety the other three ways. Do NOT read two `False` returns as an
unresponsive editor.
→ Offscreen is the fix for the GPU crash: `DXGI_ERROR_DEVICE_REMOVED` at
`D3D12Viewport.cpp:537`, 36 s after load, in the VIEWPORT PRESENT path.
→ **AND IT IS NOW THE LAUNCHER'S DEFAULT** (2026-09-13). That fix sat in
LESSONS and in this recipe for a day and NEVER REACHED
`scripts/launch_editor.ps1`, so every launch through it kept the crash
site. A lesson that exists and does not fire is a defect in the lesson.
`-Windowed` opts out.

### R-EDITOR-CLOSE — A THROWAWAY ASSET IS NOT THROWAWAY UNTIL THE EDITOR CLOSES

**⛔ CREATING AND DELETING A SCRATCH ASSET LEAVES A DIRTY PACKAGE, AN
AUTOSAVE, AND A RESTORE MODAL.** Measured 2026-09-13: a probe built
`/Game/_scratch/M_ProbeMip`, tested one property and deleted it. The
asset never reached disk (`Content/_scratch` does not exist), and yet at
close time:

    dirty census   1 package: /Game/_scratch/M_ProbeMip
    on disk        LandscapeLab/Saved/Autosaves/Game/...
                   PackageRestoreData.json  RestoreEnabled: true

**The DELETE marks the package dirty**, and the editor autosaved it. On
the next launch that raises a Restore modal, and a modal blocks the game
thread — which is the only channel that could report it is blocked.

→ The close gate WORKED: it refused to read "clean" and named the
package, which is how this was found.
→ Kill was still authorised on the other three proofs: the dirty package
was a deleted asset that never existed on disk, RSS flat at 8.18 GB over
20 s, newest `Content` write 6238 s earlier.
→ **AFTER the kill, move the autosave AND `PackageRestoreData.json` into
`_trash/`** (standing rule 2 — never a forced delete). `launch_editor.ps1`
also moves the restore file aside, but only for launches that go through
it.
→ REFERENCE: LESSONS 2026-09-13g.

| header | :line | python |
|---|---|---|

`get_editor_property(name)`; record every name that refuses in a
`names_that_would_not_read` list so a missing field is visible.

statement about the class. Reached TWICE here by two probes that both

→ CORRECT: an empty `dir()` property list is evidence about the binding
and none about the class. Confirm against the header before writing

    Alpine8K_HLODLayer_Landscape     NOT REFERENCED, NOT IN THE CHAIN

read raised on all 4,339`. A zero from a swallowing loop is not a

## R-BENCH-GAMEOVERRIDE — THE MRQ SETTING THAT WAS NEVER IN THE CONFIG (2026-09-13)

**Before 2026-09-13 `MoviePipelineGameOverrideSetting` was added ONLY
under `--truth`.** Every dev-profile and every non-truth target capture
carried a config of **five** setting classes with no GameOverride in it:

    MoviePipelineDeferredPassBase        MoviePipelineImageSequenceOutput_PNG
    MoviePipelineAntiAliasingSetting     MoviePipelineConsoleVariableSetting
    MoviePipelineOutputSetting

So `disable_hlods`, `use_lod_zero`, `use_high_quality_shadows`,
`flush_grass_streaming`, `flush_streaming_managers`,
`override_view_distance_scale` and `cinematic_quality_settings` were not
merely unread on those captures — **they were never applied.**

`--game-override KEY=VALUE` (repeatable) now adds and sets it;
`--dump-config` prints the config the engine holds and renders nothing.

**⛔ ADDING THE SETTING AT ALL IS A LARGE CHANGE, NOT A SMALL ONE.** Its
MRQ defaults, read back the moment it is added:

    disable_hlods True    use_lod_zero True    view_distance_scale 50
    texture_streaming DISABLED     shadow_distance_scale 10
    use_high_quality_shadows True  flush_grass_streaming True
    override_grass_cull_distance_scale True   grass_cull_distance_scale 50.0

A test that toggles `cinematic_quality_settings` alone still has all of
the above in force **in both arms**.

### PRECEDENCE, MEASURED

`bCinematicQualitySettings` calls `Scalability::SetQualityLevels(max)`
at setup (`MoviePipelineGameOverrideSetting.cpp:53-65`); the bench writes
`sg.*` through `MoviePipelineConsoleVariableSetting` at the same moment.

**THE CVARS WIN.** Two dev captures differing in that flag alone:
every `sg.*` `PreviousValue` identical (`sg.ShadowQuality` `1 -> 1` in
both), every `Scalability` group identical at both hooks.

The instrument: `MoviePipelineConsoleVariableSetting.cpp:253` logs
`Applying CVar "X" PreviousValue: p NewValue: n`, and `p` is the value
the instant before the bench's cvars land. Had GameOverride run first,
`p` would read Cinematic.

**AND THE DEV PROFILE IS NOT `sg.*=1`.** Two of the ten are 3:

    sg.GlobalIlluminationQuality 3      sg.ReflectionQuality 3
    everything else 1                   r.ScreenPercentage 100

### REJECTED

**Querying a scalability cvar by bare name to read its value.**
→ SYMPTOM: `sg.ShadowQuality` as a console command prints **nothing**.
The log line after `Executing Console Command "sg.ShadowQuality"` is
empty, and a parser looking for `sg.X = "1"` matches zero — then reports
`differences: NONE`, which reads as agreement and is silence.
→ CORRECT: use `Scalability`, which prints every group:
`Display:   ShadowQuality (0..3): (custom)`. `(custom)` means the group's
cvars were set individually and match no preset — informative, since a
Cinematic override prints `3`.
→ AND: report the instrument's **sample count** beside its verdict. Zero
samples must refuse, not agree.
→ REFERENCE: 2026-09-13 precedence test, both captures, 22 commands
executed and 0 parsed.

**Enumerating every property of an MRQ setting over remote exec without
suppressing warnings.**
→ SYMPTOM: `RuntimeError: Remote party failed to send a valid response!`
(`remote_execution.py:471`) against a healthy, responding editor.
→ CAUSE: UE raises a Python `DeprecationWarning` on EVERY touch of a
deprecated property, an enumerating dump touches each attribute twice,
and the text lands on the same stdout the `__LL__` marker uses.
Deprecated here: `stencil_layers` → `actor_layers`, `disable_hlo_ds` →
`disable_hlods`, `game_mode_override` → `SoftGameModeOverride`.
→ CORRECT: install a `warnings.showwarning` collector for the dump and
**write the captured warnings into the artefact** — they are the engine
answering the deprecation question, not noise.

in `"r.ForceLOD -1"` and then demands a closing quote.
→ CORRECT: a second pattern for command strings, `<cvar><ws><value>`.
→ REFERENCE: 2026-09-13; the printed `cvar writes 0` was the tell.

**Classifying cvar sites at LINE scope.**
→ SYMPTOM: 0 writes reported for a file that writes 30 cvars, because
the name is in a list and the call takes a loop variable.
→ CORRECT: also pair at FILE scope, and LABEL those rows `INDIRECT` so
the evidence grade travels with the row.

**Widening the matcher without re-checking the filter.**
→ SYMPTOM: lever count 405 → 432, of which 19 are recipe paths —
`foliage.rock_scatter.repose_deg`, `landscape.scale_xy_cm`,
`foliage.seed`. `foliage.` and `landscape.` are real cvar prefixes AND
the top-level keys of `recipes/alpine_8k.json`.
→ CORRECT: UE cvars are CamelCase after the prefix (`r.ScreenPercentage`,
`foliage.WindEnabled`, even `r.setRes`); every recipe key here is
snake_case. An all-lowercase tail is a recipe path. State it as a LIMIT
in the predicate, let `SEEDED` override it, and list every rejection in
`dropped_as_non_levers` so the filter is auditable.
→ GENERAL: **widening a matcher and narrowing a filter are the same
edit** and must be tested together.

**Assuming a lever scan that greps property NAMES has found every
writer.**
→ SYMPTOM: `lighting.sky.color` recorded as having no write site. It has
one — `scripts/apply_lighting.py:394-398` — through
`_slc.set_light_color(...)`, a METHOD, which no `set_editor_property`
search can see.
→ CORRECT: any lever set through a named setter is invisible to a
property-name scan. Recall, not precision, is this inventory's open
question.

### R-EDITOR-CLOSE — AMENDED 2026-09-13: `PackageRestoreData` PRESENCE IS NOT THE PREDICATE

**The file is present after a perfectly clean shutdown.** Measured
2026-09-13 after a kill authorized by all three gates — census 0 dirty,
RSS flat at 17.574 GB across four 12 s samples, newest Content write
6,852 s old, 0 ShaderCompileWorkers:

    LandscapeLab/Saved/Autosaves/PackageRestoreData.json   PRESENT
    contents: {"RestoreEnabled": true, "Packages": []}     94 bytes, UTF-16

The editor writes this on shutdown whether or not anything was dirty.

→ **The signal with two causes is the file's EXISTENCE. The one that
carries the meaning is whether `Packages` is NON-EMPTY.** Read the file
and check the array; `Test-Path` alone reports a benign shutdown as
unsaved work.
→ The launcher's handling is unaffected and still correct — it moves the
file aside before launch precisely so a stale one cannot raise a Restore
modal.
→ **AND THE GENERAL FORM, WHICH THIS RECIPE HAS NOW LEARNED TWICE.** The
2026-09-11 amendment fixed the CPU predicate with the words *a gate whose
signal has two causes will block on the benign one forever* — and left
this predicate, three fields away in the same gate, reading existence.
**When a gate is corrected for a two-caused signal, audit its sibling
predicates in the same commit.**

## R-LIGHTCOLOUR — WRITING A RECIPE COLOUR TO A LIGHT (2026-09-13)

**`set_light_color` ENCODES. Pass the RAW LINEAR value.**

    LightComponent.cpp:1130-1134
      void ULightComponent::SetLightColor(FLinearColor NewLightColor, bool bSRGB)
      { const FColor NewColor(NewLightColor.ToFColor(bSRGB));
        SetLightFColor(NewColor); }
    Color.h:429      ToFColor(true) -> ToFColorSRGB()
    Color.cpp:251    ToFColorSRGB() -> ConvertLinearToSRGB...   (ENCODE)

The Python binding exposes ONE argument, so `bSRGB` is always true, so
the engine ALWAYS encodes. `light_color` is an 8-bit `FColor`; the
round trip therefore has a quantisation floor of 1/255 in encoded space
and any verdict must be stated against that floor.

Correct:

    _slc.set_light_color(_u.LinearColor(0.42, 0.6, 1.0, 1.0))   # recipe, linear
    # stored FColor (173, 203, 255) -> decodes to (0.42, 0.60, 1.00)

### REJECTED

**sRGB-encoding the recipe value in the host before `set_light_color`.**
→ SYMPTOM: **none that is visible.** Everything compiles, the setter
returns, the sidecar records the request, and the light is simply the
wrong colour. Measured 2026-09-13: recipe linear `[0.42, 0.6, 1.0]`
stored as `(215, 231, 255)`, which is the value encoded TWICE, giving an
effective linear `(0.6795, 0.7991, 1.0)` — R 62 % high, G 33 % high, B
exact.
→ ⛔ **B IS ALWAYS EXACT AT 1.0**, because 1.0 is a fixed point of the
sRGB curve. A channel at full scale cannot show this defect, so the
channel most likely to be spot-checked is the one guaranteed to look
right.
→ CORRECT: pass the raw linear value; the engine's single encode is the
whole conversion.
→ REFERENCE: `apply_lighting.py:155` (the pre-encode) and `:396` (the
call); engine lines above.

**Reasoning about the round trip in a docstring instead of measuring
it.** `apply_lighting.py:388-393` argued that the binding's single
argument means the value is "decoded as sRGB" so the host's encode is
cancelled. `bSRGB = true` means EMIT sRGB — encode, not decode. The
prose was wrong and was trusted for the life of the file.
→ CORRECT: **prose that explains why two transforms cancel is a
PREDICTION; read the value back and test it.** A parameter with an
argument for why it is fine is prose that has already convinced someone.

## R-HLOD-SETUP — WHAT `-SetupHLODs` CAN AND CANNOT TELL YOU (2026-09-13)

**`-SetupHLODs -ReportOnly` writes nothing and decides nothing.**

    python scripts/hlod_build_batched.py plan --run-dir <ABSOLUTE PATH>

Measured 2026-09-13: 12 sections, 2,267 GUIDs, EngineVersion
`5.8.1-56057345+++UE5+Release-5.8`, and **0 of 2,267 packages changed**
byte-for-byte and mtime-for-mtime.

### REJECTED

**Expecting `-SetupHLODs` to report which cells are flagged dirty.**
→ SYMPTOM: a clean 2.8 MB log listing all 2,267 cells with **zero**
`final decision` lines and **zero** `Building HLOD actor` lines.
→ CAUSE, at source: `WorldPartitionHLODsBuilder.cpp:432-438` runs
`SetupHLODActors()` and then guards `BuildHLODActors()` behind
`if (!bReportOnly)`. `-ReportOnly` does NOT make the build step dry — it
**skips it entirely**, and the rebuild policy
(`HLODRebuildPolicyHashCompare`) lives inside the step that is skipped.
→ CORRECT: there is no report-only path to the flagged set in 5.8. The
only instrument that emits Approve/Reject is a real build pass, which
writes cells. The 2026-09-13 sample run got 46 approvals by BUILDING
them.
→ AND: the cell list is opaque external-actor paths, and the saved
`HLODBuildReport` holds only a header plus policy data
(`HLODActor.cpp:830-854`) — no source components — so not even the
landscape / non-landscape split of the population is derivable here.

**Attributing built cells from an Approve/Reject count.**
→ SYMPTOM: "46 cells built" with no way to know under which layer, which
is how a Landscape-layer settings change looked exercised when it was
not.
→ CORRECT: pair each decision with the PRECEDING builder line, which
names the layer folder and the source cell separately:
`Building HLOD actor Alpine8K_HLODLayer_Merged/Alpine8K_HLODLayer_Instanced_L0_X-8_Y10`
— folder = the layer the actor belongs to, cell name = what it was built
FROM. A decision line alone carries no cell identity.
→ MEASURED: 09-08 1,678 Instanced + 1,238 Merged; 09-09 1,343 + 1,134;
09-13 27 + 19. **Zero under `Alpine8K_HLODLayer_Landscape`, ever.**

**Passing a RELATIVE `--run-dir`.**
→ SYMPTOM: `rc=1` in 0.3 min, `no manifest written`, and **no log file at
all** — the run dir holds only the host's own marker.
→ CAUSE: the run dir feeds `-abslog=<dir>/manifest_setup.log`. Unreal
resolves relative paths against its own working directory, which it sets
to the engine binaries folder at startup (the 2026-08-21 defect). The
script's DEFAULT run dir is absolute, so the trap only springs when the
flag is used.
→ CORRECT: pass an absolute path. Better, `os.path.abspath()` it in the
argument parser so no caller can get it wrong.

**A landscape component is ALWAYS built by `ULandscapeHLODBuilder`,
whatever layer it sits in.**

    LandscapeComponent.cpp:97-100
      TSubclassOf<UHLODBuilder> ULandscapeComponent::GetCustomHLODBuilderClass() const
      { return ULandscapeHLODBuilder::StaticClass(); }
    HLODBuilder.cpp:354
      HLODBuildersForComponents.FindOrAdd(
          SourceComponent->GetCustomHLODBuilderClass()).Add(SourceComponent);

Unconditional — it consults no layer, no setting, no cvar.

**The real levers are on the proxy** (`LandscapeProxy.h`, all
`LandscapeOverridable`, so read EVERY proxy and not just the parent):

    :958 HLODTextureSizePolicy    :963 HLODTextureSize
    :966 HLODMaterialOverride     :971 HLODMeshSourceLODPolicy
    :974 HLODMeshSourceLOD        :954 bUseLandscapeForCullingInvisibleHLODVertices

Alpine8K, 2026-09-13, 257 actors, 257 read OK, 0 raises, 0 outliers:
`SpecificSize` / `256` / `None` / `LowestDetailLOD` / `0` / `false` —
which are exactly the 5.8 CONSTRUCTOR defaults (`Landscape.cpp:1780-1783`).

⛔ `AutomaticSize` / `AutomaticLOD` is the LEGACY path, not the modern
default: `Landscape.cpp:5044-5049` applies it only to landscapes created
BEFORE the settings existed.

A material change DOES dirty landscape HLOD — `ComputeHLODHash` hashes
`MaterialInstances` / `OverrideMaterial` / `OverrideHoleMaterial`
(`LandscapeHLODBuilder.cpp:70-90`), plus Nanite settings, the two policy
fields, and the project `HLODMaxTextureSize`.

to a layer in order to control landscape HLOD.**
→ SYMPTOM: the write reads back perfectly from a freshly loaded asset
and changes nothing that renders. This is what the 2026-09-13 Task 5
unit did; its acceptance is VOID, not failed.
→ CORRECT: the six proxy properties above.

**Reading "0 of 4,339 actors name an HLOD layer" as "not HLOD'd".**
→ SYMPTOM: a 257-actor streaming mutation proposed to fix a
non-problem.
→ CAUSE: a null per-actor `HLODLayer` **falls back to the world
default** — `WorldPartitionRuntimeHashSetConversions.cpp:45`,
`ActorDescView.GetHLODLayer().IsValid() ? ... : DefaultHLODLayer`.
→ CORRECT: 0-naming means EVERYTHING uses the world default. Read
`UWorldPartition::DefaultHLODLayer` (`WorldPartition.h:612`, reached via
`world_settings.get_editor_property("world_partition")` — it is NOT on
WorldSettings) and walk `ParentLayer` (`HLODLayer.h:135`) to a fixed
point. Alpine8K: Instanced → Merged → end.

## R-SKYCOLOR — THE SKY LIGHT IS WHITE, AND THE VALUE IS ENCODED ONCE (RULED 2026-09-13)

**`lighting.sky.color = [1, 1, 1]`.** A physical, real-time-captured sky
light is not tinted: SkyAtmosphere owns the sky's colour and the capture
picks it up, so a tint multiplies a colour that is already present.

**CORROBORATED, not assumed** — all four sky lights in the Epic sample
census read white `255,255,255`: CitySample `SkyLight_WP`, DarkRuins
`SkyLight`, and both Electric Dreams maps. The two Electric Dreams ones
are `real_time_capture` with `SLS_CAPTURED_SCENE`, the same
configuration as here.

### THE ENCODE, once and only once

    LightComponent.cpp:1130-1134  SetLightColor -> NewLightColor.ToFColor(bSRGB)
    Color.h:429                   ToFColor(true) -> ToFColorSRGB()
    Color.cpp:251-267             ToFColorSRGB  -> ConvertLinearToSRGB...

`bSRGB = true` means EMIT sRGB bytes. Pass the **raw linear** recipe
value; the engine's single encode is the whole conversion.

    _slc.set_light_color(_u.LinearColor(r, g, b, 1.0))   # r,g,b LINEAR

`light_color` is an 8-bit `FColor`, so the round trip has a quantisation
floor of 1/255 in encoded space — 0.0089 linear near white. Any verdict
states itself against that floor.

### REJECTED

**sRGB-encoding the recipe colour in the host before `set_light_color`.**
→ SYMPTOM: **nothing visible.** It compiles, the setter returns, the
sidecar records the request, and the light is the wrong colour.
Measured 2026-09-13: linear `[0.42, 0.6, 1.0]` stored as
`FColor(215, 231, 255)` = the value encoded TWICE, giving an effective
linear `(0.6795, 0.7991, 1.0)` — R 62 % high, G 33 % high.
→ ⛔ **B IS EXACT AT 1.0 BY CONSTRUCTION** — 1.0 is a fixed point of the
sRGB curve — so a channel at full scale can never show this defect, and
the channel most likely to be spot-checked is the one guaranteed to look
right.
→ CORRECT: pass linear; delete any host-side encode.

**PROVING THE FIX BY READING BACK A WHITE VALUE.**
→ SYMPTOM: `[1,1,1]` reads back `FColor(255,255,255)` — and so would the
BROKEN path, for the same fixed-point reason. The read-back confirms the
VALUE and has **no power** to confirm the CODE.
→ CORRECT: prove the code on a DISCRIMINATING colour. The payload is
generated in-process with `[0.42, 0.6, 1.0]` and the emitted literal is
asserted to be the raw triple, not its encoding. A read-back on a fixed
point is not a test.

**BELIEVING A FIELD IS "INERT FOR A PHYSICAL SKY".** The recipe's own
`_task3` note said exactly that of `sky.color`, and it is why a
double-encoded value sat unexamined for weeks. It is not inert: it is a
multiplier on the captured cubemap and it is written on every apply.

## R-CARDSOLVE — WHICH FRAME CAN CARRY A SOLVE (2026-09-13)

**A BAND AND A SOLVE ARE DIFFERENT DEMANDS ON THE SAME FRAME.** Before
solving on an instrument, compute its resolution AT THE VALUE IN FRONT
OF YOU and compare it to the signal.

Measured on `near_ground`, target class, 2026-09-13:

    FinalImage PNG   card linear [0.28315, 0.27889, 0.27889]
                     = 8-bit codes 145, 144, 144
                     one code    = 0.00425 linear = 1.526% of the card
                     WB signal   = 1.00 code (R), 0.00 codes (B)
                     card std    = 1.84 codes
    scene-linear EXR card linear [0.260498, 0.254639, 0.253418]
                     float; d(wb_R)/dK resolved cleanly at 3.472e-04

→ **SOLVE on the EXR. Read the BAND on FinalImage** (0.85–1.15 is ±10
codes and perfectly readable there).

### THE PROCEDURE, slopes measured every time

    1 capture at the current value, read the card
    2 capture at a second, KNOWN offset -- ONE variable
    3 slope = d(metric)/d(parameter)
    4 requested = (target - current)/slope, apply
    5 re-capture and CONFIRM; the residual is recorded, not tuned away

Measured 2026-09-13: `d(wb_R)/dK` 3.472e-04 (+500 K step);
`d(wb_B)/d(tint)` 1.830 (+0.06 step); `d(log2 card_luma)/dEV` 0.7598
(−0.7 EV step). The last **corroborates 0.731 from 2026-09-11** on
different data — the chain is not linear and the non-linearity is
stable.

Probes write the live PostProcessVolume **unsaved** and are restored
before the next axis; only the solved value goes into the recipe.

### REJECTED

**Measuring a slope on a frame whose quantiser is larger than the
signal.**
→ SYMPTOM: two channels identical to five decimals, which reads as
precision and is actually a shared byte.
→ CORRECT: compute codes-per-unit at the working value first.

**Solving coupled axes independently and calling the residual a
mystery.**
→ SYMPTOM: `B/G` targeted at 1.0 landed at 1.0339.
→ CAUSE: `white_temp` moves `B/G` too — d(B/G)/dK ≈ −3.678e-04. The
−66.2 K contributes +0.0244, the tint step +0.0048: predicted 1.0244,
measured 1.0339.
→ CORRECT: first-order is fine IF the coupling is measured from the same
probes and the residual is DECOMPOSED afterwards. A 2×2 solve on both
axes together is the next step and is a ruling, not a tweak.

**A SHADE BAND WITH NO INSTRUMENT NAMED.** The same two frames, same
tool, read **2.44× and 2.86× apart** between FinalImage and PPI0
(card-normalised: FinalImage 1.6427 → 1.5987, PPI0 0.6733 → 0.5592). A
band is not checkable until it says which frame it governs.

`scripts/hlod_attribution.py` is **the one implementation**;
`hlod_build_batched` and the audit tool both import it.

    LogWorldPartitionHLODsBuilder: [6 / 6] Building HLOD actor
      Alpine8K_HLODLayer_Merged/Alpine8K_HLODLayer_Instanced_L0_X-8_Y10...
      ^^^^^ the LAYER the actor    ^^^^^ the SOURCE it is built FROM
            belongs to

The decision line that FOLLOWS carries no cell identity at all, so each
decision is attributed to the most recent preceding builder line.
Validated against a known result: the 2026-09-13 run re-derives **27

loss.**

`decisions_without_a_cell` and `cells_without_a_decision` are reported
beside every count — a desynced pairing must not read as a clean one
(standing rule 13).

**Reading the CELL NAME as the layer.**
→ SYMPTOM: 19 Merged approvals reported as Instanced. The pair above is
the cascade working — Merged built FROM the Instanced level below it.

**Reporting a bare Approve/Reject count as an attribution.**
→ SYMPTOM: "46 cells built" told nobody whether the Landscape layer had
been exercised. It had not: 27 Instanced, 19 Merged, 0 Landscape.

### R-HLOD — ADDITIONS 2026-09-13

**A RELATIVE `--run-dir` PRODUCES NO LOG AT ALL.** `rc=1` in 0.3 min,
"no manifest written", empty run directory. The run dir feeds
`-abslog=`, and Unreal resolves relative paths against the engine
binaries folder. The script's DEFAULT run dir is absolute, so the trap
springs only when the flag is used. Pass an absolute path.

**VRAM CLIMBS WITHIN A BATCH AND THE BATCH BOUNDARY IS WHAT RESETS IT.**
Measured on the 2026-09-13 build, batch 0: 771 MiB at cell 1, 3,565 at
cell 45, 6,500 at cell 89 — roughly 64 MiB per cell, monotonic. At 191
cells a batch extrapolates to ~14 GB against the 15.2 GB budget whose
breach produced `DEVICE_HUNG` on 2026-09-12. **The batch size is a VRAM
decision, not only a scheduling one.**

**`--pp-pass` AND ANY `/Game/...` ARGUMENT GO THROUGH POWERSHELL.**
Git-Bash rewrote `/Game/Bench/M_PPI0_Passthrough` into
`C:/Program Files/Git/Game/Bench/M_PPI0_Passthrough`. The tool refused
and printed what it had RECEIVED, which is what made it a one-round-trip
diagnosis.

## R-LANDSCAPE-HLOD — AMENDED 2026-09-14: THE BUILD RECORDS ITS OWN INPUTS, AND THE CAP BINDS

**Every HLOD actor package contains a plain-text block holding the exact
fields the builder hashed, and the command line that wrote it.** Nothing
in this project had ever read it.

    ### HLOD_REPORT_BEGIN ###
    ### Last Build Info ###
     * CommandLine / DateTimeUTC / GraphicsRHI / EngineMode
    ### HLOD Build Details ###
    ## Global Fields ##
        * MinVisibleDistance: 25600
    <per source component>
        * HLODTextureSizePolicy:     SpecificSize(1)
        * HLODTextureSize:           4096
        * ProjectHLODMaxTextureSize: 1024
        * HLODMeshSourceLODPolicy:   LowestDetailLOD(2)
    ### HLOD_REPORT_END ###

Read it with **`python scripts/hlod_report_offdisk.py --l2 --landscape-only
--texdims`**. Read-only, no editor, whole population in seconds.

**Alpine8K, 2026-09-14, 2,267 packages, 0 missing, 0 without a block,
256 L2 landscape cells parsed, all agreeing:**

    MinVisibleDistance         25600              x256
    HLODTextureSizePolicy      SpecificSize(1)    x256
    HLODTextureSize            4096               x256
    ProjectHLODMaxTextureSize  1024               x256
    baked texture dimensions   1024x1024 (3/cell) x256

⭐ **THE CAP BINDS, AND RAISING IT IS NOT A NO-OP.** `SpecificSize` is in
force, so `:224` yields 4096 and `:234` clamps it to the project's 1024.
R-HLODTEX's 4096 IS being clamped. Raising `HLODMaxTextureSize` to 4096
WOULD lift every landscape cell to 4096 — at the cost of a full rebuild
(`:124` hashes `ProjectHLODMaxTextureSize` into the HLOD hash) and a 16x
texel increase on 256 cells. That is a budget decision, not an unknown.

⛔ **`MinVisibleDistance` IS 25,600 cm, NOT THE LAYER'S `loading_range`.**
The Instanced layer's `loading_range` reads 76,800, and three documents
derived texture sizes from it. The builder persists its OWN value on the
HLOD actor at `-SetupHLODs` time and reads it back at build time
(`WorldPartitionHLODUtilities.cpp:421-424`, `:1044`). **Read it from the
package; do not derive it from the layer.** It only matters under
`AutomaticSize` — `SpecificSize` ignores it (`:222-225`) — which is
exactly why the error survived three sessions.

**The flatten path cannot resize anything.** `ExportLandscapeMaterial`
renders the live scene orthographically, top-down, over the proxy's
bounding rect (`MaterialUtilities.cpp:1002-1032`), into a render target
sized from `GetPropertySize` alone (`:845`, `:864`, `:931`). The ONLY
post-render size change in the whole path is `OptimizeSampleArray`
(`:2428-2449`), which fires only on a perfectly uniform sample array and
collapses to **1x1**. So an empty capture yields 1x1, never a small
power of two.

### REJECTED — additions 2026-09-14

**Trusting a texture-size read-back taken from a freshly loaded package.**
→ SYMPTOM: a cell reports 32x32 where its siblings report 1024x1024, and
the SAME cell reports 1024 minutes later in the same session. Two sessions
spent attributing a build behaviour that does not exist.
→ CAUSE: a texture has two sizes — the SOURCE (what the build wrote) and
the PLATFORM DATA (derived, DDC-built, streamed). A query answered from
platform data right after load can return a mip. 1024 -> 32 is exactly
five mip levels.
→ CORRECT: read `scripts/hlod_report_offdisk.py --texdims`, which parses
`FTextureSource.SizeX`/`SizeY` out of the package bytes. If an editor must
be used, read `imported_size` (source) and compare it against
`blueprint_get_size_x()` (platform data) IN THE SAME PAYLOAD — a
disagreement indicts the accessor.
→ REFERENCE: `_verify/hlod/pilot_landscape_2026-09-14/FLATTEN_PATH_VERDICT.md`.

**Reading an instrument's self-contradiction as two data points.**
→ SYMPTOM: "the editor read 32 from disk, and held 1024 minutes later —
worth pursuing; not pursued here", followed by another round of
experiments against the same instrument.
→ CORRECT: **an instrument that disagrees with itself about one object has
already reported its verdict.** Reach for a second instrument, not a third
experiment.

**Reporting a content-size change that the container size contradicts.**
→ SYMPTOM: "three 1024x1024 textures became 32x32" recorded beside
"package before 4,198,360, after 4,198,311 (-49)".
→ CAUSE: no one compared the two numbers in the same report.
→ CORRECT: **a claim about baked content size must move the package size
in the direction and order of magnitude it implies.** Three 1024x1024
sources are ~12.6 MB raw; -49 bytes refutes the claim on arithmetic alone.

**Using `_verify/hlod/<run>/run_console.log` to check per-cell build
behaviour.**
→ SYMPTOM: 0 lines found for a cell that was definitely built, read as
"the full build says nothing about this cell".
→ CAUSE: `run_console.log` is the ORCHESTRATOR's console. The commandlet's
own per-cell lines are in `batch_NN.log`.
→ CORRECT: `grep -l "<cell label>" _verify/hlod/<run>/batch_*.log` first.

**Expecting `LogTexture: Building texture` lines from a rebuild.**
→ SYMPTOM: a single-cell rebuild emits ZERO texture-build lines and zero
`LandscapeNaniteMesh` lines, read as "the landscape was not rendered".
→ CAUSE: those lines are emitted on a DDC MISS only. Identical inputs
produce identical DDC keys and the derived data is reused.
→ CORRECT: their absence is evidence the inputs MATCHED a previous build,
not that work was skipped. To see the sizes, read the FULL build's
`batch_NN.log`, which built them cold.

## R-HLODCAP — RAISING THE LANDSCAPE HLOD TEXTURE CAP (LOCKED 2026-09-14)

**The cap binds under `SpecificSize`, and raising it rebuilds every landscape
cell and nothing else.** Verified end to end on Alpine8K: 256 cells,
1024 → 4096, 1:1 between the recorded cap and the baked dimension on every
census.

### THE VALUES

    file      LandscapeLab/Config/DefaultEngine.ini
    section   [/Script/Landscape.LandscapeSettings]
    key       HLODMaxTextureSize=4096
    class     UCLASS(config = Engine, defaultconfig)  LandscapeSettings.h:45
    clamp     ClampMin 64, ClampMax 8192              LandscapeSettings.h:136
    default   1024                                    LandscapeSettings.h:137

    read-back  python scripts/probe_landscape_settings.py  (as a commandlet)
               -> HLODMaxTextureSize = 4096

    flagged    python scripts/hlod_report_offdisk.py --l2 --landscape-only
               2,267 packages -> 256 carry landscape hash fields, 2,011 do not
    build      python scripts/hlod_build_landscape_cells.py plan|run
               --per-batch 8   VRAM abort 13 GB   free-disk abort 8 GB

### THE NUMBERS, MEASURED

    per cell      package  4.20 MB -> 60.91 MB   (14.5x)
                  VRAM     223 MiB -> 4,699 MiB  (21x, single-cell probe)
                  DDC      ~137 MB/cell
    whole world   0.89 GB -> 13.63 GB  (+12.74 GB)
                  median package 3.79 MB -> 58.02 MB
    32 batches    30.8 min, 255 approved, 0 rejected, 0 torn, 32/32 true exit
                  VRAM 10,015 - 12,116 MiB across all batches

The +12.74 GB landed within 0.5 GB of the figure projected from the
single-cell probe. **Probe one cell, then multiply.**

### WHY ONLY LANDSCAPE CELLS ARE FLAGGED

`LandscapeHLODBuilder.cpp:124` hashes `ProjectHLODMaxTextureSize` inside
`ULandscapeHLODBuilder::ComputeHLODHash` and **nowhere else**. Measured: of
2,267 packages, exactly the 256 carrying landscape hash fields went stale;
**0** non-landscape packages even record the field.

⚠ **BUT THE PARENTS GO STALE ANYWAY, AND NOT VIA THE CAP.** Each of the 256
Merged L1 cells consumes exactly one landscape L2 cell and records that
child's baked texture hashes in its own report. Rebuilding the children
leaves all 256 parents mismatched — 1:1, 0.45 GB of packages. Scope boundary,
not a defect; see `scripts/hlod_stale_parents.py`.

### REJECTED

**`unreal.LandscapeSettings` as the read-back route.**
→ SYMPTOM: `unreal.LandscapeSettings does not exist`.
→ CAUSE: `UCLASS(..., MinimalAPI)` suppresses the Python class binding.
→ CORRECT: load the CDO by path,
`unreal.find_object(None, "/Script/Landscape.Default__LandscapeSettings")`,
then `get_editor_property("HLODMaxTextureSize")` — **the EXACT C++ name**.
The snake_case `hlod_max_texture_size` RAISES; the alias is generated with
the binding and there is no binding.
→ CONTROL THAT MAKES IT A MEASUREMENT: read a PROTECTED property in the same
payload (`SideResolutionLimit`). It raises a DIFFERENT message — "is
protected and cannot be read" — proving the lookup resolved names at all.

**`imported_size` as the source-dimension getter on a texture.**
→ SYMPTOM: "Failed to find property 'imported_size' ... on 'Texture2D'",
and `ImportedSize` raises identically.
→ CAUSE: not on the reflected surface in 5.8, under either spelling.
→ CORRECT: read `FTextureSource.SizeX`/`SizeY` OFF DISK with
`scripts/uasset_lite.py`. That is the only source-side dimension instrument
this project has; both `blueprint_get_built_texture_size` and
`blueprint_get_size_x/y` are PLATFORM data.

**Sizing the batch from the previous texture size.**
→ SYMPTOM: a 16-cell batch plan carried over from 1024-era costs. At 4096 it
would have run ~22 GB VRAM against a 13 GB abort and a 15.2 GB budget whose
breach caused DEVICE_HUNG.
→ CAUSE: VRAM climbs ~1.4 GB per cell WITHIN a batch and resets only at the
boundary; one cell at 4096 peaks 4,699 MiB against 223 MiB at 1024.
→ CORRECT: **8 cells per batch on this machine**, and probe ONE cell whenever
the per-unit cost has just changed by an order of magnitude. The probe costs
20 seconds.

**Assuming the DDC lives where its name says.**
→ SYMPTOM: a cleared `%LOCALAPPDATA%\UnrealEngine\Common\DerivedDataCache`
(0 bytes, 0 files) and a disk that kept filling at ~1.1 GB per batch.
→ CAUSE: this machine's DDC is `C:\UnrealDDC` (Zen + Content + Buckets).
Nothing in the project or engine inis, the registry, or the env overrides
names it; the location was not established.
→ CORRECT: reconcile a per-directory sweep against the VOLUME's free-space
delta before reporting an attribution. A 13 GB gap between the two IS the
finding.
→ ⛔ AND DO NOT QUOTE "relocation is impossible, there is only one drive" as
though it covered this: that finding is about `%LOCALAPPDATA%`, and whether
`C:\UnrealDDC` can be relocated is UNANSWERED.

**Budgeting a DDC clear as a slow run.**
→ It is ONE slow batch. Batch 18, first after a clear, 5.36 min; every later
batch in that leg 1.00 min.
