## R-XGE — THE SHADER-DISPATCH WEDGE, AND MAKING THIS PROJECT SINGLE-MACHINE (LOCKED 2026-09-14)

**Six `-game` launches hung before `LoadMap` on 2026-09-14. The engine had
handed its shader jobs to a local IncrediBuild that never returned them.**
The fix is one ini line; the cost of not recognising it was a session.

### THE SYMPTOM, AND IT LOOKS LIKE NOTHING

    LoadMap                  NEVER appears. No "Bringing World", no StartPlay.
    CPU                      ~0.7 s per 20 s across 69 threads (~5% of ONE core)
    ShaderCompileWorker      ZERO processes
    working set              flat
    last log line            whatever ran before the stall -- often a DDC
                             maintenance pass, which is a PASSENGER, not a cause
    the log SAYS             "LogShaderCompilers: Display: Using XGE Controller
                             for shader compilation"

⛔ **THE PROCESS IS ALIVE AND IDLE, WHICH READS AS "SLOW" AND IS NOT.**
A longer dwell can never help. Distinguish in 20 seconds, on the live
process, not from the log:

    CPU delta over 20 s  < 1 s  AND  ShaderCompileWorker count 0   -> HUNG
    CPU delta over 20 s  > 100 s                                   -> compiling

### THE ONE-LINE RECOGNITION TEST

    ls "$TEMP/UnrealXGEWorkingDir" | wc -l

**Thousands of stale `.in` files = WEDGED.** Measured during the hang:
**4,238** job inputs, e.g.
`4238-xge.Global-FReflectionEnvironmentSkyLightingPS-1211.in`, all stamped
the second the run went silent. The engine wrote them; nothing consumed
them. A healthy run leaves **0**.

Corroborate in IncrediBuild's own log: `xgConsole.log` shows a `Started`
line per launch with **no matching `Stopped`** for the wedged one.

### THE TWO DOCUMENTED SWITCHES, AND WHICH TO USE

Both reach the SAME gate — `ShaderCompiler.cpp:223-233`,
`ShaderCompiler::IsRemoteCompilingAllowed()`:

    static bool bDisabledFromCommandline =
        FParse::Param(FCommandLine::Get(), TEXT("NoRemoteShaderCompile"));
    if (bDisabledFromCommandline) return false;
    return GShaderCompilerAllowDistributedCompilation != 0;

| | `-noxgecontroller` | `-NoRemoteShaderCompile` | **the ini cvar** |
|---|---|---|---|
| scope | XGE controller plugin only | every distributed backend | every distributed backend |
| plugin dependency | yes | none | none |
| names its dispatcher in the log | no | **yes** | **yes** |
| applies to | one launcher | one launcher | **every launch** |

**THE PROJECT FIX, and it is the one to reach for**
(`LandscapeLab/Config/DefaultEngine.ini`, `[SystemSettings]`):

    r.ShaderCompiler.AllowDistributedCompilation=0

Engine default is `1` (`ShaderCompiler.cpp:145`).

### THE READ-BACK, AND IT IS NOT OPTIONAL

Standing rule 12. A launch with **no command-line flag** must log:

    LogShaderCompilers: Display: Using N local workers for shader compilation

**Measured 2026-09-14**: all four perf zones and a commandlet, no flags,
all reported local workers — 7 in `-game`, 14 in a commandlet (different
thread budgets, both local). The wedged runs all said `Using XGE Controller`.
**That one line is the whole diagnosis.**

### WHAT WAS ON THE MACHINE

    IncrediBuild 10.36.3 (build 18514), C:\Program Files (x86)\IncrediBuild
    Agent / Coordinator / Endpoint / License / Manager  Running, Automatic
    BuildCache                                          Stopped, Manual
    Builder\MaxHelpers            0     <- NO helper agents. Single machine.
    BuildService\CoordHost        ""    <- no coordinator host
    InitiatorLicense 2   MaxConcurrentBuilds 1
    Coordinator\TelemetryIbManagerDataServerURL
        = https://laptop-bn8417p3:8000/data/upload   <- the port-8000 holder
                                                        environment.md records

### REJECTED

**"We forgot `-noxgecontroller` on the perf launcher."**
→ SYMPTOM: a tidy causal story that sends the next reader hunting a config
regression that never happened.
→ CAUSE: the flag was absent on **2026-09-11, when the run WORKED**, and on
2026-09-14 when it hung. Both logged `Using XGE Controller for shader
compilation`. XGE was the dispatcher both times; what changed is that it
stopped RETURNING jobs.
→ CORRECT: **the flag is a BYPASS for a path that broke, not a setting
wrongly omitted.** What broke between the dates is NOT established —
IncrediBuild ran `CheckForUpdates` on 09-14 at 19:04, but no install file
carries a post-09-10 write date evidencing an applied update.

**Reading a stalled `-game` process as "the world is slow to load".**
→ SYMPTOM: raising `--settle` from 60 s to 240 s, then 900 s, and getting
the identical failure three times.
→ CAUSE: the process is IDLE, not slow. It consumed 12.1 s of CPU across
241 s of wall clock.
→ CORRECT: the CPU-delta check above, on the live process. It settles the
question in 20 s and no dwell can substitute for it.

**Counting `LogShaderCompilers` lines as a measure of compilation.**
→ SYMPTOM: "progress lines fall across zones (29, 30, 15), so the cache is
warming" — an inference that survived two rounds and was wrong.
→ CAUSE: those lines are periodic progress reports, not work. A run logged
`Current jobs: 225, Num Already Dispatched: 1128` moments before hanging.
→ CORRECT: count `ShaderCompileWorker` PROCESSES and measure CPU.

**Blaming the DDC.** The cache was cleared, relocated to a fresh empty
directory, and its maintenance pass reduced from 35 s to **0.005 s** — the
hang was identical every time. `ZenLocal` reported `Status: OK!` and
`zenserver.exe` was alive and listening on port 8558 throughout. The DDC is
exonerated in all three respects: contents, location, and maintenance.

### ⭐ THE RULE THIS LEAVES BEHIND

**A LAUNCHER FLAG DOCUMENTED AS MANDATORY APPLIES TO EVERY LAUNCHER, NOT
THE ONE IT WAS WRITTEN IN.** `hlod_build_batched.base_args()` has carried
`-noxgecontroller` since R-HLOD 08d with a docstring calling it MANDATORY
and naming this exact wedge. `perf_standalone.py` never carried it. **32
HLOD commandlet batches ran clean on the same machine, the same night, that
six `-game` launches hung** — the mitigation existed, was documented, and
was scoped to whichever file someone happened to be editing.

When a flag is called mandatory, grep for every other process launcher in
`scripts/` before considering it handled.

## R-PROXYFRACTION — THE HLOD-PROXY BAND FRACTION AT A STATION (D-2 item 1b, 2026-09-16)

**What it answers.** Past the R-RANGE loading range (512 m) the runtime shows
the landscape World-Partition HLOD PROXY, not real cells. "How much of a
station's frame is proxy band?" is a geometry question with two instruments in
`scripts/proxy_fraction.py`, and each reports its SAMPLE COUNT beside the
verdict (rule 13):

    --mode depth  DERIVED. Threshold a SceneDepth pass rendered at the
                  editor_player (force-loaded) camera: every non-sky pixel
                  beyond 512 m is, in the runtime, a proxy pixel. Models the
                  runtime from the 512 m boundary; needs no -game process.
    --mode diff   OBSERVED. Frame-diff a real -game frame (proxies present)
                  against the editor_player force-loaded frame. BUILT and
                  selftested; DEFERRED — the MRQ-in-game still is the expensive
                  tail (Ruling R2), re-attempted at end of queue.

**LOCKED VALUE — vista, 2026-09-15 (dev, 2560x1440), DERIVED.** proxy band =
**0.05727 of visible ground** (88,065 proxy of 1,537,813 non-sky px; 2,148,587
sky px excluded; **0.02389 of the whole frame**). The source
`vistaFinalImageSceneDepth.png` is LOCAL evidence (gitignored per the
`_verify/**/*.png` convention — sidecars are the record, not frames); the
committed `proxy_fraction_vista_derived.json` and `bench_run_*_d2_1b_depth.json`
carry the result and provenance (git_sha, recipe_sha256), and the value
re-derives by re-rendering the deterministic SceneDepth pass (`bench_capture
--depth`) and re-running this tool. Cross-checked to the pixel by an independent
recount through the canonical decoder while the frame was on disk (7/7 fields,
NN8). Only 0.17% of ground px lie within ±30 m of the boundary, so 8-bit
log-depth quantisation cannot swing it.

**HOW TO RUN (depth mode).** The project SceneDepth PNG is LOG-encoded
(`haze_metrics.decode_depth_m`, ceiling 10485.76 m); pass `--depth-png` so it
decodes through that single source, OR `--depth` for a raw cm EXR/npy with
`--sky-ceiling-m` if the pass has a finite sky ceiling. Ruling: DESK_LOG R2.

### R-PROXYFRACTION REJECTED

**READING THE LOG-DEPTH PASS WITHOUT A SKY CEILING (`--mode depth --depth`
on our SceneDepth pass, no `--sky-ceiling-m`).**
→ SYMPTOM: proxy_fraction ~0.6 of frame; `excluded_infinite_or_sky = 0` though
most of the frame is sky.
→ CAUSE: our sky is a FINITE log ceiling (10485.76 m), not +inf; every finite
sky pixel is > 512 m, so it is miscounted as proxy. The synthetic selftest used
`np.inf` sky and never exercised the real ceiling — the auditor cleared it.
→ CORRECT: `--depth-png` (decodes via haze_metrics and applies the ceiling), or
`--sky-ceiling-m 10485.76`. Vista then reads 0.05727 of ground, not 0.607.
→ REFERENCE: LESSONS 2026-09-16; proxy_fraction_vista_derived.json.

**PASSING BOTH `--depth` AND `--depth-png`.**
→ SYMPTOM: a number comes back with no error, silently from the PNG.
→ CAUSE: two depth sources, one silently preferred — the e8fe3b15 ambiguity
class.
→ CORRECT: the tool REFUSES (exit 2) when both are given; pass exactly one.
→ REFERENCE: re-audit FIX-1, D-2 item 1b.

## R-SELFREPORT — script self-report discipline (LOCKED, PARTIALLY MECHANIZED)

> STATUS: CURRENT

Distilled from Pass 3 reading (2026-09-18, 178 scripts, ~648 fixes). A
probe, verifier, pilot or mutator must not report a result its execution did
not earn. Five invariants, in force for every such script:

1. **Success is gated on a non-zero sample.** `ok` / a PASS / exit 0 is set
   only after confirming at least one item was examined; a zero count REFUSES
   with a reason beside the verdict (non-negotiable 13).
2. **A read-back is COMPARED, not just reported,** and comes from a different
   instrument than the one that made the claim. `load_asset(PATH)` on a
   resident asset returns the SAME in-memory object — it verifies an in-memory
   struct write-back (via fresh struct copies), NOT disk persistence.
3. **A save's bool return is captured and required.** It is the only
   disk-persistence signal; `save_*` return False on failure without raising.
   **Mechanized:** `scripts/check_save_verified.py`, in `run_offline_suite.py`.
4. **A failed per-field read records ABSENT/UNKNOWN, never drops the key.**
   Missing must stay distinguishable from not-read.
5. **Targets are identified by property signature, not label** (labels collide
   here); a MODE is validated; a single-value restore refuses across
   heterogeneous originals; irreversible bulk ops get a dry-run (rule 8).

Narrative and the full site list: LESSONS.md 2026-09-18. Invariants 1/2/4/5
need judgement and are NOT mechanized — they are the first questions in any
review of a self-reporting script.

## R-SELFREPORT REJECTED

- `_out["ok"] = True` at the tail of a `try`, unconditionally → a run that
  found ZERO items (no volume/sample/asset/station/package) reports success
  having verified nothing; "no dangling / all resolved / no differences" from
  "nothing examined" reads identically to real agreement → **gate ok on a
  non-zero sample count and REFUSE below it** → non-negotiable 13,
  `check_save_verified.py` docstring, LESSONS 2026-09-18 shape 1.
- `Collecting a read-back into a dict and setting ok=True regardless` →
  verification theatre: a clamped/ignored/wrong write still reports success →
  **COMPARE the read-back to the requested value and fold the result into ok**
  → LESSONS 2026-09-18 shape 2 (make_scenetexture_passthrough, set_color_gamma).
- `Re-reading via load_asset() and calling it a save+reload` → load_asset
  returns the RESIDENT object, so disk persistence is unproven while the
  message claims a round-trip → **treat the save bool as the disk evidence;
  say the read-back is in-memory** → LESSONS 2026-09-18 shape 2.
- `eal.save_asset(p)` / `save_loaded_assets(...)` / `save_packages(...)` /
  `write_triangle_mesh(...)` as a bare statement → the return (False on failure
  without raising) is discarded and success prints over a save that may not
  have happened → **capture and require the bool, or add a
  `# save-return: <why>` pragma for a deliberate discard** → **now a suite
  gate: `check_save_verified.py`** (it caught hlod_set_approx_accuracy and
  hlod_set_proxy_budget after the reading pass had "finished").
- `except Exception: pass` around a per-field read → the field vanishes and
  "missing" is indistinguishable from "not read" → **record `"ABSENT"` /
  `"UNKNOWN (<err>)"`** → LESSONS 2026-09-18 shape 4.
- `get_actor_label() == X`, first match wins, to pick an actor to mutate →
  labels collide (two landscapes carried identical proxy labels), so an
  arbitrary actor is changed silently → **collect all matches, refuse on >1,
  identify by property signature** → rule 8, LESSONS 2026-09-18 shape 5
  (move_station_diagnostic, task4_shadow_lever).
- `a == b is False` to mean "unchanged and off" → Python chained comparison
  `(a == b) and (b is False)`, so the check is forced False whenever `b` was
  ever True, regardless of change → **write the intended comparison explicitly
  (`a == b`)** → hlod_set_approx_accuracy, found wiring the save gate.
- `A negative control that counts ANY non-zero exit as a correct refusal` →
  the harness "proves the gate works" whenever the tool merely crashes for an
  unrelated reason → **assert the SPECIFIC failure reason (the gate's own exit
  code / message)** → prove_gaea_reader, LESSONS 2026-09-18.

## R-GITHUB-LITE — GITHUB HOLDS THE RECIPE, THIS MACHINE HOLDS THE WORLD (RULED 2026-09-27)

**Status: RULED (Ryan, option 2), built, PROVEN 2026-09-27 21:05 -- the first push landed
(GitHub main 12e97eec, tree == github-main) via the staged tree push below.**

GitHub Free: 10 GiB Git LFS storage per account, every object version ever
pushed counts, and only deleting the repository frees it. This repo's history
carried **37.2 GB** of LFS — 22.2 GB of it 42,066 versions of World Partition
external-actor packages (~1,000 per world save). The disk holds 13 GB free, so
no history-rewrite clone fits. Ruling: recreate `ryan772177/LandscapeLab` empty
and push a SNAPSHOT branch without the world.

### THE CONTRACT

    local  main          FULL repo: world packages, fence tags, git-as-undo. Never pushed.
    local  github-main   DERIVED: HEAD tree minus the EXCLUDE list, one commit per snapshot.
    GitHub main          = github-main.  6.05 GB LFS at first push (419 objects).
    EXCLUDE              LandscapeLab/Content/__ExternalActors__, __ExternalObjects__,
                         _verify/bench   (hero binaries KEPT since 4459becc: no second copy)

    python scripts/github_lite_snapshot.py --push     # after every commit worth sharing

The world is rebuildable from `recipes/` + `foliage/` + `city/` +
`encounters/` (pipeline rule 3); the recipe is what GitHub keeps. The D3
driver, `save_level`, R-EDITOR-CLOSE and every fence tag keep working on local
`main` exactly as before.

### WHAT CHANGES FOR PRs AND REVIEWS

A branch for review is pushed the same way: build its snapshot with the
script (it refuses off `main`; extend `--source` when needed) or push a
docs/scripts-only branch, which carries no LFS. Tags stay local; name them in
STATE.md instead of expecting them on GitHub.

### FIRST PUSH TO AN EMPTY REPO (PROVEN 2026-09-27; LESSONS 2026-09-27b)

1. Account billing (GitHub Free): Settings -> Billing and plans -> Payment information -> add a
   card; Budgets and alerts -> New budget -> **Product level** -> Git LFS -> $5, **"Stop usage when
   budget limit is reached" UNCHECKED**. Until a card is on file the push answers "This repository
   exceeded its LFS budget" even on an empty repo while the deleted repo's objects still count.
2. Measure the pack BEFORE pushing (bytes, not commits):
       git rev-list --objects github-main | cut -d' ' -f1 | git cat-file --batch-check='%(objecttype) %(objectsize)'
   The 2026-09-27 snapshot: 3,889 plain blobs = 3,804 MB in the root commit. GitHub accepts ~2 GB
   of pack per push and answers `RPC failed; HTTP 500` above it, AFTER the LFS objects are up.
3. Over 2 GB in one commit -> `bash scripts/push_staged_tree.sh github-main origin research hero _verify`
   (re-roots the snapshot on a chain whose trees grow one directory per commit, pushes each step to
   main, replays the snapshot commits on top, re-points github-main). Steps landed at 0.43 / 1.46 /
   0.69 / 1.22 GB. Over 2 GB across MANY commits -> `scripts/push_chunked.py` (2026-09-20).
4. Verify: `git ls-remote --heads origin main` == `git rev-parse github-main`; the script checks the
   tree equality itself. Later snapshots are text-sized and go through `github_lite_snapshot.py --push`.

### REJECTED

**ORPHAN "SEED" BRANCHES TO PRE-LOAD BLOBS** (push `commit-tree <subtree>` as seed-* refs, then push
the real branch) -> the seeds land, the real push still sends every blob and 500s: pack-objects omits
only objects reachable from ANCESTORS of the pushed commit that the remote has. Verified with
`git rev-list --objects github-main ^<seed>`: all 810 hero/ blobs still listed. Also leaves the first
seed as GitHub's DEFAULT branch, which it refuses to delete until the default is switched.
**`http.postBuffer=1048576000` FOR THE 500** -> same HTTP 500 after the same 22 min; the limit is
server-side pack size, not client buffering.
**`push_chunked.py` ON A ONE-COMMIT BRANCH** -> halves to span 1 and its own rule says "oversized
blob, stop"; the diagnosis is wrong when no blob exceeds 100 MB (largest 98.5 MB) and the PACK does.

**PUSHING LOCAL `main` OR A TAG TO THE NEW REPO** → the push uploads every
world package the commit's tree references; the quota is gone again within
one world save → only `github-main` goes up.
**DELETING FILES IN A NEW COMMIT TO "FREE" LFS** → frees nothing; GitHub
retains every pushed object until the repo is deleted.
**A HISTORY REWRITE (`git filter-repo`) ON THIS MACHINE** → needs a second
copy of a 64 GB `.git` on a disk with 13 GB free.

### THE RISK, STATED (rule 10)

After the GitHub repo is deleted, this laptop's `.git` (64 GB, LFS 43,447
objects) is the ONLY copy of the world history. An external-drive copy of
`.git` before the delete is the mitigation; the disk itself is at 99 %.
Since 2026-09-27 21:05 GitHub holds the lite copy (everything except the
world packages and `_verify/bench`); the world packages remain single-copy.
